Throughout the course, an engineering and user-centered design approach will guide students, emphasizing the importance of creating solutions that prioritize patient needs and real-world applications. This blend of theory and practical experience prepares students to tackle challenges and fosters an appreciation for the evolving field of biomedical engineering.

cilos.description: Describe key concepts in biomedical engineering and illustrate their applications in everyday life
Apply engineering principles to solve biomedical engineering problems, supported by relevant examples from personal experiences
Describe essential human anatomy and physiology relevant to biomedical engineering professionals
Critically assess current medical technologies in the market, leveraging knowledge of biomedical engineering principles
Evaluate the social, ethical, and economic implications of innovations and technologies in biomedical engineering
Demonstrate effective teamwork and presentation skills, showcasing the ability to collaborate and communicate ideas clearly

courses.title: Modeling for Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: Modeling of physical, chemical and biological processes. Balance Equations. Dimensional and scaling analysis. Analytical and numerical solutions to initial and boundary value problems. Use of computer tools for engineering calculations. This course uses examples in the Bioengineering discipline. For BIEN students only.

cilos.description: Model simple physical, chemical and biological processes as mathematical equations.
Develop and interpret differential equations in initial and boundary value problems.
Solve differential equations analytical and/or numerically.
Describe elementary concepts in statistics and perform simple hypothesis testing and regression analysis.
Use computing tools for engineering calculations.

courses.title: Cellular and Systems Physiology for Engineers
courses.description: Essential cellular and systems physiology for engineers. Hierarchical organization of a complex organism: from organelles to organ systems. Cellular physiology, neurophysiology, vision, muscle and movement, and the cardiovascular system.
courses.prerequisite: LIFS 1901 OR Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology

cilos.description: Describe the essential concepts in cell biology and systems physiology.
Describe the principles of the neural and cardiovascular systems.
Appreciate the connection between cellular and systems physiology and the design and engineering of pharmaceutical products and biomedical devices.

courses.title: Chemical Biology for Engineers
courses.description: A concise introduction of biochemistry, cell biology, and pharmacology to engineers. Molecular and supramolecular building blocks of biological systems. Analysis and engineering of biological systems by chemical principles. Introduction to transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics.
courses.prerequisite: (CHEM 1010 (prior to 2022-23) OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

cilos.description: Describe at a basic level the biochemical machinery of living cells.
Describe and apply analytical techniques for biomolecules, including omics.
Describe techniques and application of biomolecular engineering.
Describe concepts in basic pharmacology and drug discovery.
Apply concepts in chemistry to evaluate innovative ideas in bioengineering.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: For students in the Bioengineering major. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students, to enhance their understanding of the bioengineering field, to encourage them to pursue co-curricular learning opportunities available to them, and to improve their communication skills. Students are required to attend discussion sessions with advisors and fellow students and selected workshops and seminars. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Be motivated and equipped to pursue the co-curricular learning opportunities available to bioengineering students.
Be aware of possible career paths of bioengineers and how to prepare for them.
Form a strong community with faculty and fellow students in the program.
Communicate effectively in group settings.

courses.title: Rate and Transport Processes in Biological Systems
courses.description: Analysis of transport phenomena and rate processes, including fluid flow, energy and mass transport, and reactions in biological systems. Applications in human physiology, bioreactors, medical devices, drug delivery, and biosensors. Mathematical and computational tools for solving problems and designing applications involving such processes.

cilos.description: Describe the fundamental principles of transport phenomena and reaction kinetics.
Describe and model rate and transport processes in biological systems.
Formulate and solve problems involving rate and transport processes.
Appreciate the connection between rate and transport processes and animal physiology and how it influences the effective design of various biomedical devices.
Use computing tools for problem solving involving rate and transport processes.

courses.title: Data Science for Molecular Engineering
courses.description: This course is an introductory course on the application of machine learning methods in molecular engineering problems. It covers fundamental data processing and machine learning methods to analyze data in chemistry and biology such as molecular similarity calculation and property prediction.

cilos.description: Identify problems that can be formulated as a supervised learning task.
Process different types of data to be ready for model training.
Understand the principles of supervised learning methods.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Know the application of data science methods in molecular science related problems.

courses.title: Data Science for Neural Engineering
courses.description: This is an introductory course on data science and its applications in neural engineering. The course introduces the fundamentals of data science, principles of  neuroscience, and the technologies and implementations of neural engineering. The  topics include probability, random variables, statistical detection and estimation, random process, structure and function of the nervous system, encoding and  decoding, population coding, neural network, plasticity and learning, neural interfaces and rehabilitation.
courses.prerequisite: (CENG 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR MATH 2111)

cilos.description: Understand the basic concepts of probability, random processes, expectation and averages.
Obtain a holistic view of neural engineering.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Comprehend fundamentals of basic coding theory and computation methods.
Analyze neural data and implement on neural-controlled device/robot.
Enhance the knowledge in neural engineering, signal processing and practical programming.

courses.title: Data Science for Biology and Medicine
courses.description: This is an introductory course for the application of data science in biology and medicine. The course will introduce the fundamental principles on data science, the technologies and implementations of data mining, as well as the modeling of several practical questions in biomedicine. The topics include introduction to biomedical data, data visualization, regression methods and classification methods.
courses.prerequisite: (COMP 1021 OR COMP 1023) AND (level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology OR LIFS 1901)

cilos.description: Obtain a basic understanding of data science as a discipline.
Understand high-throughput biomedical data of various types.
Visualize, analyze and interpret biomedical data with sound statistical principles.
Apply computational methods and software tools in data science in the context of biomedicine.
Develop mathematical models for scientific questions.

courses.title: Bioimaging and Image Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces various bioimaging methods and their data analysis approaches, including optical coherence tomography, fluorescence microscopy, nonlinear microscopy, super-resolution microscopy, ptychographic microscopy, and photoacoustic tomography. Students will be able to understand, design, and evaluate those imaging techniques. This course requires basic knowledge of linear algebra, calculus, and geometry.

cilos.description: Describe the working principles of widely used bioimaging technologies.
Design and evaluate bioimaging devices that can acquire biological information from the human body.
Describe how bioimaging technologies address biological and clinical needs in practice.
Research and evaluate information about bioimaging technologies and their applications.

courses.title: Biosensors and Bioinstrumentation for Healthcare
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamental principles in bioinstrumentation and biosensing devices, and practical examples of such in biomedical applications. Concepts in bioelectric and biochemical signals, their measurement and transduction will be introduced.

cilos.description: Describe the working principles of widely used bioinstrumentation and biosensors.
Design and evaluate bioinstrumentation and biosensors that can acquire bioelectrical or biochemical signals from the human body.
Describe how bioinstrumentation and biosensors address clinical needs in practice.
Appreciate how technological advances in this field can potentially revolutionize healthcare in the future.

courses.title: Bioengineering Laboratory
courses.description: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Describe the principles behind the experimental modules and how they are applied in the experiments (tentatively molecular biotechnology, biomaterials, biosensors, sequencing and bioimaging).
Design and conduct experiments relevant to the bioengineering discipline.
Process, analyze and interpret experimental data in a statistically sound manner.
Develop soft skills including teamwork, open-ended problem solving, report writing and presentation.

courses.title: Special Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest not covered by existing courses. May be graded by letter, P/F, or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Regulatory Affairs in the Healthcare Industry
courses.description: This course aims to introduce basic concepts of regulatory science, while familiarizing students with product development, manufacturing, medical and engineering operations, and quality control / quality assurance processes in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry. Students will also be introduced to the associated regulatory requirements, with an emphasis on Hong Kong, Great Bay Area, China and beyond, in topics such as Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), pharmaceutical product registration, pharmacovigilance, and clinical trials.

cilos.description: Form a conceptual framework of regulatory science and engineering that underpins regulatory affairs of medical products worldwide.
Outline the current practices of medical and engineering operations in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry.
Describe the importance and processes of quality assurance / quality control in the manufacture of both pharmaceutical products.
Outline how Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and Pharmaceutical Inspection Convention and Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) are implemented.
Outline the roles of medical affairs, medical science liaison, and pharmacovigilance in the pharmaceutical industry.
Describe the principles and practice of clinical trials and the importance of clinical trials in drug development.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent studies or projects under the directed guidance of a faculty member on a bioengineering topic. Enrollment in the course requires prior approval of the course instructor, and credits assigned depend on the workload. Students may repeat the course if different topics are taken. The course may be grade by letter or P/F subject to different offerings. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Learn the professional and technical knowledge in the bioengineering research area.
Equip students with written and presentation skills in engineering disciplines.

courses.title: Bioengineering Capstone Design
courses.description: A final-year project course offers practice of bioengineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Bioengineering Thesis Research
courses.description: A final-year project course offers an opportunity to conduct individual bioengineering research under the direct supervision of a faculty member, which leads to a Bachelor's thesis. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Manage a research project effectively by personal management and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.
Obtain and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own research.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering research on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Articulate research questions and outcomes effectively both in writing and orally.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Conduct scholarly research in the realm of bioengineering.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments.
Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.

courses.title: Bioengineering Industrial Project
courses.description: This course is intended to provide final-year bioengineering students with practical hands-on training in the form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in a bioengineering company. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: For final-year Bioengineering students. This course is designed to prepare students for the workplace, to instill in them a sense of professional responsibility, and to enhance their career management skills. Students are required to attend selected workshops and seminars by practicing bioengineers. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand the career opportunities available to bioengineering graduates.
Approach the job search process with preparedness and confidence.
Function effectively in the workplace as a professional.
Appreciate the standard of ethics and professional responsibility expected of bioengineers.

courses.title: Molecular Biology for Bioengineering
courses.description: The course introduces the basics of cell biology, molecular biology techniques, and discusses the principles of macromolecular interactions in those contexts. We will also discuss various applications of these techniques and how combined with engineering concepts, they have contributed to innovations and breakthrough tools in the world of basic research and medicine. Topics to cover include: overview of basic molecular biology and macromolecular interactions; basic biophysical structures, imaging and characterization techniques; molecular engineering; biodevices; and genomics. Active student discussion is required and students will also do a final project team presentation on a current bioengineering topic.

cilos.description: Describe the central dogma of molecular biology, and be able to recall the various molecular components (molecules, proteins/enzymes) involved in the components of the central dogma. Describe their main physical features and select appropriate tools/techniques for characterizing them.

Explain the mechanisms and functions of basic molecular biology assays, including PCR, qPCR, gel electrophoresis, molecular cloning, protein separation and purification; be able to analyze and interpret results of above assays.
Compare different types of imaging tools, and describe their usage and importance in modern biotechnology/medicine.

Explain what a stem cell is, and compare differences between embryonic stem cells, fetal stem cells, adult stem cells, and induced pluripotent cells; recall modern applications of stem cell therapies, and explain the mechanism of action for these therapies; describe current major challenges in using stem cell therapies in the clinic.

Explain and critique recent breakthroughs in molecular biology and bioengineering fields, including those outside your research area; be able to suggest potential applications of these new technologies to a relevant clinical challenge.

Present and discuss the taught ideas and concepts with peers with clarity and evidence-based reasoning; collaborate with team mates with positive attitude and strong work ethic in a group project setting.

courses.title: Introduction to Neural Engineering
courses.description: This course will provide a survey of Neuroscience and Neuroengineering research areas to provide our research postgraduate students a broad appreciation of interdisciplinary research in context. The course aims to help student recognize and understand how knowledge from science and engineering interface in this interdisciplinary application. Concepts such as neural interfacing and neural prosthesis will be introduced so that students can understand the impact of the latest technologies. The course will enhance the vision of the students and encourage them to work in future inter-disciplinary research fields.

cilos.description: Obtain a holistic view of systems neuroscience fundamentals and methods.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Write a literature review on a topic within systems neuroscience.
Explain basic neural coding theory and computation method.
Enhance the knowledge in related area, such as neural engineering.

courses.title: Global Health Ethics
courses.description: Through real-time videoconferencing with participants from different countries such as the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Mexico, and Philippines, this ONLINE course aims at helping students learn the definitions of global health ethics and bioethics, the different protocol and systems in place to ensure adherence to ethical principles, and how different stakeholders and cultures may interpret ethics differently. Through case studies on ethical challenges from real-world situations, students will analyze and discuss the complexities of global health practice and research ethics in a global context. This course is co-offered with the University of Southern California. Besides the joint LIVE sessions, face-to-face sessions and group projects are also arranged for the introduction of background knowledge, case studies, group project discussion, and technical support.

cilos.description: Articulate the important ethical considerations of biomedical research, basic and clinical, involving human subjects.
Outline the unique ethical and social implications of conducting such research in developing countries of different economic status.
Identify key trends and emerging issues in global health ethics.
Analyze situations of ethical challenges in global health practice and research from diverse perspectives.
Appreciate the role culture and religion play in the development of a sense of right and wrong and views on ethics and how protocol fitting to the local context can be justified
Describe best practices in ethical health research and practice to protect human subjects and their legal right

courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Sensing Technologies in Healthcare
courses.description: The course will introduce the basic concepts in detection of biosignals. Students will learn about the biosensing components, transduction mechanisms, novel materials in sensing, and analytical techniques to capture diverse health information. The course will also touch upon the physical and chemical sensors used for healthcare applications. We will also discuss about the emerging flexible, wearable technology toward personalized healthcare. Students will have opportunities to design and propose biosensors and bioelectronics at the end of the course.

cilos.description: Explain how biosensors work.
Describe different techniques for bio-signal determination.
Evaluate biosensors performance.
Propose biosensors for real world applications.

courses.title: Synthetic Biology
courses.description: Synthetic biology, which echoes the assertion “What I cannot create, I do not understand” made by Richard Feynman, has been hailed as a revolution for modern science and technology. Unfledged as it is, the field, arising from the synergistic combination of chemistry, biology, engineering, data science, and information/control theory, has already shown great promise in addressing energy and health-related global challenges. This course aims to expose students with diverse backgrounds to this highly interdisciplinary field and furnish them with necessary guidance and ideas for taking on synthetic biology projects.

cilos.description: Describe the basic concepts and engineering principles in synthetic biology.
Describe the central dogma of molecular biology and control strategies of gene replication, transcription, post-transcriptional modification, and translation.
Describe the genetic parts, devices, circuits, and systems in synthetic biology.
Explain the design of genetic circuits, including genetic input, biological computing, and output Modules, and describe what Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is in synthetic biology.
Explain the mechanisms of synthetic biology tools, including Gibson assembly, Golden Gate assembly, DNA recombination, DNA synthesis, directed evolution, and genome editing.
Recognize, evaluate, and criticize the design of genetic circuits in scientific literature of synthetic biology.
Explain real-world applications of synthetic biology.
Enhance communication skills.

courses.title: Equilibrium Behavior, Kinetics, and Transport Phenomena in Chemical and Biological Systems
courses.description: This course provides graduate students with a fundamental and integrated understanding of core principles in thermodynamics, chemical reaction kinetics, and transport phenomena, with applications to chemical and biological systems. It equips students - particularly those without prior chemical engineering training - with quantitative reasoning tools to interpret equilibrium and dynamic processes in biological and physiological systems. Through in-class discussions, homework, and student presentations, the course applies these principles to address research questions and practical challenges in bioengineering and related fields.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental principles of thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, and transport phenomena to analyze equilibrium and dynamic processes in chemical and biological systems.
Use quantitative engineering tools to interpret exemplary biological and physiological phenomena mechanistically.
Critically evaluate and solve research-oriented problems in chemical engineering and bioengineering through in-class discussions and applications.
Communicate technical concepts effectively via presentations and written summaries.
Collaborate in teams to apply course knowledge to design projects addressing practical or research challenges in biological systems.

courses.title: Microfluidics and Biosensors
courses.description: Introduction to Microfluidics and Biosensors; Overview of microfabrication materials & techniques; microfluidic principles; miniaturized biosensors; micro total analysis system (µTAS) & lab-on-a-chip (LOC) for clinical and research applications.

cilos.description: Describe core concepts in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Describe trends and motivations in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Analyze/critique research articles in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Formulate a potential solution for a clinical problem using Microfluidics & Biosensors.

courses.title: Bioengineering Seminar
courses.description: Seminar topics presented by students and faculty. Students are expected to attend regularly and demonstrate proficiency in their seminar presentation in accordance with the program requirements. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify current research of interest in various topics of bioengineering.
Obtain insights to how peer researchers design and conduct experiments.
Gain opportunities to make academic and social contacts with the peer researchers.
Demonstrate proficiency in presentation of research outcome coherently and thoroughly (as presenters).

courses.title: Bioengineering Colloquia
courses.description: Bioengineering Colloquia is a seminar course that brings prominent researchers in the field of bioengineering to share their research with BIEN colleagues and students. The course aims to provide a platform for discussions and exchange of ideas on the late advancements in the field of bioengineering. Students will have the opportunity to engage with the speakers and ask questions, fostering a deeper understanding of the research presented. The course will cover a broad range of topics, including chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, synthetic biology and more. Students are expected to attend regularly. Grade P or F.

cilos.description: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the latest advancements and research trends in various areas of bioengineering.
Develop the ability to critically analyze and evaluate research presentations, recognizing the significance and implications of the findings.
Improve their ability to articulate questions and engage in discussions, enhancing their communication skills in a professional setting.
Appreciate the interdisciplinary nature of bioengineering by exploring topics across chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, and synthetic biology.
Learn how to network effectively with professionals and researchers, building connections that may benefit their academic and career pursuits.
Develop informed perspectives on current challenges and future directions in the field of bioengineering.

courses.title: Special Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Selected topics in bioengineering of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to integrate knowledge and to analyse, evaluate and manage the different aspects of a special topic in bioengineering.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work.
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: Principles and Application in Biotechnology
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide an interdisciplinary, state-of-the-art introduction to biotechnology.  Topics include the molecular foundations of biotechnology, molecular microbiology, biotech process development and scale-up, product approval and regulatory affairs, genomics, microarray analysis, proteomics, computational biology, molecular modeling, analytical biotechnology, and bioterrorism and biotechnology.

cilos.description: Process factual knowledge comprehensively across the principal area of biotechnology.
Explain information related to the principles of cutting-edge biotechnology.
Evaluate information related to and data derived from experimental models in biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to research methodology of biotechnology.
Identify complexity of issues facing biotechnology and types of contributions that can be offered to society.

courses.title: Business Operations of Biotechnology
courses.description: Management perspective of R&D process, methods for planning and organizing biotechnology ventures, basic concepts of intellectual property rights and methods and principles of marketing new technology-based products and services.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a broad based knowledge in core business and management perspective of pharmaceutical industry.
State basic concepts of intellectural property rights.
Recognize the aspect of regulatory affairs of pharmaceutical products.
Apply appropriate marketing methods for new technology-based products.
Develop business plan for biotechnology-based products via team work.
Engage with professionals in the field of biotechnology business.

courses.title: Bioanalytical Technology
courses.description: The use and development of biomolecules for analytics: enzymes and immunotests, DNA probes, biosensors and biodipsticks.  Application of other analytical techniques for bio- and medical sciences will also be introduced.

cilos.description: Apply functional methods in biotechnology to solve problems in analytical work.
Identify knowledge in the experimental design for development of bioanalytical tools.
Evaluate different analytical methods used for measuring biological substances.
Describe the value of biomedical analysis on human health.

courses.title: Biomarkers and Medical Devices
courses.description: Introduction to biomarkers and its examination by medical devices, with a focus on utilization of biomarkers in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, and a comprehensive overview on the regulatory affairs and marketing strategy of medical devices.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge about biomarkers and its instrumentation.
Evaluate the wide scope of application of biomarkers in diagnosis and therapy for various diseases.
Apply functional knowledge of biomarkers for cases of clinical diagnosis and disease treatment.
Describe the methodology related to biomarker analysis.
Interpret the business competence and market potential of biomarkers.

courses.title: Biopharmaceutical Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to various laboratory techniques commonly applied in the biopharmaceutical industry for drug discovery and development applications, with a focus on gaining hands-on experience through laboratory practices. Advanced techniques such as automated screening and multiplex detection will be covered.

cilos.description: Demonstrate hands-on laboratory techniques applied to cell culture, transfection, protein detection and quantification, cytotoxicity, etc.
Evaluate the wide scope of applications for laboratory protocols involved in the process of various bioassay.
Integrate various biological and pharmacological concepts to establish possible schemes for drug screening.
Design and perform experiments for automated screening of potential drug candidates with defined targets.
Devise team-based laboratory tasks and construct formally-written report for experimental data.

courses.title: Drug Discovery and Development
courses.description: Overview of methodology employed in identification of lead compounds, drug synthesis and development.  Receptor screening technology for target identification, high-throughput screening for lead identification, and the process for turning lead compounds into marketable drug products.

cilos.description: Explain basic and in-depth information about drug discovery and development.
Apply functional knowledge in the design and selection of drug discovery assays.
Evaluate information and data derived from drug screening activities.
Describe the fundamental concepts of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.
Employ different approaches to identify lead compounds and optimize candidates for drug development.
Identify regulatory affairs and key factors in relation to the drug development process.

courses.title: Nutraceuticals and Transgenic Products
courses.description: Highlights in current applications of biotechnology on the research and development of nutraceuticals and transgenic products.  Scientific approaches to natural product drug discovery, TCM-based health products, and nutritional products will be discussed.

cilos.description: Explain the general concept underlying the use of nutraceuticals and transgenic products.
Describe how nutraceutical and transgenic products are developed.
Describe in a broad sense about experimental and clinical studies on nutraceuticals.
Evaluate the scientific and commerical potentials of a candidate nutraceutical and transgenic product, and to produce a feasibility report on it.

courses.title: Recombinant DNA Technology and Bioproducts
courses.description: The course focuses on upstream and downstream processings in biotechnology.  Molecular biology of recombinant DNA techniques, the properties of fermentation broths, the selection of source material or organisms and the separation technology for the recovery of products.

cilos.description: Review the wide scope of applications of biotechnology in medicine, agriculture, biomass utilization for energy generation, and environmental conservation.
Apply functional knowledge in microbial selection and manipulation for bioproduct synthesis.
Evaluate the key concepts and scientific principles of fermentation technology in relation to industrial biotechnology.
Describe the day-to-day business management and operation undertaken in a biotechnology corporation.
Identify the legal, social and ethical concerns in biotechnology.

courses.title: Concepts in Bioprocessing
courses.description: Weaves concepts and fundamentals common to various aspects of bioprocessing.  They include the analysis of transport phenomenon in biological systems (for example, immobilized cell or enzyme systems, artificial organs, and drug delivery systems); genetic engineering techniques applied to microorganisms, animals, and plants; and the cellular machinery and process by which biological products are synthesized by the cell.

cilos.description: Recognize the basic information of bioproduct and bioprocessing.
Define the flow of bioreactor industries from upstream to downstream processes.
Explain major examples for application and research in the bio-productive processes.
Indicate the advanced knowledge of fermentation technology in relation to industrial biotechnology.
Apply functional knowledge in molecular farming.

courses.title: Immuno Biotechnology
courses.description: A systematic review of the overall organization and function of the immune system with a special emphasis on antibody-based technology and its broad applications in various aspects of scientific research and medicine.

cilos.description: Describe basic knowledge of immunology.
Define the principles and operations of immune cell development, immune diversity and response.
Explain immunological applications and their uses in research and medicine.
Describe the latest trend in antibody-based technology.
Identify the potential of immunology for biotechnology.
Critically review the literature in immunology.
Analyze and solve problems related to immune responsiveness.

courses.title: Case Investigation in Biotechnology
courses.description: Students will review a topic of their choice in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member.  An in-depth reading and analysis by the student of the selected topic leading to the submission of a written report, and its presentation in a seminar.

cilos.description: Retrieve and explain information correlated with the business values of a biotechnological company.
Evaluate information based on comprehensive search of scientific databases, websites and international journals.
Produce high quality reseasrch independently.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking through reading, analysis and synthesis of information, and production of research reports.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Directed Biotechnological Research
courses.description: Students will undertake a research project of their choice in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member.  The results of the research will be presented in a seminar and be formally written in the form of a final report.  For MSc student who can participate in day-time laboratory work only.

cilos.description: Develop laboratory skills and methods related to research work of biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to qualitatively and quantitatively appraise experimental data and outcomes.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking for experimental design and production of research reports.
Conduct laboratory research via team work.
Engage with fellow graduates and/or professionals in the field of biotechnological research.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Advanced Biotechnological Research
courses.description: Students will undertake a research project in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member. The results of the research will be presented in a seminar and be formally written in the form of a final report. For full time MSc students only.

cilos.description: Develop laboratory skills and methods related to research work of biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to qualitatively and quantitatively appraise experimental data and outcomes.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking for experimental design and production of research reports.
Conduct laboratory research via team work.
Engage with fellow graduates and/or professionals in the field of biotechnological research.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Foundations of Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: This foundational course is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the core principles of the disciplines within the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering (CBE). It serves as a springboard for all CBE students, providing a broad overview of their major programs, essential knowledge and skills for engineering studies, and insights into career opportunities. The course combines lectures with hands-on projects, demonstrations, and experiments.

cilos.description: Formulate ideas for product design, and evaluate them based on technical, economical and societal considerations.
Synthesize a process at the conceptual level for manufacturing the product.
Specify and quantify the materials and energy that enter and leave the process, and how they are transformed in the process.
Explain the breadth and versatility of the discipline of chemical and biomolecular engineering.
Acquire elementary skills of project management.
Function effectively in a team consisting not only of students, but also supervisors and subject experts.
Articulate ideas and communicate effectively in meetings, technical reports and presentations.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: This course is designed to provide academic advising to new students in the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering, to enhance their sense of identity and belonging, to familiarize them with their major disciplines, to encourage them to pursue co-curricular learning opportunities, and to improve their communication skills. Activities include meetings with faculty advisors, senior students and alumni, seminars and workshops, and various community building activities. For CBE students only. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Be motivated and equipped to pursue the co-curricular learning opportunities available to bioengineering students.
Be aware of possible career paths of bioengineers and how to prepare for them.
Form a strong community with faculty and fellow students in the program.
Communicate effectively in group settings.

courses.title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Application of material and energy balances to batch and continuous processes involving reactive and non-reactive unit operations and recycle systems. Introductions to chemical process and product design, equipment design, simulation and computational tools.

cilos.description: Apply material and energy balance principles to analyze chemical processes.
Estimate capital/operation costs of chemical processes.
Obtain, process, and synthesize information for process analysis and evaluation.
Function in project teams tasked with process analysis and evaluation.
Communicate with stakeholders regarding process analysis and evaluation.
Self-monitor and self-assess one’s learning by using learning portfolios.

courses.title: A First Course on Materials Science and Applications
courses.description: The scope of this course is to introduce different categories of materials and to elucidate their applications. We will start from the basic concepts of matter to the basic structures at molecular scale, and then to the science and engineering of materials. The focus of the course is the structure/property relationship. The principles for designing and developing useful materials for special applications will be discussed.

cilos.description: Describe the basic structures and properties of materials used in our daily life, and discuss the novel applications of selected advanced materials
Understand basic techniques for measuring the common properties of materials, and for fabricating and processing of novel materials
Evaluate the social, economical, and environmental impact of materials

courses.title: Biotechnology and Its Business Opportunities
courses.description: This course gives an introductory overview of biotechnology from both technical and business perspectives. It surveys the current landscape of medical biotechnology, discusses the significant milestones in this field, describes underlying scientific concepts, and emphasizes the impact of innovations on human health and economy. Case studies are used to illustrate the opportunities and limitations in current and future biotechnology development. In addition, experts from industry and academia are invited to give guest lectures on course-related topics.

cilos.description: Explain the basic technical concepts, scientific and engineering principles in medical biotechnology
Describe the opportunities and challenges faced by the industry
Analyze the potential and impact of modern biotechnology on human health and economy
Identify the key components contributing to biotechnology of commercial interest
Research topics in biotechnology and its current development
Communicate technical ideas effectively
Develop ability work in a team with complementary strengths

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of environmental impact assessment will be discussed. Life cycle analysis of carbon and energy will be introduced using case studies. Principles of environmental engineering for control of air, water, solid and noise pollution will be discussed, including global pollution, pollution prevention and minimization. Cost of available technologies will be analyzed.

cilos.description: Apply data collection and analysis skills in environmental impact assessment and life cycle analysis
Comprehend and apply the basic principles of environmental engineering in pollution control
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams
Communicate and present key environmental issues and their solutions effectively
Pursue lifelong learning as self-regulated learners
Apply ethics in environmental quality control and improvement as responsible citizens and decision makers

courses.title: Introduction to Food Science and Technology
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with fundamental knowledge of food science (chemistry, nutrition, microbiology, etc.) and safety issues for daily consumption, and preliminary perspective for further exploration on food processing technologies. This course also emphasizes critical thinking skills, helps students to tell the truth/myth of healthy products, food additives, and genetically modified foods, and make a wise judgement for food consumption.

cilos.description: Identify the major nutrients and chemical components in different food products, and how they meet body’s needs
Explain the principle and operation of food related systems, and the physical or chemical methods used in food processing, preservation and production
Apply safe, sustainable and economical practices when using and developing relevant technologies
Apply principles to practice, testing and analyzing parameters through hands-on experiments
Design a food product, process or facility by incorporating food science, technology, safety, and economical aspects
Critically examine the contemporary issues related to food

courses.title: Industrial Training
courses.description: A practical training course in an industrial simulated environment. For students of the Chemical and Biological Engineering Department only. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Gain practical exposure to the operations in engineering industry through plant visits.
Utilize engineering principles to analyze and solve real-world industrial problems.
Identify and address safety issues pertinent to process design and unit operations within the engineering sector.
Communicate technical results and findings clearly and effectively in an industrial context.
Investigate various career paths available in the engineering sectors.
Foster a mindset of continuous learning through real-world applications and experiences in the field.

courses.title: Chemical and Biological Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.description: First law of thermodynamics for closed and open systems, enthalpy and the energy equation. PVT data and thermodynamic properties, methods for their estimation, phase equilibria. Second and third laws of thermodynamics, entropy and the Carnot engine. Examples from chemical and biological processes.
courses.prerequisite: (BIEN 2310 OR CENG 2310 OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024) AND (PHYS 1111 OR PHYS 1112 OR PHYS 1312)

cilos.description: State, understand, explain, and apply the laws of thermodynamics.
Apply the machinery of thermodynamics to calculate thermodynamic properties of interest.
Use published thermodynamic property tables and diagrams.
Identify, formulate and solve problems pertaining to simple chemical processes.
Develop solutions to problems in an organized, transparent, and precise manner.
Apply the concepts of thermodynamics to interpret physical phenomena in nature.

courses.title: Transport Phenomena I
courses.description: Fundamentals of transport phenomena with emphasis on physical properties, flow behavior and diffusive transport of fluids in chemical and biological systems. Engineering derivation and quantitative analysis of fluid transport in confined domains. Emphasis on practical application of transport phenomena in chemical and biological engineering. Use of software for solving problems in transport phenomena.
courses.prerequisite: (BIEN 2310 OR CENG 2310 OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024) AND (PHYS 1111 OR PHYS 1112 OR PHYS 1312)

cilos.description: Understand the fundamentals of transport phenomena with emphasis on physical properties, flow behavior and diffusive transport of fluids in chemical and biological systems.
Understand engineering derivation and quantitiatve analysis of fluid tranport in confined domains.
Identify the practical application of transport phenomena in chemical and biological engineering.
Apply software for solving problems in transport phenomena.

courses.title: Modeling for Chemical and Biological Engineering I
courses.description: This is the first of a sequence of two courses to train students on the foundational skills of mathematical modeling in chemical and biological engineering. Students will learn to use deterministic and stochastic models to describe physical, chemical and biological processes. Essential concepts in single-variable calculus, ordinary differential equations and statistics will be introduced. Scientific computing tools will be used throughout the course.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023) AND COMP 1023

cilos.description: Model simple physical, chemical and biological processes as mathematical equations.
Develop and interpret differential equations in initial and boundary value problems.
Solve ordinary differential equations analytical and/or numerically.
Describe elementary concepts in statistics and perform simple hypothesis testing and regression analysis.
Use computing tools for engineering calculations.

courses.title: Modeling for Chemical and Biological Engineering II
courses.description: This is the second of a sequence of two courses to train students on the foundational skills of mathematical modeling in chemical and biological engineering. More complex models involving higher-order ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations, and essential concepts in linear algebra and numerical methods will be introduced. Scientific computing tools will be used throughout the course.

cilos.description: Model physical, chemical and biological processes as mathematical equations.
Apply elementary principles in linear algebra and multivariable calculus in an engineering context.
Develop and interpret ordinary and partial differential equations to model engineering problems.
Solve ordinary and partial differential equations numerically.
Use scientific computing tools for engineering calculations with a basic understanding of the underlying algorithms.

courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Basic concepts, mathematical model, transfer function. Dynamics of first - and higher-order systems. Feedback control, controller tuning, frequency response methods. Cascade control, feedforward and ratio control. Introduction to computer control and multi-variable control. Control and instrumentation hardware.

cilos.description: Obtain in-depth understanding of basic concepts of process dynamics and control.
Obtain Good understanding of process instrumentation.
Be able to use MATLAB/SIMULINK to assist the learning.

courses.title: Integrated Chemical Process and Product Design
courses.description: Conceptual design of chemical processes and products. Integration of prior knowledge in the execution of a structured design project, under the direct guidance of faculty. Project topics encompass both process and product design with different emphases. Design tasks include literature and market survey, ideation, feasibility and viability studies, prototyping and/or simulation, unit operation or component design, planning and project management, and societal and environmental impact assessment. Emphasis on the design process, hands-on experimentation, teamwork, and self-learning.

cilos.description: Perform conceptual design of a chemical process and/or product in a team setting.
Assess the feasibility, viability and desirability of a chemical process/product.
Evaluate the societal impact of a chemical process/product.
Communicate and cooperate effectively in a project team.
Acquire various practical skills and knowledge required of chemical process/product design through self-learning and apprenticeship.

courses.title: Separation Processes
courses.description: Phase equilibria. Ideal and nonideal mixtures. Thermodynamic properties and VLE from equations of state. Liquid-liquid and liquid-solid systems. Stage process, short-cut and rigorous calculations in absorption, distillation or extraction. Continuous contacting processes. Separation sequences. Simulation and design.

cilos.description: Understand concepts, principles, relations and experimental basis of the separation processes.
Understand key concepts of separation processes and unit design including equilibrium stages, reflux, countercurrent contacting, limiting cases, efficiency and mass transport effects.
Model and solve problems related to flash distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, batch distillation, cascades, simple and complex binary distillation systems and absorption in packed towers.
Understand the basic principles of evaporation, absorption, liquid-liquid extraction, membrane, drying processes.
Understand scientific literature in a range of fields that uses concepts in separation processes.

courses.title: Transport Phenomena II
courses.description: Application of transport phenomena in chemical processes. Fluid flow in pipes and channels. Conductive, forced and free convective, and radiative heat transfer. Diffusive and convective mass transport. Coupling of transport and chemical reactions. Analysis and design of heat exchangers and contacting processes for separation and reaction. Numerical solutions and simulations of complex systems.

cilos.description: Understand thermodynamic concepts of heat and mass transport.
Demonstrate the thermodynamic second law enabled phenomena.
Apply Fourier's law and Fick's law to heat and mass transport.
Solve problems involving steady and unsteady heat conduction, convection, and radiation.
Solve problems involving mass transfer due to diffusion, chemical reaction, and convection.
After this course, students should be able to size some basic heat and mass transfer equipment.
Extend the solving ability to problems involving biological and environmental systems.

courses.title: Chemical and Biological Reaction Engineering
courses.description: Stoichiometry and reaction equilibria. Homogeneous reactions kinetics. Mole balances: batch, continuous-stirred tank and plug flow reactors. Collection and analysis of rate data. Catalytic and enzymatic reaction kinetics and reactor design. Diffusion effects. Examples from chemical and biological processes.
courses.prerequisite: (BIEN 2310 OR CENG 2310) AND CENG 1000 AND CHEM 1012

cilos.description: Understand the basic principle of reaction and reactor engineering.
Develop skills in the design and analysis of different reactor units.
Make informed decision on proper reactor selection.
Develop problem-solving skills.

courses.title: Data Science for Molecular Engineering
courses.description: This course is an introductory course on the application of machine learning methods in molecular engineering problems. It covers fundamental data processing and machine learning methods to analyze data in chemistry and biology such as molecular similarity calculation and property prediction.

cilos.description: Identify problems that can be formulated as a supervised learning task.
Process different types of data to be ready for model training.
Understand the principles of supervised learning methods.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Know the application of data science methods in molecular science related problems.

courses.title: Chemical and Environmental Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Integrated laboratory course for students in Chemical Engineering and Chemical and Environmental Engineering. Experimental modules on various unit operations and processes in chemical engineering and environmental engineering. Laboratory safety and risk assessment. Proper handling and interpretation of experimental data.

cilos.description: Describe the principles behind the experimental modules and how they are applied in the experiments.
Design and conduct experiments in chemical engineering and environmental engineering disciplines.
Process, analyze and interpret experimental data in a statistically sound manner.
Develop soft skills including teamwork, open-ended problem solving, report writing and presentation.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest. May be graded by letter or DI/PA/F subject to different offerings.

cilos.description: Understand the Principles of MD Simulation (Explain the fundamental concepts and theoretical foundations of molecular dynamics simulations and their significance in chemical and biological engineering.).
Design and excute MD simulations (Develop and implement MD simulation protocols for various systems, including polymers, biomolecules, and ionic systems).
Visula Simulation Data (Utilize advanced software tools to visualize simulation results effectively, enabling a deeper understanding of molecular behavior).
Analyze Simulation Results (Interpret and analyze the outcomes of MD simullations, including the calculation of thermodynamic, structural, and dynamical properties.).
Apply MD Techniques to Real-World Problems (Demonstrate the ability to apply molecular dynamics simulations to solve practical challenges in areas such as ion transport and protein folding).

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: This course is designed to provide academic advising to students in the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering, to familiarize them with possible career paths and to prepare them for the transition to the workplace or graduate studies. Activities include meeting faculty and alumni, seminars, professional training modules, industrial site visits, etc. Passing requirement also includes proof of completion of internship, research or equivalent experience. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Understand the career opportunities available to graduates from the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering.
Develop and implement MD simulation protocols for various systems, including polymers, biomolecules, and ionic systems.
Formulate a short-to-medium term plan for one's career aspiration.
Appreciate the standard of ethics and professional responsibilties expected of engineers.
Understand the importance of and pathway to lifelong learning.

courses.title: Plant Design and Economics
courses.description: Computer-aided-design and process evaluation. Risk assessment, qualitative and quantitative assessment. Hazop, Hazan, FMEA, decision tree, fault tree, reliability. Toxicity, dispersion, fire, explosion, relief. Workplace safety. Plant safety and hazard analysis. Plant equipment specification and selection. Cost estimation and profitability analysis. Project evaluation. Cost optimization. Environmental control.

cilos.description: demonstrate mastery of economic analysis in chemical process and/or product development.
Make meaningful estimates on various economic aspects such as the capital investment, product cost, depreciation and profitability of an existing or new chemical process or project.
be aware of the importance of environment/health issues in chemical industry.
Apply process safety management program, industrial hygiene, fire and explosion, toxic release and dispersion, and pressure relief system.
Conduct Hazards Identification, Risk Analysis, and HAZOP.

courses.title: Energy Resources, Conversions and Technologies
courses.description: The course will provide the fundamental knowledge of energy resources, their conversions and utilization technologies.Basic thermodynamics such as fuel and combustion models, measurement techniques will be taught to enable students to manage basic conversion calculations and to evaluate different energy utilization options. The course will also cover topics in green energies and fuels, providing an outlook of future energy uses.
courses.prerequisite: (CENG 1110 OR ENEG 1700) AND CENG 2210 AND CHEM 1012

cilos.description: Know the limitations of different energy resources.
Know the relation in between energy usage, economic development and environment protection.
Compare the pros and cons of different energy options and their limitations.
Select and compare process technologies for energy conversions.
Conduct energy forecasting from historical data.
Apply basic thermodynamic concepts in energy conversion calculations or assessments.
Demonstrate topic study, presentation and communication skills.

courses.title: Nature Engineering and DNA Nanotechnology
courses.description: Science encompasses subjects like mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology, with boundaries between them becoming increasingly blurred over time. Engineering applies science and math to solve problems, resulting in interdisciplinary fields that offer a broader perspective. The course integrates materials science, chemical engineering, thermodynamics, bioengineering, environmental engineering, and microelectronics. For BIEN and CENG students in their third or fourth year of study only. Instructor’s approval is required for enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Acquire a fundamental comprehension of the structures found in nature that are frequently encountered in our daily lives.
Gain a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental properties associated with the Constructal Law observed in nature.
Solve the structure/property relationship in nature.
Design optimal DNA sequences for DNA nanotechnology.
Communicate work with effective presentations.
Write effective project reports.

courses.title: Nanomaterials and Applications in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to nanostructured materials and nanotechnology. Synthesis and characterization of nanostructured materials. Selected applications of nanostructured materials in chemical engineering.

cilos.description: Understand how nanotechnology can be applied into chemical engineering.
Demonstrate nano-based applications are made in chemical engineering.
Apply self-assembly and nanochemisty for making nanomaterials.
Apply principles of chemistry and physics to the novel nanotechnology and nanomaterials.
Understand the working principles of nanotools such as electron microscopy and probe microscopy etc.
After this course, students should be able to analyze our daily products that are using nanomaterials.
Appreciate the role of nanotechnology for chemical engineers.

courses.title: Bioproducts and Processing
courses.description: Survey of bioproducts, cellular production hosts, production techniques (bioreactors), separation and purification processes, product formulation, product and process design.

cilos.description: Demonstrate knowledge of various biologically derived products, including their applications and significance in industry.
Apply Inoculum development, medium selection and microbial growth kinetics to optimize microbial growth and production.
Design and operate bioreactors, considering key factors such as agitation, scale-up processes, aeration, heat removal, and sterilization techniques.
Apply downstream processing techniques, including filtration, membrane separation, precipitation, and chromatography, to recover, isolate, and purify bioproducts.
Design and execute a lab experiment to create a bioproduct, gaining hands-on experience in production and processing techniques.
Assess the efficiency and effectiveness of different bioproduct production and downstream processing methods.

courses.title: Food Processing Technology
courses.description: Principles of Food Spoilage and Preservation, Thermal Processing (blanching, pasteurization, sterilization, aseptic UHT processing.), Chilling & Freezing, Dehydration, Separation and concentration, Fermentation, and concept of hurdle technology.

cilos.description: Gain appreciation of the fundamental principles of food spoilage, food preservation and processing methods that make a food safe for consumption.
Assess the storage stability of food products.
Apply the principles of food preservation and processing to solve practical, real-world problems.
Integrate knowledge of microbiology, chemistry, and engineering principles to solve problems in food preservation and processing.

courses.title: Biomolecular Engineering
courses.description: Students not studying in the Department of Chemical Engineering may enroll in the course upon instructor's approval. Molecular biology, protein engineering, enzyme kinetics, thermodynamics and energetics of biological systems, molecular and cellular processes, bioreaction networks and metabolic engineering.
courses.prerequisite: CENG 2210 AND CENG 3230 AND (Level 3 in HKDSE 1x Biology OR LIFS 1901)

cilos.description: Understand the structure-property relationship in biomacromolecules.
Learn common ways to predict, characterize, and engineer biomacromolecular properties.
Appreciate the significance of biomacromolecular engineering in biology and biotechnology.
Explore the integration of biomacromolecular engineering with other disciplines such as synthetic biology, genome engineering, epigenetics, brain science, and regenerative medicine.

courses.title: Biomaterials and Drug Delivery
courses.description: This course covers the relevant concepts in biology, material science, and engineering principles for the design and applications of biomaterials to meet medical needs, with emphasis on drug, gene, and cell delivery. Essential methods for the physiochemical characterization and preclinical evaluation of biomaterials will be introduced. Students will also learn about the roles of regulations and standard practice in industry. Case students will be featured to highlight the scientific theories and clinical translation of classical and latest therapeutic carriers. Students are expected to have basic background in fluid mechanics and mass transfer.
courses.prerequisite: (CHEM 1010 (prior to 2022-23) OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR BIEN 2410 OR BIEN 2610)

cilos.description: Describe major categories of modern biomaterials and their applications in medical areas.
Discuss the methods of evaluation for the characterization of biomaterials.
Provide qualitative and quantitative criteria for the design of biomaterials for specific applications.
Describe the regulatory considerations and the major steps in the approval process in the commercial development of biomaterials and drug delivery technologies.

courses.title: Pharmaceutical Engineering
courses.description: Survey of western pharmaceuticals; pharmaceutical processing technologies including reactions and separations; enantiomers and chiral separations; polymorphs and solid state pharmaceuticals; pharmaceutical dosage forms including tablets, capsules and transdermal patches; traditional Chinese medicine processing.

cilos.description: Explain key characteristics and mechanisms for drug action, measurement, and administration routes.
Classify and identify different solid-state forms of APIs and explain their importance for manufacturing and product quality.
Design and analyze pharmaceutical crystallization processes and workup steps.
Synthesize and explain the formulation of liquid-dosage forms.
Synthesize and explain formulations of oral solid-dosage forms and design a process sequence for tablet manufacturing.
Develop and analyze a basic mathematical model describing the API release from solid-dosage forms.

courses.title: Environmental Control
courses.description: Wastes from the process industries. Behavior of toxic chemicals in atmospheric, soil and aquatic environments. Adsorption/desorption, air stripping, steam stripping, supercritical extraction. Pyrolysis, biological, catalyzed and uncatalyzed reactions.  Integrated environmental control. Instructor's approval is required for non-CBME students' enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Identify the impact of human activities on the ecosystems.
Apply chemical engineering principles in solving environmental problems.
Identify the types and sources of air pollutants, wastewater, and solid wastes.
Employ physical, chemical, catalytic, biological and thermal methods for the treatment of solid wastes.
Use appropriate methods for the treatment of hazardous wastes.
Employ physical, chemical, catalytic, thermal and biological methods for the treatment of air emission.
Employ physical, chemical, catalytic and biological methods for the treatment of wastewater.
Perform a preliminary design for the incineration of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) in Hong Kong.

courses.title: Environmental Impact Assessment and Management Systems
courses.description: This course will review the methods for assessing environmental impacts.  Impact and management systems will be discussed in the context of both HK and international environmental legislation, which incorporates Licensing, BATNEEC, integrated pollution control, environmental management and auditing systems based on ISO 14000.  Actual case studies from the process industries will be discussed.

cilos.description: Be able to find the necessary information/legislation/procedures for an assessment of environmental impact of a “Project”.

Be able to use the technical memorandum to determine the Best Available Technologies, Best Available Technology Not Entailing Excessive Economic Cost (BATNEEC), Integrated Pollution Prevention Control (IPPC), and so on.
Be able to conduct an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) on a proposed project.
Be able to conduct a Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) on a selected process.
Be able to conduct an environmental audit on a selected company/industry.
Be able to develop a waste reduction and minimization plan for a selected company/industry.
Be able to develop an Environmental Management System for a ”Project”.

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Capstone Design
courses.description: A final-year project course offers practice of chemical engineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in Chemical Engineering, Chemical and Environmental Engineering and Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of chemical, environmental and biomolecular engineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of engineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to their disciplines, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thesis Research
courses.description: A final-year project course offers an opportunity to conduct individual chemical engineering research under the direct supervision of a faculty member, which leads to a Bachelor's thesis. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in Chemical Engineering, Chemical and Environmental Engineering, and Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering with approval from the department.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments.
Conduct scholarly research in the realm of chemical engineering.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the research questions and outcomes effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of chemical engineering research on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to their disciplines, and use it effectively in their research.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Industrial Project
courses.description: This course is intended to provide final-year chemical engineering students with practical hands-on training in the form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in an engineering company. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in Chemical Engineering, Chemical and Environmental Engineering, and Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering with approval from the department.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of chemical, environmental and biomolecular engineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of engineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to their disciplines, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Chem-E-Car
courses.description: This course is a platform for entry-level engineer students to participate in Chem-E-car competition, i.e. to design and construct a car powered by a chemical or biochemical energy source that will safely carry a specified load over a given distance and stop. The objective of this course is to develop the ability to control an electrochemical reaction, and to obtain hands-on experience on a practical engineering project, especially in chemical engineering field. Students will be given the opportunity to interact with each other, to integrate the learning experience to design and build a device, and chances to prepare for starting their future career in engineering. It is a student-led project, designed to motivate students for engineers. Graded DI/PA/F. Enrollment in the project course require instructor's approval.

cilos.description: Perform a wide range of design, fabricate and test in the contemporary chemical engineering laboratory.
Develop team work experience and learn how to divide project duties ensuring efficiency and quality of the final results.
Be equipped with ability to problem-solve, troubleshoot, and analysis results, and use statistical tactics for data evaluating.
Conduct project with professional ethics.
Use knowledge of engineering, science and technology to solve practical problems.
Obtain skills for effective communication to ensure accurate and appropriate information transfer.

Obtain skills to administrate an engineering project for quality assurance, continuous quality improvement, laboratory education, fiscal resource management, and appropriate composure under stressful conditions.

courses.title: Investigation Project
courses.description: Students conduct in-depth experimental or computational investigations on selected topics in one of the departmental research areas. Students work under supervision and are encouraged to use their own initiative to complete an appropriate program of work within the time allocated. Enrollment is subject to approval by department and supervisor. Graded Distinction/Pass/Fail. May be repeated for credits. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Conduct in-depth experimental or computational investigations on selected topics in one of the departmental research areas.
Identify their own initiative to complete an appropriate program of work within the time allocated.

courses.title: Advanced Separation Processes
