Carry out directed research by selecting appropriate topics and procedures, and presenting the results.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing with professionals and/or lay audience.
Demonstrate information technology skills, especially in the areas of information retrieval, literature searching and use of library database.
Show self-awareness, work independently and collaborate effectively with other people in a team.

courses.title: Capstone Research II
courses.description: Continuation of research project started in CHEM 4691 and to be conducted under the supervision of a faculty member/teaching staff. A written report and oral presentation are required to document their learning experiences. Students should seek instructor's approval prior to enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Demonstrate awareness of chemical topics relevant to social and daily life.
Analyze and interpret experimental data, critically assess data in literature and extract useful data from it.
Carry out directed research by selecting appropriate topics and procedures, and presenting the results.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing with professionals and/or lay audience.
Demonstrate information technology skills, especially in the areas of information retrieval, literature searching and use of library database.
Show self-awareness, work independently and collaborate effectively with other people in a team.

courses.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Mechanism and theory in organic chemistry, molecular orbital theory, structure-activity relationships, isotope effects, solvent effects, neighboring group participation, and reactive intermediates.

cilos.description: Select appropriate methods  to evaluate the reaction mechanism.
Interpret experimental results and draw conclusions about reaction mechanism with confidence.

courses.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: Stereochemistry and conformational analysis, reactions of various classes of organic compounds, synthetic organic chemistry, modern methods of synthesis including specific methodologies and multistep complex syntheses.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an interest in and understanding of fundamental principles of synthetic organic chemistry and modern methods of multistep synthesis.
Analyze and appreciate synthetic work of complex organic molecules in the current primary literature.
Apply modern organic reactions and synthetic methodologies to formulate synthetic plans of organic molecules.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing the concepts and advancements in synthetic organic chemistry and show self-awareness in green chemistry.

courses.title: Asymmetric Catalysis
courses.description: This course teaches the basic concepts and general modes of action of asymmetric catalysis and synthesis. Asymmetric catalysis is an essential tool in organic synthesis, which is used daily in various industries, such as pharmaceutical, chemical, agriculture, materials, etc. The course will provide in-depth explanation of how catalysts work in organic reactions and how asymmetric control is accomplished in different scenarios. Lectures will focus on mechanistic details of chirality control using case studies. Students are expected to be able to use this important tool to solve various synthetic problems.

cilos.description: Explain the basic principles of asymmetric synthesis.
Classify modes of action and infer catalyst design.
Explain factors affecting enantioselectivity and common strategies to perform asymmetric synthesis.
Design and propose routes to synthesize common chiral fragments.
Analyze stereochemical control in organic reactions.
Review frontier topics such as organocatalysis, photoredox catalysis, etc.
Communicate effectively in writing and by oral presentation on scientific topics of organic chemistry.

courses.title: Chemical Biology
courses.description:
This course is designed to expose students to current methodologies in the field of Chemical Biology. A key focus will be the chemical reactions and probes that have been used to build current techniques in the field. Areas that will be covered include bio-orthogonal chemistry, protein engineering, methods of protein- and cell-specific 
labelling, biological assay development, cell imaging techniques, and topics in current Chemical Biology research.

cilos.description: Classify and explain major chemical biology principles used to study biological processes.
Recognize and implement the chemical tools used to perform tasks like protein conjugation, cell imaging, activity assays, and chemical proteomics.

Analyze key concepts from journal articles related to chemical biology and evaluate their scientific
significance.

courses.title: Advanced Medicinal Chemistry
courses.description: Drug design, structure-activity relations, chemistry and biological effects of major classes of physiologically active and psycho-active drugs.

cilos.description: Classify the origins of human diseases and the molecular basis for their treatment.
Demonstrate capability to select or discover a molecular target for therapeutic intervention.
Identify leads for therapeutic targets using diverse chemical strategies.
Propose optimization of drug properties  through structural modifications.

courses.title: Computational Chemistry
courses.description: Fundamentals and applications of various computational chemistry methods, including molecular orbital calculations, molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics. Computational laboratory practice will be emphasized.

cilos.description: Build knowledge of quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, and statistical mechanics.
Apply computational chemistry approaches to solve chemistry problems.

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to basic theories of Quantum Chemistry. Popular theories used in modern Quantum Chemistry such as Hantree-Fock theory, Density Functional theory. Perturbation Theories, and other quantum chemistry theories will be introduced in this course.

cilos.description: Illustrate the Hartree-Fock approximation to treat chemical molecules.
Explain post Hartree-Fock methods including configuration interaction, coupled cluster and coupled electron pair approximations.
Apply Density Functional Theory (DFT) for ground state systems, and Time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) for excited-state and time-dependent systems.

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry I
courses.description: Symmetry, group theory; molecular orbitals, electronic states; ligand field theory; electronic structure of metal complexes; theory of bonding and structure of inorganic compounds; chemistry of the elements; major physical methods used in the determination of molecular structure and bonding.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth and well-founded knowledge of structure and bonding theories relevant to inorganic chemistry.
Apply molecular orbital theory to explain and rationalize bonding, reactivity and properties of inorganic molecules including transition metal complexes and cluster compounds.
Correlate the structure and bonding of metal complexes to their roles in catalysis.

courses.title: Chemical X-ray Crystallography
courses.description: Applications of X-ray diffraction methods to the determination of crystal structures, including crystal symmetry, reciprocal lattice, intensity of diffraction, the phase problem, and refinement of structure parameters, powder X-ray diffraction analysis.

cilos.description: Describe the principles of powder and single crystal X-ray diffraction and how they can be applied to identification of samples and determining molecular crystal structure.
Classify the main methods of crystallization and apply them to real world examples.
Discuss classification of crystals on the basis of symmetry and explain the principles of space groups and their application to crystal structure.
Employ powder diffraction software programs to i) determine unit cells from a set of diffraction peaks, and ii) identify materials from an experimental powder patterns.
Solve and refine crystal structures from hkl diffraction data using modern software packages such as SHELX and Olex2.
Critique the quality of experimental diffraction data and refined structures with published X-ray structures and identify the key geometric features.
Apply the use of databases (CSD, ICSD, PDF) to carry out data mining for structural studies, including molecular and intermolecular geometry.

courses.title: Atmospheric Chemistry
courses.description: A fundamental introduction to the physical and chemical processes determining the composition of the atmosphere and its implications for climate, ecosystems, and human welfare. Atmospheric transport and transformation. Stratospheric ozone. Oxidizing power of the atmosphere. Regional air pollution: aerosols, smog, and acid rain. Nitrogen, oxygen, carbon, sulfur geochemical cycles. Climate and the greenhouse effect.

cilos.description: Apply the fundamental concepts to describe the physical and chemical processes governing air pollution.
Identify important chemical reactions and processes in the stratosphere and troposphere.
Understand the formation mechanism and destruction processes of various pollutants in the air.
Assess the potential impacts of various atmospheric chemical processes on environment, climate and human health.
Apply investigative skills, critical thinking and ability to evaluate atmospheric chemistry-related information and  data.

courses.title: Chemistry for Advanced Materials
courses.description: Chemistry of materials with nano-dimensional structures and advanced functionalities. Working principles of liquid-crystalline displays and organic light-emitting diodes. High-tech applications of luminescent materials in optoelectronic systems, chemical sensors and biological probes.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of materials science and technology.
Recognize the power of chemical synthesis and materials preparation and carry out investigative research work with independent judgment.
Apply chemical principles to formulate and analyze analytical and synthetic problems.
Conduct analysis and interpretation of experimental data.
Communicate problem solutions using correct materials chemistry terminology and good English

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Modern Polymer synthesis, step and chain polymerizations, macromolecular structures, and polymer properties.

cilos.description: Exemplify the concepts, structures, and characterization of macromolecules.
Recognize methods and their mechanisms for preparing polymers with different architectures and properties.
Apply chemical principles to analyze macromolecular problems and interpret experimental results.
Communicate problems using correct polymer chemistry terminology.

courses.title: Chemistry Seminar
courses.description: Series of seminar topics presented by students, faculty and visiting speakers; may be repeated for credit. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Recognize the current trends and activities in Chemistry related professions and academic research.
Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate advanced research results from various Chemistry-related scientific presentations.

courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry (JCAS)
courses.description: Advanced courses in postgraduate Chemistry including those offered by sister institutions in Hong Kong under the Joint Center for Advanced Studies initiative. Credit to be determined on case by case basis based on workload.

cilos.description: Discuss the phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) and its mechanism.
Recognize different AIE materials and their properties.
Categorize the potential applications of AIE materials in electronics, optics, biomedical field, etc.

courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest to the Department not covered by existing courses.  May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental knowledges in the selected topics.
Apply the fundamental knowledge in the selected topics to their own research fields.

courses.title: Chemistry Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: This course consists of seminars delivered by PhD candidates on research topics outside the scope of their thesis work in chemical sciences. PhD(CHEM) students are required to enroll in this course for two regular terms during their third year of study. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Acquire and understand relevant research reports, reviews and books in a particular research area of interest.
Critically analyze the development, significance and application potential of the achievements in a selected area of research.
Identify new opportunities for scientific exploration in the selected area of research.
Communicate professionally the scientific development in chemistry by oral presentation.

courses.title: Professional Development in Chemistry
courses.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students basic training in teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills in chemistry. This course normally lasts for one year, and is composed of a number of mini-workshops or tasks which are coordinated by the department. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Efficiently use on-line and off-line academic resources to support their research.
Efficiently use various instruments in their research.
Understand and conform to regulations regarding the safe use of chemicals and related instruments.
Perform risk assessment and safely use chemicals and related apparatuses in research projects.
Supervise and teach undergraduate students in chemistry experiments and part of course activities.
Professionally present research outputs to chemists in the research and development community.
Demonstrate a clearer understanding of the career exploration process in chemistry-related industries.

courses.title: Research Project
courses.description: An independent research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. This course is only available for exchange, visiting and visiting internship students.

cilos.description: Apply practical or computational techniques/skills for chemical investigations.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of their area(s) of specialization.
Apply practical or computational techniques/skills for chemical investigations.
Conduct directed chemical research, develop experimental protocols and interpret results.
Communicate effectively the results of scientific research in writing and by oral presentation.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of their area(s) of specialization and chemistry in general.
Apply practical and/ or computational techniques/skills for chemical investigations.
Conduct independent chemical research, propose experiments, develop protocols, evaluate results and formulate hypotheses.
Communicate effectively the results of scientific research in writing and by oral presentation.
Evaluate and critique current research, approaches and methodologies in chemistry.

courses.title: Chemical Data Analysis
courses.description: Measurements; Statistical treatment and analysis of Data; Uncertainties; Calibrations; Detection limits; Interferences; Use of Standards and Control Charts; Quality control and assurance; Presentation of data.

cilos.description: Handle experimental errors and their mathematical manipulation correctly.
Critically analyze and interpret scientific data.
Explain and use correctly significant figures in reporting scientific data.
Distinguish between the precision (reproducibility) and accuracy (correctness) of analytical data.
Identify possible sources of systematic error, such as interferences, in analytical measurements.
Construct calibration curves and use certified reference standards appropriately in analytical methods.
Apply calibration methods, such as standard additions and internal standards, to correct analytical measurements.

courses.title: Elemental Analysis
courses.description: Atomic spectroscopies; Atomic absorption (AA) atomic emission (AE); Elemental analysis by ICP MS; Isotope analysis. Elemental analysis using X-rays; X-ray Fluorescence (XRF); X-ray Photo-electron Spectroscopy (XPS); Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometey; Energy Dispersive Analysis of X-rays (EDAX); Combustion analysis.

cilos.description: Recommend the most appropriate methods of elemental analysis based on the nature of the samples and details of the analyses required (element concentration, level of precision, number of samples, cost, etc.).
Assess the use of elemental spectroscopies, such as AA, AE and MS, and their advantages and limitations in elemental analysis cases.
Illustrate the principles of X-ray based methods of elemental analysis, primarily XRF, XPS and EDX, and explain when and how these methods are used.
Distinguish total elemental analysis from isotopic analysis or chemical speciation of elements, and identify when these factors are important or not.
Correlate the required level of precision in an elemental analysis with the working concentration range and detection limits of the most commonly used methods.
Identify likely sources of error in elemental analysis, resulting either from incompatible protocols or interferences from other components of a sample.

courses.title: Molecular Analysis
courses.description: Characterization of organic molecules; Mass Spectrometry; Ionization techniques; Mass analysis Protein MS; NMR Spectroscopy; 1H and 13C NMR; Multinuclear experiments; 2D and pulse techniques; Solid state NMR.

cilos.description: Describe the key steps and techniques used for molecular analysis and characterization.
Explain the working principles behind mass spectrometry (MS) and its application to molecular analysis.
Devise a necessary series of NMR spectra (multinuclear, 2D and pulse-sequenced) to assist with detailed analysis of molecular structure and dynamics.
Interpret complementary spectroscopic data to logically infer or determine molecular structure.
Distinguish between relative and absolute stereochemical relationships and explain how these may be determined.

courses.title: Separation Methods
courses.description: Chromatography; Gas chromatography; GC-MS; Liquid chromatography; HPLC; Choice of stationary and mobile phases; Chiral separations; Affinity chromatography; Ion chromatography; Capillary zone electrophoresis; Micro-fluidics.

cilos.description: Select appropriate chromatographic techniques for the separation of mixtures of compounds and ions.
Modify experimental protocols in a separation method to improve separation, or achieve resolution.
Explain in detail the working principles behind modern liquid (lc) and gas (gc) chromatographic methods, as well as their variants and practical use.
Appraise methods of detection of analytes after chromatographic separation, and determine the most appropriate methods based on analyte type.
Interpret fragmentation patterns in mass spectral detection and apply this knowledge to the selection of daughter ions for positive material identification.
Compare and contrast the principles behind modern separation technologies, such as capillary electrophoresis and micro-fluidics, with more traditional methods, and assess their scope and limitations.

courses.title: Optical and Electrical Methods
courses.description: Molecular spectroscopies; Vibrational (IR and Raman) and Electronic (UV-vis) spectroscopy; Fluorescence; Electrochemical analysis; REDOX chemistry and bio-chemistry; Electrochemical measurements; pH measurements; Design and use of sensors.

cilos.description: Assess the utility of various spectroscopies based on molecular vibrations, rotations and electronic transitions, for the detailed analytical information they provide.
Apply symmetry analysis, where necessary, to aid interpretation of molecular spectra, such as IR and Raman.
Select appropriate spectroscopic protocols based on the nature of the sample - whether solid, liquid or gas, and the concentration of analyte to be detected.
Explain the nature of REDOX reactions and how these can be applied to analytical titrations, ion sensing or biochemical analyses.
Compare the physical and working principles behind different types of electrochemical sensors.

courses.title: Environmental Analysis
courses.description: Environmental sampling; Trace analysis; Air analysis; Water analysis; Soils analysis; Gas-phase components and major air pollutants; Toxins and pesticides; Aerosols and particulates; Assessing general health of water and soil systems; Recent advances in environmental techniques; Numerical analysis of environmental problems.

cilos.description: Analyze general air, water, and soil quality parameters.
Identify and quantify trace components in an environmental sample.
Differentiate appropriate sampling techniques for environmental analytes.
Appraise measurement protocols for environmental analytes.
Compare classical methods of environmental analysis with modern alternatives.
Critique and environmental analytical case study by oral presentation.

courses.title: Food and Drug Analysis
courses.description: Chemical Analysis of Food and Beverages; Food composition; Food contaminants; Food Preservation; Analytical Methods in Food Analysis; Food Safety and Labeling; Drug and Pharmaceutical Analysis; Physio-chemical Properties of Drugs; Analytical Methods in Pharmaceutical Analysis; Biomedical and Forensic analysis of Drugs; Analysis of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Drug formulation.

cilos.description: Classify parts of food composition including major components, additives and contaminants.
Appraise methods of food and drug analysis for purpose.
Identify and quantify food components, additives, contaminants and toxins by relying on instrumental methods.
Analyze active pharmaceutical ingredients and common excipients.
Qualify and quantify pharmaceutical in biological fluids, environmental systems and forensic samples.
Characterize Traditional Chinese Medicines, their components and contaminants.
Prepare an oral critique of a food or pharmaceutical analytical case study.

courses.title: Macromolecular Analysis
courses.description: Polymer and Bio-molecular Techniques; Polymer separation; Gel permeation chromatography; Affinity chromatography; Polymer characterization; Molecular weight and distribution; DNA and protein analysis.

cilos.description: Classify the major types of polymer and how their structure and physical properties affect the approach to their characterization and analysis.
Contrast the separation methods applied to macromolecular samples with those for mixtures of small molecules.
Describe approaches to polymer molecular weight analysis and distinguish information on average molecular weight from molecular weight distribution.
Illustrate the main methods for protein separations and amino-acid sequencing.
Explain how protein 3D structural details can be derived from modern X-ray crystallography.
Compare the main methods for poly-nucleic acid (DNA, RNA) analysis and base-pair sequencing.
Illustrate how functional groups or residues in polymers or biopolymers can be detected spectroscopically and assist in characterization.

courses.title: Materials Analysis
courses.description: Electron Microscopies: TEM; Electron diffraction; SEM; STEM; STM; AFM. Nano-materials characterization. Thin film characterization. X-ray diffraction; powder XRD; Single crystal structure determination; SAXS.

cilos.description: Classify materials based on their nature and composition and identify the most appropriate techniques for their characterization and analysis.
Compare and contrast the use of various types of microscopy to analyze materials.
Discuss the use of appropriate techniques to study and analyze thin films, nanoparticular materials and defects in solids.
Describe the main structure types for crystalline metals, ceramic and organic molecular compounds and explain how they and defects within them can be analyzed.
Demonstrate the principle behind the use of X-ray diffraction in crystal structure determination of materials.
Illustrate how powder X-ray diffraction is a useful fingerprint analysis tool for crystalline solids from metal alloys to minerals to pharmaceuticals.

courses.title: Laboratory Management
courses.description: Good lab practices (GLP); Laboratory Safety; Risk assessment; Lab waste management; Computer-assisted Lab Info Systems; Professional development case studies: Safety officer; Lab Manager.

cilos.description: Assess whether a commercial, academic or government laboratory is following Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) with appropriate regard to safety, environmental and legal compliance issues.
Evaluate existing risk assessment protocols for an experimental procedure, and where appropriate, propose modifications for improvement.

Devise new laboratory protocols and guidelines for safe operation of hazardous equipment, and instigate appropriate engineering controls for the handling of hazardous substances, and wherever possible, their minimization or substitution.
Re-design existing procedures for the reduction (or elimination) of hazardous waste, and where necessary, implement plans for its safe handling and legal disposal.
Identify shortcomings of existing analytical procedures, and where necessary, modify them to meet local or international accreditation standards.

courses.title: Analytical Instrumentation Laboratory I
courses.description: Students will choose from an array of experiments involving modern analytical techniques that have been introduced in the core courses. These will include, but not be limited to, separation of mixtures, gc-ms, lc-ms, atomic spectroscopy and elemental analysis, IR and UV spectroscopy, electrochemistry, NMR, powder XRD. Students must attend and write up experimental reports for at least eight laboratory sessions to complete the course. Maybe graded PP.

cilos.description: Apply a variety of chromatographic methods to separate and analyze compounds.
Use various spectroscopic and other analytical methods to identify unknown components of a sample.
Establish appropriate calibration curves to enable more accurate analysis results.
Combine experimental data to derive qualitative and quantitative analytical results, with appropriate statistical handling of errors and uncertainties based on multiple measurements.
Fully report experimental protocols and correlate, tabulate and present analytical results clearly in a written report.

courses.title: Analytical Instrumentation Laboratory II
courses.description: Students will choose from a further array of experiments, complementary to CHMS 5201, involving analytical techniques that have been introduced in either the core and the elective courses. Students must attend and write up experimental reports for at least eight laboratory sessions to complete the course. Maybe graded PP.

cilos.description: Critically analyze experimental protocols and procedures for likely or possible sources of error.
Apply and extend existing analytical protocols to the analysis of new compounds or mixtures.
Formulate the design, testing and validation of new analytical procedures or protocols.
Carry out a risk assessment exercise for new experiments and analyses.

courses.title: Analytical Research Project
courses.description: Students will undertake a research project in an area related to analytical chemistry under the supervision of a faculty member. Expected time spent on the project (background, planning, execution and write-up/presentation) is 100 hours. Students will submit a written report and the results will be orally presented on completion.

cilos.description: Execute an experimental plan to test a scientific hypothesis and modify this plan based on the results obtained.
Critically analyze the experimental data they have developed through the course of their project.
Summarize the results of a research project in a written report, highlighting the rationale, methodology and comparison to existing work.
Carry out independent research involving various analytical techniques.
Conduct a risk assessment exercise for a new research project.
Present results of a research project making appropriate use of figures, tables and graphs, with summary of background to the work, discussion of the key findings and their relevance.

courses.title: Construction Project Delivery
courses.description: The course would cover Principle of Project Management, Contractor Management, Public Works Development, Consultant Management & Engineering proposal, Design & Build, BOT & PPP, Project Finance, Project Risk Management, Project Partnering, Value Management, Safety Management, Environment Management, Case Studies.

cilos.description: Define the construction industry and different stages in a construction project.
Illustrate current HKSAR Work Bureau Guidelines, Circulars and Construction Industry Code of Practices by means of real-life industry Case Studies.
Specify the responsibilities of Consultants and Contractors in Construction Safety Management, Environmental Management and Project Management.
Perform Risk Management, Value Engineering and Partnering Approach in a construction project.
Formulate and resolve the latest Construction Procurement Strategy.
Identify the funding source in Public and Private infrastructure project.

courses.title: Construction Financial Management
courses.description: Estimate, tendering strategy, budgetary control, contract account, cash flow management, depreciation, taxation effects, annual reports, strategic management, benefit cost analysis, life cycle costing, value engineering.

cilos.description: Identify the characteristics of the construction industry.
Identify fundamental knowledge in construction project planning.
Estimate construction costs.
Control construction costs.
Conduct cash flow analysis of construction projects.
Analyze the financial and operational performance of a construction company.

courses.title: Building Information Modeling and Smart Construction
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamental and technical aspects of building information modeling (BIM) and smart construction. Topics include BIM model creation and sharing, model-based analyses, clash detection, BIM standards and interoperability, BIM project execution plan, BIM for infrastructure, visualization technologies, data mining and knowledge management, decision support system, construction informatics, sensing technologies, and construction robotics.

cilos.description: Identify the principles of building information modeling (BIM) and the current technologies for BIM.
Leverage software for building information modeling and construction management.
Model and represent various kinds of information in the construction industry.
Perform data processing and mining for knowledge discovery.
Design and leverage database systems for managing information and supporting construction management.

courses.title: Construction Technology for Civil Engineering Works
courses.description: This course intends to provide an overview of modern construction technology for civil engineering works with special attention paid to recent development trends and major construction works in Hong Kong. The course starts with the design/construction interface and focuses on the Contractor’s perspective. In particular, ground improvements, reclamation works, excavation-lateral support system and modular construction as well as digital construction will be highlighted. With an aim to help students who have limited exposure to construction practice, this course uses a Capstone project to help the students to form a comprehensive view of a construction project, including site layouts, construction practice, contract type, and construction methods. Students would be required to apply the knowledge learned to describe a real-life construction project and critically analyze the construction activities.

cilos.description: Identify the routines of local construction practice with an international exposure.
Professionally describe a construction project and its main elements and characteristics.
Explain the connections between design and construction.
Analyze the full set of construction activities including both underground and superstructure works.
Identify key construction methods and technologies for both permanent and temporary works.
Be aware of the current construction practice and its future trends.
Describe ways of improving construction process by innovations.
Interpret the contract, commercial, planning and HSE (Health, Safety and Environmental) perspectives of a construction project.

courses.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution: Law and Practice
courses.description: This course provides a complete introduction to the subject of dispute resolution in construction and engineering including: the legal background to and foundation for contractual claims and disputes; standard forms and conditions of contract; the various modes of alternative dispute resolution (ADR); the nature of, practice and hearings before ADR tribunals; and the role of engineers serving as expert witnesses and adjudicators.

cilos.description: Identify construction law and practice in context.
Distinguish between and assess various standard forms and conditions of contract.
Prepare, evaluate and defend construction claims and disputes.
Describe and evaluate numerous alternative dispute resolution (ADR) processes.
Identify the law and practice of dispute resolution hearings.
Analyze the role of engineers as advocates, expert witnesses and fact-finders in dispute resolution.

courses.title: Advanced Concrete Technology
courses.description: Green concrete, concrete rheology and its tuning, concrete failure and fracture mechanics, durability of concrete under various environments, steel corrosion in concrete, non-destructive evaluation of concrete, concrete repair, special concretes (high strength, high stiffness, fiber reinforced, lightweight).

cilos.description: Describe the proper selection of concrete raw materials to enhance greenness.
Identify factors affecting concrete rheology, failure and durability.
Explain steel corrosion in concrete, including its control and inspection.
Define non-destructive methods for concrete members.
Explain repair methods and repair materials for concrete members.
Analyze the design and application of various special concretes.

courses.title: Structural Analysis and Design of Tall Buildings
courses.description: Integrated treatment of analytical methods and technical aspects in design of tall building structures, including structural modeling, frames, shear walls, outrigger-braced systems, core-walls, tubular structures, and special topics.

cilos.description: Recognize the engineering mechanics and structural modelling techniques on which the analysis and design of tall building structures are based.
Identify the structural behaviour and performance of different forms of tall buildings and the analysis and design principles of tall building structures.
Conduct analysis and preliminary design of different types of tall building structures.
Apply the modern engineering software ETABS for the analysis and design of tall building structures.

courses.title: Building Aerodynamics and Wind-Resistant Design of High-Rise Structures
courses.description: Global wind climate, extreme wind analysis, wind structures near ground, bluff body aerodynamics, wind loads on building structures, wind-induced vibrations and mitigations, wind tunnel test techniques, and wind loading codes.

cilos.description: Describe the characteristics of wind, wind structure near ground and topographical effects on wind.
Identify typhoon structures and perform simple typhoon simulation.
Determine the alongwind and crosswind forces of a structure and the wind-induced structural responses.
Analyze dynamic problem of buildings subject to different dynamic loads.
Identify the attributes of an effective wind-resistant design.
Perform a tall building design following Hong Kong and Australian wind codes.
Recognize and appreciate various types of wind tunnel testing techniques.

courses.title: Computer Aided Design Optimization of Tall Buildings
courses.description: This course provides consolidated theoretical background and practical knowledge on the analysis, computer aided modeling and design optimization of modern tall building structures. Topics include behavior of different forms of tall building structures; finite element modeling and analysis; principles and practice of structural optimization for tall building design.

cilos.description: Recognize the challenges of building taller structures and the development of modern structural systems for tall buildings.
Define computer modelling principles and applications of finite element analysis for tall building structures.
Describe advanced knowledge of numerical optimization methodology for structural design of tall buildings.
Apply the state-of-the-art computer based techniques for engineering analysis and design optimization of real-life typical high-rise building projects.

courses.title: Bridge Engineering
courses.description: This course is focused on the bridge superstructure analysis and design using limit states design method. The main objectives of this course include the introduction of limit states design method; discussion of design philosophy and code requirements; as well as analysis and design examples using limit states design method.

cilos.description: Define different bridge construction methods.
Define different bridge structural forms.
Describe how bridge construction/erection methodology affects bridge design.
Select appropriate bridge form with a given site constraint.
Estimate preliminary material quantity required for a bridge project.

courses.title: Coastal Structures Design
courses.description: The course will cover basic wave characteristics, linear wave theory, wave transformation processes, wind-wave generation, coastal processes, wave-structure interaction, design procedures and requirements for coastal structures such as seawalls, breakwaters and beaches.

cilos.description: Recognize the challenges that confront costal engineers.
Integrate various approaches and tools to analyze and design costal structures.
Describe and apply the principles that underpin the estimation of wave loads on structures.

courses.title: Risk Assessment and Contaminated Land Cleanup
courses.description: Innovative technologies for land and groundwater remediation, site investigation, risk assessment, and local case studies on land decontamination such as Kai Tak Airport, Penny's Bay, North Tsing Yi will be included.

cilos.description: Describe the regulations for contaminated land management in Hong Kong.
Assess the potential risks associated with land contamination.
Evaluate and compare the applications of various remediation technologies.
Design cost-effective remediation technology to decontaminate a site.
Identify real applications from case studies.

courses.title: Biological Waste Treatment and Management
courses.description: Principles of secondary, biological treatment processes, including sewage sand filters, trickling filters, activated sludge plants, lagoons, ponds, rotating biological contactors, aerobic and anaerobic digesters, and biological nutrient removal. Management of waste treatment systems and works.

cilos.description: Define the fundamental and advanced knowledge of current solid wastes and wastewater treatment and disposal systems and their problems in Hong Kong and beyond.
Identify key problems of water and wastewater treatment processes, and propose fundamental engineering and management solution.
Professionally judge and assess the advantages and disadvantages of various sewage treatment technologies such as MEL, AGS, BABY, Anammox, etc.
Select the treatment processes/technologies for meeting a more stringent discharge requirement for water pollution control with focus of tertiary treatment.
Design basic treatment units and systems for municipal wastewater treatment.

courses.title: Design and Management of Physico/Chemical Processes of Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Principles, design and management practices of physico/chemical treatment processes for removing contaminants from drinking water and municipal wastewaters; includes coagulation and flocculation, sedimentation, air flotation, centrifugation, filtration, membrane, air stripping, carbon adsorption, disinfection, chemical oxidation processes, operation management and residual management.

cilos.description: Describe the fundamental and advanced knowledge of physical-chemical processes in the environmental engineering field.
Identify problems and propose feasible engineering or management solutions during the operation of water and wastewater treatment processes.
Design the physical-chemical unit processes and integrate them to systems for water and wastewater treatment.
Analyze major factors impacting physical-chemical treatment systems and provide management strategies.

courses.title: Wastewater Treatment and Reuse
courses.description: Theory and conceptual design of key unit processes and unit operations in domestic wastewater treatment and reuse with emphasis on applications of compact and advanced treatment technologies.

cilos.description: Identify and evaluate the environmental problems through reviewing the key water pollution parameters of water and wastewater.
Select the sewage treatment levels and processes required to meet the discharge requirements and to protect the receiving water bodies.
Carry out the process design for municipal sewage treatment plant including primary, chemically enhanced primary, secondary and sludge treatment.
Evaluate the operational problems and identify practical solutions during the operation of the municipal sewage treatment plants.
Select the tertiary treatment processes required for meeting a more stringent discharge requirement for water pollution control.
Select the treatment processes and identify the key design parameters and monitoring requirements for wastewater reuse.

courses.title: Travel Demand Analysis
courses.description: Overview of transportation planning process, population/employment forecasting techniques, discrete choice models, simplified transportation demand models.

cilos.description: Evaluate the advanced theories and methods of traffic and transportation engineering and transportation systems planning.
Utilize mathematical or quantitative methods to model components of transportation system.
Identify transportation system planning and management problems and propose feasible solutions.
Apply key transportation planning principles to the analysis, modeling and operation of transportation system, including traffic impact analysis and transportation demand forecasting.

courses.title: Traffic Control Fundamentals and Practice
courses.description: Traffic flow fundamentals; microscopic and macroscopic traffic flow characteristics; principle and theory of traffic signal; essential modeling techniques; various traffic signal control models.

cilos.description: Analyze principles involved in the design of traffic control.
Apply traffic control principles to model signalized junctions.
Design signalized junctions based on the Hong Kong practices.
Develop advanced control methods based on dynamic traffic flow fundamentals.

courses.title: Advanced Foundation Design
courses.description: Current practice of foundation design and analysis, including design and analysis of bulkheads, deep excavation, tieback systems, tunneling in soft ground, buried conduits, lateral pile loading, pier foundations.

cilos.description: Identify basic performance requirements for foundations.
Define fundamental soil mechanics principles for foundation engineering design and construction.
Recognize the uncertainties throughout the site investigation, design and construction process, and how the uncertainties are handled in limit state design.
Design common types of foundations (shallow foundations, piles, returning walls, soil nails, offshore foundations etc.).
Conduct construction quality assurance.
Design new types of foundations (wind turbine foundations, energy piles etc.) based on first principles.

courses.title: Computer Methods for Slope Engineering
courses.description: This course aims to teach students to apply knowledge of soil mechanics and numerical methods for analysis and design of slope stability. The course covers mechanisms of slope failures, shear strength of soils, transient seepage analysis, major methodologies on slope stability analysis, and use of popular computer software programs for slope stability analysis, including SLOPE/W & SEEP/W and PLAXIS 2D.

cilos.description: Explain shear strength of soils and methods for slope stability analysis.
Evaluate soil and rock properties from laboratory tests and field data.
Apply different methods for evaluating the stability of soil slopes.
Use basic geotechnical software packages for stability analysis of soil slopes.
Analyze the stability of engineering soil slopes for safe design.

courses.title: Engineering Geology and Rock Mechanics
courses.description: The course provides fundamental knowledge in engineering geology and rock mechanics as applied to rock engineering design and practice. Topics include: major rock types, weathering process and local geological setting; mapping geologic structures and stereonet analysis; rock mass classification, stress-strain-strength properties of rock mass and joints; analysis and design methods for rock slopes, rock foundations and underground tunnels. A field trip will be arranged to visit Hong Kong GeoPark.

cilos.description: Identify local geological setting and geological process.
Identify major rock types including weathered rock profiles.
Map geologic structures and analyze discontinuities using stereonet.
Classify rock mass.
Describe stress-strain-strength behaviours of rock and joint.
Analyze slope stability, underground opening and foundation in rocks.

courses.title: Unsaturated Soil Mechanics and Engineering
courses.description: Fundamental principles, stress state variables, steady-state and transient flows, theory of shear strength and its measurements, soil stiffness, plastic and limit equilibrium analyses of earth pressures, slope stability and bearing capacity, critical state framework, instrumentation, engineering applications on slopes including static liquefaction of loose fill slopes, foundations, forensic studies such as slope failures.

cilos.description: Define the fundamental principles and advanced concepts of unsaturated soil mechanics.
Design and carry out laboratory and field tests for determining unsaturated soil properties.
Apply key principles of unsaturated soil mechanics to analyze and design geotechnical and geo-environmental structures such as landfill, pavement, foundation and slope.
Effectively communicate unsaturated soil mechanics and engineering to a range of audiences in a professional manner.

courses.title: Slope Engineering and Management
courses.description: This course will introduce in detail the slope safety management system in Hong Kong, including its background, past development, as well as its key components, e.g. geotechnical control and landslide prevention and mitigation programme. The course will also cover basic knowledge on engineering geology, Hong Kong landslides, fundamentals and methods of slope stability assessment, slope stabilisation and landslide mitigation measures as well as the advanced subjects of quantitative risk assessments and use of novel technologies in landslide assessment.

cilos.description: Recognize the background and past development of the slope safety management system in Hong Kong and describe the two key components of slope safety management system in Hong Kong, viz. (a) geotechnical control, and (b) landslide prevention and mitigation programme.
Describe the geology of Hong Kong, common types of landslides in Hong Kong and their key causal factors.
Analyze stability condition of slopes.
Analyze mobility of landslide debris.
Undertake design of common slope stabilisation works.
Undertake design of common landslide mitigation works.
Conduct quantitative risk assessment for use in slope safety management.

courses.title: Engineering Risk, Reliability and Decision
courses.description: Bayesian methods, reliability evaluation, system reliability, reliability-based design, probabilistic risk analysis, probabilistic observational methods, Monte Carlo Simulation, Fault and Event Tree models, elementary utility theory, decision with multiple objectives. Emphasis will be placed on applications. Practical examples will be used extensively to demonstrate application of these methods.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental knowledge in probability and statistics.
Develop basic skill sets to perform probabilistic calculations with commercial toolboxes.
Define the concepts of engineering risk assessment and decision making.
Conduct useful analyses related to the subject, such as Monte Carlo Simulation.

courses.title: Topics in Civil Infrastructural Engineering and Management
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental knowledge in different areas related to the course topic.
Describe advanced theories and methods related to the course topic.
Formulate and solve problems in the various areas of the course topic.
Apply theories and methods to practical implementations.

courses.title: MSc Project
courses.description: An independent project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.

cilos.description: Develop and apply self-learning and task management skills to effectively manage an independent project.
Critically analyze a selected topic to identify, formulate and solve problems and apply solutions to practical implementations.
Communicate effectively in writing, using accurate technical and scientific terminology, and demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information.

Communicate effectively in oral presentation, demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information, using appropriate style, pacing and body language, proper handling of questions, and effective time management.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development for Civil and Environmental Engineering I
courses.description: A compulsory, one year course for students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This is the first course of the APD course series (CIVL1000/2000/3000/4000) for Year 1 students. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students and/or to develop students' interpersonal skills in handling technical and non-technical issues in their professional careers. Students admitted via school-based admission are exempted from taking CIVL 1000. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental principles in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Establish career goals and develop study paths towards the goals.
Discuss academic and professional matters with their advisors.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: A compulsory, one year course for CIVL/CIEV/CIGBM students only. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students and/or to develop students' interpersonal skills in handling technical and non-technical issues in their professional careers. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental principles in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Understand Industry Trends and Professional Practices.
Establish career goals and develop study paths towards the goals.
Discuss academic and professional matters with their advisors.

courses.title: Discovering Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: A general overview of civil and environmental engineering, infrastructure development and engineering ethics is provided. The course includes both lectures and laboratory sessions, where the laboratory sessions are primarily directed to students who require the development of feasible conceptual solutions for the analysis and design of the basic problems in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a broad overview of civil and environmental engineering, including details of their major disciplines, importance and challenges through lectures
Demonstrate an overview of history and future of infrastructure developments

Demonstrate an understanding of the role of civil and environmental engineers in our society and the fundamental principle of engineering ethics and civil engineers’ obligations towards the public, employers and the profession
Demonstrate knowledge of basic physical concepts in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Identify and analyze of the basic problems associated with the design of structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Develop feasible conceptual solutions for the analysis of the basic problems in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Acquire and apply skills in written presentation of scientific and technical information

courses.title: Introduction to Computation for Civil Engineers
courses.description: This course aims to introduce Civil Engineering students with a basic understanding of the computation role in solving real-world Civil Engineering problems, and provide a broad overview of the computation for their engineering career. It will give students fundamental capabilities to write small programs that allow them to accomplish useful goals. The class will use the Python programming language.

cilos.description: Computational Problem-Solving: Students will be able to apply computational thinking to analyze and solve basic civil engineering problems.
Computational Efficiency: Students will understand basic concepts of computational efficiency and be able to optimize simple programs.
Software Tool Utilization: Gain experience using relevant software tools and libraries commonly used in civil engineering computations.
Data Manipulation and Analysis: Use Python to manipulate, analyze, and visualize engineering-related data.

courses.title: Environment and Society: Sustainable Development Goals and Carbon Neutrality
courses.description: Introduction of up-to-date environmental issues in both local and global scales and elaboration of essential concepts in physical, chemical, biological and societal aspects will be provided for students to understand the issues related to sustainable development goals and carbon neutrality. Students will learn to apply and evaluate approaches in science, engineering, management, and social science for enhancing the quality of our water, air, land, eco-systems, and urban development. The objective of this course is to equip our next-generation leaders in different disciplines with environmental awareness and knowledge of practical solutions to environmental issues. Upon completing this course, students should be able to make responsible decisions and actions, with due consideration of environmental sustainability and long-term decarbonization. By reviewing and discussing essential concepts and practical applications, students will conduct group projects and deliver presentations of their self-directed focus studies of emerging environmental issues in our society.

cilos.description: Explain and apply the basic principles of science and methods of scientific inquiry in environmental quality control and improvement
Evaluate the social and philosophical implications of scientific discoveries and technological development in environmental quality control and improvement
Apply professional knowledge in solving engineering problems related to environmental quality control and improvement
Communicate and present key environmental issues and their solutions effectively
Apply ethics in environmental quality control and improvement as responsible citizens and decision makers

courses.title: Civil Engineering and Modern Society
courses.description: An introduction to civil engineering practice and infrastructure development, with an emphasis on Hong Kong projects. The basic principles, materials and technology used in typical civil engineering works such as foundations, buildings, bridges, slopes and water supply systems, etc. Infrastructure management and maintenance issues; social-economic aspects of large-scale civil engineering projects such as environmental protection, urban planning and development, etc.

cilos.description:
Understand the role of the civil engineers in the provision of basic infrastructure necessary to support the development and maintenance of
urban and rural settlement
Understand the engineering approach in processes of design, construction, operation and maintenance of infrastructure

Understand the history and future plans of civil engineering development in Hong Kong, as well as the need to consider the demands and expectations of the community, while having due regard for both the developed and fragile natural environment
Gain experience in solving problems using the engineering approach to apply data collection and analysis skills
Develop effective verbal and written communication skills, as well as leadership skills

Understand the engineering background, theory and operation of civil engineering projects for potable water supply; waste water treatment,
flooding control, highway development etc.

Understand and analyze social and ethical issues from an engineering as
well as humanistic perspective

courses.title: Building the Future: Civil Engineering Challenges & Solutions
courses.description: This course offers an exploration of civil engineering practices in Hong Kong, with a focus on the solutions engineers implement to address current infrastructure challenges. Students will develop an understanding of how advanced technology and sustainable practices are influencing the built environment. The course includes a collaborative group project that encourages students to critically analyze recent civil engineering developments globally. Additionally, students may participate in optional site visits to ongoing civil engineering projects and operational facilities, providing practical insights into the skills and competencies necessary for designing, constructing, and managing engineering projects. By engaging in this course, students will gain knowledge and skills relevant to addressing the infrastructure needs of the future while considering sustainability and resilience in engineering practices.

cilos.description: Articulate the vital role of civil engineers in designing, constructing, and maintaining essential infrastructure that supports both urban and rural development; and recognize how these contributions are integral to societal progress and quality of life

Acquire a comprehensive understanding of the engineering processes involved in the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure; and develop the ability to critically analyze each phase and appreciate the complexities and interdependencies inherent in civil engineering projects

Demonstrate an informed appreciation of the history of civil engineering development in Hong Kong, including key milestones and innovations; and analyze future technology development trends and plans in the field, considering the implications for sustainable development and urban resilience

Develop and apply data collection and analysis skills to identify, define, and solve engineering problems effectively; and utilize quantitative and qualitative methods to support decision-making processes in real-world scenarios

Analyze contemporary social issues related to infrastructure development from both engineering and humanistic perspectives; and engage in discussions with professional engineers to explore the ethical impacts of infrastructure projects, including the social unrest in Hong Kong, and reflect on the engineer's role in addressing these challenges

Cultivate teamwork and communication skills by participating in collaborative projects and discussions; and understand the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in addressing complex engineering challenges and promoting innovative solutions for the future

courses.title: Monitoring Changing Climate from Space
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of satellite remote sensing and its role in monitoring our changing climate and environment. It covers the science underlying remote sensing, various remote sensing methods and technologies, observational evidence of climate change from space, and use of satellite data to advance science understanding and assist decision-making. The characteristics of satellite data and common methods to process and analyze satellite data will be introduced.

cilos.description: Explain remote sensing principles, approaches, and methods
Describe satellite observations of climate change and associate the changes to human activities
Discuss and evaluate the complexity of physical science, and its limitation and future developments
Process, analyze, and interpret spatiotemporally varying data
Assess the soundness of climate-related policies using scientific knowledge policymaking
Write quantitative evidence-based reports with critical thinking and technical writing skills

courses.title: Climate Change, Big History and Sustainability
courses.description: Big History as an emerging interdisciplinary framework, provides a long-term perspective to see the world through reconstructing the history from the big bang all the way to the present. In such a longer time scale, overview of stars, planetary and species evolution, as well as concepts in climate change and how it is related to sustainability of the planet’s environment for its current inhabitants, including humanity, will be discussed. The physical science basis, impacts, risk, mitigation and adaptation measures of climate change will also be investigated (including technical and social solutions). For local and regional vulnerabilities, such as extreme weather events, sea levels rise, storm surge and coastal flooding, will be covered. The significance of collective learning under the big history framework, both as a driver for our exponentially growing impacts, as well as for better solutions, will be highlighted.

cilos.description: Analyze the historical contingencies of environmental impacts and atmospheric composition changes under the Big History perspective, focusing on the role of collective learning in industrial and economic development over the past 250 years
Apply physical principles to explain the science of star formation, planetary evolution, the greenhouse effect, and global climate change
Justify the rationales for climate change mitigation and adaptation measures adopted by governments and corporations, considering uncertainties in climate modeling
Synthesize observational evidence and modeling frameworks to interpret and argue for or against the occurrence of anthropogenic climate change

Apply Big History concepts, e.g., complexity and fragility and collective learning, to critically assess social, political, and economic implications of climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

Evaluate sustainability-related issues within the Big History framework, recognizing Homo sapiens’ role in ecosystem sustainability, and argue effectively on controversial climate-related topics for diverse audiences

courses.title: Fundamental of Green Buildings
courses.description: This course will dive into the fundamental elements of green building at two scales: the building scale and the city. Strategies and techniques that optimize various perspectives of green buildings will be taught and discussed. Students will learn how to achieve energy efficiency and sustainability in building design and operation, as well as the fundamental principles behind these designs.

cilos.description: Describe the concept of green buildings and measures to evaluate them
Explain energy efficient building design from both indoor and outdoor perspectives
Analyze the impact of buildings on environment with governing equations
Describe the fundamental process and principle of indoor-outdoor thermal exchange

courses.title: Big Data for Smarter Cities
courses.description: Students will discover the exciting world of smart cities. Smart cities and big data have become an integral part of our daily lives. With the advent of big data and artificial intelligence, we now have effective tools to understand and improve the quality of our urban environments. This course will provide a glimpse into the exciting advances in this field. Students will be introduced about the unique qualities of urban big data and the concepts on how to analyze it using powerful techniques like data visualization, data mining, and AI. With hands-on projects, students will see and appreciate how data science can help tackle real-world urban problems and make our cities more sustainable and livable.

cilos.description: Explain and discuss the concepts of the Smart City and Urban Data Science
Identify urban issues and analyze existing urban decisions
Evaluate basic data management, visualization, and analysis methods
Apply basic programming commands in urban data analytics
Apply data-driven thinking on urban studies or applications

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development for Civil and Environmental Engineering II
courses.description: Continuation of CIVL 1000. A compulsory, one year course for students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students and/or to develop students' interpersonal skills in handling technical and non-technical issues in their professional careers. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental principles in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Understand Industry Trends and Professional Practices.
Establish career goals and develop study paths towards the goals.
Discuss academic and professional matters with their advisors.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: Continuation of CIVL 1010. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Build industry awareness and professionalism.
Understand Industry Trends and Workplace Environments.
Prepare for Academic and Professional Growth.
Discuss academic and professional matters with their advisors.

courses.title: Industrial and BIM Training
courses.description: A practical training course in an industrial simulated environment. For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Understand the basics of CAD and BIM.
Use CAD and BIM software, for both buildings and civil infrastructure.
Draw BIM models and generate corresponding drawings.
Perform basic analyses using 3D BIM models.

courses.title: Industrial Training: BIM, Drawing, Surveying, and Sustainability
courses.description: The course provides an introduction to building information modeling (BIM), engineering drawings, engineering surveying, and sustainability. It includes theoretical and practical training on BIM model creation and analyses, engineering drawing generation, and related topics such as BIM standards and digital smart construction. The course also includes an introduction to the theory and practice of engineering surveying, including the measurement of level differences, angles and distances using construction levels and total stations, with applications in building structures. In addition, the course offers safety training and environmental training as well. For CIVL and CIEV students only.

cilos.description: Understand the basics of BIM and CAD, and use BIM and CAD software for both buildings and civil infrastructure applications.
Draw BIM models and perform basic analyses using 3D BIM models.
Use a construction level to measure differences in heights, apply such techniques in settlement monitoring and land profile determination, and process the data collected to obtain reduced levels.

Use a total station to measure vertical and horizontal angles and slope distances, convert the collected data to 3D coordinates, and apply such techniques to the measurements of buildings and structures such as the HKUST Sundial.
Identify potential hazards and apply appropriate control measures with a positive safety attitude in civil and construction activities.
Understand the role of construction innovations and sustainable practices in improving productivity, safety, and environmental performance in the construction industry.
Identify common parameters for water and air quality assessment and demonstrate correct use of portable instruments for field measurement and sampling.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods for Civil Engineers
courses.description: This course provides a concise introduction to multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and differential equations with an emphasis on civil engineering applications. Main topics include vector operations, partial derivatives and gradients, maximum/minimum problems, line integrals, vector fields and potential functions; systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; first and second order ODEs, Fourier series, Delta functions, Green’s functions (Duhamel integrals), and introduction to PDEs. Efficient computational and visualization tools such as graphing calculators and spreadsheets will also be introduced. For CIVL and CIEV students only.

cilos.description: Perform vector operations such as dot products and cross products, both by hand and using a graphing calculator, and explain the geometrical/physical meaning behind the computations.

Visualize functions of two variables, compute partial derivatives both by hand and using a graphing calculator, understand the meaning of directional derivatives, and solve problems involving maxima and minima.

Evaluate double and triple integrals, perform integration to obtain centroids, calculate area moments of inertia (/) through integration (for simple shapes) and using AutoCAD’s MASSPROP function (for complicated shapes), and appreciate the physical significance of / in bending of beams.
Formulate linear equations in terms of matrices and obtain solutions via matrix algebra, both by hand and using Excel’s matrix functions such as MMULT and MINVERSE.
Understand the eigenvalue problem, obtain eigenvalues and eigenvectors by hand, and by using numerical software when matrix size is large.

Perform line integrals and understand the concept of vector fields; construct potential functions in the context of elastic energy, generate stiffness matrices using repeated partial derivatives on the elastic energy, and utilize computer algebra systems to expedite such matrix assembly.

Solve first and second ODEs using various methods such as characteristic equations, Delta functions, Fourier series, Green’s functions (Duhamel integrals) and computer software such as deSolve; understand the relation between ODEs and Newton’s second law of motion.

Understand basic terminology of PDEs and recognize basic types of PDEs such as the wave equation, apply series method to solve selected PDEs arising in vibration theory, and visualize time behavior of solutions using a graphing calculator.

courses.title: Statics
courses.description: Application of Newton’s laws to engineering problems; statics of particles; rigid bodies; equivalent systems of forces; equilibrium of rigid bodies; distributed forces; centroids; moments of inertia; analysis of truss & frame structures; axial, shear and bending moment diagrams; friction.

cilos.description: Reduce a loaded structure to a model, i.e. creating proper free-body diagrams (FBD) of the structure or the parts in it.
Examine the stability of this structure, and classify a stable structure as the statically determinate orindeterminate.
Perform static analysis to a statically indeterminate structure, e.g. truss or certain frames.
Calculate and sketch the internal force in a structural member, e.g. axial force, shear force, bendingmoment.
Identify the structural analysis that is NOT covered in this course, and what future courses (e.g.mechanics of materials, structural analysis), will cover the relevant topics.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Analysis of stress, strain and deformation; linear and non-linear material behavior; strain energy; bending of beams, deflection; stability and buckling of compression members; shear and torsional stresses.

cilos.description: Examine the key principles used in the analysis of stress, strain and deformation, properties of engineering materials and safety factors.
Apply physical models to perform stress calculations and determine deflection, including thermal effects, in structural members such as axially loaded bars, torsional rods and beams.
Analyze and design simple structural members and determinate systems such as trusses, torsional members and beams on foundations.

courses.title: Modeling Systems with Uncertainties
courses.description: Identification and modeling of non-deterministic problems in civil engineering, and the treatment thereof relative to engineering design and decision making. Development of stochastic concepts and simulation models, and their relevance to real design and decision problems in various areas of civil engineering.

cilos.description: Acquire fundamental knowledge in uncertainty, probability and statistics.
Identify and model non-deterministic problems in civil engineering, and the treatment thereof as related to engineering design and decision making.
Formulate probability models based on the developed stochastic concepts, and their relevance to design and decision problems in various areas of civil engineering.
Solve engineering problems involving inherent uncertainties via probabilistic modelling and statistical tools.
Acquire basic simulation skills to solve realistic engineering problems effectively.

courses.title: Infrastructure Systems Engineering and Management
courses.description: This course will cover basic principles and techniques for analyzing engineering systems. It will entail an introduction to linear programs, network analysis, critical path method, benefit-cost and present value analyses of engineering projects.

cilos.description: Formulate and solve engineering optimization problems with the technique of linear programs and network analysis.
Conduct engineering economic analysis and project planning and scheduling.
Identify and formulate engineering problems.
Apply quantitative methods to solve engineering problems.
Appreciate the breadth of engineering problems.
Conduct economic feasibility study and project scheduling of engineering systems.

courses.title: Environmental Assessment and Management
courses.description: Present current environmental issues and management concepts; apply essential chemical and physical principles required to understand pollution problems; integrate knowledge from science and engineering to solve and assess environmental problems affecting water, air, noise and waste; cover concepts, ordinances and case studies of environmental impact assessment of civil infrastructure projects.

cilos.description: Develop a technical understanding of real-world environmental pollution problems affecting water, air and land resources.
Master basic scientific and engineering principles governing methods of solving problems affecting water, air and land resource quality.
Understand and formulate key elements of the Environmental Impact Assessment process that govern the application of the process to civil infrastructure projects.
Be aware of major environmental issues of today and their implications for human well-being.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: An introduction to the mechanics of fluids, including fluid statics, kinematics and fundamental equations of fluid flow, laminar and turbulent flow, boundary layers and applications in the design of hydraulic structures.

cilos.description: Describe the fundamental concepts of fluid mechanics.
Apply basic equations to determine pressure by static fluid.
Analyze fluid flows with fundamental laws including mass, momentum, and energy conservation.
Apply principles of dimensional analysis to conceptualize and simplify real problems.
Understand the broad application of fluid mechanics in civil and environmental engineering.

courses.title: Construction Materials
courses.description: Properties of engineering materials and their relation to the internal structure of materials; includes physical properties of construction materials like portland cement concrete, asphalt, polymers, ferrous metals and non-ferrous metals.

cilos.description: Understand basic properties of engineering materials and various factors affecting material behavior.
Understand the basis of material tests and correctly interpret the results.
Understand the effect of environmental and mechanical actions on the long-term behavior of materials.
Specify the appropriate construction material for a given project.
Make sound engineering judgements when new construction materials or modifications to existing construction materials are proposed.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development for Civil and Environmental Engineering III
courses.description: Continuation of CIVL 2000. A compulsory, one year course for students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students and/or to develop students' interpersonal skills in handling technical and non-technical issues in their professional careers. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Build industry awareness and professionalism.
Understand Industry Trends and Workplace Environments.
Prepare for Academic and Professional Growth.
Discuss academic and professional matters with their advisors.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development III
courses.description: Continuation of CIVL 2010. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Explore Career Opportunities in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Gain Awareness of Latest Professional Practices and Real-World Applications.
Prepare for Professional Growth in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Develop skills for effective job application and interview.

courses.title: Internship Training
courses.description: For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. Internship training provides students the opportunity to gain professional experience and to apply theories to real-life situations.
