courses.description: For QFIN students in their fourth year of study only. This is a capstone course for final year students in the BSc Quantitative Finance program. Working in groups, the students will bring together all the knowledge learned in the program to develop and execute a quantitative trading strategy through a simulated platform. The instructor will guide the students through the following stages: (1) idea generation, (2) strategy backtesting, (3) risk management planning, (4) system development, (5) trade execution, and (6) performance evaluation. Students will also have the opportunity to develop their leadership and presentation skills.

cilos.description: Develop a quantitative trading strategy.
Develop a risk management overlay.
Execute a trading strategy effectively.
Evaluate a trading strategy's performance.
Present a trading strategy in a professional manner.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Directed study of selected issues in Finance. May be graded by letter, or P/F for different offerings. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. Subject to approval by the department, students may repeat the course once if a different topic is selected.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of finance topics through independent research and literature review.
Apply appropriate data collection and analysis techniques to investigate a finance-related research question.
Generate insights and support evidence-based conclusions.
Communicate research findings clearly and professionally through written reports and/or oral presentations.

courses.title: Special Topics in Finance
courses.description: Covers current developments in finance. Topics selected by instructors.  May be graded P or F.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of key concepts, frameworks, or practices relevant to the course topic.
Analyze issues related to the course content using appropriate reasoning, frameworks, or tools.
Interpret and evaluate case studies, scenarios, or other relevant materials using critical thinking and appropriate analytical reasoning.

courses.title: Central Bank Operations
courses.description: This course is designed for students who intend to work in the finance industry as economists or strategists (e.g. rates strategist), both on the sell-side or the buy-side. This course starts from the fundamentals of central banks, particularly the balance sheet and relates it to central bank operations and the money creation process. The course will deep dive the Federal Reserve, covering both traditional and non-conventional policy tools. By incorporating macroeconomic diagnostics, students are encouraged to put themselves in the shoes of policymakers and predict policy decisions. This course will also study the monetary policy transmission mechanism and the link between financial and real sectors. In addition, this course links policy decisions to the pricing of assets, such as rates. The core principle of this course is “Learning by Doing”: students will be given plenty of opportunities to conduct data analysis to study the monetary policy impact to financial markets and real economy.

cilos.description: Read and interpret central bank balance sheets.
Recognize central bank tools, decision making process and communication.
Diagnose current macroeconomic environment.
Assess the impact of central bank policy on the financial markets and the real economy.
Understand the fundamentals of treasury securities and rates pricing.

courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Valuation of cash flow streams (PV of cash flow streams, annuities, and perpetuities); valuation of bonds; valuation of stocks using dividend discount model; capital budgeting decisions (NPV, IRR, payback); capital structure; limits to the use of debt (trade-off models); estimation of cost of debt and equity; WACC; terminal value.

cilos.description: Identify and analyze the objective of the firm.
Apply the concept of time value of money and discounting cash flows to situations when the cash flows and the discount rate is known.

Analyze the pros and cons of the common methods used in firms to evaluate and pick investment projects, and explain why the net present value (NPV) rule is the only one that is consistent with maximizing firm value.
Define the principles for identifying the cash flows that need to be discounted to calculate the NPV of a project.
Calculate the weighed average cost of capital and apply this to a real company.
Apply the above tools to cases that involve deciding whether to take a project and to merger decisions.

courses.title: Corporate Governance for Value Creation
courses.description: Corporate governance (CG) is about shaping incentives. CG examines how corporations induce their managers to maximize shareholder value through incentives and oversight systems (monitoring). This course examines how good corporate governance can mitigate incentive and information problems, nurture great leaders, and foster great companies. Through numerous cases and examples, we also show how bad governance can worsen these problems, lead managers to cheat, and cause companies to fall.

cilos.description: Describe the governance challenges facing companies and the tools of corporate governance (CG).
Explain how and why poor (good) CG destroys (creates) shareholder value.
Explain how and why the interests of various stakeholders and monitors converge or diverge.
Illustrate CG problems and solutions by drawing on a large set of illustrative cases and examples.
Critically read a CG report to assess the strengths and weaknesses of a company’s CG.
Propose a structured CG audit of a company or a situation based on sound economic principles.
Interpret the results of such an audit and make well-reasoned recommendations for improvement.
Professionally communicate audit results, interpretation, recommendations, in writing and orally.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Financial Management
courses.description: Valuation of projects (advanced capital budgeting); estimating cost of capital; risk assessment of projects; decision tree analysis; real option valuation of projects; warrants and convertibles; leasing; dividend policy.

cilos.description: Solve real world finance problems that are often encountered by corporate financial managers, bankers, and asset managers.
Work effectively in a team with people from different background.
Design financial strategy and present findings, insights, and advices in an accurate manner to future clients in the financial industry.

courses.title: Corporate Risk Management
courses.description: Practical and theoretical issues in risk management from the corporate end-user's perspective; benefits and optimal strategies of risk management; current cases which have been debated in the media.

cilos.description: Describe the risks facing companies and the tools of corporate risk management (CRM).
Explain and illustrate the main theories relating corporate risk management to firm value.
Summarize the main empirical and survey results on the practice of corporate risk management.
Master the case studies covered and relate them to decision-making in today’s risk environment.
Conduct a structured CRM audit and make well-reasoned recommendations for improvement.

courses.title: Family Business
courses.description: This course is tailored for individuals who are currently working in or are contemplating to work in a family business, either as a family member or a non-family executive. The material covered also gives greater understanding of the dynamics of family business for current or future private and investment bankers, family office professionals, accountants, lawyers and other service professionals working closely with families of wealth in the region.

cilos.description: Summarize the fundamentals of family business including its definition, importance, complexity, and how it differs from non-family business.
Analyze the factors contributing to the longevity of family businesses, and the causes for the potential early demise, especially for ethnic Chinese family businesses.
Design suitable wealth management strategies, structure and governance systems for wealth creators to preserve family wealth, family legacy, and harmony across generations.
Prepare future leaders of family businesses.
Identify the similarities of and differences between Chinese family businesses and those from other ethnic groups around the world.

courses.title: Investment Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to fundamental concepts in investment analysis. The first part covers risk and return tradeoff, portfolio diversification, and modern portfolio theory including the capital asset pricing model and arbitrage pricing theory. The second part covers basic analytical tools used in analyzing fixed income securities. Topics include interest rates and yield curve mathematics, duration and convexity.

cilos.description: Apply Utility theory in finance, identifying the risk-return tradeoff, and derive the ‘correct’ price for financial assets using models such as the CAPM.
Practically apply CAPM and other models (e.g. Fama-French 3 factor model) in Excel-based applications.
Explain efficient markets, behavioral finance, and some trading strategies based on perceived violations of efficient market theory.

courses.title: Equity Investment Management
courses.description: The course covers the complete investment process including: constructing investment objectives, outlining investment policies; choosing asset allocations; monitoring investments; and measuring performance.  Practical issues relating to investment style, active management, and passive management are discussed. Advanced techniques in portfolio construction such as the Black-Litterman model and multi-factor models are studied.

cilos.description: Apply the concepts of diversification, and adopt risk hedging, and optimal portfolio model to search for an optimal risk-return profile for a risky portfolio.
Apply multi-factor risk model in active equity investment management.
Analyze the effect of asymmetric information and liquidity on equity portfolio.

courses.title: ESG Investing
courses.description: This course puts together a collection of industry cases, projects and academic papers on Sustainable Investing, also known as ESG Investing. It is an investment approach that integrates three additional factors - environment (E), social (S) and governance (G), into security analysis and portfolio allocation. As the industry successfully adopts these factors into their double bottom line financial analysis, only a handful of courses - such as this one - would tackle the subject. This course will discuss the market terminology, practices, usages and dollar impact of ESG factors. The main focus is on the identification, measurement and the materiality of ESG indicators. The students will learn that financial analysis with ESG integration provides the basis for a more informed investment decision. Discussion on existing academic papers will shed light on the cost and benefits of sustainable investing. This course will empower the students with cutting edge information, tools and solid research on the subject.

cilos.description: Analyze and comment on complex real-world financial problems.
Adapt investment strategies to meet business needs.
Propose asset/risk-management solutions that maximize stakeholder value.
Apply the principles, skills, methods, techniques, and knowledge of modern finance to the process of investment management and securities valuation.

courses.title: FinTech Analytics
courses.description: The course will be based on the open-source Python language which provides a wide variety of statistical and graphical techniques, and is well-suited for data manipulation, calculation and graphical display. The first part of the course will be for general introduction to Python, and then use of specific tools like matrix manipulation, optimization, random numbers and simulation, etc. will be illustrated with financial applications. Some familiarity and prior experience with a proper programming language, beyond standard Excel, is recommended.

cilos.description: Demonstrate functional proficiency in Python programming.
Apply the control and data structures to solve computational problems.
Perform data input/output and simulations, and produce high quality graphics/plots.
Use packages of relevance to quantitative finance.
Apply the programming techniques in financial context.

courses.title: Empirical Methods in Finance
courses.description: This course studies the techniques of empirical investigation in finance. Students are introduced to recent empirical findings based on asset pricing and corporate finance models. The course includes a selection of econometrics topics and their finance applications. Students will apply the techniques using a programming language.

cilos.description: Apply econometric techniques for financial data analysis.
Analyze important facts and puzzles in asset pricing and corporate finance.
Use R programming language for data analysis.

courses.title: FinTech: The Future of the Financial Industry
courses.description: This is an introductory course to Financial Technology (FinTech) which includes Insurance Technology (InsurTech) and Regulation Technology (RegTech). The student will have a solid understanding of the underlying information technology being applied in various innovative business models to disrupt the finance and banking landscape globally. The critical business, social/ethical, legal and technology issues and the related risks faced by corporate executives when planning FinTech projects using quant finance models, DLT, crypto-token, AI, big data and algorithms to drive innovations in banking and finance will be discussed in class. Live demos will be conducted to illustrate the proof-of-concept and their applications in real world scenarios.  Key industry developments and the impact to stakeholders will be examined.

cilos.description: Identify the FinTech, InsurTech and RegTech landscape, its segment, regulations and ecosystem.
Confidently drive FinTech project developments as part of the executive team and deal with arising issues from various stakeholders, i.e. IT, legal, audit, compliance and regulations.

courses.title: Portfolio Management with Fintech Applications
courses.description: This course will focus on the key dimensions of Portfolio Management with FinTech Applications, and will give a predominant place to Artificial Intelligence, as a way to process and leverage the “Big Data” and automate the Portfolio and Wealth Management processes. The course will begin by a brief review of the fundamentals of Portfolio Management, FinTech and Artificial Intelligence and the advances in technology and data that has led the industry to where it is today. It will then delve into the Asset Management and Wealth Management value chains through a series of applications that enable students the critical skills they need to operate as expert actors in FinTech. The course will also expose students to the existing FinTech landscape and ecosystem within the portfolio management industry and will also touch upon on how Artificial Intelligence augments humans to make them better portfolio and wealth managers.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamentals of portfolio management with FinTech applications.
Recognize the FinTech landscape within the Portfolio Management space.
Use Artificial Intelligence in Portfolio Management to solve applied Business Problems.
Present the future trends that are coming to Portfolio Management.

courses.title: Smart Applications of Distributed Ledger Technology
courses.description: Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) are growing in use. This course covers the fundamental concept, design and implementation of the distributed ledgers and blockchain technologies in FinTech, InsurTech and other business areas. The characteristics and properties, as well as misconceptions, of blockchains will be discussed.

cilos.description: Understand what is Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) / Blockchain that supports the disruptive business strategies/models in banking and finance.
Explore and critically examine the deployment of any one or more of the DLTs, i.e. Blockchain, Ethereum, Hyperledger, R3 Corda and Stella in different environments.
Design the FinTech/InsurTech/RegTech business using BIDT and LoNG PESTEL model.
Analyze the socio-economic impact in the deployment of DLT instead of the traditional model.
Acquire the fundamental and practical knowledge to be entrepreneur or project management in the FinTech and Innovation industry.

courses.title: Derivatives Analysis
courses.description: Basic characteristics of derivatives instruments such as forwards, futures, options, and swaps. Topics include pricing of futures and forward contracts, forward-spot basis risk, option strategies, put-call parity and introduction to the Black-Scholes model. The development and use of interest rate and currency swaps are also discussed.

cilos.description: Define the mechanics of the derivatives markets including futures, options and swaps.
Use derivatives for hedging risks.
Use derivatives for trading various views on direction and volatility.
Explain price derivatives and how prices change with respect to different factors.

courses.title: Investment and Finance in China and Asia
courses.description: This course provides a practical understanding of foreign investment in China and Asia, and how financing is used for trade and investment in the region. Students will be able to develop ability to successfully complete deals in China and other Asian markets through taking this course.

cilos.description: To compare different kinds of financial structures in the Chinese and Asian contexts.
To analyze new situations to identify which techniques and contextual factors are the most critical.
To design and implement strategies using financial techniques in order to structure, negotiate and close deals in a variety of Chinese and Asian contexts.

courses.title: Fixed Income Analysis
courses.description: Includes techniques in fixed-income portfolio management and introduction of fixed-income derivatives. Topics include term-structure theories, yield-curve fitting techniques and yield curve trading strategies, portfolio performance evaluation, floating rate securities, forward rate agreements, bond and interest rate futures, and interest rate swaps.

cilos.description: Identify basic valuation techniques of the traditional fixed-income securities, based on concepts such as price-yield relationship, alternative definitions of yields, price sensitivity measures (durations and convexities).
Calculate spot rates, discount factors, forward rates, par-bond yields, holding period returns, and identify classical theories of the term structure of interest rate.
Implement yield-curve fitting techniques and some simple portfolio strategies.
Recognize more advanced concepts like repos and floating rate, and develop the necessary economic intuition and quantitative skills.

courses.title: Equity Valuation
courses.description: Basic valuation approaches including dividend discount model, free cash flows model, and valuation by multiples; measures of company performance and value added; valuation in special situations such as emerging markets, closely held companies, mergers, and divestitures.

cilos.description: Use standard equity valuation models, like discounted cash flow (DCF) , to assess the value of a firm or a project.
Understand the value driving factors, for example, management team, market monopolistic power, and technological barrier, from the angle of a private equity manager.
Understand the difference in the equity pricing/valuation practice between the western world and the Greater China region.
Use certain models to detect the potential frauds in financial statements.
Use real options in assessing the value of firm or project when facing high uncertainty.

courses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
courses.description: Topics include: (1) An overview of the venture capital and private equity markets in Asia; (2) Deal structuring; (3) Valuation techniques; (4) Due diligence and post-investment management; (5) Understanding the terms in term sheets; (6) Negotiating term sheets; (7) Going public, trade sale and other exit strategies.  Real-world examples from throughout Asia will be used to illustrate these topics.

cilos.description: Explain the world of VCPE investments.
Analyze challenges associated with each cycle of the VCPE process from pre-investment to post-investment.

Implement VCPE key screening criteria to identify and screen prospective investee companies, and develop skills and understanding necessary to perform VCPE due diligence for prospective investee firms.
Evaluate term sheet structure, key terms and understand their limitations and challenges.
Apply VCPE fund governance, management, and return measures in practice.

Apply valuation techniques to value private firms, including market, income, and asset-based approaches, and describe practical limitations of various valuation techniques and the importance of understanding assumptions of the underlying business valuations.
Administer the highly practical approach to mitigating, adjusting VCPE risks.
Draft investment memo to address investment rationale, risks, and rewards in practice.
Evaluate routes of VCPE exits, including trade sale, secondary buyout, IPO, among others.

“Experience” the realm of being a VCPE professional by engaging in a “hackathon” way of negotiation between the buyer (VCPE) and the seller (investee firm) that aims to mimic the real world environment.

courses.title: Market Microstructure
courses.description: The course is designed to provide students with an overview of how supply equals demand in real-world financial markets. After taking this course , students would be able to appreciate the frictions existing in actual financial markets - bid-ask spreads, trade impact on price, brokerage commissions, quantity limitations, time delays, market manipulation, etc. - and be able to devise trading strategies that minimize these frictions.

cilos.description: Broaden and deepen their understanding of finance, explain how financial markets actually work and minimize trading costs when they trade for themselves or their employers.
Apply practical skills to explain real-time quotes and analyze the costs of trading.
Demonstrate effective communication in oral English through group presentations.
Develop creative and critical thinking through the group project of developing their original trading strategy or analysis of a brewing trading controversy.
Work effectively in multi-cultural settings.
Recognize ethical and professional responsibility of finance professionals; in particular through the discussions of the dark side of trading.

courses.title: Risk Management for Financial Institutions
courses.description: Brief overview of financial intermediaries and their functions.  Measures of interest rate risk: periodic (re-pricing) gap, duration gap.  Management of interest rate risk using appropriate composition of assets and liabilities, futures, options, caps, floors, collars, swaps.  Market risk: value at risk measures.  Management of credit risk, off-balance sheet risk, liquidity risk, capital adequacy.  Deposit insurance.  With selected case studies.

cilos.description: Understand how a bank organizes itself to manage different types of risks.
Critically review structures and proposals to identify key risks and think about potential mitigants.
Understand the latest concepts in risk management.

courses.title: Hedge Funds
courses.description: Alternative investments are the fastest growing sector of the financial industry, and probably the least understood, including by several market professionals.  Although the range of sophistication in people associated with alternative investments varies substantially, it is more and more common to use them in investment strategies, either as direct investments or through funds of funds or structured products.  The purpose of this course is to give participants a good understanding and workable knowledge of the techniques that should be part of the tool kit of anyone investing in, analyzing and/or advising private and institutional clients on the inclusion of alternative investments - and more specifically hedge funds - in their portfolios.  Furthermore, this course will enable the participants to absorb the analytical arguments in the technical publications - the in-house research notes of financial institutions and in practitioner oriented journal - that deal with alternative investments and to apply them.

cilos.description: Understand what hedge funds are and how they are structured.
Understand the major hedge fund strategies, their potential risks and expected rewards.
Understand how to analyze hedge funds qualitatively and quantitatively.

courses.title: Mergers, Acquisitions and Restructuring
courses.description: Focuses on the design, analysis, and implementation of financial strategies aimed at repositioning and revitalizing companies.  Corporate value creation by restructuring a company or by undergoing a business combination.

cilos.description: Measure the value created by M&A/Restructuring.
Evaluate the tactics and the effect of management opposition to M&A.
Understand the role of Private Equity, activists/raiders in corporate restructuring.
Implement merger arbitrage tactics.
Understand the role of corporate governance in M&A/Restructuring decisions.

courses.title: Commodities, Trade Finance and Infrastructures
courses.description: This course will focus on three alternative "asset classes", namely commodities, trade finance and infrastructures. The purpose of this course is to give participants a good understanding and workable knowledge of the techniques that should be part of the toolkit of anyone investing in, trading, hedging, analyzing and/or advising private and institutional clients on these three alternative asset classes. Furthermore, this course will enable the participants to absorb the analytical arguments in the technical publications – the in-house research notes of financial institutions and in practitioner oriented journals – that deal with commodities and their markets, and to apply them.

cilos.description: Identify and explain the types and nature of commodities in general, their pricing mechanisms and the methods by which these commodities are traded.
Implement commodity trades and size them appropriately.
Explain the contractual principles underpinning trade finance.
Describe and explain infrastructure investing.
Present a research topic about these alternative investments.

courses.title: Advanced Venture Capital Investing
courses.description: This course is a follow-up of FINA 5390 Venture Capital and Private Equity, with a particular focus on early-stage venture companies. Students will be able to experience and practice all the learned materials, particularly those related to the venture capital (VC) endeavors, in real-world VC settings. Students will “invest” alongside VC practitioners as well as being guided by them on various topics such as screening prospective investee companies in a live pitch session and drafting and compiling due diligence lists, term sheets, the required closing documentations, and valuation assessments, in addition to presenting early-read memos to industry professionals (e.g., members of the investment committee (IC)) for deal approvals, among other topics. The professor will frequently relate concepts discussed in class to transactions currently in the news to illustrate their application and limitations.

cilos.description: Use venture capital (VC) investing fundamentals in the real world.
Interact with investee companies.
Select investee companies and enhance themselves using advanced evaluation matrices.
Generate due diligence list and explain the rationale behind it.
Conduct due diligence on investee companies and explain how Investment Committee (IC) members approve investment deals.

Value investee companies using methods recommended by International Private Equity Valuation
Guidelines (IPEVG), including option pricing.
Negotiate term sheets and explore deal structures with investee companies.
Close deals (or not) with investee companies, draft closing reports, and conduct post-deal analyses.

courses.title: VC Entrepreneurships
courses.description: This course will cover how the Venture Capital (VC) industry works, all the parties involved, and the dynamics therein. By illustrating real world examples in some of the largest and most respected and successful VC firms in the world, students will learn how VCs raise money, how they construct a fund portfolio, how they make investment decisions, how VC returns are calculated, and how to land a job in this mysterious sector of high finance.

cilos.description: Understand the latest industry best practices to launch and manage a VC fund
Construct a VC fund portfolio
Decide the most appropriate valuation method for a startup
Conduct a due diligence process on a startup company
Construct a best-practice term sheet that reflects considerations to all parties
Determine the most appropriate exit strategy for an investment
Answer the question: is venture capital the right career choice for me?

courses.title: Decision Making in Financial Institutions
courses.description: In this course, students will be able to examine the nature of main financial institutions (i.e., banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, and hedge funds) as well as the incentives of decision makers in these institutions. The course also covers the purpose of bank regulation and financial crises.

cilos.description: Examine the nature of main financial institutions (i.e., banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, and hedge funds)
Examine the incentives of decision makers in main financial institutions
Understand the role of main financial institutions in the economy
Understand the effects of informational problems in main financial institutions
Understand the effects of agency costs on behavior of agents in main financial institutions
Critically evaluate the incentives of different economic actors in development of financial crises

courses.title: Financial Data Analysis
courses.description: Headline financial data are informative but not fully revealing, concealing hidden gems and traps. This course applies a wise-investor perspective to looking behind the scenes of financial statements. Building from the ground up, students learn how to spot abnormalities, develop pro-forma financials, build solid valuation models, and gain the knowledge and skills to pitch sound investment strategies. These foundations are supplemented by several real-world study cases illustrating accounting issues such as revenue recognition, valuation, and failed unicorns.

cilos.description: Explain the connections between the financial statements.
Demonstrate key accounting concepts such as cash vs. accruals, revenue recognition, and cost structure.
Build pro-forma financials and convert them to discounted cash flow projections.
Cite relevant case studies to show how and why appealing investments can go wrong.
Integrate micro-foundations, macro-conditions, and market sentiment in formulating an investment case.
Compare and contrast the pros and cons of various valuation methods.

courses.title: Green Finance: Markets and Institutions
courses.description:
Overview of the major issues in green finance pertaining to markets and financial institutions from the standpoint of both investors and policymakers. One of the main references is a report by the Network for Greening the Financial System. Topics: 
taxonomies and green classification frameworks, green external review, climate transition metrics, disclosure requirements, green rating systems, the role  of technology in green data collection and market transparency, green product adaptations, challenges specific to China and Asia, and preparation for ESG certifications.

cilos.description: Trace the history of green finance, situate its current state, and project likely future trajectories.
Differentiate among financial instruments, green and traditional, and critique their shortcomings.
Review the changing disclosure environment and the reliability of key carbon emissions disclosure items.
Describe and critique the various institutions and methods for green certification and verification.
Describe the rating harmonization challenges and the role of technology in green data collection.
Narrate the green experience in emerging Asia and Japan and the case of China in particular.

courses.title: Alternative Investment Management
courses.description: This course aims to provide students a holistic introduction to the alternative investment ecosystem, covering sectors such as private equity, real estate, infrastructure, credit, hedge funds, secondaries, and others.

cilos.description: Describe the overall Alternative Investment (AI) ecosystem, including the various market participants and investment strategies.
Develop an Investment Policy Statement from the perspective of the different Asset Owners.
Compare and contrast across the different AI strategies in terms of the relative risk and return profiles, strengths and weaknesses, and relevance for different market participants.
Describe the different methods for accessing, evaluating, and selecting different AI strategies and investment opportunities.
Develop, prepare, and present marketing materials for different investment strategy and products.

courses.title: Carbon Management Basics for Financial Institutions
courses.description: The world needs to reach net zero emission by 2050 to keep global warming within 1.5 °C by the end of this century. Financial sector plays an important role in this net zero transition. This course equips the students with the basic knowledge and practical tools of net zero strategy for financial institutions. It elaborates the concepts on climate change, the measurement tool of greenhouse emissions, the low-carbon roadmap for financial institutions and the development of sustainable finance products related to climate change.

cilos.description: Understand the climate change risks and impacts.
Understand the financial institutions’ roles in net zero transition.
Master the practical skills of carbon measurement and climate reporting.
Develop the climate finance products.

courses.title: Real Estate Financing
courses.description: This course focuses on how real estate financing is undertaken and the key considerations for the borrower and the lender. This is achieved through a master case study which runs through the duration of the course and evolves as different aspects of real estate financing are discussed. The course will focus on the key steps in a transaction life-cycle and require participants to prepare basic cash-flow models, approval memos and negotiate term-sheets. The course also includes additional case studies around hedging and considerations around cross border real estate financings.

cilos.description: Describe the typical deal life-cycle of a financing transaction and how they differ for different type of clients, situations and products.
Undertake due diligence of a real estate transaction.
Write a credit approval memo for internal bank discussions.
Negotiate a term sheet.
Evaluate financing proposals from a borrower's perspective.
Identify the different financing situations and markets available to borrowers.

courses.title: Wealth Management
courses.description: With an introduction to the principles of wealth management and the financial planning process, this course progresses to cover various wealth management topics including consumption planning, investment planning and retirement planning. In particular, this course emphasizes on the provision of investment advisory services. It discusses client expectations and concerns including risk and other cognitive issues before applying the concepts and techniques to construct and manage investment portfolios for individual clients.

cilos.description: Apply personal profiling and risk profiling techniques to comprehend the unique situation and preferences of the client.
Prioritize goals for client given their unique situations and determine the feasibility of achieving these goals.
Construct personal financial statements and use ratios and other techniques to analyze the client's financial situation.
Construct optimal portfolios and make asset allocation decisions which match goals, risk tolerance and other client characteristics.
Clearly discuss and justify recommendations.

courses.title: Asia's Stock Markets
courses.description: This course is highly relevant to students interested to become macro-traders, portfolio managers, buy/sell-side analysts or work at a hedge fund, with a particular focus on Asia. The course will teach students the characteristics of the larger, liquid stock markets across Asia, from China and Hong Kong to Korea, Taiwan, India and ASEAN markets. Students will learn what drives these markets, what they have in common and how they behave.

cilos.description: Describe the differences in composition and architecture of the major Asian stock markets.
Explain “top-down” (macro) and “bottom-up” drivers of the major Asian stock markets.
Narrate recent dynamics in Asian equities and map these to a concrete investment plan.
Formulate an Asian stock market outlook.
Adapt an existing Asian market outlook to reflect changes in investment views.
Present a complex investment view in a concise and clear format.

courses.title: Family Office
courses.description: This course will provide students with a comprehensive and most up-to-date understanding of family office, as well as insiders’ view and practical aspects of family offices, especially Asian family offices. The course will address questions based on the extensive research and the latest case studies on family offices in Asia and around the world by the instructor.

cilos.description: Manage the wealth and achieve greater meaning of the wealth.
Understand fundamentals and wealth management role of family office.
Understand the impact investing and risk management of family office.
Understand the concepts of family trust and family governance.
Understand the family philanthropy and the family office development in China.

courses.title: Responsible Finance
courses.description: The aim of this course is to develop a deep understanding why the economic doctrine that the only social responsibility of corporations is to maximize profits does no longer work in today’s capital markets. The course provides theoretical and empirical findings that illustrate that financial decisions need to incorporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors to ensure long-term financial success of firms. The course also covers new trends, such as U.S. political polarization and the important role of China in establishing a global leadership role in green finance, which may impact how corporations are becoming more responsible.

cilos.description: Describe the fundamental driving forces of responsible finance.
Compare and contrast responsible finance and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) in relation to corporate objectives.
Explain how investors may engage with firms in effective manners.
Work in teams on cases to apply responsible finance theory to practice.
Utilize the tools and data sets used in evaluating ESG performance.
Propose a novel corporate project that grows the pie.
Broaden firm performance evaluation encompassing ESG methods.

courses.title: Green Finance and Capital Markets
courses.description: This course will cover sustainable and green finance with a focus in Hong Kong and China. Various green finance instruments, how green elements are factored in credit ratings and assessments, and the major external green review approaches are covered. This course will empower the students with the most updated knowledge, market trends and direct first-hand cases (rather than the public domain) in the green finance and capital market fields.

cilos.description: Compare and contrast various green finance and capital market products.
Describe and quantify the costs and benefits of green finance as it impacts credit ratings.
Explain and critique the green bond assessment process performed by credit rating agencies.
Apply the green certification approaches to the green bonds performed by certification service providers.

courses.title: Financial Advisory and Transaction Execution for M&A
courses.description: The course provides an understanding of executing mergers and acquisitions (M&A) transactions, with a specific focus on Asia and China. An in-depth exploration of M&A processes will help students to develop a working knowledge of how to execute an M&A deal - from identifying and analyzing target companies to conducting due diligence, securing financing, and closing the transaction. It will also cover constructing financial models and performing analyses throughout.

cilos.description: Analyze and identify various structures of M&A transactions for different types of situations.
Execute tools to complete M&A transactions and structure them in both public and private market environments.
Recognize how M&A transactions are financed, the implications of the funding mix, and how value is created in M&A through common analyses.
Plan M&A transactions from the perspective of financial investors, focusing on leveraged buyouts (LBOs).

courses.title: Sustainable Finance and Reporting Strategies in Hong Kong
courses.description: This course aims to develop students’ comprehensive knowledge, skills, and understanding of ESG, sustainable finance, and ESG reporting. Particular focus will be placed on the impact of ESG and sustainable finance on listed companies in Hong Kong. This course comprises both formal lectures and guest lectures to allow students to develop solid ESG and green finance knowledge, as well as understand the latest market and regulatory developments in Hong Kong.

cilos.description: List the latest ESG market and regulatory development.
Compare and contrast various sustainable finance products.
Develop a solid knowledge of green taxonomy and ESG reporting.

courses.title: Essential Financial Market Tools
courses.description: This course offers an advantage by empowering students with hands-on experience using some of the industry-leading financial tools. There are various certificates (e.g., Bloomberg Market Concepts, London Stock Exchange Group Finance Essentials) that students can earn during the course. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Learn about the financial markets, Bloomberg data, news, and analytics via four core modules – Economic Indicators, Currencies, Fixed Income and Equities.
Access trusted, real-world market data, news and statistics that power the global financial community, so they can advance applied learning.
Perform financial analysis using Bloomberg terminal, London Stock Exchange group Workspace, Wind terminal and Morningstar Direct.

courses.title: Structured Product
courses.description: Structured products are one of the major products manufactured and distributed by investment banks given the increasing demand from institutional and individual investors. This course covers basic concepts of structured products, introduces popular products in the market (e.g., principal protected notes and equity-linked notes), and discusses the landscape of product manufacturing and distribution process. It focuses on applications rather than theory by illustrating real-world examples as well as their practical implementations in the industry.

cilos.description: Understand the nature of structured products.
Explain the key features, risks, and benefits of structured products.
Understand how structured products are manufactured and sold to clients.
Be familiar with popular structured products in the market and understand their pros and cons.
Analyze the typical structured products in the market.
Identify suitable products for potential clients given their risk appetite.
Make effective presentations to pitch potential clients.

courses.title: Navigating Capital Markets: A Practitioner's Guide to Capital Flows
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration into the realm of global capital markets in practice. We will delve into the inner workings of financial markets, including primary and secondary markets, trading floors and market dynamics. Students will apply analytical skills to learn to identify opportunities across capital markets including synthesizing information, identifying capital uses and interpreting market sentiment and behavior. This course is designed to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical application. The focus is on equipping students with the insights needed to excel in the complex world of capital markets, providing a foundation for exploring more advanced subjects.

cilos.description: Explain the role of capital markets, from theory to practice.
Explain the flows of capital across market participants.
Explain various instruments used across the various asset classes.
Identify opportunities in the movement of capital.
Understand the mechanics and role of capital markets in managing flows between stakeholders.
Identify the different roles available and how a potential career in capital markets may develop.

courses.title: Strategic Corporate Financing: IPOs, Debt, and Private Equity Solutions
courses.description: This course provides a practical understanding of corporate financing solutions from issuers' and investors' perspectives. Public market equity funding is explored, focusing on initial public offerings (IPOs) and their impact on companies and stakeholders. Debt as a funding source is examined, with key debt instruments analyzed in the context of leveraged buyouts. Private market equity financing is covered, using early-stage and pre-IPO companies as examples. Hands-on elements include constructing Excel models and conducting analyses throughout the course.

cilos.description: Recognize how to structure and execute capital raising transactions for businesses at various stages of their life cycles.
Evaluate how companies are valued in the context of such transactions.
Develop deeper understanding of the impact of various forms of capital raising on both the company (or the issuer) and the investor.
Execute their knowledge of corporate finance and apply it to real-world situations and transactions.

courses.title: Climate Finance and Energy Transition
courses.description: This course examines how climate and transition finance can help avert climate change and accelerate the shift to clean energy. It focuses on financial instruments, market mechanisms, and policy frameworks that support decarbonization, carbon pricing, and emissions reduction. Key topics include carbon markets, renewable and climate tech investments, nature-based solutions, and corporate finance for the energy transition.

cilos.description: Explain possible financial solutions to climate change and its social and economic contexts using finance and management knowledge and concepts.
Evaluate financial sector impacts on climate solutions and the energy transition with evidence-based approaches.
Appropriately communicate the role of the financial industry in climate change and transition finance including positive and negative examples of climate finance to different stakeholders.
Develop strategies and solutions to promote effective financial tools to mitigate climate change and transition away from fossil fuels.

courses.title: Financial Modeling
courses.description: This is a course about financial modeling.  The goal is to make financial models that produce useful answers to economic questions.  Selected topics which lend themselves to financial modeling will be covered, such as (but not limited to) loan amortization schedules; valuation and private equity; equity derivatives; mutual fund performance and style analysis; fixed income derivatives, and optimal portfolio selection.

cilos.description: Use Excel formulas, functions and commands in finance-related applications.
Implement in spreadsheet format concepts from finance theory, with emphasis on portfolio choice and valuation of derivatives and fixed income securities.
Gain hands-on experience in designing finance models.
Critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of the output of various financial models in principle, and those implemented in a spreadsheet in particular.

courses.title: Big Data in Finance
courses.description: This course introduces students to the concepts of big data and machine learning with a special focus on how these tools can be applied in a financial context. During the course students will learn Python and how it can be used to build and estimate some of the most commonly used machine learning models such as regression, clustering and classification. Students will also learn the basics of cloud computing and how the cloud can be employed to quickly estimate complex models with very large data sets.
courses.prerequisite: ISOM 5510 OR ISOM 5520 (prior to 2022-23) OR FINA 5240 OR FINA 5250

cilos.description: Define what big data is and how it relates to finance.
Work with Python.
Use Python to produce basic statistics and visualize data.
Describe the basic mathematical rationale for state-of-the-art machine learning models.
Use Python to estimate machine learning models on real-world data.
Explain how cloud computing technologies can be employed to facilitate quick estimation of complex.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Current developments in finance. Topics selected by the instructor.

cilos.description: Apply the financial knowledge to real-world investment management and securities valuation.
Develop sophisticated financial models to support decision making.
Propose asset/risk-management solutions that maximize firm value.

courses.title: Finance Practicum
courses.description: This course is a unique opportunity for students in the MSc in Finance program to gain practical experience and apply their knowledge in a professional setting. By completing the Practicum, students will be equipped with practical experience, enhanced professional skills, and a deeper understanding of the complexities and challenges in the financial industry. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply theoretical knowledge and skills acquired throughout the program to real-world scenarios in the financial industry.
Demonstrate effective problem-solving, critical thinking, and communication skills in a professional setting.
Understand the complexities and challenges faced in the financial industry and develop strategies to address them.
Reflect on their internship experiences and identify areas of personal and professional growth.
Integrate academic knowledge with practical experiences in real scenarios in the financial industry.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Study of selected financial issues under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)

cilos.description: Have up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of finance, leading to independent substantive scholarly research.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: Current research topics in corporate finance, investments, financial markets and institutions, derivative securities, and empirical research in financial economics.

cilos.description: Present their discipline knowledge clearly to laymen.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Theoretical Corporate Finance
courses.description: The course will emphasize theoretical frameworks that underlie some of the important ideas in modern corporate finance.  Topics covered will be (i) Financial Contracting, (ii) Capital Structure and Corporate Strategy , (iii) Agency Problems, Investment Distortions, and Discipline, (iv) Information Asymmetry and Financing,(v) Corporate Governance. The theory will be motivated by and connected to empirical facts, although we will not go into details of empirical papers on the topics. An important goal is to help students learn how to write down a basic model to capture an idea.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Theoretical Asset Pricing
courses.description: This course offers an introduction to asset pricing. The intention of the course is to provide a basis in the neoclassical theory of finance that underlies the other PhD-level finance courses. It uses the theory of choice under uncertainty to develop classical asset pricing theory in discrete time. The two main parts of the course focus on static asset pricing models and dynamic asset pricing models with a representative agent. Throughout, the course discusses several empirical puzzles and theories that have been developed to try to solve them.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Empirical Corporate Finance
courses.description: This course covers major topics in empirical corporate finance. A large part of this course is devoted to examining research questions in capital structure, corporate investments, and corporate governance. The focus is on the more recent literature in these broad areas of corporate finance. The goal of the course is to help students get ready for doing their own research.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Empirical Asset Pricing
courses.description: Part one of the course covers various issues and empirical methods in asset pricing studies. Empirical issues regarding time-series properties of asset prices are discussed first, followed by the cross-sectional implications of asset pricing models. Applications in bond, currency, and futures markets will also be discussed. Part two of the course is designed to provide students with the exposure to empirical finance, with the focus on investment and behavioral finance.

courses.title: Finance Workshops
courses.description: Papers presented by faculty, students and visitors. Mandatory for all PhD students.  May be repeated for credit. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Have up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of finance, leading to independent substantive scholarly research.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.

courses.title: Family Governance
courses.description: The course equips students with the specialized knowledge and skills needed to address the increasing complexity faced by family businesses and family offices in managing wealth, family relationships and family legacy across generations. Students will learn the key elements of effective family governance, analyze influencing factors, and develop competencies to establish robust governance frameworks. The course prepares students to serve as trusted advisors/family professionals and support/drive the smooth generational transitions for wealthy families.

cilos.description: Understand the reason for setting up family governance and the role of family governance.
Understand the key elements of the family governance structure.
Understand how cultural differences influence the design of family governance.
Understand how family governance could preserve family harmony and family values throughout generations.
Develop the skills to design and implement an effective family governance structure.
Understand the differences and relationships among family governance, corporate governance and family office governance.

courses.title: Managing and Transferring Wealth for Sustainable Growth:Overview of Structures,Tools and Regulations
courses.description: This course provides students with knowledge of the legal structures (including family office, family investment funds and family trusts) used for wealth management, succession planning and tax planning. It also discusses governance issues of these structures, philanthropic structures and other succession planning tools, and relevant trust laws, financial regulations and tax rules.

cilos.description: Understand different types of legal structuring options available in setting up family office, family investment funds and family trusts.
Understand legal structuring options for philanthropic purposes and other succession planning tools.
Identify governance and internal compliance issues related to such structures and explain the factors that contribute to best practices.
Acquire basic knowledge in relevant trust laws, financial regulations and tax rules.
Apply the knowledge learnt in complex cross-border planning situations.

courses.title: Impact Investment and Family Philanthropy
courses.description: This course describes the wide spectrum of investment strategies, ranging from those focusing on financial returns and others focusing on social returns. It provides students with knowledge of the current trend in impact investing and philanthropy, how it influences firms and the society, and the challenges faced by firms and the financial industry, with a focus on family office.

cilos.description: Understand the definition and importance of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance).
Understand the tradeoff between financial and social returns in the context of family office.
Describe the trends in the asset management industry, family office, impact investing, and philanthropy.
Identify the channels through which impact investing and philanthropy improve sustainability.
Explain the relationship between ESG, impact investing and philanthropy, and firms’ performance.

courses.title: Family Wealth Management
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of wealth management, encompassing strategies and techniques. Students will delve into advanced topics in financial planning, investment management, risk assessment, and estate planning from asset owners’ perspectives. Special focus will be placed on mastering the framework and practical skills required to develop effective asset allocations.

cilos.description: Demonstrate proficiency in executing the complete wealth management process, encompassing personal profiling, risk profiling, goal setting, designing and implementing asset allocations, and effectively managing portfolios.

Deeply understand and carry out long-term strategic asset allocation and portfolio management, and internalize the concept of diversification in wealth and asset management, understanding its significance and application within the field.
Exhibit competence in initiating and maintaining client communications, while comprehensively understanding the Know Your Customer (KYC) process.
Develop a routine of monitoring and updating critical macroeconomic data, enabling the formulation of informed opinions on major economic trends so they are well-prepared for investment roles.

courses.title: Preserving Harmony: Dispute Resolution in Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course is intended to introduce students to the legal and regulatory issues surrounding alternative methods of dispute resolution aside from litigation. Specifically, the course focuses on the practical factors relevant to selecting appropriate dispute resolution methods in resolving conflicts in distinct circumstances, within family businesses.

cilos.description: Understand the concepts and theories of Alternative Dispute Resolution.
Understand the emotional, legal, financial complexities as well as cultural and generational differences that disputes bring to the family setting.
Understand the factors that influence family members to resolve disputes in a harmonious manner.
Develop the soft skills to preserve relationships, protecting reputational risks, ensuring business continuity and above all ensuring compliance with regulatory and legal requirements.
Draft appropriate dispute resolution clauses/agreements to cater for different scenarios.

courses.title: Managing Generational Family Dynamics
courses.description: This course explores the complexities of relationship dynamics and conflict resolution in family businesses and family offices. Students will develop awareness and sensitivity to intra-generational and trans-generational relationship dynamics, acquire practical conflict resolution skills, and enhance self-awareness to manage interpersonal challenges effectively. The course integrates theoretical frameworks with practical tools and strategies, enabling students to navigate complex family relationships while fostering harmony and collaboration.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of intra-generational and trans-generational relationship dynamics in family businesses.
Integrate conflict resolution theories into analyzing and addressing interpersonal and generational conflicts.
Design and implement practical strategies to resolve family conflicts and foster collaboration.
Reflect on personal conflict styles and develop emotional intelligence to manage conflicts effectively.
Exhibit ethical and responsible decision-making in managing family relationships.
Communicate effectively and collaborate across generational and stakeholder groups.

courses.title: Growing and Advancing Family Heritage through Entrepreneurship
courses.description: The course provides a platform where students will attain insights and practical experience required to support and enable their aspirations of taking their inheritance into the future. Insights and experience, in particular, related to areas of entrepreneurial skill sets and mindsets in the context of family business, essential leadership skills and ethical practices required of a next-generation family business owner.

cilos.description: Understand the building blocks of modern entrepreneurship in the context of family business.
Formulate one’s own view of bringing innovation into family legacy.
Understand and manage dynamics between family heritage and personal entrepreneurial initiatives.
Apprehend management leadership skills essential to take the helm.
Understand and practice ethics and morals in family business.
Develop creative and critical thinking skills and gain hands-on experience to champion business development through consulting and advising start-up business entity to achieve key milestones.

courses.title: Art and Business Integration
courses.description: The course explores the dynamic relationship between art and commerce, focusing on how art can be leveraged to enhance business strategies, brand identity, and corporate culture. Students will examine the role of art in various business contexts, including branding, product innovation, corporate culture, investment, philanthropy, and community engagement.

cilos.description: Analyze the role of art in branding, corporate identity, and fostering a collaborative, value-driven culture.
Apply artistic principles and strategies to drive innovation in products, services, and business problem-solving.
Evaluate art as an investment asset, exploring its potential for wealth preservation, diversification, and philanthropy.
Propose strategies for integrating art into Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives and community enrichment.
Develop approaches to enhance productivity, morale, and client loyalty through art-based programs in business and family enterprises.

courses.title: Family Collections: Appreciation, Transaction, Investment and Management
courses.description: Building a collection is a natural expansion of a mature family business. As the art and luxury goods markets evolve, family collections increasingly reflect cultural values and taste, while also serving as investment assets. This course, led by industry experts in art and luxury goods, will delve into various aspects of family collecting with participants through firsthand experiences and case studies.

cilos.description: Understand the significance of building a family collection.
Understand the development trends of the international collectibles market.
Master the basic appreciation and collection methods of mainstream collection items.
Experience firsthand the joy and value of appreciating and collecting art and luxury goods.
Establish connections with experts in mainstream collection projects.
Gain practical experience in collection-building operations through field trips and group reports.

courses.title: Leading a Family Business in a Changing World
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide students with understanding and insight into a set of leadership challenges facing all businesses and organizations in the world today. This course will identify how privately-held family businesses may need to understand and address these challenges differently from other types of business organizations.

cilos.description: Understand key themes in responsible and ethical leadership that leaders of family-run businesses should appreciate for effective leadership of their organizations.
Gain insight into the latest research on how concepts of ethical leadership are less well-embedded in family-run businesses today.
Learn key approaches to Individual Leadership that are important for generating performance in organizations and potentially challenging in the culture of a family-owned business.
Learn key approaches to Leadership of Teams that are important for generating performance in teams and potentially challenging in the culture of a family-owned business.

courses.title: Integrated Disciplines in the Family World
courses.description: This course provides students with knowledge about how family office can adopt an Integral Approach and combine tangible (such as legal, financial and operational) and intangible (such as relational, emotional and spiritual/transpersonal) aspects in its service provision. Students will get first-hand exposure in the form of self reflection workshops, individual sharing and group project works.

cilos.description: Understand how the Integral Approach could be used to address legal and other issues involved in family office and legal works.
Explain the dynamics of families as a system using Bowen Family Systems Theory.
Explain key concepts in Emotion-Focused Therapy and the significance of emotions in the context of family office.
Explain how spiritual and transpersonal approaches including Psychosynthesis and Intuitive Inquiry can benefit families.
Apply the knowledge learnt in understanding and improving dynamics of their own families and client families.

courses.title: Overview of Alternative Investments
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with a holistic introduction to the alternative investment ecosystem, covering sectors such as private equity, venture capital, real estate, infrastructure, private credit, hedge funds, secondaries, royalties, and others.

cilos.description: Describe the overall Alternative Investment (AI) ecosystem, including the various market participants and investment strategies.
Develop an Investment Policy Statement from the perspective of the different asset owners, including family offices.
Compare and contrast across the different AI strategies in terms of the relative risk and return profiles, strengths and weaknesses, and relevance for different market participants.
Describe the different methods for accessing, evaluating, and selecting different AI strategies and investment opportunities.
Develop, prepare, and present marketing materials for different investment strategies and products.
Promote a better understanding of the AI environment through case studies and other relevant real-life examples.

courses.title: Family Office and Family Business Project
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the unique dynamics and challenges faced by family offices and family businesses. It offers a deep dive into the intricacies of managing and operating these specialized entities while emphasizing the importance of effective project management and problem-solving skills. It will be delivered through a combination of interactive discussions, data analysis, and hands-on project work. Students will gain practical experience by actively participating in planning and executing a real business project.

cilos.description: Gain a comprehensive understanding of family office and family business dynamics.
Apply theoretical knowledge and skills to analyze and solve real-life complex problems.

Identify opportunities and analyze operational challenges within family business and formulate effective strategies for improvement, considering the unique characteristics and complexities of family businesses.
Enhance project management capabilities in managing project timelines, resources and stakeholders.
Develop strong collaboration and teamwork skills to work with diverse perspectives effectively.

courses.title: Family Office and Family Business Practicum
courses.description: This course is a unique opportunity for students in the MSc in Family Office and Family Business program to gain practical experience and apply their knowledge in a professional setting. By completing the Practicum, students will be equipped with practical experience, enhanced professional skills, and a deeper understanding of the complexities and challenges of family office and family business management. Grade P or F.

cilos.description: Apply theoretical knowledge and skills acquired throughout the program to real-world family office and family business scenarios.
Demonstrate effective problem-solving, critical thinking, and communication skills in a professional setting.
Understand the complexities and challenges faced in family offices and family businesses and develop strategies to address them.
Reflect on their internship experiences and identify areas of personal and professional growth.
Integrate academic knowledge with practical experiences in real family office and family business scenarios.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Financial Technology.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: Global Leadership Development
courses.description: The course is designed to promote students' personal development, teamwork, communications skills, career preparation, leadership capability, and a global mindset. For GBUS students only. Grade PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of personal strengths, leadership styles to determine areas for growth as a global business.
Identify key principles of effective professional communication and their role in global business environments.
Develop career skillsets by identifying global opportunities and aligning professional goals with market trends.

courses.title: Global Business Analysis
courses.description: This course develops students' proficiency in business analysis by building competence in using fundamental tools for business problem solving and delivering professional presentations. For GBUS students or students with consent from the instructor.

cilos.description: Identify basic skills required to solve common business problems.
Apply a structured approach to problem-solving.
Describe the appropriate fact-based analysis tools, such as modeling technique.
Develop and deliver a clear, fact-based business recommendation using PowerPoint, supported by a logical storyline and high-quality charts.
Demonstrate effective teamwork skills by collaborating with peers.

courses.title: From Zero to Exit – Journey of A Start-up
courses.description: This course is designed for students who are interested in starting a business or working for an entrepreneurial company. Students are expected to understand the opportunities and challenges of a start-up journey, from coming up with their own start up idea to incepting the idea, pitching for funding and to growing their own start-up. At the end of the course, they will be equipped with the skills and knowledge necessary to kick start their business as an entrepreneur. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. For GBUS students only.

cilos.description: Analyze start-up ecosystems and evaluate the dynamic challenges faced by founders.
Evaluate key aspects of entrepreneurial ventures—particularly technology ventures—from both buy-side and sell-side perspectives.
Demonstarte broad understanding of core business functions and practices, those not typically covered by academic curriculum.
Apply critical and creative thinking to make effective decisions supported by analytical techniques.
Demonstarte resilient by constructively handling objetcion and rejection.

courses.title: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Corporate Project
courses.description: This is a required course for Global Business students that aims to cultivate students’ interest and commitment in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG). In this course, students will work with organizations (e.g., non-governmental organizations (NGO) or small and medium enterprise (SME)) to explore ESG initiatives and strategies. This course takes an experiential learning approach that allows students to apply their business knowledge and skill in helping organizations address pressing ESG needs so as to generate value and effect positive changes. For GBUS students. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand and analyze ESG needs and issues from various stakeholders’ perspectives.
Design appropriate initiatives or strategies to address organizations’ ESG-related needs.
Work effectively in teams and with organization executives in ESG projects.

courses.title: Blue Ocean Strategy Innovation and Execution
courses.description: This course introduces students to Blue Ocean Strategy, one of the most original ways of developing innovative strategy to appear in business thinking in recent years. This approach to strategy innovation distinguishes between the conventional cutthroat way most companies compete based on price and product features, known as the red ocean, and a new way of competing that emphasizes finding new markets that are free of competition – blue oceans. The course equips students with a set of highly practical tools that can be used in any organization both to develop strategic innovation and then to implement this change successfully. For GBUS students only.

cilos.description: Analyze and gain insights from case studies from well-known global companies that illustrate the Blue Ocean approach in a stimulating way.
Develop a practical set of tools for building and implementing innovative strategies.
Develop a highly relevant approach to lead significant change in teams or organizations.
Apply the tools learned in the course to real-world scenarios and become familiar with their use and application.

courses.title: Global Perspectives on Contemporary Issues
courses.description: This course aims to develop students' capacity for critical reflection.  To deal with human interactions in a global setting, we need to equip ourselves with a spectrum of understanding and responses that go beyond our parochial mind-set.  The course exposes students to issues outside the business field, providing an opportunity to explore relevant topics concerning their community, their world and themselves.  For GBUS students or students with consent from instructor.

cilos.description: Demonstarte a well-developed awareness of major political, economic, social and ethical issues that are relevant to anyone operating in the global environment.
Formulate and communicate their views on these issues in a clear and persuasive manner.
Develop and present convincing arguments in a debating environment.
Experience how to collaborate successfully and effectively with newly-formed teams.
Understand how to give and receive feedback and learn from others.
Critically reflect on their own perceptions and mindset and demonstarte a willingness to adapt or change these.

courses.title: Global Business Case Studies
courses.description: This is an advanced case studies course that develops students' proficiency in conducting business problem solving and presentations under conditions simulating real business settings. For GBUS students or students with consent from the instructor.

cilos.description: Apply a structured approach to problem-solving, as used in top management consulting companies.
Develop and deliver a clear, fact-based business recommendation using PowerPoint, supported by a logical storyline and high-quality charts.
Deliver profesional presentation and improve skills by incorporating feedback from peers and instructors.
Demonstarte effective collaboration skills in a team settings.
Apply business judgment to new situations.

courses.title: Business and ESG Management for Asia and Emerging Markets
courses.description: This course intends to develop a deep understanding of the contextual factors of Asia and emerging market countries, with a specific emphasis on the risks, challenges, and mitigants to doing business in these countries. In studying key business, political, economic, social, financial, and cultural characteristics of these countries, students will recognize regional differences and learn to develop relevant business strategies. Students will also explore how country differences impact business strategies and managerial decision-making. In addition, concepts that relate to corruption, corporate governance, and ESG will be covered. For GBUS students or students with instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Communicate ideas persuasively to inform and convince others.

Demonstrate an understanding into the drivers of business decision making in Asia and the role played by managers in ensuring the integrity of the firm and maintaining appropriate levels of environment, social and corporate responsibility via case practice.
Demonstrate the ability to derive and evaluate entry and market segmentation strategies in emerging markets and understand the impact of business model in marketing decisions via case practice.
Develop their “business sense” in the solution of practical business problems in real world settings.
Apply their understanding of ethical behavior to the solution of real-world business problems.
Collaborate positively by actively seeking, and engaging in discussion of, the views of others while showing sensitivity to opposing views.
Contribute to the successful and timely completion of a group project in line with their roles in teams.
Approach business problems from alternative perspectives and with unconventional concepts or solutions.

courses.title: Deal Making in Asia and Emerging Markets
