courses.title: Responsible Conduct of Biomedical and Biotechnology Research
courses.description: This course will present some of the most common ethical issues encountered in biomedical research and biotechnology. Students will engage in active discussion to provide deeper understanding of each issue. The objective of this course is to raise awareness of the ethical issues around biomedical/bioengineering research, and encourage critical and responsible consideration of research conduct. Topics covered will fall into three categories: 1) Research integrity, 2) Applied ethics in biological research and biotechnology, and 3) Contemporary ethical issues arisen from emerging biotechnologies. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Describe potential important ethical issues that biomedical researchers may face in their careers.
When presented with a case or specific scenario, identify the explicit or potential ethical issues, arguments, and perspectives arising from the case or scenario.
Critically analyze and evaluate ethical issues revolving around contemporary biomedical/life science research in a contextual manner, and form and justify their own position on these ethical issues.
Recall and describe key principles, policies, and regulations relevant to the ethical and responsible conduct of research (e.g. Nuremberg Code).
Identify administrative or other resources on campus that researchers can access to seek assistance with ethical issues they may be facing.
Communicate and present ideas to others in a clear and critical manner about complex issues, both in presentation and written format.
Engage in open and thoughtful discussions with peers on complex ethical issues.

courses.title: Workshops in Biosciences
courses.description: Laboratory exercises, including recombinant DNA technology, protein purification, microscopy, tissue culture and other technologies currently in use.

cilos.description: Acquire knowledge of experimental technologies.
Analyze and interpret numerical data and demonstrate proficiency in selected modern technology for life science .
Formulate  questioning in a practical settings.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Structural Biology
courses.description: This postgraduate course offers an in-depth exploration of structural biology for students interested in understanding the intricate relationship between molecular structure and biological function. Students will engage with fundamental concepts, advanced techniques, and current research topics in the field. In addition to theoretical knowledge, the course emphasizes practical skills through hands-on sessions with software programs like Chimera and PyMOL. Students will learn how to visualize molecular structures and create publication-quality figures and videos, essential tools for effective scientific communication.

cilos.description: Have a comprehensive understanding of structural biology principles and their applications in research for advanced studies and professional opportunities in the field.
Read structural biology papers with a critical eye.
Present structural biology results in publication quality.

courses.title: Biochemical and Molecular Basis of Diseases
courses.description: Advanced topics on the biochemical basis of human diseases, molecular medicine and structure based drug design; an oral presentation and a written essay on a specific topic are required.

cilos.description: Recognize the molecular mechanism underling certain human diseases.
Apply knowledge from modern biomedical sciences to evaluate current treatments and envision potential future treatments.

courses.title: Biostatistics: Theory and Application in Life Science Research
courses.description: Statistical analysis has become an essential component in research for testing hypothesis and designing experiments. This course is tailored to postgraduate students in Life Science. We will introduce common methodologies used in research, such as ANOVA, linear regression, nonparametric methods, and bootstrapping. The students will also gain practical skills of using R for analysis.

cilos.description: Translate scientific questions into appropriate statistical models and hypothesis.
Perform statistical analysis using R given experimental data.
Interpret analysis results in the scientific context.
Determine the power of hypothesis testing and use it to guide experimental design.
Develop statistical thinking and describe the basic theories, potential pitfalls, and limitations of main methods.

courses.title: Cellular Regulation
courses.description: Molecular basis of cellular regulation. Cellular signal transduction cascades.

cilos.description: Identify the latest concepts in selected cellular processes and the basic mechanisms underlying these processes.
Recognize how new discoveries can improve ways to treat different diseases.
Apply the knowledge learnt in the course to problem solving in their own research.

courses.description: This course includes selected topics of current interest in Life Science which are not covered by existing courses. Credit to be determined on case by case basis based on workload. May be repeated for credit, if different topics are covered. Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental knowledge of the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

cilos.description: Prepare effectively abstracts announcing a scientific presentation.
Give formal research seminars of their own research topic in an organized and rational manner.
Develop efficient presentation and communication skills.
Identify the latest development in different research areas of Life Science.
Critically analyze data on other research presentations and provide constructive suggestion to speakers.

courses.title: Molecular Medicine
courses.description: This joint course offered under the HKU-CUHK-HKUST Centre for Advanced Study will give an introduction to basic concepts as well as modern techniques and technologies in Molecular Medicine. Cancer as well as neurodegenerative diseases will be used as disease models in most of the examples covered in the course. Classes will be held in the campus of the university concerned for that part of the course offered.

cilos.description: Obtain basic knowledge of chromosomal abnormalities in tumour cells, methods for detection and their clinical significance.
Discuss the genetic basis of cancer and implications for clinical diagnosis, prognostication and disease monitoring.
Special topics in neuroscience/cancer biology: to focus on neuronal signaling and neurodegenerative diseases, and cell cycle control.
Cell signaling: to discuss the concept and techniques used in signal transduction study and its connection with cancer.
To obtain basic knowledge in molecular diagnostics.
To obtain basic concepts on the design of molecular medicine studies, including statistical considerations.
To obtain basic knowledge on high throughput molecular technologies, including those used in proteomics and the mass spectrometric analysis of nucleic acids.

courses.title: Frontiers in Nucleic Acid Research
courses.description: This course will cover the biogenesis and function of non-coding RNAs, drawn from molecular, biochemical and cell biological studies. Dysfunction of non-coding RNA in disease and the application of non-coding RNA as research tools will be discussed.

cilos.description: Explain how diverse classes of non-coding RNA were discovered and characterized.
Explain how biological processes can be regulated by non-coding RNA.
Critically assess the scientific literature in writing.
Critically review and present scientific literature in oral presentations.
Develop experiments concerning the use or characterization of non-coding RNA in biological studies.

courses.title: Mathematical Analysis and Its Applications I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to analysis and its applications. Countable and uncountable sets, metrics, norms, open sets, closed sets, continuity, homeomorphisms, connectedness, complete metric spaces, totally bounded sets, fixed points, compact metric spaces, uniform continuity, category, the Baire Category Theorem, sequences of functions, pointwise and uniform convergence, the space of bounded functions.

cilos.description: Analyze if a given set is countable or uncountable, construct bijections between two sets, and analyze the cardinality of the Cantor set.

Analyze if a function defined on a set is a metric or a norm, analyze if a sequence in a metric or norm space converges, determine whether or not two metrics or two norms are equivalent, analyze if a metric space is of the second category, and apply the Baire Category Theorem in different contexts.
Analyze if a given subset of a metric space is open or closed, compact, connected, totally bounded, and construct the relative metric.

Analyze if a given mapping from a metric space into another metric space is continuous and uniformly continuous by using different continuity characterizations, and determine if a given map is a homeomorphism.
Analyze if a metric space is complete by using nested set theorem and Balzono-Weierstrass Theorem.
Apply fixed point theorem in the context of differential equations.

courses.title: Applications of Geometry and Analysis
courses.description: This course will show how mathematical analysis can be used to investigate a variety of physical phenomena. Kepler's laws of planetary motion will be derived from Newton's law gravitation. Further topics will be the use of differential geometry, in particular Gaussian curvature, in describing space curves and surfaces. Additional topics will be other historically important uses of differential equations, Fourier series and harmonic analysis.

cilos.description: Formulate the quantities that describe space curves.
Present standard examples of curves that are interesting in high school education.
Formulate a curve as the motion of a point particle.
Formulate the quantities that describe surfaces.
Present standard examples of surfaces that are interesting in high school education.
Formulate arc-length in the language of Riemannian metrics.
Formulate the use of normal vectors and curvature in the description of surfaces.
Apply the theory of curves, and  surfaces to physical problems.

courses.title: Complex Analysis for Mathematics Educators
courses.description: This course is about analysis of functions in a complex variable. Topics include holomorphic functions, line integrals in the complex plane, Cauchy integral formula, isolated singularities, Taylor series and Laurent series, residues, conformal mappings, Weierstrass factorization, and the Riemann Zeta function. Applications of these ideas will lead to a broader and deeper understanding about topics in secondary school mathematics, including plane geometry, roots of polynomials, trigonometry, evaluation of series and integrals, and the study of prime numbers.

cilos.description: Describe the geometry and topology of various sets in the complex plane.
Analyze continuous functions in the complex domain, and solve problems involving continuity and approximation.
Identify holomorphic functions in the complex domain, and characterize these functions using the Cauchy-Riemann equations.
Compute line integrals of complex functions and Laurent series of meromorphic functions, and explain these computations clearly using concepts from complex analysis.
Justify the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra using complex analysis, and explain its implication about roots of polynomials.
Evaluate integrals using the residue theory.
Explain the construction of the Riemann Zeta function, and its relationship with the study of prime numbers.

courses.title: Classical and Abstract Algebra
courses.description: This is a course which develops the rigorous definition of real and complex numbers, and various aspects of polynomials.

cilos.description: Use Peano axioms to define natural numbers and their arithmetic rigorously.
Use the method of Dedekind cuts to rigorously define the field of real numbers.
Define complex numbers and apply them to algebraic and geometric problems.
Describe the connection between polynomials and geometric objects defined by them.
Work with various special polynomials and show a variety of their applications.

courses.title: Algebra and Its Applications I
courses.description: This course reviews the notion of groups, rings and homomorphisms and quotient constructions. Applications are then described for finite fields and number theory, and coding theory.

cilos.description: Formulate precisely the mathematical axioms which a group (and ring) must satisfy.
Derive certain more advanced properties of groups and rings from the axioms.
Identify when a group or ring occurs in a physical or mathematical situation, and infer useful information based on properties satisfied by groups and rings.
Apply algebraic concepts to organize and solve problems.
Explain how abstract algebra is used to solve certain classical questions of geometry and algebra.
Explain how abstract algebra is used to prove certain number theory results, and how these results are used for encryption purposes in modern day communications.

courses.title: Classical and Modern Geometry
courses.description: This course is about important ideas in the development of geometry. Topics include logic and axiomatic system, projective geometry, Hilbert’s axioms, hyperbolic models, geometric transformations, hyperbolic trigonometry.

cilos.description: Explain the axiomatic nature of Euclid’s Elements and its shortcomings and show how Hilbert's axioms provide a rigorous foundation for Euclidean geometry.
Formulate the parallel postulate and explain its role in the development of hyperbolic geometry.
Use geometric transformations to characterize various geometries.
Use hyperbolic trigonometry to study various properties of hyperbolic geometry.

courses.title: Combinatorics
courses.description: Topics in combinatorics including counting combinations and counting permutations, generating functions, and enumerative combinatorics. Inclusion-exclusion principle, Polya’s theory of counting, graph theory and applications.

cilos.description: Explain the reasons behind combinatorial principles and applications.
Design combinatorial problems using the principles taught in class.
Present projects related to certain theorems or problems in combinatorics.
Construct problems to show the usefulness of the principles for teaching purposes.

courses.title: Methodology of Mathematics
courses.description: This course is about mathematical thinking in mathematics. One purpose is to show how mathematical concepts, terminologies, formulas, equations, and theories are developed through examples of calculus, analysis, algebra, geometry, combinatorics, and probability, etc. The other purpose is to provide a global picture of mathematics by discussing its foundations, structures, internal relations, crises, and envisions. It is a combination of history, pedagogy, methodology, and philosophy of mathematics.

cilos.description: Solve problems by the methods of induction, analogy and association.
Apply the methods of axiomatization/foundations of mathematics.
Explain and solve the classical three Greek math problems.
Apply the art of infinity -- the distinction between elementary math and advanced math.
Apply the methods of infinitesimal and integration – the foundation of differential and integral calculus.
Solve problems by the Relation Mapping Inversion Principle.
Analyze problems by the method of Simulation Principle.
Describe interesting stories, events, historic schools and philosophy of mathematics.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: This course illustrates how to use statistical and probabilistic techniques with an open source statistics package R to analyze data, especially in education.

cilos.description: Identify the core ideas on analyzing data.
Communicate effectively the statistical results to both lay and expert audiences utilizing appropriate information and suitable technology.
Apply rigorous, analytic and highly numerate methods to analyze and solve problems in daily life and at work.
Carry out objective analysis and prediction of quantitative information with independent judgement.

courses.title: Teaching Mathematics in the Digital Age
courses.description: This course is about the use of various digital tools to produce interactive teaching materials for mathematics and the pedagogical framework of designing mathematics lessons using digital tools that can enhance the effectiveness of students’ learning.

cilos.description: Apply the theoretical frameworks that guide the process of developing mathematics pedagogy using digital tools.
Use various e-learning tools to design effective mathematics lessons.
Convey fundamental concepts in geometry, calculus, algebra, and statistics with the help of digital tools.

courses.title: Pedagogy in Mathematics Teaching
courses.description: This course focuses on intricate teaching methods and best practices in mathematics education. It delves into effective teaching strategies, the application of advanced technology in mathematics instruction, current trends and challenges in mathematics education, and the integration of cultural diversity in the classroom. Designed for educators and those aspiring to specialize in mathematics education, this course aims to enhance their teaching proficiency. Upon completion, participants will have a full grasp of effective strategies for math instruction and will be equipped to design compelling math lessons for their students.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of historical and theoretical foundations in mathematics education.
Apply a range of effective teaching strategies and techniques that promote mathematical understanding, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Utilize various digital tools and resources to enhance student engagement and learning in mathematics.
Develop differentiated and inclusive learning experiences that cater to the diverse needs and abilities of students in the mathematics classroom.
Design and implement authentic formative and summative assessments to evaluate student progress and provide constructive feedback.
Critically analyze real-life teaching practices and integrate best practices observed in teaching practice videos.
Create well-structured, engaging, and inclusive mathematics lesson plans that incorporate effective teaching strategies, tools, and assessments.
Engage in continuous professional development, reflection, and collaboration, setting future goals for improvement in mathematics teaching practices.

courses.title: Problem Solving Strategies
courses.description: This course covers ways to teach strategies and techniques to students to solve mathematical problems as they appeared in mathematical competitions. It covers many techniques, including transformation methods for solving geometry problems, and graph theoretical methods for solving combinatorial problems.

cilos.description: Recognize various techniques to solve certain types of math problems.
Present solutions and compare the strength and weakness of the techniques.
Modify problems to create new problems.
Identify conditions in solving problems to investigate further applications.

courses.title: Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: This course introduces a selection of topics from interdisciplinary mathematics, which may include mathematical physics, mathematical biology, image processing, etc.

cilos.description: Apply theoretical knowledge, principles and techniques to mathematical physics, mathematical biology and traffic flows.
Recognize roles of mathematics in solving some mathematical physics, mathematical biology and traffic flows.
Apply various theorems to study ideal mathematical models, such as ideal 2-dimensional fluid flows, ideal electrostatic force fields, steady state temperature, etc.
Present solutions of some physical problems in a systematic way.

courses.title: Topics in Applied Mathematics for Mathematics Educators
courses.description: This course introduces a selection of topics in applied mathematics, which may include mathematical modelling, differential equations, data analysis and visualization, scientific computation, etc., and their connections with mathematical applications and pedagogy approaches.

cilos.description: Identify and appreciate the concepts, techniques and processes of mathematical modelling originated from secondary school Mathematics curriculum.
Appreciate and formulate the use of numerical methods in specific daily life scenarios.
Solve formulated mathematical problems with the aids of appropriate numerical methods and coding techniques.
Interpret the numerical results and compare the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches.
Present standard examples of mathematical modelling that are connected with secondary school Mathematics topics.
Design a method to improve the original technique or scientific model adopted.
Incorporate the mathematical ideas and IT tools into education activities and teaching.

courses.title: Scientific Computation
courses.description: This course introduces various case studies drawn from different areas of science to illustrate the use of computers as a problem-solving tool. Each integrates physical principles and mathematical models, as well as numerical techniques and computer implementations, into a coherent perspective.

cilos.description: Apply theoretical knowledge, principles and techniques to physical problems.
Recognize roles of mathematics in scientific computation.
Implement various numerical algorithms on computers and apply them to real life problems.
Present numerical output from a computer code in a systematic way.

courses.title: MSc Project
courses.description: In this course, the student will do a project in an area of mathematics or mathematics education under the guidance of a faculty member. The project either surveys a topic, develops teaching plans and materials, or describes an investigation completed by the student.

cilos.description: Explain advanced mathematical theories, concepts and principles using precise mathematical language, and identify the applications of this knowledge in different daily life scenarios.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work or relevant educational materials.
Apply a rigorous, logical and analytic approach to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Communicate mathematical concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.
Work effectively on a prescribed topic in mathematics or mathematics education, and show the capability of delivering presentations in front of professional teachers or scientific experts.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study of selected mathematical topic(s) under the supervision of a faculty member. Consent of instructor is required, and each student can only study this course for once.

cilos.description: Explain and apply mathematical knowledge of the selected topic(s) of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work.
Present findings and solutions in a systematic way.

courses.title: Future Educators Internship
courses.description: This course is specifically designed for aspiring educators, providing students with the opportunity to undertake internships in various school settings, including primary and secondary schools. Through hands-on teaching practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the roles and responsibilities of educators, explore their future career paths in education, and develop essential teaching skills and professional competencies. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Explain the connection between basic mathematics taught in secondary schools and more advanced mathematical concepts, fostering student understanding.
Apply problem-solving strategies pedagogically to enhance student engagement and understanding in secondary school mathematics.
Investigate and reflect on additional areas of mathematics and their applications to improve teaching practices and deepen subject knowledge.

courses.title: Stochastic Calculus
courses.description: Random walk models.  Filtration. Martingales.  Brownian motions.  Diffusion processes.  Forward and backward Kolmogorov equations.  Ito's calculus.  Stochastic differential equations.  Stochastic optimal control problems in finance.

cilos.description: Develop a rigorous probabilistic framework and lay a firm foundation for stochastic calculus.
Recognize the most important results, including Ito's Lemma, Girsanov change of measure.
Employ numerical PDE or Monte Carlo method to solve the stochastic differential equations.
Recognize the Black-Scholes models and more general diffusion models.
Apply the theory in stochastic calculus to financial problems, e.g. option pricing.

courses.title: Advanced Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Probability spaces, measurable functions and distributions, conditional probability, conditional expectations, asymptotic theorems, stopping times, martingales, Markov chains, Brownian motion, sampling distributions, sufficiency, statistical decision theory, statistical inference, unbiased estimation, method of maximum likelihood.

cilos.description: Recognize fundamental concept of randomness and analyze it using probability framework.
Recognize the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem and their applications.
Evaluate the statistical procedure of data analysis.
Formulate the basic statistical problems from one sample problem to linear regression.
Apply methodology of statistical inference to solve practical problems.

courses.title: Quantitative Modeling of Derivatives Securities
courses.description: Forward, futures contracts and options. Static and dynamical replication. Arbitrage pricing. Binomial option model. Brownian motion and Ito's calculus. Black-Scholes-Merton model. Risk neutral pricing and martingale pricing methodology. General stochastic asset-price dynamics. Monte Carlo methods. Exotic options and American options.

cilos.description: Formulate and evaluate pricing models for derivatives.
Analyze effectiveness of hedging strategies for monitoring risks in derivatives.
Make appraisal of the dynamics of stock prices and commodity prices.
Provide solution using structural derivatives in wealth management.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Fixed-Income Instruments
courses.description: Bonds and bond yields. Bond markets. Bond portfolio management. Fixed-income derivatives markets. Term structure models and Heath-Jarrow-Morton framework for arbitrage pricing. Short-rate models and lattice tree implementations. LIBOR Market models. Hedging. Bermudan swaptions and Monte Carlo methods. Convexity adjustments. Mortgage-backed securities. Asset-backed securities. Collateralized debt obligations.

cilos.description: Describe the operation of fixed-income markets and the roles of the fixed-income derivative.
Apply major mathematical tools for fixed-income modeling.
Formulate major classes of fixed-income models and apply them for fixed-income pricing and risk management.
Evaluate the effectiveness of popular models for different sectors of derivatives.
Analyze exotic derivatives and choose pricing models.

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis of Financial Time Series
courses.description: Analysis of asset returns: autocorrelation, predictability and prediction. Volatility models: GARCH-type models, long range dependence. High frequency data analysis: transactions data, duration. Markov switching and threshold models. Multivariate time series: cointegration models and vector GARCH models.

cilos.description: Recognize market indexes, financial time series and their features.
Recognize the foundation of time series and basic time series models.
Formulate time series models to study financial data, including market returns and volatility.
Evaluate the relationships of different markets via the cointegration time series and ECM models.
Analyze the real financial data with the statistical techniques from this course via a course project.

courses.title: Statistical Methods in Quantitative Finance
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to statistical models used in financial data analysis. Students learn about various basic and advanced regression models, and techniques of data analysis. These statistical methods are applied in quantitative finance, including portfolio theory, asset pricing models and risk management.

cilos.description: Apply data analysis and statistical inference in financial applications.
Formulate the construction of the factor models and apply them in asset management and other applications.
Perform statistical analysis of investment models.
Analyze financial problems using the Bayesian methods and nonlinear regression models.
Evaluate the effectiveness of statistical trading strategies.
Design and evaluate statistical models of risk management and their implementation.

courses.title: Mathematical Models of Investment
courses.description: Utility theory, stochastic dominance.  Portfolio analysis: mean-variance approach, one-fund and two-fund theorems.  Capital asset pricing models.  Arbitrage pricing theory.  Consumption-investment problems.

cilos.description: Apply investment models in financial applications.
Formulate quantitative investment with Mean-Variance Optimization and Black-Litterman models.
Analyze equity valuation using asset pricing models.
Evaluate the effectiveness of investment strategies.
Design and implement asset management strategies and structured solutions.

courses.title: Quantitative Risk Management
courses.description: Nature of risk and risk measures. Reduced form models including Hazard rates and calibration, Exponential models of defaults and Contagion models. Mixture models including Bernoulli mixture models and CreditRisk+ models. Structural models including Merton model and mKMV, CreditMetrics and Gaussian copula, Vasicek model and Hull-White model. Credit derivatives and counter party risks.

cilos.description: Analyze risk on derivatives and other financial products using quantitative and statistical methods.
Evaluate the price impact on financial products due to quantifiable risks.
Devise computer programs to compute the risk using numerical methods.
Analyze the capital requirements for financial institutions using quantitative and statistical methods.

courses.title: Software Development with C++ for Quantitative Finance
courses.description: This course introduces C++ with applications in derivative pricing.  Contents include abstract data types; object creation, initialization, and toolkit for large-scale component programming; reusable components for path-dependent options under the Monte Carlo framework.

cilos.description: Design and develop functions in C++ for financial applications.
Recognize the basic object oriented modeling and programming paradigm and its application on computational finance.
Translate financial models into C++ applications.
Handle the complexities in real world financial calculations.

courses.title: Mathematical Market Microstructure
courses.description: This course will study special classes of stochastic processes that can capture market behavior at micro level and their practical implications in algorithmic and low-latency trading. Topics covered include structural models of price formation process at microstructure level, information-based vs. inventory-based models, stochastic control and optimization in trading, and real time risk management.

cilos.description: Apply mathematical theory of market microstructure in trading risk management.
Conduct data analysis with computer programming languages such as R and/or Python.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as tick market data and trading data).
Draw meaningful implications to capture market behavior at micro level in algorithmic and low-latency trading.
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world trading applications.

courses.title: Financial Markets in Hong Kong and China
courses.description: The ﬁnancial reforms in China have offered vast opportunities for companies to tap the onshore and offshore markets in financing, investment and risk management. This course introduces cross-border channels, structure products, and other emerging mechanisms for fund raising and risk hedging in Hong Kong and China. It also covers analyses of market players and the impacts on capital raising, investment strategies and FX hedging. Relevant current events and landmark deals are examined to illustrate teaching points.

cilos.description: Apply financial mathematical models in studying capital market transactions, especially for markets in greater China region.
Analyze cross-border financial transactions with real industry data at both macro- and micro-levels.
Apply risk models to assess and hedge currency exposure (in particular RMB/RMH).
Draw meaningful implications to tap the market opportunities in both onshore and offshore markets in financing, investment and risk management.
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world finance applications.

courses.title: Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application
courses.description: This course delves into the realm of portfolio optimization, from Markowitz's foundational mean - variance formulation to modern extensions such as robust portfolios, risk parity portfolios, CVaR portfolios, high-order portfolios, index tracking, and pairs trading, among others. It bridges rigorous mathematical formulations with practical numerical algorithms, with special emphasis on convex optimization methods. Each week is devoted to a specific topic, during which the theory is first presented, followed by hands-on implementation in Python/R.

cilos.description: Formulate portfolio optimization problems — from mean–variance to CVaR, risk parity, index tracking, and robust portfolios — within a convex optimization framework.
Implement and solve portfolio optimization methods in Python/R using both general-purpose solvers and tailored numerical algorithms.
Design and execute realistic backtesting strategies to evaluate portfolio performance with real market price data.
Critically assess the practical limitations of portfolio models and adapt formulations to handle real-world complexities.
Conduct independent research on a portfolio optimization topic and present the findings.

courses.title: Structured Products: Analysis and Pricing
courses.description: Structured solutions including payoff design / packaging / distribution / pricing / hedging / funding; The popular structures in practice across the asset classes (Equity, Funds, FX, Interest Rate, Credit and Commodities); The customized index business based on factors, portfolio theory and other trading models with up-to-date industry practices; Computational methods for derivatives and structured products, including lattice tree methods, finite difference approach for PDE, multi-dimensional and American Monte Carlo simulation.

cilos.description: Design computer algorithms for pricing structured derivatives.
Devise and compute hedging strategies for monitoring risks in derivatives.
Construct numerical algorithms for performing model calibration in pricing models of financial derivatives.
Provide solution using structural derivatives in wealth management.

courses.title: Machine Learning and Its Applications
courses.description: This course is designed for those who are interested in learning from data. It emphasizes the seamless integration of models and algorithms for real applications. Topics include linear methods for regression and classification, tree-based methods, kernel methods, expectation and maximization algorithm, variational auto-encoder, and generative adversarial networks. This course aims to make connections among these topics rather than treating them separately, laying a solid foundation for machine learning and its applications.

cilos.description: Describe and explain machine learning methods.
Conduct data analysis with computer programming languages such as R and/or Python.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data).
Interpret the data analysis results.
Derive machine learning algorithms.

courses.title: Computing for Finance in Python
courses.description: This course teaches Python programming techniques with a strong focus on using mini-projects with industry backgrounds in trading, aiming to equip students with solid program-solving skills in the following contexts: medium- and high-frequency multi-factor model development, OTC trading system development with block-chain technology applied, abnormal trading behavior detection, trading simulator design and development.

cilos.description: Apply mathematical theories to derive trading algorithms and implement using Python.
Conduct data analysis using Python.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data).
Draw meaningful implications to capture market behaviors in trading.
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world trading applications.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning with Financial Applications
courses.description: With the application of artificial intelligence (AI) growing rapidly in finance industries and related sectors, this course introduces the use of reinforcement learning techniques in financial applications. Topics include finite action space and finite state space problem, classical RL algorithms, Q learning, policy gradient methods, and deep Q learning.

cilos.description: Apply mathematical theories to derive models of reinforcement learning in finance applications.
Apply programming techniques in implementing the reinforcement learning models.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data).
Draw meaningful implications to capture market behaviors in trading.
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world trading applications.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship in Fintech
courses.description: The course covers how to identify and evaluate business opportunities in the fintech context, formulate the business model and strategy, and how to raise venture capital (VC). The financial issues confronting fintech startups are different from traditional financing approaches. The course will discuss in detail on preparing an effective pitch deck, the key terms of VC financing, and initial public offering (IPO).

cilos.description: Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in emerging trading applications and finance technologies.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data and market data).
Apply financial mathematical theories to assess the values for fintech startups and new ventures.
Draw meaningful implications to capture market behaviors and make forecasting.
Develop an effective pitch deck and present to VC investors.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Fintech
courses.description: By providing opportunities for hands-on experimentation with machine learning applications, the course aims to inspire students to devise innovative approaches to address real-life problems in Fintech using readily-available artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. This course offers a comprehensive exploration of the fundamental concepts and underlying principles of AI. It delves into the core principles of machine learning and provides valuable insights through case studies of relevant technologies.

cilos.description: Understand AI principles: statistics, optimization.
Apply programming techniques in implementing AI models.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data).
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world applications.
Draw meaningful implications from research and analysis.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Financial Mathematics
courses.description: In this course, financial firms will be invited to offer projects covering a broad range of essential topics for the training of professionals in quantitative finance. The capstone projects involve a combination of quantitative skills (e.g., mathematical models, statistical analysis, machine learning techniques, etc.) and emerging technologies adopted in the field of financial mathematics. Students will be working in a group of 2 to 4 to complete a project. The normal duration of a project is one regular term.

cilos.description: Develop and evaluate quantitative models/strategies for emerging financial technologies.
Perform effective scenario simulations using statistical techniques in financial mathematics.
Program and develop applications for analysis of financial data and design numerical methods for calibration of model parameters from market data.
Analyze problems from finance in quantitative terms and develop strategies for effective solution of the problems.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Financial Mathematics II
courses.description: In this course, financial firms will be invited to offer projects covering a broad range of essential topics for the training of professionals in quantitative finance. The capstone projects involve a combination of quantitative skills (e.g., mathematical models, statistical analysis, machine learning techniques, etc.) and emerging technologies adopted in the field of financial mathematics. Students will be working in a group of 2 to 4 to complete a project. The normal duration of a project is one regular term.

cilos.description: Develop and evaluate quantitative models/strategies for emerging financial technologies.
Perform effective scenario simulations using statistical techniques in financial mathematics.
Program and develop applications for analysis of financial data and design numerical methods for calibration of model parameters from market data.
Analyze problems from finance in quantitative terms and develop strategies for effective solution of the problems.

courses.title: Special Topics in Financial Mathematics
courses.description: Selected special topics in Financial Mathematics of current interest but not covered by existing courses.

cilos.description: Identify and apply the theories and methods related to the course topic.
Recognize the major issues and updated development in the area of the course topic.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation in the financial industries.

courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: Completion of an independent project under the supervisor of a faculty in financial mathematics or statistics.  Scope may include (i) identifying a non-reference problem and proposing the methods of solution, (ii) acquiring a specific research skill.

cilos.description: Critically analyze a selected topic to identify and formulate practical problems in financial mathematics.
Recognize the key issues analyzed in the models and their limitations.
Design effective analytical and computational solution methodologies to solve the formulated models.
Provide quantitative interpretations of various financial phenomena in the formulated problems from the numerical results.
Communicate solution concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.

courses.title: Programming for Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course covers advanced programming skills for artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Students will learn to use popular AI libraries such as NumPy, Matplotlib, and Pandas, as well as deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch. Topics covered include data manipulation, visualization, and building neural networks. Prior experience in object-oriented programming is required.

cilos.description: Develop advanced programming skills, including the ability to manipulate and analyze large datasets, visualize data, and build and train neural network models.
Gain proficiency in using popular AI libraries and frameworks.
Learn how to deploy AI models for real-world applications.

courses.title: AI Fundamentals: Concepts and Methods
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of both the theoretical and practical foundations of artificial intelligence. Students will gain an understanding of fundamental concepts and methods in key AI subfields such as search algorithms, logic, knowledge representation, machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, sequential decision-making, and probabilistic reasoning. The course aims to equip students with the necessary knowledge to pursue more advanced AI courses.

cilos.description: Identify real-world problems where artificial intelligence techniques can be applied and propose appropriate solutions.
Apply a wide range of artificial intelligence techniques to solve problems.
Design intelligent systems that can learn from experience and make decisions based on data.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics
courses.description: This course delves into the ethical considerations involved in designing, developing, and deploying artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Students will investigate the societal impacts of AI and the ethical dilemmas that emerge in areas such as privacy, bias, transparency, and accountability. Through case studies and discussions, students will build a framework for ethical decision-making in the development and implementation of AI systems.

cilos.description: Identify ethical issues that arise in the design, development, and use of artificial intelligence systems.
Evaluate the fairness and bias of artificial intelligence systems and propose ways to mitigate these issues.
Analyze the impact of artificial intelligence on society and the workforce and propose ethical guidelines for its development and deployment.
Develop ethical frameworks for the governance and regulation of artificial intelligence.

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: This course presents the fundamental techniques for designing efficient computer algorithms, proving their correctness, and analyzing their running times. General topics include mathematical analysis of algorithms (summations and recurrences), advanced data structures (balanced search trees), algorithm design techniques (divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, and greedy algorithms), graph algorithms (breadth-first and depth-first search, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths).

cilos.description: Describe fundamental concepts and techniques for determining the asymptotic behavior of real-valued functions defined in natural numbers.
Explain recurrence equations and solve common recurrences using a variety of techniques.
Analyze an algorithm described in plain language or some form of pseudocode in terms of its time (or space) efficiency as a function of the size of a problem instance.
Explain how various data structures, including trees, heaps and disjoint set structures, influence the time efficiency of algorithms.
Apply general algorithmic design and analysis techniques to solving problems, including greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic programming.
Identify randomization in algorithms and analyze basic randomized algorithms such as randomized quicksort and selection.

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the foundation of computation, and aims at answering some of the most fundamental questions in computer science: What is an algorithm? What can and cannot be computed at all? What can and cannot be computed efficiently? The topics covered include set theory and countability, formal languages, finite automata and regular languages, pushdown automata and context-free languages, Turing machines, undecidability, P and NP, NP-completeness.

cilos.description: Develop advanced programming skills, including the ability to manipulate and analyze large datasets, visualize data, and build and train neural network models.
Prove the equivalence of DFA, NFA, regular expressions and the equivalence of PDA and CFG.
Design finite automata and write regular expressions for regular languages.
Write context-free grammar (CFG) for context-free languages, especially for expressions occurring in programming languages.
Design pushdown automata for context-free languages, and given a context-free grammar, construct a PDA that accepts the language generated by the given grammar.

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: This course offers an extensive overview of traditional and contemporary machine learning paradigms and computational techniques. Learners will delve into the theoretical underpinnings of machine learning and acquire practical skills through engaging in software development projects. The curriculum encompasses both supervised and unsupervised learning methodologies to address a diverse array of machine learning challenges. Additionally, students will be trained in the assessment and selection of suitable machine learning models and will be equipped to implement these strategies to tackle real-world issues.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of the theoretical foundations of representative machine learning models and algorithms for different learning paradigms.
Apply machine learning models and algorithms to solve real-world problems.
Evaluate the performance of machine learning models and algorithms using appropriate metrics and techniques.
Design and implement machine learning models and algorithms for various application sectors.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: This course is designed to offer a comprehensive grasp of machine learning strategies tailored for natural language processing, along with their utilization in artificial intelligence contexts. Learners will be equipped to construct and refine an array of machine learning models to address a variety of natural language processing objectives, including sentiment analysis, text categorization, and linguistic translation. A foundational understanding of Python programming and machine learning principles is a prerequisite for this course.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of natural language processing and its applications in the field of artificial intelligence.
Gain proficiency in building and training popular machine learning models for a wide range of natural language processing tasks.
Integrate conventional and machine learning techniques to solve natural language processing problems in real-world applications.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement natural language processing systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.description: This course offers a thorough comprehension of the machine learning methodologies utilized in computer vision, along with their relevance in artificial intelligence contexts. Participants will be trained in the construction and education of various machine learning models tailored for diverse computer vision objectives, such as image segmentation, object recognition, and the creation of visual content. A prerequisite for this course is familiarity with Python programming and foundational knowledge in machine learning.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of computer vision and its applications in the field of artificial intelligence.
Gain proficiency in building and training popular machine learning models for a wide range of computer vision tasks.
Integrate conventional and machine learning techniques to solve computer vision problems in real-world applications.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement computer vision systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Generative Al and Large Language Models
courses.description: This course aims to explore the fast-evolving technologies behind generative Al and large language models. Students will gain a deep understanding of the core concepts and techniques for training these models, as well as practical skills in using them effectively through prompting and integration into broader AI systems. Prior experience in Python programming and machine learning is necessary.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental concepts of generative Al and large language models.
Interact effectively with large language and multimodal models through prompting for a wide range of tasks in real-world applications.
Integrate generative Al into AI application development.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement generative AI systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Machine Learning System
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of the principles, methodologies, and technologies that form the backbone of machine learning systems. It covers essential aspects of building and optimizing these systems, with a balanced emphasis on both theoretical foundations and practical implementations. Throughout the course, we will delve into the design principles of these systems and explore the challenges and opportunities in creating future machine learning systems for next-generation applications and hardware platforms.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of machine learning system.
Design scalable and efficient systems for training and deploying machine learning models.
Implement machine learning systems using appropriate programming languages and frameworks.
Optimize computational resources and algorithms to improve the performance of machine learning systems.
Evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of machine learning systems using relevant metrics and benchmarks.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity
courses.description: This course aims to teach students using artificial intelligence (AI) to solve cybersecurity problems. Students will learn general principles in different cybersecurity domains, e.g., cybersecurity mindsets, cryptographic methods, software security, network security, and hardware security. Moreover, they will also learn how to effectively apply AI techniques to solve problems in cybersecurity domains and contexts.

cilos.description: Describe mainstream security issues in different computer systems and applications.
Use AI techniques to solve common security challenges and protect computer systems and applications.
Identify common security and privacy pitfalls in AI and technical solutions to harden AI systems.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to use AI techniques to solve cybersecurity problems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Me
courses.description: This course equips aspiring AI entrepreneurs with the essential skills to launch and sustain successful ventures. The course covers entrepreneurial mindset, business planning and development, technology as competitive advantages, financing and investment, and navigating operational, legal and other challenges, complemented by real-world case studies from Hong Kong and beyond. Additionally, students will develop exit strategies to ensure business viability.

cilos.description: Clearly formulate, articulate, and pitch a technology based startup business.
Identify the basic principles and practices involved in either starting a company or planning to work in an AI start-up company, and any pitfalls to be avoided.
Summarize the basic principles of AI entrepreneurship.
Recognize and act upon opportunities for building a personal business network.
Evaluate potential business opportunities and develop appropriate decision-making skills so as to take best advantage of those opportunities.

courses.title: Startup Seminars for AI
courses.description: This hands-on course explores the real-world challenges of launching an AI-driven startup through detailed case studies of both successful and failed ventures. Students will gain valuable insights into the key factors that determine startup outcomes. Interactive workshops will focus on Shanghai, covering local regulations, essential agencies and organizations. The curriculum combines open-format lectures with practical sessions to provide both theoretical knowledge and actionable skills. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyze an AI startup business to identify potential risks and opportunities.
Identify unique/novel elements of an idea/product based on patent searches.
Register an AI company.
Execute operational details related to setting up a start-up, including banking, personnel, accounting and tax.
Articulate the various government and non-government support structures in Shanghai area for a given area-focused startup.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This course covers selected topics in artificial intelligence and entrepreneurship that reflect recent developments not covered by existing MSc(AIE) courses. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Recognize the technical and business problems in a specific topic in artificial intelligence.
Identify key technical and business solutions to the problems in the topic.
Solve specific problems in the topic with responsible technical and business innovations.

courses.title: Innovation Management for AI
courses.description: This course aims to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of AI technology innovation management, leadership, and entrepreneurship. It delves into the intricacies of how AI technology innovation processes function, the strategies to effectively lead and manage these processes, and the methods to cultivate an environment that fosters and rewards innovation and entrepreneurial endeavors. Through a combination of seminars, interactive workshops and company visits, students will gain the essential knowledge and skills needed to drive AI innovation and entrepreneurial success in various organizational contexts. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Describe AI technology innovation management and techniques.
Identify and assess AI product market potential and conduct competitive analysis.
Describe leadership thoughts and behaviors, and steps to motivate teams to get results.
Identify the basics of AI product development and management.

courses.title: Internship and Entrepreneurship for AI
courses.description: Students will acquire and practice the project planning and reporting skills essential for completing a group project on a specific artificial intelligence (AI) topic relevant to the MSc(AIE) program. Students are required to complete a final report with oral examination on the final output from the internship or entrepreneurship project and whether the student indeed knows how to apply AI techniques to concrete applications. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Apply project planning and management skills effectively by taking into consideration the characteristics of AI projects.
Develop effective written and oral communication skills to facilitate interdisciplinary collaboration and project reporting.
Develop an understanding of ethical and legal issues in AI.
Demonstrate professionalism and integrity in AI system development.

courses.title: Marketing and Society
courses.description: This course will challenge the dynamics of marketing and the role it plays within a social, sustainable and ethical context in various industries. Current social issues affecting marketing decisions within the context of business strategy will be explored. Students will understand the dynamics of marketing decision-making and the impact these decisions have on society's well-being with a focus on sustainability. Students should be able to: (i) appreciate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level; (ii) identify/analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as advertising to children, addressing health and poverty issues, resource conservation, and climate change; (iii) critically evaluate the debates around the societal and ethical responsibilities of marketers; (iv) apply the above learning to real world cases. Students will gain the ability to apply basic theoretical and analytical frameworks to real world marketing problems and cases and reflect on their own behavior and experiences as consumers.

cilos.description: Identify and analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as social goods, health and poverty, resource conservation, climate change, consumerism, and conduct of societal marketing strategies and tactics

Identify, explain and evaluate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level as the organization deals with its triple bottom-line objective benefits to the consumer, benefits to the company/ organization, and benefits to the society in general
Discuss ways in which the issue of environmental sustainability becomes part of a marketer’s positioning strategy
Critically evaluate the debates around the ethical and social responsibilities of marketers to fulfill the triple bottom-line objectives
Explain and discuss application of societal and sustainable marketing strategies in real world cases and situation

courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.description: Introduction to marketing from the perspective of the decision-maker; controllable variables (product, price, promotion and distribution), uncontrollable variables (competition, law, society, technology, and economy), consumer behavior and marketing research.

cilos.description: Acquire an understanding of basic marketing concepts.
Understand the strategic role of marketing.
Describe elements of the marketing mix and explain how they contribute to marketing strategy.
Identify and address the key decisions facing marketing managers.
Analyze market data to identify opportunities, Formulate market strategy, and interpret their implications for strategic planning.
Demonstrate a global outlook and an understanding of cultural diversity.
Apply business concepts and theories to make proper business decisions in real-life settings.

courses.title: Marketing Research
courses.description: Basic research tools and procedures used in marketing research, and strategic uses of marketing research information in managerial decision making.

cilos.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of marketing research in improving marketing outcomes and explain the role of marketing research in segmentation, targeting, positioning, and other marketing functions.
Describe the process of conducting a marketing research project.
Develop research skills to conduct common types of market research.

courses.title: Promotion and Advertising Management
courses.description: Major aspects of promotion, with emphasis on advertising: setting of advertising objectives, strategies, tactics, choice of media, budget determination and measuring advertising effectiveness.

cilos.description: Acquire an understanding of the marketing communication process.
Understand the role of promotion and advertising in strategic marketing.
Analyze and evaluate the key issues involved in planning and assessing integrated marketing communications strategies.
Apply the appropriate theories and tools to plan, develop, and evaluate marketing communications.
Design and implement a strategic marketing communication campaign through applied, hands-on experience.
Apply business concepts and theories in making proper business decisions in real-life Settings.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior
courses.description: Psychological concepts such as perception, learning and motivation, sociological concepts such as reference groups, family and culture and theories of purchase decision processes underlying consumer buying behavior.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a thorough understanding of the mental processes that guide consumer perceptions, attitudes, memory, and choices.
Analyze how these processes might differ as a consequence of social, cultural, and group influences.
Apply this knowledge to generate integrated and effective marketing strategies and tactics.
Forumulate recommendations if needed for public policy to protect consumer rights.

courses.title: Global Marketing
courses.description: Understanding the formulation of international/multinational marketing strategy; factors influencing international trade, assessment of market potential, threats and opportunities in the international market environment, global marketing activities.

cilos.description: Analyze the global business environment—including economic, cultural, and legal-political factors—and apply these insights to the development of effective marketing strategies and tactics.
Assess and address the needs of global consumers.
Demonstarte an ability to prepare go-to-market strategies for new markets.
Develop targeting and positioning strategies in a global environment.
Develop and formulate global marketing mix strategies and tactics.
Understand the challenges of marketing operations in emerging markets.
Comprehend the role and impact of sustainability on global marketing operations.

courses.title: Retail management in the digital age
courses.description: This course explores the critical concepts and strategies that define the modern retail landscape. It examines the impact of technology on retail operations, consumer behavior, and market dynamics. Students will learn about emerging trends such as e-commerce, mobile shopping, and data analytics, while also gaining insights into effective merchandising, customer engagement, and supply chain management. Through case studies, interactive discussions, and hands-on projects, students will develop the skills needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving retail environment and understand how to meet the demands of today's tech-savvy consumers.

cilos.description: Understand the concept of retailing from a customer-centric perspective.
Analyze customers’ shopping behavior to inform retail strategies.
Develop effective retailing strategies based on consumer buying motivations.
Evaluate key topics such as in-store space management, pricing, and promotion.

Gain insights relevant to careers in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics. Explain and evaluate career opportunities in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics.

Build a foundational knowledge of merchandising, pricing, promotion, and site selection in retailing. Describe and explain the fundamental concepts of merchandising, pricing and promotion in retailing.

courses.title: Pricing Strategy
courses.description: This course is designed to deepen understanding of pricing issues which marketing managers may face under some degree of market power.  The course will develop basic pricing theories and concepts from economics and marketing and present managerial implications for decision making.

cilos.description: Apply the Value Based Pricing Framework to formulate pricing decisions.
Understand how to estimate consumers’ willingness to pay and its role in pricing decisions.
Explain the impact of psychological factors on consumers’ willingness to pay.
Understand the role of price segmentation in developing pricing strategies, such as promotions, versioning, bundling, and subscriptions.
Understand the role and effectiveness of innovative pricing strategies, such as revenue management, freemiums, and online auctions.
Understand the role of ethics and legal issues in pricing decisions.

courses.title: Business to Business Marketing
courses.description: The fundamental character of business markets and the decision-making nature of organizational customers; different approaches to business marketing, as typified in the relationships between buyers and sellers, and built around the concept of value; current trends changing the face of business-to-business marketing; critical analysis and problem-solving with respect to business market management.

cilos.description: Understand the nature, structure, and distinguishing characteristics of business-to-business markets.
Develop and apply a framework to analyse organizational buying behavior across commercial, enterprises (large and small) as well as government, and institutional buyers.
Apply demand analysis and segmentation techniques to the business market.
Develop effective sales and marketing strategies and tactics in product and service management, pricing, promotion, distribution, and sales to take advantage of business marketing opportunities.

courses.title: Digital Marketing
courses.description: Digital Marketing has reshaped the consumer landscape, and it is offering business new challenges and opportunities. In this course, students will learn important concepts related to digital marketing, factors that facilitate effective digital marketing initiative, and a consumer-centric approach to develop marketing plans. Students will also have hands-on experiences with web analytics and other real-life examples.

cilos.description: Develop theoretical basis for digital consumer behavior.
Understand the key characteristics digital environment to develop insights for yourself as a marketer, but also as a consumer.
Acquire hands-on experience using web analytics tools for data-driven marketing.
Develop skills to visualize and present analytical results.
Learn how to develop a digital marketing strategy based on real-life examples.
Familiarize yourself to opportunities and challenges offered by new marketing channels.
Utilize generative AI and latest technology for marketing campaigns.

courses.title: Marketing Analytics
courses.description: This course develops the foundation and integrated framework for understanding marketing analytics. It introduces major applications of data analytics in marketing, including customer analytics, product analytics, pricing analytics, and advertising analytics.

cilos.description: Understand why and where marketing analytics are needed.
Understand basic and some advanced regression methods.
Understand basic principles of predictive models.
Understand principles and practices of field experiments.
Familiarize basic applications related customer, advertising, product, and pricing.

courses.title: Strategic Marketing
courses.description: Developing a comprehensive and integrated framework for directing and managing the marketing functions of a company; methods to analyze marketing opportunities, assess competitive advantages and forecast market changes.

cilos.description: Apply the key concepts and theoretical frameworks, and practical knowledge, to solve marketing problems using both qualitative and quantitative analyses.
Criticially think and evaluate the challenges to make strategic marketing decisions.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in current marketing thought and practices; topics vary from semester to semester.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.

courses.title: Brand Management
courses.description: This course is designed to help students develop a practical understanding of the tools, rules, and strategies of brand management.  By the end of the semester, students will be able to assess critical aspects of a branding strategy such as: how to introduce and name new products; how to interpret brand performance; and how to manage a brand over time, product categories, and geographical markets.  MARK 4450 is intended for individuals considering careers at senior levels of corporate management or as consultants in strategy firms, ad agencies, and market research companies.

cilos.description: Assess critical aspects of brand management.
Design brand positioning strategies.
Generate brand resonance.
Evaluate appropriate brand elements.
Leverage secondary brand associations.
Manage a brand over time and across various geographical markets.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Directed study of selected problems in marketing not covered in other courses. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge and understanding on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Apply suitable business theories and framework to analyze and evaluate data relevant to the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.

courses.title: Customer Relationship Management
courses.description: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is a strategic approach that businesses use to manage interactions with current and potential customers. In today’s competitive market, fostering strong customer relationships enhances loyalty and retention, directly impacting revenue growth. In this course, students will (1) learn the domains of strategic, operational and analytic CRM; (2) be able to create a CRM plan for businesses; and (3) be capable of objectively critiquing CRM programs.

cilos.description: Understand the history of CRM and see the evolution and progression.
Understand and identify the three different spheres of CRM and their objectives, including strategic, operational, and analytical spheres.
Create a realistic and viable CRM plan for businesses.
Gain enough insight into this functional specialty of marketing so that they may in the future choose this area of specialization if desired.
Develop a solid foundation of critical working knowledge of each CRM sphere: strategic, operational, analytical.
Gain a broad and deep understanding of the power generated by information/data to change behavior, particularly as it relates to customer retention.
Objectively critique CRM programs and judge their probability of success/failure.

courses.title: Content Marketing
courses.description: Content marketing is a strategic marketing approach focused on creating and distributing valuable, relevant, and consistent content to attract and retain a clearly defined audience - and, ultimately, to drive profitable customer action. This course will look at content marketing strategy and execution from a holistic perspective, as a journey that includes an understanding of all the content brands are creating, from paid channels, earned channels to owned channels - TV commercials, brand websites, campaigns and events, company social media accounts, E-commerce flagship stores, etc. This course aims to bring students to the real marketing world.

cilos.description: Understand what content marketing is.
Be familiar with the key steps to develop content marketing executions.
Develop the channel-specific content strategy and execution.
Develop the consumer journey stage-specific content strategy and execution.
Apply the principles to evaluate and comment on content development outputs.
Be prepared for the future of content marketing.

courses.title: Marketing Strategy
courses.description: Strategic marketing objectives and implementation of strategies through pricing, distribution channels, promotion and new-product decisions.  This is a core course for MBA.

cilos.description: Conduct a marketing environmental analysis and identify market opportunities that will be strategically fit with the company or organization.
Identify and evaluate segments, and decide on the appropriate target(s) within a given market.
Construct a persuasive value proposition and positioning statement for a given offering.
Formulate marketing strategies and make strategic marketing decisions, including specific marketing mix strategies.
Monitor and control strategic marketing plans.
Make effective presentations of a company’s or organization’s marketing plan.

courses.title: The Art of War and Eastern Wisdom in Business Competition
courses.description: This course aims to explore and integrate the ancient Eastern wisdom into modern Western management science and apply to modern business competition. To achieve this goal, this course will use Sun Tzu's "The Art of War" as a vehicle to introduce the foundation of Eastern wisdom (Confucianism, Taoism, Buddhism) to management executives. Sun Tzu's "The Art of War " has proved to be a classic work on strategy, applicable to both military and business situation. This course is to crystallize some concepts and ideas put forth in "The Art of War" into a few business strategic principles and an innovative framework of 4Stop so that these can be more easily understood and applied.

cilos.description: Identify the profound wisdom of the East and the competitive edge strategic thinking.
Integrate the ancient Eastern Wisdom into modern Western management science.
Apply the wisdom of the East into daily life and into any competitive environment.

courses.title: Luxury Strategy
courses.description: This intensive block week course addresses the unique properties, opportunities, and challenges of the luxury industry by studying issues relevant to the field in the various aspects of the business, from production and management to distribution and promotion. Students will have the unique opportunity to interact with senior executives from a renowned luxury brand as they feedback on students' research and recommendations, and guide them to understand their brand strategy and implementation.

cilos.description: Recognize the unique properties, opportunities and challenges of the luxury industry.
Identify and analyze key issues specific to the luxury industry.
Apply marketing knowledge and strategy to solve issues at hand.

courses.title: Retailing
courses.description: This course discusses the retailing strategies that aim to foster a long-term win-win situation that benefits all players in the marketplace - consumers, retailers and manufactures. The primary focus of this course will be on understanding customers’ shopping behavior and developing retailing strategy with the understanding of why and how consumers buy. The topics we will cover provide a firm foundation in many dimensions of retailing, including merchandising, pricing, promotion and customer relationship management.

cilos.description: Identify the needs of consumers based on an in-depth understanding of their buying behavior.
Develop the market positioning of the retailer based on the analysis of the market environment and the preferences of target consumers.
Develop skills to build retailer brands that will prosper in the global marketplace.
Develop and implement retailing strategies in the digital marketplace.
Develop sustainable retailing strategies and develop a sense of social responsibility as a future market leader.

courses.title: Understanding Consumers
courses.description: This course combines an in-depth exploration of consumer psychology with elements of advertising and marketing research, with the goal of enhancing students' understanding of marketing tactics and strategy.

cilos.description: Identify key principles and concepts relating to consumer behavior.
Examine the available theory and research concerning the psychology of the consumer.
Design and develop an effective marketing mix for a product or service relying on in-depth knowledge of the consumers.

courses.title: Pricing Strategy
