Make progress in coming to a personal set of ethical principles to be applied in their study and career.
Appreciate and promulgate the necessity for ethical behavior and leadership to academic and business enterprise at all levels.
Write about and discuss ethical issues cogently and persuasively with internal and external audiences.

courses.title: New Venture Creation
courses.description: This course introduces students to the fundamental knowledge, mindset, and skill sets required to create and manage new ventures. Through a combination of theory, practical exercises, case studies, and projects, students will learn to recognise, assess, and articulate new opportunities for entrepreneurial ventures, generate innovative business ideas based on technological concepts, and understand the resources and strategies necessary for implementation. Students will be exposed to the real-world challenges of creating a new technical venture and will acquire the essential knowledge and skills for setting up and managing a venture. The course also help participants develop a greater awareness of their personal goals, strengths and limitations in venture creation and growth. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Understand the process of designing a new venture concept from a technical idea and developing innovative business model for implementation.
Develop practical strategies for identifying, evaluating, and exploiting business opportunity.
Understand the process and acquire fundamental knowledge and skillset in creating a new venture, developing viable business models, and making business plan.
Effectively communicate and articulate the value proposition of a new venture to investors, stakeholders, and decision makers.
Demonstrate foundational business literacy to evaluate the resource required for implementing the designed concept and business model.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Human behavior and behavioral issues in organizations studied from the perspective of the individual and that of the organization.

cilos.description: Demonstrate your understanding of major concepts and theories in OB.

Analyze management issues at the individual, team and organizational levels critically and creatively. 
a. Being critical refers to the application of OB theories to solving organizational problems in a manner that shows your awareness of (i) exactly how the theory of your choice applies to the issue being analyzed and (ii) the risks and benefits associated with each solution suggested. 
b. Being creative refers to finding solutions to management issues not necessarily referred to in your textbook, as long as such solutions are theoretically justified.
Apply concepts and theories in OB learned in this course to solve business problems.
Communicate and present your ideas clearly, persuasively, and professionally (through writing, presentations, and discussions).
Enhance your personal ability to function effectively in a multicultural settings.
Develop an understanding of personal strengths and weaknesses in organizational contexts.

courses.title: Business Ethics and Social Responsibility
courses.description: Taking a discussion-based approach to examining ethical issues in a corporate context, this intermediate business ethics course will focus mainly on the ethical issues related to the interaction between business and society. Students will further develop their ethical knowledge, moral reasoning skills, and attitudes towards social responsibility by considering the overarching corporate implications of their decisions. This highly interactive course will draw upon relevant current issues to help students understand (and overcome) some of the real-world challenges that business executives confront.
courses.prerequisite: (for non-BIBU, non-RMBI and non-SGFN students) MGMT 2010

cilos.description: Understand concepts / terminology associated with business ethics and social responsibility.
Know the basic principles of ethical decision-making and Stakeholder Management.
Identify ethical dilemmas in business.
Analyze arid propose solutions to business challenges involving moral ambiguity.
Appreciate the importance of behaving ethically in society.
Gain an awareness of one's professional and ethical responsibility in society.

courses.title: Human Resources Management
courses.description: Manpower planning, job analysis and design, recruitment, performance appraisal, compensation, training and development, health and safety at work and discrimination.

cilos.description: Explain, compare, and contrast, and apply basic HRM concepts, techniques and industrial practices.
Critically analyze HRM issues in real organizations, develop, and defend reasoned solutions with sound theoretical viewpoints.
Produce quality HRM case reports and present professionally in English.

courses.title: Managerial Leadership
courses.description: Understand the nature of leadership and how it goes beyond managership. To develop an appreciation for the complexities of dealing with people who hold different values. To introduce, develop and encourage new strategies and techniques to enhance both teamwork and effectiveness in the workplace.

cilos.description: Demonstrate understanding of key leadership theories and concepts.
Apply leadership theories critically to analyze and address real-world challenges.
Reflect on personal leadership development and cultivate leadership skills to navigate complex, fast-changing professional contexts.

courses.title: Judgement and Decision Making in Organizations
courses.description: This course is about how people make decisions, with special emphasis on decision making in an organizational context. It attempts to provide an understanding of employee and manager decision making at two levels - the individual and the group.

cilos.description: Explain why decision making is an important component in managing organizations.
Perform decision analysis and solve decision problems using quantitative and analytical techniques.
Describe various biases in individual decision making and group decision making.
Apply theories related to judgment and decision making in organization-relevant domains such as human resources management, marketing, entrepreneurship, and ethics.
Develop skills for effective teamwork.
Develop skills for effective communication.

courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Theories and processes of negotiation; negotiation strategies; contextual factors in negotiation; other issues in negotiation.

cilos.description: Understand the core negotiation concepts and the situations where they apply. This will involve leaning how to compare, contrast, and differentiate among negotiation situations.
Develop greater confidence when negotiating.
Demonstrate the ability to understand and predict the behavior and motives of individuals and groups across negotiation situations.
Critically analyze negotiation situations to identify where they can be applied versus where they need to be modified.
Demonstarte the ability to design and implement strategies for negotiating effectively across a wide range of contexts, including novel situations.

courses.title: Environmental Business Strategies
courses.description: This course covers strategic opportunities arising from environmental risks. Public and regulatory demand for environmental products and services must co-exist with the need for corporations to maximize shareholder wealth. The course examines both theoretical and practical issues that arise in attempting to balance the health of the natural environment with value creation. Is there an inherent conflict between the institutions of business and our ability to care for the environment? What competitive opportunities are created for firms and what do they have to do to seize these opportunities? Lessons from the course will be interest to the students of strategy and the environment. Restricted to MGMT and BBA students.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the conceptual relationships between environmental impacts and a firm's business strategy.
Assess the efficacy of the incorporation of environmental perspectives into the design of competitive strategies.
Analyze business situations to identify alternative environmental strategies and recommend environmentally responsible solutions.
Apply an understanding of how environmental issues affect strategic business decisions.
Synthesize an environmentally sustainable business model for a business.
Develop and understanding of how firms can engage in environmental stewardship and practice environmental and social responsibility.
Practice teamwork.

courses.title: Managing CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility)
courses.description: This course will focus on specific CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) issues facing companies today. Along with changing attitudes, new global regulatory CSR requirements are increasingly putting firms under pressure to demonstrate positive social and environmental impacts, while maintaining their commitments to investors. Students will investigate how actual firms are managing these pressures while continuing to address the needs of their stakeholders. Incorporating aspects of the benchmark standards such as the GRI and various ESG (Environmental Social Governance) initiatives will help students to strengthen their own knowledge, skill, and attitudes in this area. The course has an embedded project, with direct links to one or more businesses, which will give students the necessary practical grounding for effectively understanding the challenges of CSR in the contemporary business environment.

cilos.description: Understand concepts / terminology associated with CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility).
Understand the need for businesses to address CSR issues.
Identify key value drivers for CSR.
Analyze and propose solutions to help businesses overcome some of the challenges that accompany CSR in terms of its monitoring and reporting.
Appreciate how businesses can develop strategies that incorporate CSR components while ensuring their own commercial viability.
Gain an awareness of the rising expectations from various stakeholders who want to see companies take up their genuine corporate social responsibility.

courses.title: Special Topics in Management
courses.description: Current development issues in the field of organization and management; topics selected by instructors.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Faculty directed independent study.  May be graded letter grades or P/F subject to different offerings.

cilos.description: Analyze key concepts and theories to demonstrate in-depth, substantial knowledge of the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.
Apply communication strategies to articulate and present arguments systematically in professional-quality written reports or oral presentations.
Apply self-assessment strategies to monitor learning progress and cultivate motivation for lifelong learning.

courses.title: Corporate Strategy
courses.description: Major techniques and approaches to the development and implementation of corporate strategies. Underlying concepts; analytical techniques; internal and external competitor analysis and evaluation of strategic options.

cilos.description: Develop proficiency in strategy-related concepts, analytical tools, and frameworks.
Enhance analytical and evaluative skills to identify and assess strategic problems and opportunities.
Strengthen communication, teamwork, and leadership skills in strategic contexts.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
courses.description: This is an interactive course that introduces knowledge about the creation and management of new business ventures. Attention is also given to key issues in corporate entrepreneurship, social entrepreneurship, and family businesses.

cilos.description: Understand the nature of entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial processes.
Recognize and evaluate business opportunities.
Familiarize with key terminology of entrepreneurship.
Identify and analyze major entrepreneurial issues.
Develop fundamental and economic understanding of innovation.

courses.title: International Management
courses.description: Understanding and managing multinational corporations in different economic, social, cultural, legal and technological environments.

cilos.description: Explain the nature of competitive advantages and assess the competitiveness of companies in international business.

Apply your knowledge to analyze the international business environment facing a firm, assess the attractiveness of its industry and isolate potential sources of competitive advantages and disadvantages.
Develop solutions designed to build and sustain international competitive advantages.
Develop effective implementation plans while considering the human element of organizations.

courses.title: Strategic Management in China
courses.description: The overall goal of this course is to teach the students key theories and frameworks in strategic management and apply them to Chinese context.  it takes a comparative perspective to analyze the similarities and differences in strategic management between East and West.  It is case intensive course which involves extensive student participation in analyzing cases of business in China.

cilos.description: Understand the extent to which China is different from other countries and how such differences affect business strategies in the Chinese context.
Assess the opportunities and challenges of setting up business operations in China, and develop corresponding sound business & corporate strategies.
Design and evaluate recommendations for multinational companies seeking to develop China strategies in order to compete in the Chinese market more successfully.

courses.title: Management Consulting
courses.description: To meet the increasing demand from both the private and public sectors in local and international firms in Hong Kong, South East Asia and mainland China, Management Consulting is a course to be offered by faculty with consulting experience who will train students in management with the fundamental and practical skills to understand and analyse business problems in order to work out a number of scenarios for solving problems. More importantly, the students will be encouraged to work in teams and propose innovative and strategic consulting plans to meet a set of specified goals from time to time.

cilos.description: Learn key consulting techniques.
Apply consulting techniques to an actual project and recommend an actionable solution.
Demonstrate mastery by presenting a deck.

courses.title: Training and Development
courses.description: In today's competitive business world, organizations need to implement training and development initiatives to continuously cultivate their human resources. This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the training and developing process in organizations. Topics include training needs assessment, learning motivation, theories of learning, transfer of training, training methods, and training evaluation. The course will also examine special topics of interest such as cross-cultural training, career development, and the role of information technology and social responsibility in training and development.

cilos.description: Articulate how training and development contributes to the achievement of organizational goals.
Conduct training needs assessment, and identify training objectives.
Apply various theories of motivation, learning, and transfer to design effective training activities and select training methods.
Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs.
Describe recent trends in training and development such as cross-cultural training, career development, and the role of information technology and social responsibility in training and development.
Develop skills for effective teamwork.
Develop skills for effective communication.

courses.title: Transnational Legal Issues and Dispute Settlement
courses.description: The course introduces students to core legal principles of transnational economic law with special emphasis on cross-border commercial legal issues, alongside mechanisms for settling trade and investment disputes. Key focus areas include legal challenges in cross-border commercial contracts (choice of law, jurisdiction clauses, force majeure, anti-bribery compliance), arbitration (UNCITRAL, HKIAC), mediation, and ICSID investor-state arbitration. Lectures analyze how domestic laws, WTO agreements, and international conventions impact multinational operations in sectors like energy, infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals. Students learn practical strategies to mitigate risks through robust contract drafting and ADR, drawing from real-world cases like jurisdictional battles and enforcement under the New York Convention.

cilos.description: Understand why knowing the law is an advantage for a business leader.
Develop an understanding of the laws, regulations, and institutions that govern transnational economic activities.
Develop their knowledge of the core principles of international contract drafting and the settlement of international commercial disputes.
Understand the role of the WTO trade agreements and dispute settlement mechanism.
Develop an understanding of international labour regulations.
Learn the core principles of investor-state arbitration.
Develop their understanding of alternative dispute resolutions mechanism Arbitration and Mediation.
Learn how to do basic legal research.
Acquire skills and knowledge that will expand their career opportunities.

courses.title: HR Analytics
courses.description: HR analytics, also known as “people analytics” and “talent analytics”, is the use of HR data and analytical tools to improve decision making in human resources and ultimately contribute to organizational effectiveness. It is an evidence-based, data-driven approach to managing people at work. In this course, we will examine the HR data and analytical tools necessary to conducting HR analytics, and apply them in resolving HR issues such as recruitment and selection, performance evaluation, training and development, compensation, and retention. We will also discuss the ethical aspects related to HR analytics.

cilos.description: Articulate how HR analytics contributes to organizational effectiveness, and illustrate with examples in international settings.
Formulate HR problems into research designs that will generate insights for decision making in various HR functions (e.g. recruitment and selection, talent retention).
Analyze HR data using descriptive and predictive analytical techniques, with the help of statistical data analysis software.
Communicate findings and insights generated from HR analytics.
Demonstrate awareness of ethical aspects of collecting and utilizing HR data.
Develop effective teamwork skills for team projects.

courses.title: Power, Influence, and Persuasion
courses.description: This is an advanced experiential course allowing students to explore and practice the strategies of power and influence experienced in the business world. The course connects scientific theory with relevant practice and focuses on experimenting with specific techniques to achieve desired outcomes in investing, management, and entrepreneurship contexts. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Understand core concepts related to persuasion, decision making, and behavior.
Use basic concepts in their daily life and have an ability to apply them to a variety of situations.
Understand how people judge one another and the various dimensions and trade-offs involved in how we are judged.
Understand their own persuasive profile and how they are different from others on specific dimensions related to persuasion and influence.

courses.title: Managerial Communication
courses.description: Communication skill ranks at the top of contributors to job effectiveness, satisfaction and success. Managerial communication gives students an opportunity to improve students' ability to communicate efficiently and effectively as a manager and to develop those critical communication capabilities that students will need as a business leader.

cilos.description: Communicate more effectively in business environments as managers and leaders.
Continue practicing their communication skills for continuous improvement in the future.

courses.title: Preparing to Lead
courses.description: The practical study of managerial work. Examines communication skills and offers the opportunity for assessment and feedback. Organizational contexts, team building and case work. This is a required immersion program for MBA programs. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Define the concept of leadership in organizations.
Develop skills and competencies that enable effective leadership.
Develop a plan that will enable an immediate and noticeable impact on how they lead at work.

courses.title: Management of Organizations
courses.description: Include motivation theories, leadership, group dynamics, job design, decision making, power and politics, organizational structure and design, and organizational change.

cilos.description: Improve general decision making and managerial decision making.
Lead a team and work within a group.
Motivate and manage others at work.
Negotiate effectively.
Identify ethical challenges in oneself and others.

courses.title: Strategic Management
courses.description: Major techniques and approaches to the development and implementation of corporate strategies. Underlying concepts, analytical techniques, internal and external competitor analysis and evaluation of strategic options. This is a core course for MBA.

cilos.description: Apply theories/frameworks (e.g. SWOT Analysis and Porter’s Five Forces) for in-depth industry analysis, for anticipating and predicting future industry development.
Examine some of the firm's specific underpinnings of competitive advantage and growth in both domestic and international settings.
Evaluate some of the challenges in implementing the strategy that has been formulated.

courses.title: Strategic Management in China
courses.description: The primary topic of this course is strategic management in the Chinese context.  This course has three major objectives: 1) to help students understand the conditions under which different kinds of strategy have the potential to create economic value and competitive advantage for Chinese context; 2) to help students who plan to work in Chinese companies understand their roles and responsibilities in helping the companies to achieve competitive advantage; and 3)to help those, who work in foreign companies that either already have or will have operations in China, obtain the knowledge necessary to compete or cooperate with companies in Chinese context more successfully.

cilos.description: Understand the extent to which China is different from other countries and how such differences affect business strategies in the Chinese context.
More accurately assess the opportunities and challenges in setting up business operations in China and to develop corresponding sound business and corporate strategies.
Be better prepared to help multi-national companies to develop sound China strategies in order to compete in the Chinese market more successfully.

courses.title: Judgment in Managerial Decision Making
courses.description: This is a course with an in-depth discussion on the nature of human thinking and judgment. The overall emphasis of this course will be on illustrating errors and biases in thinking and judgment and their managerial implications. In other words, the class is designed to give students a "rational mind". The concepts we will discuss are key to removing the obstacles in thinking, solving problems, and making decisions. Topics that we will focus on include Common Biases, Experts and Novices, Heuristics, Judgment under Uncertainty, Nonrational Escalation of Commitment, and the Psychology of Delaying Decisions.

cilos.description: Evaluate the general nature of human thinking and judgment.
Identify the major errors and biases in thinking and judgment.
Recognize the obstacles in problem solving and decision making, and develop an awareness to removing them.
Develop strategies to overcome the obstacles in problem solving and decision making.
Apply the newly learned methodology in managerial contexts.

courses.title: Applied Strategic Thinking
courses.description: This course will explore the immediate ability to contribute to top management's strategic conversations in students' current organization.  It teaches how to think strategically and provides the opportunity to apply this thinking in a team environment.  Students will be able to immediately apply the thinking and skills learnt to the current job.

cilos.description: Explain a summarized company strategy.
Apply strategic thinking tools and presepectives to see the future of their industry.
Generate alternative strategies for a business unit.
Construct an implementation plan for business strategy and decision making.

courses.title: Effective Negotiations
courses.description: This course focuses on two-party negotiations in a wide variety of settings ranging from simple buyer-seller bargains to complex, multiple-issue strategic relationships.

cilos.description: Develop the ability to compare, contrast, and differentiate among different negotiation situations.
Judge the behavior and motives of individuals and groups in various negotiating situations.
Analyze negotiation situations to identify which effective core negotiating concepts can be applied and modified.
Design and implement strategies for negotiating effectively across a wide range of situations.

courses.title: Applied Merger and Acquisition for Corporates
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare business managers to succeed as members of a merger and acquisition project team. Students will be able to work out how merger and acquisition can help to achieve the strategy, to know how merger and acquisition transactions work in practice from search to merger integration, to get insight into the particular opportunities and challenges of merger and acquisition, and to apply this thinking in a team environment.

cilos.description: Appraise how merger and acquisition can help achieve a firm's strategy.
Identify how merger and acquisition transactions work in practice, from initial search through to merger integration.
Recognize nsight into the opportunities and challenges of merger and acquisition in China.
Execute the merger and acquisition thinking in a team environment.

courses.title: Responsible Leadership
courses.description: Great leaders and corporations take greater responsibilities for its customers, employees, shareholders, and society. This class is to learn what it takes to be a responsible leader and how leaders can create responsible corporations. This course also intends to change behavior for future leaders by teaching decision making framework for making responsible and ethical decisions as they face these challenges. Maybe graded PP. This is a core course for MBA.

cilos.description: Recognize the differing perspectives of defining and applying ‘responsible leadership’ and ‘ethics’ by exposure to conceptual frameworks from management science (and philosophy) and from ‘everyday discourses’ from business practitioners.

Identify and apply tools, concepts, and theories to perform analyses of the different approaches to responsible leadership and ethics in practice, motives and inspiration (moral, strategic, shareholder, philanthropic, etc.) behind these differences.
Enhance personal development to consider moral reflections on how to respond to ethical dilemmas in a business environment.
Examine practical case studies relating to the applied nature of responsible leadership and ethics in relation to local and global settings and the issues and controversies that surround them.

courses.title: Time to Lead
courses.description: This course will help students reflect on their learning in the MBA program and prepare them for their leadership roles in the future. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Develop skills and competencies that enable effective leadership.
Develop a plan that will enable an immediate and noticeable impact on how they lead at work.
Reconcile skills and competencies at the beginning of the program with skill and competency growth at the end of the program.

courses.title: Managing Change
courses.description: This course helps you understand your strengths and development areas as a change agent. It then explores a model of change and the role of the change agent as a leader and influencer of others. An online simulation is used to help understand motivation and resistance in recipients of change. Finally, hands on practice is conducted for some key change agent competencies including creating a vision and communication.

cilos.description: Recognize how personal characteristics impact a person role as change agent and nd deal with resistance in yourself and others.
Define the stages of change and associated challenges of each.
Identify how to  design and facilitate change.
Use the experience in practicing communication and decision skills of a change agent.
Design a personal development plan to improve required skills as a change agent.

courses.title: Deal Making across Asia and China
courses.description: This course specifically focuses on formulating and applying practical deal-making strategies to real-world transactions in the Asia Pacific region. This is a highly participatory and interactive course instead of purely lecture-style. Participants are asked to play the roles of deal makers -- which role may be as a lead negotiator, investor, investment banker, salesman, consultant, or investment advisor -- in pioneering transactions.

cilos.description: Define different kinds of transaction structures in the Chinese and Asian contexts.
Identify the different country and cultural contexts in China and Asia.
Compare, contrast, and differentiate between different types of deals and the contexts in which they take place.
Critically analyze a new situation to identify which techniques and contextual factors are the most critical.
Design and implement strategies using the above knowledge in order to structure, negotiate, and close deals in a variety of Chinese and Asian contexts.
Present the deals effectively to potential deal partners and other members of the team.
Tackle ethical challenges conducting deals in China and Asia.

courses.title: Management Consulting
courses.description: This course is intended for students who are exploring consulting as a career option or who want to be more effective at working out and communicating recommendations. This course will teach students the key skills that management consultants use to solve business problems. This will be a demanding case-based course where students will learn the tools, skills and approaches adopted in leading management consultancies.

cilos.description: Diagnose the situation of a business problem.
Structure the business problem.
Prove a hypothesis.
Apply relevant frameworks to solve a business problem.
Apply fact-based analytical tools to identify insights.
Design compelling communications to share their thinking.

courses.title: Global Leadership and Governance
courses.description: This course is designed to inform and inspire MBA students to evolve in their development as global leaders. Drawing from the instructor’s extensive experience in researching, teaching and practicing leadership and governance, students will be provided with actual experiences and lessons learned from the instructor.

cilos.description: Identify the important characteristics that distinguish a leader from a manager.
Recognize different leadership styles and the limitations that come with them.
Apply relevant leadership principles for effective time management and staff empowerment.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation in FinTech
courses.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts relevant for developing FinTech entrepreneurial opportunities. The course begins with frameworks for understanding technology innovation and evolution, and then dives into how new ideas can be generated and assessed, and brought to market by developing an effective organization and relationships in the financial ecosystem.

cilos.description: Define technology innovation and evolution.
Develop and assess creative FinTech ideas.
Develop the business model for a FinTech innovation.
Develop effective external collaborations in the financial ecosystem.
Building an effective entrepreneurial organization to harness the FinTech ideas.

courses.title: Managing Creativity and Innovation
courses.description: Creativity is the generation of new and useful ideas. Innovation is the successful implementation of those ideas. Creativity is therefore the foundation of innovation. In a world of accelerating change and fleeting opportunity, creativity and innovation are critical aspects of every manager’s job. This course is designed to help students enhance their creativity, their team’s creativity, the creativity of the people working with them, and ultimately the innovation in their organization. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Develop innovation, especially disruptive innovation, in organization.
Identify specific techniques for fostering creativity in themselves, others and innovation in organization.
Assess the enhancement and environment for individual and team creativity.

courses.title: Principles for Global Leaders
courses.description: Through ample case studies, group work and reflection time, the course aims at helping students to enhance their self-awareness, improve their communication skills, build stronger connections and trust with classmates and provide deeper knowledge in the principles of global leadership. This learning has the potential to propel students faster in their leadership career development.

cilos.description: Solve business problems and develop advanced solution as a leader.
Apply responsible leader skills into business management.
Recognize and identify own core values, goal and interest which determine career success.
Evaluate areas of compatibility and conflict among team members for effective business decision.
Execute leadership to manage a team efficiently.

courses.title: Achieving High Performance in Teams
courses.description: The course offers a unique opportunity to develop students’ understanding of how to lead and participate in a high performance team as well as address the challenge of virtual teamwork. The course offers a highly unusual and exciting experiential component when students will form small virtual teams to compete in a competitive team performance challenge.

cilos.description: Recognize the impact of their personalities and behaviour on others.
Evaluate the impact of their cultural values and behaviour on others.
Identify the necessary tools of a feedback culture for team effectiveness.
Plan and navigate a team development journey.
Assess the performance of a team they are leading or a member of the team and introduce changes to improve performance.

courses.title: Leading Virtual Teams to High Performance
courses.description: Teaming in a virtual environment has never been so widespread. The Covid-19 pandemic was a major catalyst for organizations of all kinds to switch to, invest in and accept virtual team collaboration. What new skills do members of virtual teams need to master to achieve effective collaboration and high performance? How has operating remotely and through video impacted group dynamics and interpersonal behavior? Whether the students are leaders or members of a team, in this course they will deepen their understanding of teaming and master the latest skills needed to take virtual teams to high performance. The students will also have opportunities to engage in virtual teaming, both collaboratively and competitively, with their fellow class participants and in a new simulation in which teams compete on a voyage in outer space. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Lead teams operating in a virtual environment more effectively.
Contribute more constructively to a team operating in a virtual environment.
Empower a team more successfully to strive for high performance.
Understand how to address hurdles encountered by team operating in virtual environments.
Leverage real virtual team experiences from simulations in the course to learn how to improve their virtual teaming capabilities.

courses.title: Innovating via Entrepreneurship and Intrapreneurship
courses.description: This course focuses on the essence of innovation, which is relevant to both entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship in startups, large corporations, or family businesses. Throughout the course, students will gain self-insight and learn practical tools for innovation as they create a business plan, project proposal, or new business line to present to a panel of experienced innovators.

cilos.description: Recognize personal values, passions and purpose to decide between entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship.
Evaluate project and venture viability.
Develop and pitch a business case.
Apply the skills to pitch project and venture proposals to key stakeholders.

courses.title: Interpersonal Dynamics, Networking and the Art of Influencing Business Leaders
courses.description: The course focuses on effective client relationships for students pursuing advisory roles. The curriculum will concentrate on day-to-day client relationship practices, equipping students to become competent professionals. To enhance student learning, the course will also outline specific strategies for applying these insights during internships or entry-level positions after graduation. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Classify the key debates between different approaches to influencing executives.
Assess personal networking patterns and identify options to improve the ability to network.
Recognize the process of selling and implications for influence in other situations.
Develop their approach to networking, collaborating with others, and influencing executives.

courses.title: Managerial Decision Making
courses.description: Successful organizations excel by the quality of their offerings and services in the market place. Internally, leaders and managers distinguish themselves by the quality of their decisions. As leaders and managers, you will find that your decision making ability is tested and challenged at work every day. Your ability to make quality decisions will determine your long term professional success and the success of your organization. Quality management decisions do not need to be hit and miss, nor should they be based on titles and ranks. Quality decision making is a competence that can be acquired and a discipline that should be practiced.

cilos.description: Identify approaches to lead team(s) in making the best decisions to achieve organizational goals.
Apply a decision making framework, tested by many practical situations, hence approach any decision with confidence.
Articulate, defend, and successfully implement the decisions made.
Recognize the most effective leadership styles in leading the team to make the best decisions.

courses.title: Introduction to Management
courses.description: This course provides an accelerated overview of the materials covered in undergraduate classes in management and strategy, aimed at postgraduate students with no undergraduate background in business. It will cover essential frameworks in both organizational behavior (leadership and motivation, organizational culture and design) and strategy (business and corporate strategy, international business). It also provides an introduction to the case method.

courses.title: Strategy Consulting Analytics and Operations Consulting Analytics
courses.description: This course gives students the opportunity to practice the skills learned in  the previous courses on real-world projects sourced from real-world clients. In this course, students will focus on recommending a solution to a business problem. Later, in MGMT 6985 Strategic Analytics Implementation, students will focus on implementing this solution.

cilos.description: Apply consulting techniques in a corporate environment, working with client-side executives, technologists, and data scientists to deliver the right solutions for the right problems.
Apply technical knowledge within a business environment to solve real problems.
Match specific technologies and analytical tools to specific problems faced by specific clients.

Analyze the strategic and operational impacts of specific technologies and analytical tools within specific client environments, especially given the configuration of the operational processes involved.
Understand client-side stakeholder needs to manage the project and impact how the results will be received by the clients.

courses.title: Strategic Analytics Implementation
courses.description: This course continues the real-world projects initiated in MGMT 5984 Strategy Consulting Analytics and Operations Consulting Analytics, focusing on implementing the solution to the business case recommended during MGMT 5984.

cilos.description: Apply operational consulting techniques in a corporate environment, working with client-side executives, technologists, and data scientists to implement a technical solution within the context of client-side processes.
Leverage statistical analyses and machine learning algorithms in a corporate data environment, working with client-side personnel to obtain access to data and analysis platforms.
Quickly and efficiently prototype and refine technical solutions via code reuse and API-based access to publicly available tools.
Understand client-side stakeholder needs to manage the project and impact how the results will be received by the clients.

courses.title: Digital Transformation in the Exponential Age
courses.description: Reinvention is at the core of transformation, leveraging digital technology as a force multiplier. In this course, the instructor provides practical tips, approaches, methodology, and frameworks to address the challenges that students will be called upon to deliver at some point in their careers. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Explain the underlying principles, basic concepts, and methodology around Digital Transformation strategy and execution.
Summarize the common approaches, organizational design options, transformation frameworks, change theory, and leadership techniques for transformation.
Recognize the limits of theory and gain an understanding of the common pitfalls and tradeoffs when theory is applied in practice for Digital Transformation.
Recognize how to leverage and apply technology in real life environments and use cases.
Use techniques to overcome organizational resistance, inertia, and other structural and nonstructural obstacles.
Apply the skills to implement and drive transformation in their own organizations.

courses.title: AI, Innovation, and Product Management
courses.description: This course provides the basic principles and tools that business managers need to ensure outcomes align with business needs. Students will gain an industry insider’s view that goes beyond theory to cover actionable guidelines, practical tips, and best practices. By examining the differing modes of product development in Silicon Valley and China, this course provides a new framework and approach for competition and innovation in the Age of AI. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Explain the basic concepts, use cases, applications, and limitations of artificial intelligence.
Apply the skills to leverage AI to capture market opportunities and address operational needs.
Explain the basic methodology, tools, and concepts of product management, including how to build AI into a company’s products and services.
Develop product strategy at both the corporate and startup level.
Differentiate the different modes of innovation and AI between the East and West.

courses.title: Effective People Decisions and Career Management: Unlocking Talent and Personal Success
courses.description: This course is designed to empower MBA students with the skills and insights needed to make impactful people decisions and maximize their full career potential. By delving into the art and science of making smart people decisions, students will learn how to recruit the right talents for the right roles in order to build high-performing teams, nurture individual potential, and drive organizational success. Through interactive discussions, real-world case studies, and fun exercises, students will gain the confidence and expertise to define talent gaps, needs, screen, attract, retain and develop the right people on their teams.

cilos.description: Understand the impact of people decisions on performance, teams, and career success.
Apply effective methods to identify talent needs and hire the right people.
Manage workplace relationships and collaborate effectively in complex organizations.
Develop a flexible, values-based career plan and navigate career changes confidently.

courses.title: Consequential Communication for Business Leader
courses.description: One of the must learn to be a successful effective leader is to communicate consequentially internally and externally. This course provides students chance to enhance skills including summarization, elaboration and Question and Answer, through different modes of communications like One-to-many speeches and presentation and Many-to-many meetings and discussions. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Construct and organize consequential communication.
Deliver consequential communication efficiently and effectively.
Evaluate self and other’s communications.
Recommend useful feedback for individual and team communication.
Develop continuous improvement plan for consequential communication.

courses.title: Agile Leadership in the Digital Age
courses.description: This course explores how organizations navigate exponential disruptions through transformation journeys such as digitalization, market expansion, agile teamwork, innovation leadership, and ESG strategy implementation. It spans industries including banking, global industrials, family business, media, social commerce, and fast fashion across global and Asian contexts. Students will develop strong mental frameworks, practical tools, and opportunities for cross‑learning to navigate rapid change.

cilos.description: Apply sensemaking frameworks to interpret and respond to exponential disruptions.
Demonstrate curiosity-driven leadership to foster innovation and adaptability.
Strengthen self-awareness to develop an authentic and engaging leadership style.
Design and implement agile strategies for business model transformation in diverse contexts.

courses.title: Communication for Business Leaders
courses.description: In order to be an effective leader, one must learn to communicate effectively and consequently. This course will focus on effective leadership through effective and consequential communication. Whether leaders are effective largely depends on how effectively leaders communicate. Immediate feedback for continuous improvements will be given by peers and the instructor during the class and in breakout sessions. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify how effective communication supports and strengthens a leader’s effectiveness in a business environment.
Summarize the key points using the golden rules of responsible business leadership as a guide.
Evaluate potential crisis outcomes and apply effective solutions to practical business scenarios.

courses.title: Special Topics in Human Resources Management
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in human resources management.

cilos.description: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

courses.title: Special Topics in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in organizational behavior.

cilos.description: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.

courses.title: Special Topics in Management
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in Management.

cilos.description: Analyze and evaluate the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.
Develop hands-on research skills.
Advance their own research agendas such as papers targeted for submission to top tier management journals.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Study of selected issues in organizational management under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)

cilos.description: Examine a specific topic in Management.
Read academic articles critically.
Write academic articles effectively.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member. A successful defense of the thesis leads to Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in management studies.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: Behavioral Science
courses.description: In-depth study of the foundations of behavioral science research using examples from organizational behavior and other related business disciplines.

cilos.description: Recognize the philosophical development of behavioral science (Part 1).
Understand the trend and predicted future of behavioral science.
Know the position of past and current management research under the history and tend of behavior science.
Seek new directions of management research by knowing the past and current positions.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Management
courses.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in Organizational Behavior and Human Resources Management for doctoral students.

cilos.description: Make use of up-to-date and in-depth knowledge about management research in general and organizational behavior in particular, providing them with the foundation to conduct independent substantive scholarly research.
Demonstrate an in depth understanding of contemporary issues in organizational behaviors.
Perform different aspects of the role of faculty in academia, such as conducting research, writing research reviews.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Organization Theory and Strategy
courses.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in organization theory and strategic management for doctoral students.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a sound grasp of the literature in their specialization.
Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve business problems within their area of specialization.
Teach independent courses or lead lab/tutorial sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Behavioral Research Methods
courses.description: Presentations and discussions of current research topics in Behavioral Research Methods for doctoral students.

cilos.description: Recognize common research methods and techniques used in behavioral research.
Understand how these methods were used by researchers to address important research questions.
Develop hand-on knowledge on statistical packages.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Frontiers in Strategy Research
courses.description: This course is designed as a doctoral seminar discussion that provides an overview of some of the most contemporary research topics in strategic management. We will survey a select set of strategy topics including ESG and sustainability, global strategy, corporate governance, innovation models, digital economy, mergers and acquisitions, and global value chains. Through in-depth and in-class discussion of some of the cutting-edge research in the field of strategic management, we focus on developing ideas for a research proposal in terms of theory development and research design.

cilos.description: Conduct in-depth discussions of selected research papers to have a good understanding of major theories in the field of strategic management and international business.
Work closely on the development of ideas for a research proposal.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in management studies.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Identify engineering significances in microelectronics.
Engage critical thinking skills that are essential for microelectronics research.
Advance technologies in microelectronics.
Demonstrate effective communication skills.

courses.title: Language Learning
courses.description: This course provides students with a broad grounding on the generative, cognitive, sociocultural, and sociolinguistic dimensions of how languages are learned. Topics that center on the generative and cognitive aspects of language learning include the effect of one’s first language on the acquisition of second or subsequent languages, universal constraints in language acquisition, the effect of a critical period (i.e. age effects) on learning languages, the influence of explicit/implicit instruction, corrective feedback, and interaction. Topics to be discussed on the social dimension cover both learner-internal factors such as motivation, affect, agency and identity, and learner-external factors such as how social context affects language learning, at both the conversational and situational level, and social and cultural level. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Understand and evaluate different theoretical approaches to second language learning and how they are related to language pedagogy ;
Analyze the cognitive development and mechanisms involved in language learning ;
Explain how social and cultural factors contribute to the process of language learning;
Analyze learner data by applying different perspectives to language learning ;
Identify resources relevant to topics on second language learning for future teaching preparation.

courses.title: Language Teaching Methodology and Curriculum Design
courses.description: This course aims to introduce experienced language-teaching professionals worldwide and those with language-/linguistics-based backgrounds but little or no language-teaching experience to theories and principles of teaching second or foreign language, helping them construct a fundamental understanding of current theories and research in language acquisition and relate these to the practice of  language pedagogy. The course also investigates ways in which various approaches and methods can be utilized in the delivery of a foreign language curriculum and the teaching of language knowledge, including vocabulary and grammar, and both receptive and productive language skills. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Articulate important concepts related to language education.
Trace the development of the various language teaching approaches and methods in the 20th and 21st centuries.
Discuss key issues in particular language teaching situations by taking into consideration relevant contextual factors.
Apply and explain various principles governing curriculum design and material development for language teaching.
Critically analyze pedagogic designs for teaching particular aspects of a language to specifically-defined populations of language learners.

courses.title: Understanding Research in Language Education
courses.description: The course will provide students with an introduction to the principles of research in language education and relevant research methods. The course will begin with an examination of key dimensions of research, then move on to look at research methodologies from a theoretical and practical perspective. For assessment, students will critically review published research in language education, and will respond to questions requiring them to demonstrate their understanding of key concepts in language education research and their ability to evaluate methods commonly used in the field. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a theoretical and conceptual understanding of research in language education.
Critically review published research in the field.
Evaluate methods commonly used in language education research.

courses.title: Descriptions of Language for English Teachers
courses.description: The course provides students with a broad grounding on the nature and structure of language by introducing them to English linguistic analysis. Topics to be discussed include key subfields of linguistics: phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a clear understanding of fundamental concepts in phonetics and phonology.
Analyze simple English phonetic and phonological data.
Describe morphological processes and analyze languages based on their morphological types.
Describe syntactic properties, syntactic constituency, and syntactic categories, and construct a grammar for English.
Describe and analyze the aspectual categories of verbs and their selectional restrictions.
Describe and analyze how the meaning of sentences are compositionally derived from individual words.
Describe and analyze how the meaning of utterances change based on context.

courses.title: Descriptions of Language for Chinese Teachers
courses.description: The course provides students with a broad grounding on the nature and structure of language by introducing them to linguistic analysis, with emphasis on that of Chinese. Topics to be discussed include the subfields of linguistics such as phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a clear understanding of the fundamental concepts in phonetics and phonology.
Analyze Chinese sounds, both in L1 and L2 speech, from phonetic and phonological perspectives.
Demonstrate a solid grasp of key concepts and terms of Chinese grammar.
Analyse the structure of Chinese expressions at lexical, phrasal and sentential levels.
Develop a basic understanding of semantics and pragmatics.

courses.title: Testing and Assessment
courses.description: This course is aimed at raising the students' awareness level of the rudiments of effective assessment of language related performance, such as essential global concepts of language testing and assessment as well as practical skills for local language teachers to develop, use and evaluate language tests. Students will also be introduced to alternative means for classroom language assessment. Advanced oral presentation as well as basic negotiation, project management, and cooperative teamwork skills are given an opportunity for further development through outside-class preparation and in-class practice in a supportive learning environment. The teaching/learning approach adopted in this course is in line with the constructivist view and cooperative learning principles. There is a balance of individual efforts and cooperative inter-dependent learning. Hence, the assessment will be contributed equally by individual work and group activities. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Understand various types of language tests and assessments.
Develop classroom-oriented language assessment tools.
Analyze the quality of language tests in terms of validity, reliability, and difficulty.
Apply appropriate assessment tools for various purposes.
Conduct classroom-based language assessments fairly and effectively.

courses.title: Contrastive Analysis between Chinese and English
courses.description: This course aims to equip students with an in-depth understanding of the sound and grammatical systems of Chinese and English. By adopting a comparative approach, students will find surprising similarities as well as interesting differences between the two languages. On completing the course, students will acquire a functional-descriptive framework and skills in analyzing and explaining the key features of Chinese and English. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Develop an in-depth understanding of the sound and grammatical systems of Chinese and English within a functional-descriptive framework.
Identify the key phonological and grammatical features of Chinese and English.
Establish the targeting-the-difference method and skills in second language learning and teaching.

courses.title: Foundations of Technology-enhanced Language Education
courses.description: Technology and language have always been at the forefront of human development and civilization. Fundamental to the advancement of society are the ways that changing technologies impact and shape learning. This course explores the issues of how information technologies structure human cognition and social interaction and the ways which teachers can use these technologies to improve student learning. This course capitalizes on these new modes of learning to advance language teaching and learning. Gaining a better understanding of these emerging technologies can enrich teaching methodologies and extend theoretical concepts. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Explain how information technologies are shaping social interaction in and through the medium of language.
Analyze how learning in general, and language learning in specific, can be enhanced through the use of information technologies.
Examine how technologies can bridge communities and create pathways for greater interaction and social harmony.
Design and implement research-embedded technology-enhanced teaching approaches for second-language acquisition.

courses.title: Bi/Multilingual Approaches to Language Education
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce potential language teachers to general issues and current developments in bi/multilingual approaches to language education. The first part of the course focuses on individual bi/multilingualism. It will examine the basics of how bi/multilingualism is defined and measured, types of bi/multilingualism, and bi/multilingual language behaviors. The second part of the course explores foundations of bi/multilingual language education. Topics include second language versus bilingual acquisition, bilingualism and cognition, and bilingual education for bilingualism and biliteracy. The third part of the course focuses on pedagogical issues and practices in bi/multilingual language education. We will discuss the uses and roles of translation in language teaching, translanguaging in pedagogy, and mixed code and classroom code-switching, with special attention given to the teaching of Chinese and English in the context of Hong Kong. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Describe and illustrate different definitions of bi/multilingualism and methods of measuring bi/multilingualism.
Describe and illustrate how bi/multilinguals learn and use their languages.
Describe different kinds of bi/multilingual education and how they have been evaluated.
Discuss pedagogical issues and practices in bi/multilingual language education.
Design appropriate teaching plans taking into account the characteristics of the school context and the larger sociolinguistic context.
Appreciate the importance of bi/multilingualism in the age of globalization.

courses.title: World Englishes
courses.description: The position of English as a global language is commonly asserted. This course will examine the complex web of circumstances which lie behind the assertion. The presumption of the course is that it is useful and possibly essential for teachers of English to know something of the life story of the language, its varieties and place in the world at the beginning of the 21st century. A significant part of the course will examine, through the medium of seminars and workshops, how the global nature of the language can be exploited in teaching and learning environments. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Describe the outline of the journey of English from dialect to world language.
Recognize the status of English as a global language from a multidisciplinary perspective.
Apply knowledge learned from the course to practical use in the context of language teaching.

courses.title: Teaching Second Language Vocabulary
courses.description: This course examines the factors involved in developing second language (L2) learners' acquisition of English vocabulary. It covers three main areas: (a) words and the description of the vocabulary content of an English curriculum, (b) the representation of L2 vocabulary in the mental lexicon and related acquisitor issues, and (c) approaches to teaching L2 vocabulary. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Describe the internal structure of English words and the main lexical relations.
Recognize how second language vocabulary is acquired.
Identify factors that contribute to successful vocabulary acquisition.
Evaluate the merits of different approaches for teaching L2 vocabulary.

courses.title: Phonetics and Phonology for English Teachers
courses.description: This course aims to introduce the essential knowledge of English phonetics and phonology to teachers and potential teachers of English. Students will learn about the physiological aspects of human sounds and how linguists characterize and study them. They will also study how the sounds are organized in the English sound system. The pedagogical applications of English phonetics and phonology in pronunciation teaching will also be discussed. Moreover, the differences between English and other sound systems (such as Cantonese and Mandarin) are studied for further understanding of how these differences may result in different L2 features. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a clear understanding of fundamental concepts in phonetics and phonology.
Analyze English data, comprising different dialectal varieties and comparing L1/L2 users' speech, from phonetic and phonological perspectives.
Explain and correct pronunciation, intonation, and other speech errors commonly made by second language learners.
Determine the effectiveness of various methods and approaches for teaching speaking.

courses.title: Grammar for English Teachers
courses.description: This course aims to equip students with a framework and the necessary tools for analysing how the English language is used in diverse contexts today. The course consists of three main parts. Part I presents an overview of the key concepts and terminology in English grammar. Part II provides opportunities for students to apply what they have learned as they explore how grammar works within texts (e.g. student writing). In Part III, which has a pedagogical focus, students determine the effectiveness of major grammar teaching methods/approaches and evaluate instructional materials. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a firm grasp of key concepts and terms of English grammar.
Analyze how language works at the sentence level and beyond.
Evaluate how students use grammatical resources to create texts.
Explain and correct grammatical errors commonly made by second language learners.
Conduct a grammar teaching activity in a micro-teaching context.

courses.title: Teaching English for Academic Purposes
courses.description: This course explores the field of English for Academic Purposes (EAP), in terms of both theory and practice. Because EAP is primarily associated with teaching at tertiary level, the orientation of EAP requires a high level of scholarly engagement by those who teach EAP. There is also a rich amount of research in EAP which informs and shapes the teaching of EAP. This course is recommended for students who seek better understanding of English language teaching at university level in terms of both theoretical frameworks and matters of teaching. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description:
Understand the roles, and responsibilities of EAP teachers in different
educational contexts.
Analyze and explain the nature of academic discourse.
Critically evaluate core issues in EAP, in terms of both theory and practice.
Design teaching and learning materials based on needs analyses and scholarship in EAP.

courses.title: Discourse Analysis
courses.description: Discourse Analysis is the study of patterns of language within written and spoken texts and the social contexts in which the texts occur. The course aims to introduce key concepts of discourse analysis and a number of approaches to analyzing written and spoken texts. The course places emphasis on hands-on discourse analysis so students are able to familiarize themselves with the different approaches and become competent in the text analysis process. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Understand key concepts in discourse analysis.
Develop a grasp of key approaches to analyzing written and spoken texts.
Explain and analyze significant features of different types of discourse.
Apply discourse analysis in language teaching and learning.

courses.title: English-Medium Instruction and International Education
courses.description: English-Medium Instruction (EMI), an emerging educational approach, has become a global phenomenon in higher education and has received increasing attention in primary and secondary education. This course approaches the EMI phenomenon from a critical perspective. We will cover national policies and institutional practices in overseas and local contexts, teacher perceptions and student attitudes, drivers and difficulties for EMI implementation, etc. By the end of this course, students will have formed a comprehensive and critical understanding of the key issues in EMI research. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Explain the definition, origin, and current development of EMI research.
Illustrate the features of EMI development in different regions of the world and the historical, social, and cultural factors that influence this development.
Critically analyze different stakeholders’ perceptions of the importance, benefits, and challenges of EMI and why EMI is a contested notion.
Identify the challenges of implementing EMI in the classroom and potential solutions and coping strategies.
Apply research-informed principles or decisions in EMI curricula development and student assessment.

courses.title: Functional Linguistics
courses.description: This course takes a functional perspective to emphasize the way spoken and written language operate in different social situations. Using the systemic functional approach to language analysis, the course explores how grammar and discourse features can be used to teach language in context. It focuses on the knowledge and skills needed to design and implement effective language teaching materials that incorporate the principles of functional linguistics in the language classroom and examines the benefits and drawbacks of using a functional approach to language pedagogy. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the key concepts and principles of functional linguistics, including the systemic functional approach to language analysis.
Analyze different types of textual genres - including written, spoken, and multimodal texts – using functional linguistics.
Analyze and evaluate language teaching and learning materials using functional linguistic principles, and develop strategies for integrating these principles into language teaching materials.
Design research-informed classroom activities, lesson plans and assessments that incorporate functional linguistic principles, and evaluate their effectiveness in promoting language learning.
Reflect on the strengths and shortcomings of the functional linguistic approach to language teaching and learning.

courses.title: Chinese Writing and Culture
courses.description: An advanced-level study of the Chinese writing system as a quintessential embodiment and carrier of Chinese culture, covering its origin, development, classification and its orthographical and cultural characteristics. The course will begin with a theoretical introduction about the nature of the ancient scripts and modern writing systems from historical and comparative perspectives, followed by a systematic exploration of the internal structure of Chinese script in accordance with a newly-developed framework, i.e., the three-principle theory of Chinese script, by which thousands of characters coming from the archeological materials such as jiaguwen (oracle bone inscriptions), jinwen (bronze inscriptions) and jianbowenzi (bamboo and silk scripts) can be appropriately analyzed and classified. This course also offers a critical survey of important issues related to Chinese script in modern times, including simplification, Romanization (Latinization), recognition, and adaptability to various Sinitic and Sinosphere languages, taking into consideration research in general linguistics, sociolinguistics, and heritage history. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description:
Gain a systematic understanding of how Chinese writing originated and
developed.
Analyze Chinese characters and classify them into different categories in accordance with a new framework, i.e. the three-principle theory of Chinese script;

Understand the characteristics of Chinese script at its different styles, including the oracle bone inscriptions (jiaguwen), bronze inscriptions (jinwen), clerical script (lishu) and standard script (kaishu).
Better understand various problems arising from the current use of Chinese script.
Function more effectively in L2 Chinese language/character teaching and learning;
Identify the historical and cultural components implied in the Chinese writing system.

courses.title: Mandarin Chinese Grammar for L2 Chinese Teachers
courses.description: This course aims to equip students concentrating in Teaching Chinese as a Second Language with an in-depth understanding of Modern Chinese grammar, necessary skills in analyzing grammatical features of Chinese in a cognitive and functional framework, and capability of applying the knowledge and skills in practical situations of teaching Chinese to L2 learners. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Apply a cognitive and functional framework enabling them to identify, describe, and analyze major features of Chinese grammar, and convey the knowledge to L2 learners of Chinese in an accessible way.
Provoke students to think deeply about characteristics of Chinese grammar and apply the findings to the L2 Chinese teaching and learning process.
Analyze and explain key grammatical features of Chinese to beginners of Chinese in English.

courses.title: Advanced Phonetics and Phonology of the Chinese Language
courses.description: This course focuses on speech sounds in Standard Chinese. Its aim is to explain how different Chinese speech sounds are from the world's languages in general; and in what ways they are typical. This course provides a basis for understanding Chinese phonetics and phonology from theoretical and practical perspectives. It teaches students about how speech sounds are made by the human vocal tract and how they are organized for linguistic purposes. It will also equip students with essential knowledge in teaching Chinese sounds to second language (L2) learners. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Understand the fundamental concepts in phonetics and phonology.
Explain speech sounds (consonants, vowels and tones) of the Chinese language to L2 learners.

courses.title: Chinese Lexicology
courses.description: This course provides a theoretical and practical introduction to Chinese lexicology, covering general and peculiar aspects of Chinese words and vocabulary, including word formation, semantic and grammatical structure of words, lexicalization, development and evolution of lexical items over time, the relationship between sound and meaning, and the cultural dimension of words. This course will also train students in using language corpora and other online resources to investigate Chinese vocabulary and deal with issues related to second language vocabulary teaching and learning. For MA(ILE) students or students with program director or course instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Appreciate and analyze basic concepts in Chinese lexicology including zi (字) and word (詞) in different contexts; compound and complex words; idiomatic expressions; lexical meaning and grammatical meaning; synonymy; antonymy; hypernymy; hyponymy; word structure and word formation.
Explain Chinese word development over time and across different speech communities.
Recognize approaches and methodologies in lexicology, including aspects of lexical semantics.

Use corpora to investigate and develop lexical knowledge, and apply corpus-based method in vocabulary learning and
teaching.
Enhance abilities to deal with pedagogical issues in Chinese vocabulary teaching and learning.

courses.title: The Practice of Teaching International Chinese
