Describe, compare, and contrast different research methodologies.
Analyze the contextual features leading to particular individual, organizational, or social outcomes in a chosen business setting and problem.
Apply or adapt appropriate research methodology to study the chosen problem.
Develop a research paper with scope and quality commensurate with a top conference paper in the selected business discipline.
Present the research to an expert panel.

courses.title: Accounting for Managers
courses.description: The first part of the course provides students with a basic foundation and practical understanding of financial accounting.  Focus is on the design, use and impact of financial information and accounting measures in organizational planning and control.  The second part of the course is to apply and analyze accounting information in managerial decision making with the fundamental concepts of accrual accounting given in the first part.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Comprehensively explain major principles governing financial and managerial accounting.
Develop analytical and basic technical skills required to prepare financial accounting records and reports, as well as to use and interpret them.
Identify the role of managerial accounting in decision-making process of managers in business organizations.
Form critical judgement by identifying and defining accounting and business problems, applying analytical and quantitative techniques, and making and justifying decision.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Economics and Finance
courses.description: The first part of the course covers managerial economics: understanding of economics and the application of economic analysis in the context of the needs of management and of managerial decision-making in today's changing environment.  The second part of the course covers the basic concepts in finance.  Topics include time value of money, valuation of securities, capital budgeting including computation of cash flows, NPV, IRR, portfolio theory and capital asset pricing model, and rudimentary concepts about options and futures contracts.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Identify basic Microeconomic theories such as consumer theory, firms' optimal decision making under different contexts, and the operation and properties of perfectly competitive markets.
Recognize the Economics methodology and apply economic analysis in managerial decision making.

courses.title: Marketing Management and Strategy
courses.description: The first part of this module covers marketing management using the framework of the 4P's (Product, Price, Promotion and Place).  Topics include consumer needs and wants, marketing research, advertising and sales promotion, pricing theory, etc.  The impact of the Internet on all aspects of marketing will also be examined.  The second part will cover marketing and business policy from a strategic perspective.  Decision making in a competitive environment in the face of environmental constraints will also be examined.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Conduct a marketing environmental analysis and identify market opportunities that will be strategically fit with the company or organization.
Identify and evaluate segments, and decide on the appropriate target(s) within a given market.
Construct a persuasive value proposition and positioning statement for a given offering.
Formulate marketing strategies and make strategic marketing decisions, including specific marketing mix strategies.
Monitor and control strategic marketing plans.
Make effective presentations of a company’s or organization’s marketing plan.

courses.title: ESG Investing and Green Finance Strategy for Portfolio Management
courses.description: This course examines the different frameworks for incorporating environmental, social and governance (ESG) and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives. The various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, ESG integration, ESG engagement and ESG screening will be covered comprehensively. The full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes will be covered.

cilos.description: Understand different frameworks for incorporating ESG and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives.
Master the various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, integration, engagement and screening.
Familiarize with full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes.
Acknowledge traps and pitfalls in implementing an ESG strategy via case study of practical ESG investing application.
Understand carbon pricing and trading.

courses.title: Creativity and Innovation in Marketing
courses.description: This course will cover several systematic creative problem-solving methodologies which are appropriately implemented when a decision has been made to search for a creative solution. Apart from focusing on new product ideation and creative marketing actions, it offers skills to learn how to solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.

cilos.description: Master systematic creative problem-solving methodologies and its implementation.
Solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.
Understand product ideation and creative marketing actions.
Identify and resolve communications dilemma.

courses.title: Sustainability Applications in the Corporate World
courses.description: Sustainability is a topic of increasing focus for public and private companies around the world. With global environmental and other societal challenges increasing, and with increasing interest anticipated, trillions of dollars in market share are beginning to shift. This battle for future market share may well be won by those who respond best to this new corporate, policy and investment paradigm. This course provides students with the experience, tools and community of practice they will need to become an important part of this global paradigm. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand real-world applications of sustainability.
Develop responses to Environmental, Social and Governance challenges.
Analyze short-term profitability versus long-term sustainability and tradeoffs.

courses.title: C-suite Life
courses.description: The course aims to provide a simulated and role-play environment to enable students to apply their MBA learnings and experience in a complex management world. C-Suite Life is a real-time, live case study that covers a broad range of business challenges spanning the field of management. Full engagement from students is expected.

cilos.description: Analyze the crisis with managerial insight and instinct.
Generate well-structured solutions, actions, and responses timely when a crisis occurs.
Apply theory and practice for effective decision-making.
Develop a crisis management team.

courses.title: Enhancing Professional Skills
courses.description: It aims at helping MBA students work intensively on developing or improving some key presentation skills which will be useful to them throughout their business careers. Simply put, the essence of Enhancing Professional Skills as “Making a Logical, Effective and Persuasive Business Presentation". Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify the key issues from a tangle of issues, to analyze and develop solutions.
Create and deliver logical, effective and persuasive business presentations.
Enhance communication effectiveness.

courses.title: Business Plans Competition
courses.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to start a successful business from the business plan, to funding, to beginning operations.  Students will go overseas to participate in international business plan competitions.  Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Create ideas and formulate feasible strategies for startups or venture at early growth stage.
Develop and deliver persuasive business presentations.
Integrate and apply the knowledge learnt in business operation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

courses.title: Case Analysis Competition
courses.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to analyze a real-life business case.  Students will go overseas to participant in international case competitions.  Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyse a relevant  current case.
Evaluate various business solutions.
Develop and prepare a convincing presentation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Accounting
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in financial accounting, managerial accounting and finance to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. The course will also cover the basic business concepts, financial statement analysis, cost classifications and how to do managerial decisions. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in both financial and managerial accounting.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Evaluate cost-volume-profit analysis and apply core managerial accounting information to strategic decision making.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Python
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in technical skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. Python is used for creating high-level abstractions for well-written and well-optimized frameworks, where business applications rely on. The course will cover Python programming language for developing business applications, the practical libraries and packages. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in business programming and Python syntax.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in technical knowledge level among students from different background to assist  smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Design and debug Python programs.
Develop business applications with Python.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Data Analysis
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in quantitative and analysis hard skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. It will cover data and variation, probability model and association between random variables at introductory level. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in quantitative skills and statistics analysis.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of statistics and hard skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Recognize and describe statistical methods typically used in the analysis of business data.

courses.title: Fundamental Value Investing: Applications to Public and Private Equity
courses.description: This course covers value investing from a practitioner’s perspective and is oriented around the value investing framework and process culminating in an interactive presentation to an Investment Committee. Participants will learn key concepts and tools used in value investing, how to analyze and determine what makes a good business, and how to assess intrinsic value.

cilos.description: Identify and evaluate investment opportunities.
Develop value investment analysis, including analyzing businesses, financial modelling and valuation.
Recognize risks and the due diligence process.
Differentiate the commonalities and differences between value investing in private and public companies.

courses.title: Financial and Money Markets from Macroeconomic Perspectives
courses.description: The course will discuss the main financial markets, their characteristics and how they are linked to the economy. It starts by explaining how global financial markets are structured and how this structure services both borrowers and investors. Asset classes for investor funds are reviewed before the focus turns to the macroeconomic environment. Fixed income, equities, commodities and real estate are also covered in detail and students will explore how hedge funds and private equity firms create value for their stakeholders.

cilos.description: Analyze the impacts from the release of economic data.
Compare the key derivative products which are relevant to most major securities markets.
Evaluate time value of money, yield curves, the price/yield relationship and market quoting conventions.
Recognize the process of investing in real estate assets.

courses.title: From MBA to Stock Market: Applied Value Investing
courses.description: This course will deliver the frameworks and processes of value investing that some of the most successful investors in the world employ to manage and preserve capital. Students will learn to use quantitative valuation techniques, such as asset-based, earning power, and the value of growth, to develop a strategic methodology for estimating a company's franchise value. A number of case studies will be used throughout the program to improve students’ ability to manage a value portfolio. Graded P or F.

courses.title: Personal Wealth Management for Working Professionals
courses.description: The course aims to focus on several major financial products which are widely traded, but not widely understood, such as stock, foreign exchange, bonds, insurance and other derivatives. Students will learn about managing own personal wealth by using technical analytics skills to breakdown different common investment products and examine the impacts of behavioral psychology in the trading market. The course will also systematically introduce how the macro-economic cycles and megatrends affect businesses and markets. Students will acquire how to identify and analyze the investment opportunities, manage risks and articulate their views in portfolio construction. An overview of common insurance products available in the retail market will be discussed, with an emphasis on finding the right insurance coverage for individual needs, as part of one’s wealth management strategy.

cilos.description: Execute the portfolio construction.
Recognize the foreign exchange (FX) market, the commonly traded FX derivatives and the reasons for trading them.
Evaluate appropriate insurance package for different individual needs.
Apply technical skills to analyze different investment products.

courses.title: Economic Development in Asia: A Practitioner’s Perspective
courses.description: This course examines how economic development has occurred in East Asia, emphasizing the importance of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity. Throughout the course, students will discover growth opportunities for businesses in Asia not only from a corporate strategy and operations perspective but also from an investor’s perspective.

cilos.description: Recognize the key principles and practices of economic development, focusing on the role of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity.
Analyze and evaluate contemporary growth and development challenges faced by major Asian economies.
Identify and interpret the implications of growth and development challenges on business opportunities and investment strategies.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in business and management. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Analyse current hot topics relevant to the business world.
Address the challenges and opportunities from the selected business topics.

courses.title: Field Study Project
courses.description: This is a supervised study of a real-life issue faced by an organization, including identification of strategic questions, design of studies, collection and analysis of data, development and reporting recommendation. The projects selected should bring a meaningful economic performance impact to the sponsoring companies. May be graded by letter, PP or P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Develop a consulting project effectively.
Combine therotical knowledge and analytical skills to formulate solutions to practical business problems in real world settings.
Organize clear and engaging business presentations for a senior management audience.
Produce professional quality project deliverables including agendas, briefs, proposals, models and reports.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Study of selected issues from various departments under the supervision of a faculty member from SBM. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)

cilos.description: Identify a certain business issue.
Apply the knowledge learnt in tackling real business issue.
Analyse different aspects of the business issue.
Generate feasible, sensible and practial recommendations / solutions.

courses.title: Global Study Tour
courses.description: The course aims to expand students' horizon and understanding on the social, economic and business context of different cultures. Led by HKUST faculty, the study tour provides students with the opportunity to learn from leading professionals in selected locations globally through visits to partner universities or corporates, as well as meetings with local business leaders or alumni. Course duration will range from one week to multi-weeks. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credit if the locations of the study tours are different. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Advance social, economic and cultural knowledge in a global setting.
Adapt to local business practices to enhance leadership capabilities.
Recognize core concepts of business functions required for global business leaders.
Communicate effectively through oral presentations and paper writing.

courses.title: DBi Study Tour
courses.description: This course is hosted by partner schools in different countries. The tour gives an overview of doing business, including an introduction to the economy, history, culture and legal framework of the visiting country. Typically, it will include lectures on-campus and off-campus, corporate visits and meeting with local business leaders upon a range of industry sectors which will offer students a unique synthesis between state of the art academic studies and practical, hands-on experience. It is suitable for those who are specifically interested in doing business in the visiting place in future or in international business and enhancing their international experience. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify implications for the economy and business of different government and tax policies.
Identify the drivers of the economy, economic condition and global position.
Recognize the local market condition and impact of culture on business operation.
Develop top management perspective and design competitive business-level strategies for the industry.
Explain the role of local government policies with respect to international trade.

courses.title: Career Trek
courses.description: Career Trek is an overseas tour for participants to expand their business horizon and to explore the latest career opportunities in other countries. It mainly involves company visits to give students a practical understanding of day-to-day-operations in different fields of interest through meeting prospective employers to discuss specific jobs and career paths within each organization. Students can expand their networks, learn about the countries’ cultures and understand the hiring landscape in different regions across industries. The duration of the treks will range from several days to a full-week. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credits if the locations of the treks are different. Consent of instructor is required. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyze the professional culture of the organization they visit and explain how their skills potentially relate to a particular profession.
Identify regional job markets and the best way to successfully find a career in a specific field.
Develop professional connection with organizations and other professionals visited during the trek.
Apply knowledge about the world of work and career development to their lives.

courses.title: MBA Practical Internship Experience
courses.description: This course is to provide students with practical work experience. Internships provide entry-level, career-related experience, and workplace competencies that employers value when hiring new employees. It is also an opportunity to explore career fields. Students can gain a clearer sense of what they still need to learn and to build professional networks. The experience will enhance students’ knowledge and likelihood of success in post-MBA job search. Course duration and credits depend on the cumulative working hours. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credits if they have more than one internship. Consent of instructor is required. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Generate practical experience, insights and knowledge in a field relevant to their major of studies.
Apply major and academic specific knowledge in a workplace setting.
Develop connections with industry professionals which lead to more job offers.
Acquire technical and soft skills which only come with experience, including skills important for time management, discipline and self-learning.
Execute practically teamwork, effective communication, collaboration and leadership.

courses.title: MBA Career Development Program
courses.description: The course provides students access to practical and customized learning opportunities to be equipped with knowledge, skills and attributes to further advance in their careers. Workshops and training sessions such as recruitment talks and executive sharing can keep students exposed to valuable career connections, abreast with the latest development in the commercial world and trends in the job market. Through these career development activities, students will get to evaluate their own strengths and weaknesses, identify areas for improvement, collect feedback on interview techniques, further improve and formulate a personalized strategy to develop their career goals. Consent of instructor is required. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Confidently and professionally present themselves to potential employers via their professional resumes and profiles.
Identify resources and collaborators among staff, trainers, alumni, and peers who can help them in their career development process.
Plan their career timeline, options and goal, and accelerate their job search progress.
Analyze one’s career strengths and weaknesses, and essential continuous improvements which drive career growth.

courses.title: Global Network Week
courses.description: The course aims to integrate global horizons and foster cross-cultural, economic, and social understanding by immersing MBA/MSc students in another culture. Students will have the opportunity to study a short-term program at one of the top business schools of the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM) and learn from leading professionals in selected locations globally. Some of the GNAM member schools include INSEAD, HEC Paris, UC Berkeley, LSE, IE Business School, etc. Typically the program will include lectures on-campus and off-campus, corporate visits, and meeting with local business leaders, etc. This course may be repeated for credits if students participate more than once in Global Network Week. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Advance social, economic and cultural knowledge in a global setting.
Adapt to local business practices to enhance leadership capabilities.
Integrate learnings of global student peers from partner business schools around the world.

courses.title: GNAM Small Network Online Courses
courses.description: The Small Network Online Courses (SNOC) enroll a select group of students engaged in a common effort to build management skills. They are offered virtually by a member school of the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM), connecting students online for lectures and discussions, and collaborative team projects, developing teamwork skills and cross-cultural perspectives. The course may be repeated for credits if the SNOCs taken are offered by different schools. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Develop international connections with the GNAM member schools’ students.
Recognize the member schools’ counties market condition and impact of culture on business operation.
Apply top management perspective and design competitive business-level strategies for the GNAM member schools’ local industries.
Analyze the first-hand case studies from different countries to investigate the global business problems.

courses.title: MSc Practicum
courses.description: This course offers MSc students the opportunities to gain hands-on experience through real-world practice. Students apply advanced business concepts to solve practical challenges, enhancing problem-solving, teamwork, and professional skills. The practicum bridges academic learning and industry practice, preparing graduates for impactful careers in a dynamic business environment. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Gain practical experience and insights in a field relevant to their area of study.
Apply academic and discipline-specific knowledge effectively in a professional setting.
Build meaningful connections with industry professionals, enhancing career opportunities.
Develop technical and soft skills such as time management, discipline, adaptability, and self-directed learning.
Demonstrate teamwork, communication, collaboration, and leadership in real-world business contexts.

courses.title: MSc Study Tour
courses.description: This experiential course provides MSc students with an immersive learning opportunity through international or regional study tours. Each tour focuses on either a specific industry or a particular geographic region, enabling students to gain a comprehensive understanding of the job market and emerging career opportunities. During the tour, students will engage with industry leaders, cultural institutions, and academic partners to acquire practical insights and broaden their global business perspectives. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyze global business practices within diverse cultural, economic and industry contexts.
Apply theoretical knowledge to real-world business scenarios.
Demonstrate intercultural communication and professional networking skills.
Reflect on personal and professional development gained through experiential learning.

courses.title: Professional Development in Ethics, Innovation and Technology for Research Postgraduate Students
courses.description: This one-credit course is intended to provide basic professional training to research postgraduate students in the School of Business and Management. The course will begin with lectures and a workshop on ethics in research, which is designed to enable students to keep abreast of current issues in research and trends within the corporate, private and government sectors, as it relates to the impact and usage of technology. Students will be provided with the opportunities to interact with individuals in the corporate sector to engage in discourse of a practical nature. The mode of delivery will consist of lectures given by faculty and/ or guest speakers, students reading groups, discipline-specific workshops on various topics. Graded  PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Explain ethical issues in regards to research for human subjects.
Recognize such ethical issues as it relates to private information of clients in industry.
Identify new research techniques employed in their discipline.
Exemplify various impacts of new technology in business sector.
Consult and comment on matters relevant to the academic and lay communities.

courses.title: Science School Induction
courses.description: This is a one-year course designed for year 1 science students. It provides induction activities to help students adapt to university life, and to understand the program structure of the school and the meaning of university education. Led by faculties, staffs, and peers, students will learn and practice skills such as teamwork, communication, time management, and goal setting. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Express their opinions and concerns about their education to faculty members and their fellow students in both small and large group settings.
Participate in small group discussions on various topical issues.
Summarize the key concepts needed for effective teamwork and time management.
Search for and retrieve information on a variety of topics relevant to lifelong learning.

courses.title: Enrichment Project
courses.description: For Science students only. This course aims to provide complementary educational experience to students outside normal academic curriculum through engagements in internship or outside-classroom project activities related to his/her own discipline.  Students enrolled would work under the supervision of a faculty member and are required to submit a report by the end of the semester, in addition to other criteria set by his/her supervisor. Course coordinator's approval is required for taking the course. 1 credit is normally assigned for 40 hours of work. Graded P or F. May be graded PP. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Identify and explain the application key concepts or methods from their discipline in the internship or project context.
Demonstrate effective communication skills.
Identify areas of professional or personal growth experienced during the internship or project.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in Science.  May be repeated for credit, if different topics taken. May be graded by letter or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Explain key concepts, principles, or methods.
Apply appropriate scientific reasoning or techniques to analyze problems or case studies.
Communicate scientific ideas effectively using discipline-appropriate terminology and formats.
Critically reflect on how the selected topic contributes to broader scientific knowledge or societal relevance.

courses.title: Development and Management on Science Activities
courses.description: For Science students only.  Under the supervision of a faculty member, students are given an opportunity to apply scientific knowledge and experimental skills, through developing 6 to 12 hours Science courses/ workshops/activities for primary/secondary school students, and drafting the operation procedures.  They would also be able to polish their skills in aspects like resource and manpower management, team building, etc.  Course instructor's approval is required for taking the course.  Maybe graded PP.

cilos.description: Design engaging science activities or workshops.
Apply scientific knowledge and experimental skills in the development of educational content.
Demonstrate effective communication of scientific concepts to non-specialist audiences.

courses.title: Community Services Project
courses.description: The course is offered in a form of a community project at a designated non-governmental organization (NGO) under the supervision of the School. Students are required to attend all the training sessions, design and implement the service project / participate in the service learning tasks as instructed by the host NGO and/or the course instructors. By the end of the course, students have to submit a reflective statement in the format of a paper, a group project report or a presentation to demonstrate the attainment of all intended learning outcomes, in addition to other requirements of the relevant NGO as appropriate. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded PP, P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Demonstrate understanding of the social needs addressed by the community project and how scientific knowledge can contribute to meeting those needs.
Collaborate effectively with team members to achieve project goals.
Communicate project objectives, processes, and outcomes clearly in oral and/or written form.

courses.title: Career Building for Science Students
courses.description: For Science students only. Co-offered by the School of Science and the Career Center (Dean of Students' Office), this course helps students in exploring careers within the arena of Science and beyond. To achieve this, it guides students to have basic understanding of the career planning process, the current job market and employers' expectation in different fields. This course also equips students with practical job application skills, such as the skills for resume writing, aptitude tests, interviews, group discussions, etc. Experiential learning opportunities and individual feedback will be provided to actively engage students in the learning process. Graded DI, PA or F.

cilos.description: Identify own strengths, skills and talents.
Understand what employers look for and express a basic understanding of the job market requirements.
Produce a professional resume and cover letter.
Demonstrate winning interview skills.
Indicate the appropriate way of job offer handling.
Explain the key elements of professionalism in the workplace.

courses.title: Designing Your Life for Science Students
courses.description: Originated from Stanford University’s Life Design Lab (Bill Burnett and Dave Evans), this course employs a method called “design thinking” to help students from any program develop a constructive and effective approach to finding and designing their vocation after university. Through small group discussions, in-class activities, personal reflections and individual coaching, this course teaches students to use design thinking to explore many of life’s major challenges, such as pursuing careers they love and finding personal fulfillment. Topics include the integration of work and worldviews, ideation techniques, a portfolio approach to thriving, designing to increase balance and energy and how to prototype all aspects of your life. We also touch on the realities of engaging the workplace, and practices that support vocation formation throughout your life. The capstone assignment is the creation of an “Odyssey Plan” focusing on taking actions in the 3-5 years following your HKUST graduation. For Science students only. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Use design thinking to develop a growth mindset that is an essential foundation for life design.
Apply the skills of self-management, reflection, and way finding to chart a personal life and career path.
Develop confidence and self-belief to explore different career options.
Integrate different planning strategies to design a successful life.

courses.title: Great Ideas in Science
courses.description: The course is designed for students with no science background. Using historical great breakthroughs in science and mathematics as examples, the course intends to inspire students to appreciate scientific approaches and develop a genuine appreciation towards human curiosity in the understanding of the world and the power of ingenuity observation to overcome ignorance. The course is composed of 4 modules covering topics in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology. Examples of topics include geometry, quantum physics, forensic chemistry and theory of evolution. In addition, the course develops students' sense of enquiry thinking and foundation of scientific methods through various active learning processes.

cilos.description: Recognize fundamental concepts in the chosen topics of sciences
Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts by elaborating their applications or explanation(s) of key observation and classic experiments
Demonstrate basic scientific inquiry skills
Recognize the importance of the human curiosity in the understanding of our world and the power of observation

courses.title: Chemistry and Life
courses.description: The course aims to introduce students without an extensive science background into the chemistry of life and in life as well as some elementary units and mechanisms of life shaped by core chemical molecules and other compounds. Co-taught by lecturers from chemistry and life science, respectively, approximately one half of the course deals with an introduction into the chemical universe that makes life possible; simple sugars and complex carbohydrates, amino acids, peptides and proteins, DNA, RNA and lipids. Interactions and laws governing these substances and ways we can observe what they are doing are covered. The other half of the course is about how these compounds are involved in some of the basic mechanisms of life; from the functions and evolution of membranes to cells all the way up to humans and other organisms; areas covered include genetics and genomics, diseases, food and health, and biotechnology.
courses.exclusion: Any 2000-level or above courses in CHEM, LIFS, CENG, BIEN

cilos.description: Define the major classes of the molecules of life
Describe the structure and constituents of macromolecules
Differentiate the roles of different types of chemical compounds and the type of interactions they undergo
Propose suitable analytical methods for molecules, ions and complexes, organelles, cells and bigger assemblies on the micro- and nanoscale
Reproduce the effects food, drugs, infections and environmental factors have on cells and metabolism
Formulate the mechanisms involved in DNA replication and repair, transcription and translation and genetic diseases
List great achievements in science history such as discovery of the periodic table, cell structure and contents, the DNA double helix, genetic forensics and others and describe their story

courses.title: Scientific Understanding of Our World
courses.description: This course aims to provide students an overall scientific understanding of our world. This course will deal with fundamental questions, such as: Where does this universe come from? What is the origin of matter? What is the origin of life? What guides the human behavior? What shapes the development of the human society? What will be the future of this world? Students are expected to have Science background. Graded DI/PA/F.

cilos.description: Being stimulated to think about important problems in science.
Acquire an overall scientific understanding of the world from cosmology to living system to the evolution of human society.
Gain the ability to integrate concepts from different fields of study.
Develop a macroscopic perspective towards science and how it informs us about our world.
Develop a habit of independent thinking.

courses.title: Guided Study on Research I
courses.description: Studies under the directed guidance of a faculty member on a life science / chemistry / environmental science / mathematics / physics topic which serves as the first step in exploring and being exposed to knowledge of different disciplines and fields to build a foundation of interdisciplinary knowledge. An individual general written report and/or presentations of exploratory nature on self-discovery of future directions of research and/or various disciplines by young scientists are required. For IRE students only. Non-IRE students may enroll in the course upon instructor's approval only.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge, principles and use of tools in science at college level.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, and develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.
Access, evaluate and use library databases to search for relevant information resources.
Communicate effectively, both orally and tn writing, in the forms of general reports and presentations.
Show appreciation of science, arouse audience's interest in the beauty, logic and precision of science.
View issues in science with a global perspective in conjunction with scientific knowledge.

courses.title: Guided Study on Research II
courses.description: Studies under the directed supervision of a faculty member on a life science / chemistry / environmental science / mathematics / physics topic which serves as the first step in equipping the students with hands-on experience in supervised independent study. An individual written report and/or presentations on a chosen topic are required. For IRE students only.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge, principles and use of tools in science at college level.
Access, evaluate and use library databases to search for relevant information resources.
Apply appropriate experimental skills and quantitative reasoning methods, in conjunction with scientific principles to solve problems.
Make independent judgment and evaluate information critically by applying principles and methods in science.
Seif-evaluate their own learning progress, and develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, in the forms of scientific reports and presentations.
Show appreciation of science; arouse audience's interest in the beauty, logic and precision of science.
View issues in science with a global perspective in conjunction with scientific knowledge.
Recognize the important of complying with ethics of research.

courses.title: SCIE Cooperative Education Program
courses.description: This course is intended to enhance Science students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs offered by the Career Center or those as recognized by the School, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For SSCI Year 2 students or above only. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

courses.title: Teaching Science Using Innovative Teaching Tools
courses.description: This course presents a unique opportunity for students to experience the process of preparing learning activities in contrast to being taught. The experiential program will provide a preview to potential students who wish to pursue a teaching career. Students will develop teaching tools for secondary school students under the guidance of instructors. They will participate in organizing science workshops in which they will deliver their teaching tools through innovative learning activities such as analyzing movie clips using the knowledge of science. The experiential course also serves to strengthen students' concepts in science, and improves their organization and presentation skills which are important in future success. Instructor's consent is required for enrollment.
courses.prerequisite: Level 4 or above in HKDSE (1x Biology OR 1x Physics OR 1x Chemistry OR Mathematics M1/M2 )

cilos.description: Create and develop engaging teaching tools for effectively teaching science.
Communicate succinctly and coherently with secondary school students, delivering clear instructions and engaging them in a manner that captures their attention.
Plan, design, and carry out science workshop activities: mini-lecture, demonstration, and STEM project.

courses.title: IRE Research Project I
courses.description: This course is a one-term research project course specially designed for students in the IRE track. Together with SCIE 4500, these two courses comprise of two terms of research experience on a non-textbook specialized topic under the supervision of a faculty member, aiming to equip students with hands-on laboratory experience or independent studies and doing research reports. The course also aims at training  students’  research  communication  and collaboration skills through discussion on their research topics and presentation of findings to peers and faculty members in different disciplines / areas of research. For IRE students only.
courses.prerequisite: (for IRE students in LIFS, MATH, PHYS and OST) SCIE 2500; (for IRE students in CHEM) SCIE 2500 AND CHEM 3550

cilos.description: Explain knowledge, principles and use of tools in science at college level.
Effectively communicate in the forms of scientific oral presentations with professionals and/or to lay audience.
Self-evaluate and develop strategies to continuously enrich themselves for their whole-person wellness.
Recognize the importance of complying with ethics of scientific research and citizenship towards the environment and the community.
Show appreciation of science; arouse audience's interest in the beauty, logic and precision of science.

courses.title: International Research Experience
courses.description: Research project under the direct supervision of a local faculty member and a co-supervising foreign faculty member in a foreign institution/national laboratory, which aims to guide students to explore advanced cutting-edge research opportunities with international visions and hands-on experience. Assessments comprise an individual written report and a presentation on a chosen topic. For IRE students only. Graded DI, PA or F.

cilos.description: Apply appropriate experimental skills and quantitative reasoning methods, in conjunction with scientific principles, to execute tasks and solve problems at work and in daily life.
Work independently and collaborate effectively with peers in research projects and communicate effectively with professors.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, in the forms of scientific reports and presentations with professionals and/or lay audience.
Self-evaluate and develop strategies to continuously enrich themselves for their whole-person wellness.
Recognize the importance of complying with ethics of scientific research and citizenship towards the environment and the community.
View issues in science with a global perspective in conjunction with scientific knowledge.

courses.title: IRE Research Project II
courses.description: This course is a one-term research project course specially designed for students in the IRE track. Together with SCIE 3500, these two courses comprise of two terms of research experience on a non-textbook specialized topic under the supervision of a faculty member, aiming to equip students with hands-on laboratory experience or independent studies and doing research reports. The course also aims at training students’ research communication and collaboration skills through discussion on their research topics and presentation of findings to peers and faculty members in different disciplines / areas of research. For IRE students only.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge, principles and use of tools in science at college level.
Effectively communicate in the forms of scientific oral presentations with professionals and/or to lay audience.
Self-evaluate and develop strategies to continuously enrich themselves for their whole-person wellness.
Recognize the importance of complying with ethics of scientific research and citizenship towards the environment and the community.
Show appreciation of science; arouse audience's interest in the beauty, logic and precision of science.

courses.title: Young Entrepreneurial Syndicate in Applied Sciences Project
courses.description: In this course, students will team up to work on entrepreneurial projects under the guidance of faculty and/or mentors from industry. Each team will be assessed based on their engagement and preparation of a business proposal, which includes background and market research, product design and / or technology development, financing and operation plans. Outstanding teams may be supported to join various entrepreneurship competitions. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Understand the principles in scientific innovations which achieve and maintain the competitiveness of science and technology-based enterprise.
Apply functional knowledge to solve problems in management and operations of entrepreneurship in science and technology-based industry.
Deliver business proposal and communicate with lay audiences effectively.
Put in practice of team work in research, preparation and in enterprise perspective.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking for commercialization of product ideas in various scientific and technological fields.
Recognize the importance and impact of social responsibilities and ethical practices of a scientific and technological enterprise.
Evaluate and analyze the information relevant to contemporary scientific and technological innovations with a global perspective.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Identify comprehensively the current development and the original scientific or technical problems in the field of Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
Demonstrate mastery of knowledge in the chosen field of research.
Synthesize and create original new knowledge.
Demonstrate evidences for having made substantial original contributions to the field of study.

courses.title: Green Finance Case Analyses
courses.description: This course provides students with practical experience of sustainable and green finance through the use of case studies and real life situations. Cases from Harvard Business School, HKUST, UC-Berkeley and other institutions, as well as Yale-style cases based on publicly available information, with a strong focus on Asia will be utilized. Students will be put in the manager’s or protagonist’s role to gather and analyze information before ultimately making decisions. All students in this course are expected to have full and active participation under the seminar style instruction. For SGFN students in their third year of study and above.

cilos.description: Critically evaluate the core issues of sustainable and green finance situations/challenges.
Analyze the interests of various stakeholders that affecting the decision making.
Interpret practical cases in Asia context mainly.
Communicate effectively across different disciplines in sustainable and green finance.
Integrate interdisciplinary skills and knowledge to make practical recommendations.

courses.title: Humanities and Social Science Internship
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with internship educational opportunities locally and globally. Under the guidance of the course coordinator, students will undertake training and supervised internships with our potential collaborators (including government departments, NGOs, museums, media and press, cultural industries, social enterprises, social service organizations, business firms, and public corporations). Course assessment will be based on students' written reports and supervisors' evaluation. Cantonese may be used in off-campus trainings and internships, in some situations. May be repeated for credits. For students of GCS and QSA program only. Instructor's approval is required for enrolling in the course. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge to the real-life situation.
Communicate knowledge about the organization and operation of a particular job sector relating to the history, culture, society, politics and economy of China, Hong Kong, and/or the world.
Collaborate in team work.
Reflect on their learning progress, and develop a motivation for lifelong learning.

courses.title: Career Building for GCS and QSA Students
courses.description: Co-offered by the School of Humanities and Social Science and the Career Center of the Dean of Students' Office, this course helps students in exploring careers within the arena of Humanities and Social Science and beyond. To achieve this, it guides students to develop basic knowledge of the career planning process, the current job market and employers' expectation in different fields. This course also equips students with practical job application skills, such as the skills of resume writing, aptitude tests, interviews, group discussions, etc. Experiential learning opportunities and individual feedback will be provided to actively engage students in the learning process. Instructor's approval is required for enrolling in the course. Graded DI, PA or F.

cilos.description: Learn to write a professional CV and cover letter.
Practice varieties of job interviewing skills.
Get familiarized with proper business networking skills.
Have a basic understanding of job market requirements.
Know the meaning of professionalism at workplace and the appropriate ways of handling job offers.
Identify their strengths, interests, talents and values.
Have a clearer understanding of further study as an option and careers in academia.

courses.title: Service Learning in the Humanities and Social Science
courses.description: This course aims to cultivate students' humanitarian concern and social awareness through engagement in community services. It will provide students a variety of learning opportunities through community services programs initiated by the faculty of the School of Humanities and Social Science, or in collaboration with the faculty of other Schools and local or non-local NGOs. Students will be guided to apply knowledge in the humanities and social science to understand the needs of service recipients and the work of community service providers, and to reflect on their own active participation. Seminars, talks, training sessions, and project guidance will be provided to broaden students' horizon, build up their interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills, and cultivate their leadership and teamwork spirit. Corresponding to the objective and requirement of individual courses and respective course credits, students will be required to work on reports, reflection papers, group projects, and presentations. Cantonese, or other working languages may be used in off-campus environment, in some situations. Students may repeat the course if different topics are taken. For SHSS students only. Instructor's approval is required for enrolling in the course. May be graded letter, DI/PA/F, P/F and PP subject to different offerings.

cilos.description: Apply knowledge in the humanities / social science to interact with service providers and understand the needs of the service recipients.
Understand the historical, political, economic, social, and cultural conditions in local-global contexts that impact the life of the service recipients.
Communicate with people who are involved in community service including service providers, volunteers, and the beneficiaries in oral or written form.
Apply hands-on skills creatively to assist those who are in need in real life situation.
Evaluate the methods used in providing community service.
Develop humanitarian concern and social awareness as responsible citizens.

courses.title: Humanities and Social Science Co-op Program
courses.description: This course aims to engage students in working as an intern at an internship partner workplace in order to gain work experience while being guided by an alumni mentor and/or the staff of the DAO and SHSS program office. Course assessments will be based on students' written reports and supervisors' evaluation. Credits will only be granted for working at an internship partner recognized by DAO and SHSS. Course enrollment excludes SHSS students in their final year. Instructor's approval is required for enrolling in the course. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Have developed practical, hands-on experience in an industry related to his/her studies and/or career interests.
Have improved his/her communication skills and techniques.
Have applied what s/he had learnt to the workplace.
Have built an evidence-based work portfolio.

courses.title: SHSS Cooperative Education Program
courses.description: This course is intended to enhance SHSS students' career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For SHSS Year 2 students or above only. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

courses.title: SHSS Independent Study
courses.description: The course allows students to undertake a pilot project, explore a research theme or complete focused reading on a topic or a seminal book under the supervision of a faculty member. It is restricted to students in the BSc Global China Studies program. Enrollment in the course requires approval from the course coordinator. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply concepts from humanities or social science to articulate a point of interest relating to specific social or cultural issues.
Understand and analyze the cultural, philosophical or historical aspect of Greater China or world from the perspective of humanities and social science.
Explore preliminary research interest and develop academic oral and writing skills.
Develop a pilot project or a specific topic and practice self-learning and independent study skills.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: The capstone project aims to prepare students for research in humanities and social science, and may serve as an introduction to conducting research and writing a quality research project. For those students that do not wish to do a senior thesis, it will still enable them to learn the skills associated with a detailed research project and the presentation of research results. Enrollment in the course requires approval of the course coordinator.

cilos.description: Formulate, design and conduct a research project relating to Global China.
Apply and/or extend the knowledge and research methods they have learned from the GCS program.
Analyze the data based on the research.
Explain the value of the work.

courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Qualified students in the SHSS Global China Studies program are provided the option of writing a Senior Theses on an academic topic in a field of their own choice during the final year of study. The senior thesis is based on independent research conducted under the close supervision of a faculty member from SHSS. Enrollment in the course requires approval of the course coordinator.

cilos.description: Formulate, design and conduct a research project relating to Global China.
Apply and/or extend the knowledge and research methods they have learned from the GCS program.
Analyze the data based on the research.
Explain the value of the work.

courses.title: Honors Research
courses.description: The honors research teaches the student to utilize relevant theories and methodologies in a concrete research task. It requires the student to conduct more in-depth research based on the capstone project, to collect and analyze relevant material and to complete a thesis that meets academic standards of using citations and references, statement of a problem or an issue, and a clearly identified theoretical point. Enrollment in the course requires approval of the course coordinator.

cilos.description: Formulate, design and conduct a research project relating to Global China.
Apply and/or extend the knowledge and research methods they have learned from the GCS program.
Analyze the data based on the research.
Explain the value of the work.

courses.title: Innovation in STEM Projects
courses.description: This course aims to introduce STEM projects and state-of-the-art technologies in science and engineering to solve environmental problems in daily life. This experiential course will provide an overview to potential students who wish to engage in STEM education. Students will design and develop a prototype through various innovative learning activities under the guidance of instructors, explain the underlying scientific principles, integrate the multidisciplinary knowledge with innovation and creativity to critically evaluate complex, real-world problems. This course also serves to strengthen students' concepts in science and engineering, and improves their organization and presentation skills, which are important in their future study.

cilos.description: Demonstrate fundamental understanding and concepts of STEM.
Address challenges by integrating the knowledge, technical skills, innovation and creativity in STEM projects.
Employ methods to critically evaluate complex, real-world problems.
Communicate effectively in both oral and written formats to covey scientific knowledge and multi-disciplinary training to the audience.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Appreciate the interdisciplinary nature of STEM, and arouse audience’s interest in STEM education.

courses.title: Appreciation of Our Nature
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. The course aims at introducing the richness of diversity of living organisms around the world and their conservation programs. Local and global case studies will be used to illustrate the concepts. Course activities include lectures, field trip, and students’ project presentations. At the end of the course, students are expected to enhance their appreciation on our nature.

cilos.description: Gain the knowledge and understanding of principle concepts of the topics discussed.
Appreciate the pedagogical approach and learning experience at HKUST.
Increase proficiency in skills that sustain lifelong learning, particularly the abilities to think critically and responsibly and to access, evaluate and integrate information.
Improve oral and written English communication skills and be able to produce quality analysis and communicate ideas effectively.
Be inspired to explore further on the topics discussed to gain deeper understanding.

courses.title: Chemistry in the Modern World
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. Starting with fundamental chemistry concepts, this course intends to inspire students to appreciate how chemistry benefits our society. This course has both lecture and laboratory components covering topics of applications of chemistry to environmental and materials science and medicine.

cilos.description: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental chemistry concepts.
Explain the relationship between chemical structure and properties.
Discuss the role of chemical substances in everyday life applications.
Appreciate how chemistry benefits our society.

courses.title: Introductory Game Theory
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course is a brief introduction of Game Theory. It intends to give a glimpse of some basic concepts in game theory. Students will be taught how interaction of players be modeled in precise mathematics, and solve the corresponding mathematical problems. Topics include: combinational game; games in extensive form; two-person general-sum games; games in coalition form; ordinal matching game.

cilos.description: Appreciate how to use quantitative tools to analyse issues related to game theory.
Recognize the importance of applying rigorous and numerate approach to analyse and solve problem in game theory.
Apply mathematical modelling and analytic proofs to describe and explain phenomena in game theory.
Communicate the solutions of mathematical models of game theory using mathematical terminology and English language.

courses.title: Calculus: the First Steps
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. Calculus is an important mathematical subject with fascinating applications in a wide range of disciplines. This course aims at providing a general perspective on Calculus for students interested in mathematics. The fundamental ideas and concepts in Calculus discussed in this course include the following: challenging problems in the historical development of Calculus, concepts of functions and limits, derivatives and the shapes of graphs, areas and integration, anti-derivatives and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and interesting applications of Calculus in problem solving.

cilos.description: Gain the knowledge and understanding of principle concepts of the topics discussed.
Appreciate the pedagogical approach and learning experience at HKUST.
Increase proficiency in skills that sustain lifelong learning, particularly the abilities to think critically and responsibly and to access, evaluate and integrate information.
Improve oral and written English communication skills and be able to produce quality analysis and communicate ideas effectively.
Be inspired to explore further on the topics discussed to gain deeper understanding.

courses.title: The Physics of Everyday Life
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course discusses many examples where simple and basic physics theories are used to understand everyday phenomena. Topics include inertia, formation of typhoons, tidal force and tides, energy crisis, greenhouse effect, sound waves and the physics of hearing, light waves and the physics of vision, formation of rainbows, etc.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts covered.
Recognize and appreciate the pedagogical approach and learning environment at HKUST.
Enhance their lifelong learning skills, particularly the abilities to think critically and responsibly, and to access, evaluate, and integrate information effectively.
Improve their oral and written English communication skills, enabling them to produce high-quality analyses and convey ideas clearly.
Cultivate a curiosity to further explore the topics discussed, fostering a deeper understanding and engagement with the subject matter.

courses.title: Combinatorics: The Art of Counting and Its Applications
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. The objective of this course is to introduce to students various powerful counting methods such as permutations and combinations, recurrence relations, generating functions and so on, which can be applied to many real-world problems.

cilos.description: Understand the mathematics behind various counting techniques.
Apply suitable counting techniques to a variety of real-world problems.

courses.title: Amazing Innovations in Biotechnology
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. The field of biotechnology is constantly advancing. From finding ways to slow down the process of food spoilage and increase pest resistance to adapting organisms to clean up contaminated environments. New applications and biotechnological inventions are continuously being developed to help improve our world. The course is designed to be an interacting as well as a creative course to allow students to gain further insights into what biotechnology can be used in daily lives. Case studies will be primarily used with the blended learning approach to discuss the power of biotechnology with an aim to enable students to discuss, interact and express their views.

cilos.description: Understand the principle of genetic engineering.
Appreciate the ethical issues behind exploiting biotechnology.
Think logically.
Openly discuss scientific issues.
Practice the skill of self-learning.

courses.title: A First Step to Data Science with Python
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course provides fundamental concepts and techniques in the field of data science. Students in this course can take the first step in the world of data science by studying basic concepts in probability, statistics and programming. Some daily-life applications of statistics implemented with an open source package Python will also be discussed to expose students to practical issues of real-world data, e.g. in house pricing, in pricing exchange rates, in classification problems, etc.

cilos.description: Develop a full understanding of the main idea on data science by using statistical models.
Find a “good” regression line to describe the relationship between a response variable and an explanatory variable, with a given data set.
Formulate a statistical solution to real-data problems and interpret the results by using Python.
Carry out objective analysis and prediction of quantitative information in data science with independent judgment.

courses.title: A Logical Approach to Organic Chemistry
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course aims to introduce students to a logical approach to organic chemistry. The course first introduces some fundamental and general chemical knowledge, followed by a training on basic thinking skills for organic chemistry. The lectures will differ from high school organic chemistry class: throughout the course, the students will be encouraged to think about how and why chemical reactions occur, and the focus will be placed on explanation of chemical ideas rather than on the delivery of chemical facts. This set of skills should help them tackle chemistry problems in their school curriculum, public exams as well as prepare them for university-level chemistry courses. In addition, the students enrolling in this course will have a chance to visit the NMR facility of the Chemistry Department.

cilos.description: Demonstrate basic understanding of fundamental organic chemistry concepts .
Communicate organic chemistry using chemical structures and reaction schemes.
Predict the outcome of simple organic reactions and explain how they happen using curly arrow mechanism.
Analyse simple IR and NMR spectra and describe how these spectra are recorded.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Neuroscience
courses.description: The course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for secondary school students by the School of Science. This course serves as an introductory survey of topics in neuroscience, such as organization of nervous system, neuronal communication, the senses, and neurological disorders.

cilos.description: Describe the anatomical and functional relations between major brain areas.
Identify cell types of the nervous system, describe the physical and functional interactions between them and explain their role in the nervous system.
Understand how we perceive the outside world and move our bodies voluntarily.
Appreciate how research can benefit our health in the context of neuroscience.

courses.title: Physics in Movies
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. Physics is in our vicinity and movies are entertaining. Scenes of movies are sometimes described in a grossly exaggerated manner violating the laws of physics. By analyzing the situations portrayed in some movies featuring action, sci-fi, and fantasy, we seek to illustrate the correct and incorrect concepts of physics. This could help students think scientific and critical; and recognize the empirical, theoretical, and philosophical foundation of physics.

cilos.description: Use physical principles and basic mathematics to do simple calculations and order-of-magnitude estimation.
Judge critically whether the action sequences shown in movies conform to the laws of physics.
Communicate effectively with audience, and to collaborate effectively in a team.
Evaluate the ethical, social and philosophical implications of scientific discoveries and technological development.

courses.title: Matrix Algebra
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course is about matrices. Matrices are rectangular arrays of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns. The course defines matrices and shows how to add and multiply them. It also shows how to use matrices to solve a system of linear equations, and how to compute a matrix inverse. Students can also learn about determinants and learn how to find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix.

cilos.description: Understand how to add and multiply matrices.
Understand how to perform Gaussian elimination to solve a system of linear equations.
Understand how to construct the LU decomposition of a square matrix.
Define linear independence and orthonormal vectors.
Explain the Gram-Schmidt process.
Compute determinants.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix.
Diagonalize a matrix.

courses.title: Human Body and Diseases
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course aims to provide an overview of the structure and function of the human body. Fundamental principles of bioscience such as cell biology, anatomy, and physiology will be introduced. The relationship between human health and the environment will be discussed. Students will also analyze factors that disrupt normal body functions, explore mechanisms of disease, and learn about the prevention of diseases through the control of risk factors. From the physiological and anatomical perspective, students will be guided to analyze the marvels and limitations of the human body, and what they would do if they were to ‘re-design’ it. Students can also try to design, conceptualize, or build prototypes of devices that can be beneficial to human well-being or prevent diseases.

cilos.description: Understand the fundamental concepts of human anatomy and physiology, and explain the relationships between human health and the environment.
Analyze how diseases impact human health and identify relevant technological advancements in disease treatment.
Apply skills to work independently and collaborate effectively in group settings.
Evaluate information critically and solve real-life problems through analytical thinking.
Communicate effectively in oral discussions about scientific topics, demonstrating clarity and engagement.

courses.title: Mathematical Wonders in Biology
courses.description: This course is offered under the program of the HKUST Summer Institute for Secondary School Students by the School of Science. This course aims to offer an overview of fundamental concepts in quantitative biology, including biological numeracy, biophysical laws and quantitative research methodologies. Concepts such as stoichiometry, energies, forces, information and dynamics will be introduced to help students develop an intuition for the spatiotemporal scales of various biological entities and processes. Quantitative reasoning is at the core of all topics covered. Guided by examples from both classic and contemporary scientific findings, students will learn to move beyond phenomenological descriptions and (re)think biology in terms of quantitative and generalizable principles. Along the way, students will cultivate an appreciation for numbers, equations, and math models as effective tools for describing, comprehending, and predicting living systems.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a basic understanding of fundamental concepts and methodologies in quantitative biology.
Develop an intuition for the dimensions and scopes of common biological entities and processes in quantitative terms.
Perform back-of-the-envelope calculations for simple but biologically relevant questions.
