Important issues such as short channel effects, high-field behavior, hot carrier effects, reliability and device scaling for present and future technology will be covered.

cilos.description: Make projects  on the future CMOS technology.
Perform 2-D device simulation to generate the characteristics of semiconductor devices.
Describe the theory governing device reliability and aging process.
Describe the role of device models in the process of circuit simulation.
Explain the process of device parameter extraction to match the device model output to physical data.

courses.title: Microelectronics Fabrication Technology
courses.description: Process technologies in IC fabrication: epitaxial growth; chemical-vapor and physical-vapor deposition of films; thermal oxidation; diffusion; ion implantation; microlithography; wet/dry etching processes; process integration of MOS and bipolar technologies.

cilos.description: Understand the science and engineering of micro-fabrication technology.

courses.title: Integrated-Circuit Fabrication Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory course requiring hands-on work in fabricating MOS transistors.  Process modules including photolithography, dry etching, wet etching, metal sputtering, oxidation, diffusion and low-pressure chemical-vapor deposition will be covered. Student will also learn to characterize the fabricated devices.

cilos.description: Gaining practical experience of micro-fabrication technology.

courses.title: Advanced Photonics Technologies
courses.description: A brief review of modern optics theories, Fourier optics based devices and systems, fundamentals of laser physics, optoelectronics, nonlinear optics and laser spectroscopy.

cilos.description: Demonstrate capability to apply the fundamental principles of optics and photonics on technology applications.
Demonstrate capability to apply the fundamental principles of quantum electronics on technology applications.
Demonstrate capability to apply the fundamental principles of laser physics on technology applications.
Demonstrate capability to apply the fundamental principles of nonlinear optics on technology applications.

courses.title: Nanoelectronic Materials for Energy Technologies
courses.description: Conventional and unconventional fabrication of nanostructures including electron beam lithography, nanoimprint, chemical synthesis, self-assembly, etc.; size dependent electronic and optoelectronic properties of nanomaterials; large-scale assembly and integration of nanomaterials for electronics; energy harvesting and storage devices using nanoelectronic materials.

cilos.description: Understand the difference between nanomaterials and micro/bulk materials.
Learn the fabrication methods of various kinds of nanomaterials.
Understand the origin of size dependent physical properties of nanomaterials.
Understand working principle of solar cells and the role nanostructures can play in improving device performance so acquire capability to design nanostructured solar cells.
Understand the working principle of other energy harvesting technologies include thermoelectrics and triboelectrics and their applications.
Understand the working principle of energy storage devices including batteries and supercapacitors.

courses.title: Semiconductor Power and Energy Conversion Technologies
courses.description: Analysis of power semiconductor device technologies in the context of electric power conversion and transmission; emphasis on the understanding of the critical roles of semiconductor device technologies in power and energy conversion. The mainstream silicon and emerging semiconductor power devices technologies; material properties, device structure design, advanced fabrication techniques, and device characteristics. Critical device-circuit interaction issues and basic power electronics circuits will be covered focusing on the role of these circuits in electric power conversion and transmission.

cilos.description: Understand the roles of power semiconductor devices in the context of electric power conversion and transmission.
Understand the structure and operating principles of power semiconductor rectifiers and switches.
Apply semiconductor physics to analyze the critical performance parameters of power semiconductor devices.
Understand the mainstream silicon and emerging semiconductor power device technologies, material properties, advanced fabrication properties.
Understand the basic power electronic circuits and the critical device-circuit interaction issues.

courses.title: RF Microsystems: Devices and Applications
courses.description: Students will receive the following knowledge: Electromagnetic fields & waves, transmission line theory, Smith Chart, S-parameters, and Network Analysis; RF wireless communication systems; Properties of passive components; Impedance Matching network, RLC networks, and 2-port parameters; Microwave measurement and calibration; Simulation methods for EM passive devices: HFSS & PathWave Advanced Design System (ADS); Micron passive acoustic wave devices: resonators, filters, delay lines; Simulation methods for multi-physic devices: COMSOL; MEMS technologies for RF microsystems. This course discusses methodologies to synthesize and model the operation of several key passive components currently employed in commercial Radio Frequency (RF) microsystems. The operation, design methodologies, and equivalent circuit representations relative to RF devices will be presented.

cilos.description: Design matching network for RF systems.
Design RF transmission lines in RF systems to connect different components.
Utilize HFSS to simulate basic negative components in RF microsystem.
Identify the architecture of radio frequency front-end module.
Provide comprehensive, practical exposure to RF microsystem fabrication and characterization.
Apply slide making, writing, and presentation skills.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.description: The course introduces the important building blocks in modern computing systems including superscalar processor pipeline, memory hierarchies, network design in the multicore‐processors. The design techniques, evaluation metrics and optimization techniques will be discussed in detail with the example of real computer systems. The students will gain not only theoretical knowledge through lectures, but also hands‐on experiences through projects.

cilos.description: Explain the processor design and the collaboration between software and hardware.
Evaluate and analyze the performance of a computer system.
Develop the simple improvement of a computer architecture design.
Optimize the performance of program running on the commercial computer systems.

courses.title: 21st Century Solid-State Devices: From Principles to Applications
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive survey of solid-state devices developed after 2000. Topics include advanced thin-film device physics, next-generation transistors, perovskite and organic photovoltaics (including tandem configurations), memristors, in-memory computing, and sensors/organic electrochemical transistors. The course places a strong emphasis on quantitative electrical characterizations and luminescent measurement techniques, model-based reasoning, reliability and variability assessments, and device-system co-design, particularly for applications in displays, imaging, and energy.

cilos.description: Apply transport/band theory to derive DC/AC behavior of TFTs/MOSFETs and junction devices.
Extract contact/heterojunction and device parameters from I–V/C–V and small-signal data.
Evaluate PV device metrics (JV, qVOC, ΔEF), equivalent circuits, and tandem design trade-offs.
Explain memristor state variables/ionic drift models and relate them to IMC/neuromorphic tasks.
Compare sensor architectures (solid-state vs liquid-gated, OECTs) with Debye/charge-screening limits.
Communicate analyses effectively via technical write-up and oral presentation.

courses.title: Digital VLSI System Design and Design Automation
courses.description: Structured design styles; specification, synthesis and simulation using Hardware Descriptive Language (HDL); Structural chip design and system design; Circuit design of system building blocks: arithmetic unit, memory systems; clocking and performance issues in system design; Design-Automation tools and their applications.

cilos.description: Recognize, understand the flow of designing complex digital system such as System-on-a-chip (SOC).
Understand the use of high-level hardware descriptive language in design digital system.
Use commercial ECAD tools to design, synthesize, analyze, simulate and debug simple  digital systems.
Understand the design of the VLSI architecture for basic digital arithmetic building blocks.
Understand the circuit and architecture design of different types of memory blocks.
Understand the techniques of designing low-power and high-performance digital circuits and systems.

courses.title: RF/Microwave Circuit Design and Measurement
courses.description: Introduction to techniques for analyzing, engineering and testing of circuits for RF/microwave frequencies using CAD tools.  The lab provides hands-on CAD/simulation, building and testing of low-noise amplifier, mixer, VCO, filter, IF AGC, detectors and other circuits discussed in lecture.

cilos.description: Understand the concepts of the wave and distributive properties of various components (passive and active) and circuits at radio- and microwave frequencies.
Master the new concepts and new terminologies for RF/microwave circuit analysis, such as transmission line theory, S-parameters, Smith chart, impedance matching, etc..
Analyze and design RF/microwave front-end functional blocks such as linear and low-noise amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, using computer-aided design tools.
Implement, characterize and verify the RF/microwave circuits designs, facilitated by hands-on experience in the lab.

courses.title: Solid State and Semiconductor Electronics
courses.description: Crystal Lattices; lattice vibration and thermal properties of crystals; free-electron theory; electrons in periodic lattices; carrier transport; metal semiconductor contacts and semiconductor surfaces; optical processes.

cilos.description: Know the special terms (and meaning) used in semiconductors and devices.
Describe the device operational principles and the characteristics of semiconductor devices.
Carry out project research (literature search) on special semiconductor materials and devices.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Nanoelectronics
courses.description: Introduction to state-of-the-art development in the broad area of nanoelectronics, including concepts and devices for spin electronics and quantum information science. Students are expected to demonstrate the capability of applying fundamental principles to understand advanced electronic devices through hands-on homework projects.

cilos.description: Demonstrate the capability to understand new developments in the broad area of nanoelectronics in terms of their significance, content, and objectives.
Identify fundamental principles of new electronic devices.
Develop intuitions about new electronic devices through performing hands-on homework projects.

courses.title: Advanced Display Technologies
courses.description: Introduction of the human visual system, Colorimetry and photometry, Introduction of the modern TFTs, Modern AMLCD, AMOLED, Fluorescence and phosphorescence, Introduction of Electrophoretic displays, Color electrophoretic displays, Nano-material for displays, Electroluminescence and Photoluminescence, Quantum dot, Quantum rods, State-of-the-art development in the area of display technology: High-resolution displays (4k, 8k, and 10k), Local backlight dimming, Introduction to AR/VR display solutions, Holographic displays, Flexible displays etc.

cilos.description: Obtain basic knowledge of display technology.
Understand the design principle of LCD, OLED and LEDs.
Understand the design principle of nanomaterials for display and LEDs.
Understand the principles of AR/VR and Flexible Display.

courses.title: High Frequency Circuit Design
courses.description: High frequency circuit design for wireless applications.  S-parameters, front-end amp, VCO, PLL, power amplifier, and integration issues will be covered.

cilos.description: Develop clear understanding of wireless communication system design including link budget (Shannon's channel capacity limit, Friis's formula for radio frequency signal propagation), modulation scheme, and multi-access  techniques.
Analyze and design radio-frequency wireless circuit including low-noise amplifier, mixer, voltage-controlled oscillator, PLL, and power amplifier.
Demonstrate capability to analyze and design RF circuits using state-of-the-art computer-aided design (CAD) software.
Identity the device characteristics and circuit specifications that directly dictate the overall wireless system performance.
Evaluate and optimize the performance of RF transistor and passive components including inductors and transformers.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes
courses.description: Borel/sigma fields.  Sequences of random variables and convergence.  Spectral factorization.  Karhunen-Loeve Expansion.  Stationarity, ergodicity and spectral estimation.  Mean square estimation and Kalman filtering.  Entropy.  System identification.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the theoretical foundation of the methods of multiple random variables and stochastic processes.
Demonstrate mastery of, and critical understanding of, the relevant methods in random signal representation and analysis.
Critically apply the methods of multiple random variables and stochastic processes to address important questions in optimal filtering and parameter estimation.

Demonstrate the ability to address ECE-relevant theoretical questions using rigorous mathematical notations and derivation steps, and deduce important engineering insights from the mathematical solutions.

courses.title: Principles of Digital Communications
courses.description: The aim of this course is to provide an in-depth treatment of the theoretical basis, analysis, and design of digital communication systems. The first half of the course will focus on the theoretical foundations of a basic digital communication system, including source coding, modulating and channel coding, and introductory information theory. The second half will deal with advanced techniques including orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), multi-antenna communications, spread-spectrum communications, and cooperative communications.

cilos.description: Comprehend M-ary digital modulation schemes.
Identify the fundamental principles related to digital communication technology.
Comprehend digital communications transmission over fading channels.
Comprehend technical specifications and understand how and why practical digital communications systems are designed.

courses.title: Neural Data Representation, Generation, and Compression
courses.description: This course introduces state-of-the-art development in the interplay between information theory, data compression, and machine learning, including source coding theory, deep generative models, neural data compression, representation learning, compressibility and learnability, and neural network compression.

cilos.description: Understand source coding theory and representative source coding algorithms.
Understand representative deep generative models.
Have in-depth knowledge of deep lossless and lossy data compression.
Have in-depth knowledge of the relationship between data compressibility and learnability.
Implement deep data compression algorithms and deep generative models.

courses.title: Stochastic Optimization for Wireless Systems and Federated-Learning
courses.description: Stochastic Optimization plays a critical role in radio resource optimization of wireless networks, optimal control theory as well as financial engineering (portfolio optimization). This course will focus on the stochastic optimization theory and the application to the design and optimization of next generation wireless systems and federated learning applications. Topics covered include (A) Physical Layer Modeling: review of information theory for wireless fading channels, MIMO spatial diversity and spatial multiplexing, (B) Theory of Stochastic Optimization: classifications and motivating examples of stochastic optimizations [Type I stochastic Optimization and Type II stochastic optimization problems], theory of Stochastic Approximation, Stochastic Gradient, (C) Applications of Type I SO: Robust optimizations and Federated Learning: (D) Applications of Type II SO: Markov Decision Process, Stochastic Stability and Delay-optimal wireless resource control.

cilos.description: Learn the basic theory of stochastic optimization.
Learn the basic comm and information theory for the sake of modeling of the PHY.
Learn the basic techniques of stochastic optimization formulation for comm-related problems.
Learn the basic techniques of stochastic optimization algorithm designs.

courses.title: Convex Optimization
courses.description: Convex optimization theory with applications to communication systems and signal processing: convex sets/functions/problems; Lagrange duality and KKT conditions; saddle points and minimax problems; numerical algorithms; primal/dual decomposition methods. Applications: filter design; robust beamforming; power control in wireless systems; design of MIMO systems; GP duality in information theory; network utility maximization. For PG students in second year or above.

cilos.description: Learn the basic theory of convex optimization.
Read a paper and understand the optimization component in a critical way.
Learn fundamental optimization techniques such as majorization-minimization method, robust optimization, sparse optimization, low-rank optimization, SDP relaxation, and decomposition methods.

Learn specific applications such as low-rank optimization for matrix completion, portfolio optimization, sparse regression in index tracking, SDP relaxation for maximum likelihood detection, graph learning from data, Internet as a convex optimization problem, support vector machine for classification, etc.
Deal with a new problem using the learned optimization tools.

courses.title: Switch Mode Power Converters
courses.description: DC-DC conversion: topologies, continuous and discontinuous conduction modes, steady state analysis, loop gain analysis and relevant mathematical tools, stability and compensation; AC-DC conversion: power factor correctors.

cilos.description: Analyze and design the power stage of switch mode power converters.
Analyze and design the feedback compensator of switch mode power converters.
Apply and understand the limitation of averaging techniques in modeling a periodically switching system.

courses.title: Power Management Integrated Circuit Design
courses.description: Integrated circuit techniques for power management components such as voltage references, linear voltage regulators, low dropout regulators, switch mode power converters and switched-capacitor power converters.

cilos.description: Analyze and design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Use simulation tools to help design power management integrated circuits and systems.
Communicate effectively design choices and considerations via written reports.

courses.title: Mixed-Signal Integrated Bio-Sensory Circuit Design
courses.description: The course aims to systematically introduce major issues of mixed-signal circuit designs and their applications in bio-medical and sensory systems. The first half course is dedicated to mixed-signal IC design. The course starts with 2 review classes on OPAMP design, filter design and circuit noise. Then, the course covers topics on pipelined ADC, Sigma-delta ADC, and SAR ADC. The second half course is dedicated to sensory and bio-medical IC design. The topics include bio-potential detection, implants, DNA detection, CCD, CMOS imaging, and CT/SPECT.

cilos.description: Demonstrate in-depth understanding of fundamental theories of advanced mixed-signal IC design, and their application to critical mixed-signal circuit blocks.
Demonstrate understanding of the technological status of mixed-signal IC design field.
Execute critical analysis of state-of-the-art mixed-signal IC designs.
Develop skills of mixed-signal IC circuits design through practicing design projects in the course.

courses.title: Electronic Design Automation for VLSI Design
courses.description: The course introduces Electronic Design Automation (EDA) techniques for VLSI digital IC design. The modern RTL to GDS-II design flow and related tools will be explained in detail. Classical automated algorithms adopted in logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), routing, etc. will be covered. Simulation and optimization techniques of key IC design objectives, including recent research on AI-assisted EDA, will be presented.

cilos.description: Understand the RTL to GDS-II VLSI digital design flow and implement any given design with this flow.
Understand the simulation and optimization techniques for key IC design objectives and constraints and apply EDA tools to simulate and optimize any given design.
Understand key design stages including logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, etc. and use EDA tools to control design trade-offs at each stage.
Understand data structure and algorithms related to digital IC design and implementation.
Develop algorithms for key IC design topics and stages, including logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, etc.
Be familiar with recent research topics and works on AI-assisted EDA.

courses.title: Linear-System Theory
courses.description: Introduces modern system theory, with applications to control, signal processing and related topics.  Basic system concepts, state-space and I/O representation, properties of linear systems, controllability, observability, minimality, transfer-function matrices, state and output feedback, stability, observers, optimal regulators.

cilos.description: Get acquainted with advanced linear algebra applicable to a broad range of engineering problems.
Get trained in rigorous mathematical reasoning.
Learn the basic concepts and techniques of dynamical system theory.

courses.title: First Principles of Computer Vision
courses.description: This course focuses on the fundamental mathematical and physical principles of computer vision. It begins by introducing the physical imaging process, encompassing crucial subjects such as color, polarization, radiometry, reflectance models, and photometric methods. Subsequently, it explores the realm of geometric multi-view vision, encompassing topics like features, multi-view stereo, optical flow, structure-from-motion, visual SLAM, and NeRF. Finally, the course delves into the domain of learning-based methods including classification, segmentation, detection, and diffusion models.

cilos.description: Understand the principles of physically based computer vision.
Develop algorithms to solve radiometric vision problems, such as photometric stereo.
Understand the principles of multiple view geometry.
Develop algorithms to solve 3D vision problems such as visual SLAM, SfM, and depth estimation.

courses.title: Robot Manipulation
courses.description: Extensive introduction to robot manipulation theory from a geometric viewpoint. Rigid-body kinematics; spatial and body representation of rigid-body velocities; coordinate transformations; forward kinematics of open-chain manipulators; solution of inverse kinematics; robot workspaces; nonlinear decoupling control and force control.

cilos.description: Understand the fundamentals of robot kinematics and dynamics.
Understand the basics of robotic planning and control.
Implement robotic solutions on real robot platforms.
Advance technical writing and presentation skills.

courses.title: Introduction to Networked Sensing, Estimation and Control
courses.description: The course gives an introduction to the analysis and design of sensing, estimation and control systems in a networked setting. It consists of three parts: the first part introduces necessary background knowledge in communication networks, sensor networks, linear state estimation, MAP and ML estimators, Kalman filtering, and modern control theory; the second part focuses on analysis of network effect to remote state estimation and control; the third part presents some advanced topics including distributed state estimation and resource allocation through scheduling.

cilos.description: Understand critical issues in modern networked control applications.
Distinguish the differences between MAP, ML, MMSE, and LMMSE estimators and know their respective application scenorios.
Design a stabilizing controller for a linear Gaussian control systems using Kalman filter and LQR regulator.
Quantify data packet drop rate and maximum delays which may lead to instability of a networked control system.

courses.title: Introduction to Aerial Robotics
courses.description: This course gives a comprehensive introduction to aerial robots. The goal of this course is to expose students to relevant mathematical foundations and algorithms, and train them to develop real-time software modules for aerial robotic systems. Topics to be covered include rigid-body dynamics, system modeling, control, trajectory planning, sensor fusion, and vision-based state estimation. Students will complete a series of projects which combine into an aerial robot that is capable of vision-based autonomous indoor navigation.

cilos.description: Recognize the history and development of aerial robotics.
Explain fundamentals in rigid body dynamics and aerial robot modeling.
Explain computer vision and state estimation techniques for aerial robots.
Implement trajectory planning and feedback control methods for aerial robots.
Implement real-time visual-inertial state estimators for aerial robots.
Analyze performance of algorithm implementations, and improve performance in an iterative manner.
Design and construct a complete autonomous aerial robot system under resource constraints.
Debug and fix real-time robotics system.

courses.title: Advanced Deep Learning Architectures
courses.description: This course focuses on advanced deep learning architectures and their applications in various areas. Specifically, the topics include various deep neural network architectures with applications in computer vision, signal processing, graph analysis, and natural language processing. Different state-of-the-art neural network models will be introduced, including graph neural networks, normalizing flows, point cloud models, sparse convolutions,and neural architecture search. The students have the opportunities to implement deep learning models for some AI-related tasks such as visual perception, image processing and generation, graph processing, speech enhancement, sentiment classification, and novel view synthesis.

cilos.description: Understand a broad range of advanced deep learning models.
Have in-depth knowledge of the differences and similarities of deep learning architectures in various areas.
Apply learned deep learning models to solve a problem of interests with a written technical report and presentation.
Write programs in Tensorflow or Pytorch to implement several given deep neural network architectures.
Combine different neural network architectures to solve a problem.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Artificial Intelligence for Medical Image Analysis
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the latest advancements in the broad area of artificial intelligence and its applications in healthcare. It covers basic concepts of deep learning as well as advanced approaches for analyzing diverse healthcare data, including medical images, clinical reports, and biological data. Through hands-on homework projects, students are expected to demonstrate their capability in applying fundamental deep learning techniques to tackle various real-world healthcare problems and challenges.

cilos.description: Deploy deep learning algorithms to perform fundamental image recognition tasks using PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Gain a solid understanding of the latest advancements in Artificial Intelligence.
Acquire a foundational understanding of the challenges faced in healthcare problems.
Obtain the basic skills required to solve healthcare issues using AI techniques.
Develop the ability to execute projects utilizing AI to address real-world healthcare problems.

courses.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Algorithms
courses.description: This is an introductory course on computational biology at the molecular level. It will cover basic biological knowledge, important biological questions, common data acquisition techniques, popular data analysis algorithms and their applications. The major content of this course is computation-oriented.

cilos.description: Understand the fundamentals of bioinformatics.
Demonstrate mastery of, and critical understanding of, relevant scientific literature related to bioinformatics.
Summarize the key points from related literature, make comparisons among different papers, and carry out insightful discussions.

courses.title: Microfluidics and Biosensors
courses.description: Introduction to Microfluidics and Biosensors; Overview of microfabrication materials & techniques; microfluidic principles; miniaturized biosensors; micro total analysis system (µTAS) & lab-on-a-chip (LOC) for clinical and research applications.

cilos.description: Describe core concepts in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Describe trends and motivations in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Analyze/critique research articles in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Formulate a potential solution for a clinical problem using Microfluidics & Biosensors.

courses.title: Modern Engineering Research Methodologies
courses.description: The course provides a high-level description of modern engineering research practices. It covers topics including research mentality, the scientific method, evaluating research topics, literature search, report writing, presenting data, publication, research management, research ethics and technology transfer.

cilos.description: Describe the scientific method for doing research.
Distinguish and categorize different types of researches.
Evaluate the quality of research papers.
Develop a research proposal independently.
Identify different components in a published paper.
Write a critical review of a research paper.
Analyze the arguments concerning research ethics.
Explain the process of technology transfer.

courses.title: Professional Development in Electronic and Computer Engineering
courses.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students with basic training in teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills. This course consists of a number of mini-workshops. Some department-specific workshops will be coordinated by Department of ECE. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Acquire teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Selected topics in electronic and computer engineering studied under the supervision of a faculty member. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Acquire knowledge of special topics related to electronic and computer enginnering.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest. May be repeated for credit, if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Acquire knowledge of special topics related to electronic and computer enginnering.

courses.title: Departmental Seminar
courses.description: Series of seminar topics presented by students, faculty and guest speakers. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Acquire, enhance, and practice presentation skills.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Carry out Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.
Defend the thesis research conducted by the Thesis Examination Committee.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Carry out original and independent doctoral thesis research.
Defend the thesis research conducted by the Thesis Examination Committee.

courses.title: Frameworks for Strategic Analysis
courses.description: Explores economic principles of business strategy and develops an analytic framework for identifying and evaluating alternative strategies.

cilos.description: Apply the concepts of value creation, capture and added value to make strategic decisions.
Use conceptual tools (e.g. Porters 5 Forces) to analyze an industry.
Identify and articulate sources of competitive advantage.

courses.title: Analytical Approach to Uncertainty
courses.description: Introduces fundamental probabilistic concepts that enable managers to make critical business decisions in the face of uncertainty.

cilos.description: Apply tools of probability theory (e.g. decision trees) to help conceptualize and solve decision problems involving risk.
Articulate qualitative principles of decision-making, such as the “flaw of averages”.
Use spreadsheet models to represent and solve managerial decision problems.

courses.title: Accounting: Financial Reports, Control and Analysis
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the two major areas in accounting: financial accounting and managerial accounting.

cilos.description: Conduct basic financial statement analysis.
Identify how the three financial statements interrelate.
Interpret data in financial accounts in order to make business decisions.

courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.description: Introduces the importance of companies being market-driven and customer-focused and presents current theories and practices of marketing management.

cilos.description: Develop a marketing strategy and a marketing mix that delivers it.
Apply frameworks (e.g. segmentation) to analyze marketing problems.

courses.title: Leadership and Organizations
courses.description: Focuses on the skills and ideas behind effective leadership: working well with teams, utilizing your personal and organizational resources, making difficult but critical decisions, and negotiating well, all with a broad, multifaceted outlook.

cilos.description: Apply team-building approaches to create trust, shared vision and reduce interpersonal friction.
Negotiate roles on a team.
Identify common decision biases and use this awareness to improve their own decision-making.

courses.title: Statistical Decision Analysis
courses.description: Explores the use of sample data for purposes of estimating, predicting, forecasting, and decision-making.

cilos.description: Construct and interpret Confidence Intervals.
Formulate and test hypotheses.
Apply multiple regression analysis to make business decisions.

courses.title: Managerial Finance
courses.description: Introduces the basic techniques of finance. Topics include discounting techniques and applications; evaluation of capital expenditures; firm valuation; and the implication of financing decisions for shareholder value creation.

cilos.description: Assess the desirability and value of corporate assets, investment projects and acquisition targets.
Evaluate investment decisions.
Estimate the cost of capital.
Value a company using discounted cashflow valuation.

courses.title: Leadership and Decision Making
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to leadership and a managerial overview of the science of decision making. Successful organizations excel by the quality of their offerings and services in the marketplace. Internally, leaders and managers distinguish themselves by the quality of their decisions. Quality decision making is a competence that can be acquired and a discipline that should be practiced. This course offers an overview of leadership concepts and practice and a proven framework including cases for effective decision making.

cilos.description: Develop leadership skills and knowledge
Improve ability to lead the team in making the best decisions to achieve organizational goals
Provide a decision-making framework tested by many practical situations
Develop ability to articulate, defend decisions, and position for successful implementation
Learn the most effective leadership styles in leading the team to make the best decisions

courses.title: Operations Management
courses.description: Examines the basic principles and useful tools of managing the production of goods or services.  Emphasizes tools and principles that are equally useful in service and manufacturing sectors.

cilos.description: Design an operations approach that fits company strategy.
Analyze and evaluate an operational process.
Apply principles of lean operations and supply chain management.

courses.title: Accounting for Management Planning and Control
courses.description: Details the use of financial information in management. Topics include profitability and performance measurement and activity-based management and decision support.

cilos.description: Conduct breakeven analysis, identifying cost drivers (e.g. Activity Based Costing).
Create a balanced scorecard to manage their business.
Use management accounting principles to manage their business through capital and operational budgeting decisions.

courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Develops negotiation and dispute resolution skills through simulations set in dyads, groups, and multilateral contexts within and between organizations and across cultures.

cilos.description: Apply the central concepts of negotiation (e.g. Win-Win, BATNA, ZOPA).
Design an overall strategic plan for a negotiation.
Apply cross-cultural negotiation to resolve conflicts.

courses.title: Strategic Marketing Decisions
courses.description: Examines topics of new product development, marketing resource allocation, and competitive strategy.  Concepts are reinforced by playing MARKSTRT, a simulation game.

cilos.description: Apply marketing principles to make dynamic marketing decisions.
Communicate their marketing thinking through a strong marketing plan.

courses.title: Law and the Corporate Manager
courses.description: Studies the legal environment in which business organizations operate.  Topics include rights of shareholders, director's and officer's liability, mergers, acquisitions, takeovers and securities regulation.

cilos.description: Apply basic legal concepts to their businesses.
Recognize when and how to use in-house and external counsel.

courses.title: Foundations for Strategy Formulation
courses.description: Explores economic principles essential for the formulation and evaluation of strategy. Topics include industry analysis, strategic positioning and the boundaries of the firm.

cilos.description: Analyze how industries change and can be changed by companies.
Analyze the steps that organizations should take in order to be more successful as they navigate growth and change.
Identify which activities should be done by the firm and which should be outsourced.

courses.title: Deal Making in China and Asia
courses.description: The course offers participants the opportunity to strategize and be the decision maker in practical, real-world business situations throughout the Asia Pacific region, including China and India, which illustrate successful and unsuccessful deal-making strategies in Asia.

cilos.description: Craft deals through negotiations focused on a value-creating process.
Understand the domestic strategic objectives of the key players in China and Asia.
Formulate and apply practical, deal-making strategies to real-world transactions.

courses.title: Crisis Management
courses.description: Explores crisis management from the point of view of managers and consultants.  Understands the motivations and strategic capabilities of stakeholders, and the importance of value-based management in preventing and managing corporate crises.

cilos.description: Scan their business practices for reputational, political and regulatory risks.
Design reputation management strategies and processes.
Develop approaches for managing stakeholders, public opinion, media relations and public officials.

courses.title: Macroeconomics
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide a framework for addressing issues about the global economic environment.  It will then apply the framework to understanding the global economy.  It will introduce important insights in the labor, money and foreign exchange markets.

cilos.description: Identify the frameworks and tools of macroeconomics.
Apply these frameworks and tools to current global macroeconomic issues.

courses.title: Understanding Consumers
courses.description: This course will give participants an appreciation of how getting inside the mind of the consumer enables the marketing manager to design better effective marketing strategies, with a particular emphasis on effective communication tactics.  This course provides both a micro and macro perspective on the factors influencing a customer.

cilos.description: Develop effective managerial marketing strategies.
Examine the theory and research concerning the psychology of the consumer, with the goal of understanding how marketing managers can use these ideas.
Assess the appropriate use of consumer behavior concepts, logical development of conclusions and implications.

courses.title: Digital Marketing
courses.description: The objectives of this course are to 1) provide participants with an understanding of the impact of digital and social networks on customer behavior and marketing strategies 2) share conceptual frameworks and analytical tools for formulating and implementing marketing strategies 3) help participants understand best practices in digital marketing through cases, exercises and examples.

cilos.description: Generate customer insights and understand customer motives.
Accelerate marketing execution through Agile Marketing.
Apply Artificial Intelligence in marketing.

courses.title: International Growth
courses.description: The why and the how of corporate international growth will be analyzed throughout the course. In a world fixated by "globalization", the most fundamental questions for companies planning and managing their overseas growth will be examined. Successes and failures will be discussed in order to understand what management teams must do to get international growth right.

cilos.description: Manage international growth in the era of scale insurgency.
Plan and assess a company’s international growth plan for likelihood of success.
Connect the actions of growth with the talent and organization models.

courses.title: Private Equity in Asia
courses.description: Provides an overview of private equity, underwriting methods and various details in structuring. Focus will be put on the Asian market. The course is taught by the head of an Asian private equity platform.

cilos.description: Acquire a general understanding of private equity origination, due intelligence approach, deal structuring and valuation methods.
Identify potential sources of value in private, public, and closely-held firms.
Conduct venture capital and private equity transactions applying analytical framework and tools.

courses.title: Managerial Finance II
courses.description: The course deals with firm valuation and the implication of financing decisions for shareholder value creation. Topics covered include sources of financing and the process of raising capital, capital structure, firm valuation, leverage and cost of capital, and cash distribution policy.

cilos.description: Assess the optimum capital structure for a company.
Value a company using discounted cashflow valuation.
Apply principles of valuation to make value creating decisions in PE and M&A situations.

courses.title: Strategic Decisions in Operations
courses.description: The goal of the course is to understand how strategic decisions in operations impact the performance of the firm. The key will be to understand the link between operations configurations, the customer experience, and the financial performance of the firm.

cilos.description: Design an operational strategy linking operations, financials and the customer experience.
Assess the attractiveness of a firm’s operating system.
Evaluate whether to build or buy supply chain competences.

courses.title: Capstone
courses.description: This course is intended as a capstone for students' Executive MBA experience. Students will develop an integrated understanding of business planning and strategy and test strategies in a competitive environment.

cilos.description: Integrate their accumulated knowledge to analyze how different topics fit together in a C-level perspective.
Formulate a company strategy and execute it through multiple complex tactical decisions.

courses.title: Microeconomics
courses.description: The course will focus on the economic forces that determine the extent to which businesses can capture the value that they create.

cilos.description: Construct a fact-based, logically grounded analysis of a competitive market that will allow them to make educated conjectures about the likely path of prices in that market.
Identify the categories of cost relevant for critical business decisions.
Construct models of how government interactions shape the determination of prices and the distribution of value in competitive markets.
Make profit maximizing pricing decisions based on cost and demand fundamentals.

courses.title: Applied Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: Applied Mergers and Acquisitions is designed to prepare executives to succeed as members of an M&A project team. It takes the perspective of a company involved in M&A, not investment bankers or private equity.

cilos.description: Generate merger and acquisition plan to achieve corporate strategy.
Identify and mitigate the weaknesses of businesses and to bolster their combined strengths.
Identify commercial terms dynamics in negotiation.

courses.title: Strategic Human Resources Management
courses.description: Most organizations declare their employees to be among their most valuable assets, yet an examination of their systems and practices show inconsistencies in the management of this valuable asset. This course is designed to provide a basic understanding of five key challenges that general managers face in managing their human resources.

cilos.description: Explain, compare, and apply basic HRM concepts and techniques.
Critically analyze current HRM issues affecting organizations as well as defend feasible, well-thought-out solutions.
Develop fundamental knowledge, skills, and attitudes associated with the HRM profession.

courses.title: Leading a Global Company
courses.description: The focus of this class is to provide a thorough understanding of what is involved in leading a global company. Through a combination of lectures, cases and readings, the class will discuss and debate the key ingredients required to establish and manage a global company.

cilos.description: Apply the critical leadership foundation “bricks” to their own leadership role.
Design management processes critical to running a global company.
Apply the principles of Values-Based Management to their future leadership development plan.

courses.title: Value Investing
courses.description: This course will systematically present the fundamental tenets of value investing: search; valuation; and the construction of a portfolio. It will also introduce the styles of famous value investors and discuss the basic similarities and differences between them. The course is intended for 'active' investors who are willing and able to devote significant amount of time to continually research, select and monitor stocks.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental philosophy, style and tools of value investing.
Apply concepts in Accounting, Microeconomics and Corporate Finance to analyze companies and their stocks.
Demonstrate research report writing and presentation skills.

courses.title: New Venture Discovery
courses.description: The course focuses on the 'customer discovery' process, often referred to as "Phase Zero" in the innovation process. This is perhaps the most important moment in the life of a business. This is designed to help participants identify opportunities and then improve the quality of their ideas, whether they want to pursue an entrepreneurial path or innovate inside an existing firm.

cilos.description: Identify the process of translating problems into viable products or services.
Articulate a proposed solution in the form of a value proposition.
Develop a rigorous set of hypotheses to test with customers.
Implement the process of “customer development”, being evidence, not assumption-driven.
Develop human-centered research and design techniques.
Construct business model and prototype (using the Business Model Canvas).
Effectively articulate a business model and offer to key constituents.

courses.title: Managing Emerging Technologies
courses.description: This course provides a managerial overview of new technological innovations such as Internet of Things, big data analytics, AI, FinTech, blockchain, and cryptocurrencies. We will go through the technological foundation of these new developments and how they connect with each other to transform businesses. The course will conclude with practical advice on how to strategically utilize and manage these new technological innovations.

cilos.description: Identify the properties and trends of emerging technologies.
Compare and contrast different data analytic techniques, AI, and their strategic or managerial values.
Characterize the FinTech landscape and opportunities and related technology development.
Explain the key features of blockchain and its design principles.
Compare and contrast the purposes of blockchain payment transactions and smart contracts.
Characterize initial coin offering (ICO) and its business and social values.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: The course intends to explore an array of emerging business topics which business students should be made aware of. Students may repeat the course for credit as long as the topics covered are different.

cilos.description: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the concepts and theories on each special topic.
Apply the frameworks from class to real life by communicating complex ideas related to the topic in professional and other settings.
Develop an interest and appreciation of the intricacies in new emerging business topics.

courses.title: Introduction to Smart City Development
courses.description: Smart city development is a crucial area in today's public policy, technology, and business landscapes. This course provides students with foundational knowledge in this interdisciplinary field, focusing on public policy, technological innovations, and urban challenges. Students will explore Dr. Boyd Cohen's Smart City Wheel, covering six key areas: Smart People, Smart Economy, Smart Environment, Smart Government, Smart Living, and Smart Mobility. Through lectures and guest speakers from industry, students will gain insights into real-world applications and case studies. A special workshop on the use of open data and common spatial data infrastructure (CSDI) in smart city innovations. Assessments include formative evaluations, critical reflections, active discussions, and group projects. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to propose sustainable solutions, critically evaluate technology adoption, and understand future trends in smart city development. This knowledge will help them make informed decisions when selecting majors and minors in technology, social science, environmental science, business, and sustainability.

cilos.description: Identify the key concepts and terminologies related to smart city development, including public policy, technological innovations, and the challenges faced by many cities
Explain the six areas of smart city development
Apply open data to propose innovative and sustainable solutions for smart city development
Critically evaluate and assess the adoption of technology in smart city projects, considering both opportunities and challenges
Identify and discuss future trends and opportunities in the use of open data and geospatial data in smart city development, and critically evaluate their potential impact on urban environments
Adopt an inter-disciplinary approach to tackle complex real-world problems
Collaborate in group activities to develop projects that promote social improvement in urban settings

courses.title: Digital Information Governance in the AI Era
courses.description: This course explores how digital information disorder - including misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes, and AI-generated content - shapes public discourse, trust, and governance in today’s globalized world. Through interdisciplinary perspectives from media studies, political science, and technology ethics, students examine real-world cases from Hong Kong, Asia, Europe, and the U.S., and analyze how different societies respond to these challenges. The course covers key topics such as algorithmic bias, social media manipulation, media regulation, AI ethics, and platform governance. Interactive activities - including debates, policy simulations, and fact-checking workshops - equip students with practical skills to analyze and respond to digital misinformation. By integrating international case studies and ethical reasoning, the course prepares students to think critically, engage in informed debate, and develop responsible solutions to address digital information disorder in both local and global contexts.

cilos.description: Explore the historical development and global manifestations of digital information disorder, examining how regions such as Asia, Europe, and the US experience and address these challenges
Examine and compare diverse policy approaches and regulatory strategies designed to mitigate digital information disorder, while engaging with the key intellectual debates shaping media governance

Develop research and investigative skills in media analysis, fact-checking, and social media monitoring, ensuring the ability to identify and address digital information disorder in real-world contexts
Integrate interdisciplinary theories and methods to develop comprehensive strategies for mitigating digital information disorder
Apply ethical frameworks to assess the societal impact of digital misinformation and develop responsible, evidence-based interventions

courses.title: Cross-disciplinary Seminar
courses.description: A compulsory course for students enrolling in the extended major programs throughout their course of study. It is a seminar series presented by faculty members and guest speakers on interdisciplinary topics in extended major area and its applications related to the major. For Year 2 or above students with extended major. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify the basic issues of the extended major and the relation to your own major.
Explain contemporary global issue from diverse disciplinary approaches.
Develop ideas and inputs from cross-disciplinary sources.
Develop communication skills for delivering academic and professional presentation.

courses.title: Cross-disciplinary Design Thinking
courses.description: This course focuses on user-collaborative design methods for generating inclusive product solutions that integrate stakeholder and product functionality perspectives. Students will create specified product/ process /policy /protocol /plan (5P) concept models using recursive user feedback engagement methods, experimental prototyping, and divergent and convergent ideation strategies. Featured topics include design thinking; stakeholder research; concept development, screening, and selection; and interaction design. For students enrolling in extended major programs and students with consent from the instructor.

cilos.description: Explain and practice design thinking in problem solving.
Communicate and collaborate effectively in a teamwork environment.
Perform presentations efficiently.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Media and Culture
courses.description: This course provides an integrated introduction to the theories, cultures, and practical techniques of digital media, designed to prepare students for advanced study and opportunities in the Extended Major Program in DMCA. Through a balanced focus on both conceptual and technical skills, students will explore the aesthetics, theory, and practice of digital photography, cinematography, content creation, visual storytelling, media design, interactive and immersive media, and generative arts. The course combines lectures, workshops, demonstrations, and critiques, covering topics such as digital graphics editing, stop-motion, data visualization, AI-generated art, and virtual production. Students will gain hands-on experience with industry-relevant software and hardware, including picture and sound editing, digital effects, motion capture, and VR applications. Guest speakers and curators from leading institutions enrich the learning experience with current practices and insights. For students enrolled in the Extended Major Program in DMCA.

cilos.description: Explain and contextualize the key theories, culture, and practices of different forms and technology of digital media.
Analyze the evolution of digital media from artistic, cultural, and aesthetic perspectives.
Apply creative and critical design thinking to digital media.
Apply hands-on skills and techniques to digital media.
Design and produce creative digital media project informed by research.

courses.title: Sci-Fi Storytelling
courses.description: Sci-fi Storytelling offers a creative exploration of sci-fi topics such as perception of reality, existentialism in the multiverse, and philosophical and ethical questions on identity, AI, genetic engineering and so on. This course not only discusses these topics, it also offers students opportunities to exercise power of creative imagination and to practice art of storytelling by developing students’ own original sci-fi story. In this analytical, creative, critical thinking and collaborative process, students will team up to develop and present their story analysis and creation. This course offers visions of the future through studying important visionary film masters and related creative sci-fi works in films, TV and animations, which stimulate thought-provoking discussion and forward thinking. Students will combine sci-fi knowledge, art and technique of visual storytelling, analytical, creative and critical thinking to screen-related research, analysis, sci-fi story creation through world, character and tension building. For students enrolling in extended major program in DMCA and students with consent from the instructor.

cilos.description: Critically analyze the creative narrative content and cinematic form of the key sci-fi works.
Critically analyze the human, social and other thematic issues addressed in these works.
Conduct story research that informs creation of original sci-fi story with imagination.
Effectively present the original sci-fi story and research verbally and visually.

courses.title: Technical Theater Arts
courses.description: Offered by EMIA in collaboration with MTPC, this 3-credit Technical Theater Arts course delves into the backstage realm of theater production. Students will explore the collaborative nature of diverse technical disciplines in shaping a stage production. Through hands-on experience with hardware, software, and a custom-designed meta-verse training tool, they will study techniques that deliver real-world performance and presentation. The course also covers front of house fundamentals, field trips, and a performance-based capstone project, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of theater operations.  Students will be required to submit an introductory video and obtain the instructor's approval for enrolling in the course.  Interview may also be required.

cilos.description: Gain an understanding of the diverse technical disciplines, collaborative teams, and the operational workflow involved in theater production.
Understand the terminology of hardware and software in a theater setting and communicate effectively to technical personnel.
Appreciate the aesthetics of each technical theater arts and their collaboration with other disciplines.
Apply the learned materials in production & field trip.

courses.title: Special Topics (I)
courses.description: This special topic course will help students to gain a more in-depth knowledge and to have a better understanding on the topics related to their interdisciplinary studies or emerging interdisciplinary areas. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings or structured readings. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

courses.description: This special topic course will help students to gain a more in-depth knowledge and to have a better understanding on the topics related to their interdisciplinary studies or emerging interdisciplinary areas. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

courses.title: Practical Machine Learning
courses.description: This course consists of three parts: 1) the foundation of machine learning including its history and core algorithms;  2) the mainstream open platforms and sources for machine learning with an emphasis on practical applications; 3) case studies to illustrate how machine learning can be used to solve the problems from different fields. This course will equip students from different backgrounds with the essential knowledge about machine learning and practical algorithms, systems, and platforms available for solving real-world problems. For students enrolled in extended major programs only.

cilos.description: Understand the major machine learning algorithms like supervised learning, deep learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
Use major machine learning platforms like Tensorflow and PyTorch.
Apply the major learning algorithms and platforms to solve real-word problems from different disciplines.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent studies or projects under the directed guidance of a faculty member. Course requirements include readings on the relevant topic and a research or survey project specifically defined for the research topic. Credits assigned depend on the workload and may be repeated if different topics are taken. For students with approval from instructor for enrolling in the course. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge and understanding on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.
Articulate and present their arguments in a systematic way in a professional quality written report or oral presentation.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Design
courses.description: This course is to be taken simultaneously with a Final Year or Capstone Project offered by a student’s enrolled Major.  Students will apply knowledge learnt in the Extended Major and interdisciplinary problem-solving skills to solve real-world problems in their Major areas. Approval from EMIA is required to ensure the Final Year or Capstone Project integrates the knowledge of the extended AI major. If the enrolled Final Year or Capstone Project is in a major which is not the student's enrolled first major, they must also seek approval from their enrolled first major confirming that the project also integrates knowledge of their first major. Graded P or F. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Apply knowledge, tools and techniques learnt from the courses taken to a variety of tasks relevant to the students' major and extended major.
Design a cross-disciplinary solution to a challenging contemporary problem within realistic constraints.
Use project management and teamwork skills (if it is a group project) to deliver a solution within time constraints.
Demonstrate effective written technical and professional communication skills through final project reports and presentation.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Project
courses.description: Students are expected to complete an interdisciplinary Capstone Project with strong components in an emerging area of specialization under the guidance of faculty members. The objective is to train students to apply knowledge learnt in the extended major and interdisciplinary problem-solving skills to solve real-world problems in their Major areas. For extended major students who do not take Final Year or Capstone Projects offered by any majors only. Maybe graded PP.

cilos.description: Apply knowledge, tools and techniques learnt from the courses taken to a variety of tasks relevant to the students' major and extended major.
Design a cross-disciplinary solution to a challenging contemporary problem within realistic constraints.
Use project management and teamwork skills (if it is a group project) to deliver a solution within time constraints.
Demonstrate effective written technical and professional communication skills through final project reports and presentation.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Emerging Interdisciplinary Areas
courses.description: This course covers selected topics of current interest in emerging interdisciplinary areas which are not covered in the present curriculum. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. Maybe graded by letter, P/F or PP.

cilos.description: Communicate complex ideas related to interdisciplinary topic in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of impacts in the topic concerned.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent studies or projects under the direct guidance of a faculty member. Course requirements include readings on the relevant topic and a research or survey project specifically defined for the research topic. Credits assigned depend on the workload and may be repeated if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or PP for different offerings.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge and understanding on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.

Self-evaluate their own learning progress, develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.

courses.title: Introduction to Energy and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: This course provides an overview of fundamental concepts and principles in energy and environmental engineering. It covers a range of topics related to energy resources, conversion technologies, environmental systems, and sustainable development. Emphasis is placed on understanding the interplay between energy production, environmental impact, and sustainable practices.

cilos.description: Describe and apply the foundational principles of energy and environmental engineering.
Analyze and evaluate various systems and processes in the realm of energy and environmental engineering such as power generation, waste management, and so on.
Appreciate the interplay between energy production and utilization, environmental conservation, and sustainable development.
Form an informed perspective on emerging technological trends in the realm of energy and environmental engineering.

courses.title: Industrial Training
courses.description: This course is mainly for the module of internship and plant visits for Sustainable Energy Engineering students, offering practical training to students in the industry sectors.  Students are required to take both internship for a duration in the industry sectors and plant visits, learning solid skills to solve technical problems in the working environment.  For students in the Sustainable Energy Engineering Program only.  Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Gain exposure to the industrial operation of energy.
Apply technical knowledge to industry problems.
Address safety and environment issues relevant to energy industry.
Communicate technical results in an industrial setting.
Explore career options in energy related industry.
Pursue lifelong learning through the real context.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: This course is designed to provide academic advising to students, to enhance their understanding of the energy industries and career opportunities available to them, and to improve their communication skills. Students are required to attend discussion sessions with advisors and selected workshops and seminars. For students in the Sustainable Energy Engineering program only. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Appreciate the versatility and breadth of an engineering education.
Recognize the need and benefit of out-of-classroom, co-curricular learning experiences.
Develop a sense of belonging to the program and the profession of energy engineering.

courses.title: Materials for Energy Technologies
courses.description: The societal energy transition from fossil fuels to renewable sources requires novel energy technologies, with material design and engineering at the center of the innovation process. In this course, we will explain the enabling materials science and engineering behind advanced energy technologies by answering questions such as why lithium powers our batteries and why it takes silicon to make a solar panel. Major material challenges of emerging energy technologies will also be discussed. During the course, the students will be exposed to 1) the knowledge of material structure-property correlations used in energy technologies, 2) materials synthesis and fabrication techniques for their incorporation into energy devices, and 3) material evaluation principles in energy applications. After taking the course, students will be able to identify desirable material properties and potentially propose new materials and manufacturing methods for specific energy technologies.

cilos.description: Acquire the knowledge of materials structure-property correlations utilized in energy applications.
Understand operating principles of advanced energy devices.
Understand critical material challenges facing the adoption of renewable energy sources.
Study literature in multidisciplinary fields.
Connect scientific principles to daily lives.

courses.title: Sustainable Energy Laboratory
courses.description: This course aims to further students' understanding of various energy technologies and systems through laboratory experiments and to provide training in experimental techniques and laboratory procedures, data acquisition, analysis, creative and innovative design of experiments, and technical communication. For students in the Sustainable Energy Engineering program only.

cilos.description: Have an understanding on the operation principles of various energy systems.
Acquire hands-on experiences in fabricating components and operation energy devices.
Apply a range of diagnostic methods and approaches to analyze and determine creative solutions to a variety of engineering problems.
Conduct effective data analysis, and present findings in professional reportsand presentations.

courses.title: Special Topics in Energy and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest in Energy and Environmental Engineering not covered by existing courses. May be graded by letter, P/F, or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: (Course ILOs vary depending on the topic covered.)

courses.title: Photovoltaic Materials and Devices
courses.description: This course elaborates the fundamental basics, manufacturing, and process/device engineering of the commercial and near-commercial photovoltaic technologies from the perspective of materials science and chemical engineering. The knowledge imparted from this course will be key to the future chemical/materials engineers for the solar energy industry.

cilos.description: Explain the properties of sunlight and its spectrum.
Explain the basic principles of photovoltaics.
Explain the structural basics and PV-related properties of (near-)commercial photovoltaic materials (Si, GaAs, CdTd, CIGS, and perovskite).
Explain the methodologies used to process and tailor each PV material.
Explain the design principle and engineering methods of PV devices using each material.
Summarize the updated PV industry.
Produce a report and presentation on the cutting-edge developments of the PV industry.

courses.title: Energy Storage Technology
courses.description: Electrochemical energy conversion and storage technologies such as fuel cells, batteries, electrolyzers, supercapacitors, solar cells, CO2 reduction, etc. help overcome the energy and environmental problems that have become prevalent in our society. This course will deliver the electrochemistry fundamentals first and then focus on the principles, critical materials, limitations, current status and development trend for each technology.

cilos.description: Understand the working principles of each electrochemical energy technology.
Understand the advantages and limitations of each technology.
Know the current research trend of each technology.
Know the critical materials including anode, cathode, electrolytes, etc. for each technology.
Understand basic electrochemistry principles and their applications in energy conversion and storage.
Know how to write a scientific report and give a presentation.

courses.title: Final Year Design Project
courses.description: A one-year project course offers practice of engineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Each student will be assigned a component of a large project which may be sponsored by industry. Credit load will be spread over the year. For students in the Sustainable Energy Engineering program in their fourth year of study only. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Design processes and products in the realm of energy engineering to meet societal needs.
Develop an awareness of contemporary issues as they relate to engineering.
Solve energy and related problems critically and creatively.
Communicate clearly and concisely both in writing and orally.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Pursue lifelong learning as self-regulated learners.
Exercise integrity, high ethical standards, and care in their personal and professional lives.
Select and use appropriate engineering tools and data effectively.

courses.title: Energy and Environmental Engineering Thesis Research
courses.description: A final-year project course offers an opportunity to conduct individual energy and environmental engineering research under the direct supervision of a faculty member, which leads to a Bachelor’s thesis. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Energy and Environmental Engineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of energy and environmental engineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate research questions and outcomes effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of energy and environmental engineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to energy and environmental engineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Energy and Environmental Engineering Industrial Project
courses.description: This course is intended to provide final-year energy and environmental engineering students with practical hands-on training in the form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in a company. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Energy and Environmental Engineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of energy and environmental engineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of energy and environmental engineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to energy and environmental engineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Investigation Project
courses.description: Students conduct in-depth experimental or computational investigations on selected topics related to energy. The research experience will be beneficial for them to expose to cutting-edge research projects and apply for graduate school later on. Students work under supervision and are encouraged to use their own initiative to complete an appropriate program of work within the time allocated. Enrollment is subject to approval by the program director and supervisor. May be repeated for credits. May be graded PP. For SUSEE students only.

cilos.description: Be familiar with various research and characterization tools.
Be familiar with the research environment.
Know how to write scientific reports and present scientific results.
Know the current research trend of the research area.
Know how to conduct literature survey.
Know how to process and analyze experimental data.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: Continuation of ENEG 2990. For students in the Sustainable Energy Engineering program in their fourth year of study only. Graded P or F.
