Evaluate the effectiveness of marketing and advertising programs using relevant consumer behavior concepts and frameworks.
Make strategic and ethical marketing mix recommendations to enhance business performance based on the application of relevant consumer behavior concepts, frameworks and theories.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.description: This course covers the essential project management skills to ensure successful implementation of business projects. Topics include investment decisions, resource planning, budgeting, scheduling, outsourcing, and risk assessment and control, etc.

cilos.description: Analyze the core issues in project management and identify critical success factors.
Solve several project management problems with appropriate tools and techniques.
Compare and contrast different project management methodologies.
Identify the major project deliverables and when they are due.

courses.title: Business and Climate Change in Asia Pacific
courses.description: Climate change is the biggest challenge of today and tomorrow. Businesses contribute to climate change but also suffer from its consequences, while for selected industries it poses great opportunities. This course provides a comprehensive, interactive, and multi-disciplinary understanding of the threats, challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. The students could gain the competitive insights and tools required to be at the forefront of change.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a real-world understanding of the multifaceted business risks posed by climate change, and the strategic opportunities and untapped value that arise from taking action.
Identify and explain different developments in the region related to climate change and the possibilities to counteract it.
Summarize the diverging interests of parties involved in global climate policy negotiations, including governments, industry associations, global companies, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs).

Apply strategic tools for assessing the impact of climate change on firms, consumers and financial markets for developing successful corporate strategies to hedge against climate risk and embrace low-carbon business opportunities.
Implement consensus solutions, and experience the global dimension of the climate challenge.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Strategy for the Digital and Global Era
courses.description: This curated course offers a window to the real-world entrepreneurial journey, using contemporary case studies, class and online discussions, and collaborative projects. These enable students to better grasp fundamental issues in entrepreneurship: addressing root causes of failure, identifying a winning Minimum Viable Product (MVP), attracting investors, and succeeding in platform and data-driven businesses. Students emerge equipped to launch or join new ventures or lead entrepreneurial initiatives within established organizations.

cilos.description: Understand and use key theoretical concepts in entrepreneurship and innovation from strategy and organizational perspectives.
Evaluate the interplay of start-ups, investors, governments, and other key players in today’s ecosystem.
Generate creative business ideas and evaluate their feasibility as entrepreneurial opportunities.
Communicate entrepreneurial ideas effectively to prospective investors and customers.
Assess the role of established corporations in driving innovation, and the interplay between them and new business ventures.
Identify the tradeoffs involving co-founders, hires, investors, and alliance partners in the start-up.

courses.title: Management and Decision Making with Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: In the rapidly evolving landscape of modern business, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a cornerstone technology driving strategic decision-making processes. This course is a comprehensive course designed to equip current and future leaders with the knowledge and skills necessary to leverage AI tools effectively in managerial contexts. Over this course, participants will dive into the fundamentals of AI, exploring how machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics can inform and enhance decision-making in various business domains. By the end of this course, participants will have a solid foundation in managing with AI, ready to harness its potential to transform decision-making and competitive strategies across multiple industries.

cilos.description: Identify opportunities where AI can add value to decision-making processes.
Evaluate the capabilities and limitations of current AI-based decision-making technologies.
Implement AI tools to analyze data, forecast trends, and make informed strategic decisions.
Navigate the ethical and societal implications of deploying AI-based decision-making technologies in business settings.
Cultivate a mindset of innovation and agility, preparing them to lead in a technology-driven future.

courses.title: The Art and Science of Crisis Negotiation and Management
courses.description: Conflict is an unavoidable human phenomenon. Wherever people interact, arising from different preferences and perspectives. Effective communication and negotiation skills are essential to navigate challenges and unlock positive outcomes. This course aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills and mindset to navigate, manage and resolve conflicts for themselves and others. Students will be introduced to concepts like active listening, the Behavioral Change Stairway Model and key strategies for managing challenging people and building collaboration. Through this course, students will undertake a journey of self-discovery, exploring their strengths and limitations in understanding themselves and others. Adopting a person-centered approach, the curriculum will focus on enhancing each student's innate motivation to change, turning moments of difficulty into opportunities for growth, understanding and positive transformation.

cilos.description: Understand the basic knowledge, attitude and skills in communication.
Acknowledge the importance of developing holistic wellness in preparing for daily challenges and crisis.
Identify and critique their own basic communication style, identifying areas of strength and areas for development.
Identify and demonstrate non-verbal behaviors and skills which indicate relationship attending.
Identify the occurrence of conflict, de-escalate the situation, and facilitate a collaborative and mutually beneficial resolution.
Demonstrate appropriate use of listening and communication skills in managing conflicts.
Apply active listening skills in crisis situations in the workplace.

courses.title: Leveraging Personality in the Workplace
courses.description: This course covers major psychological perspectives and current research on personality. It provides an in-depth examination of how personality theories can be applied to understanding personality in the workplace.

cilos.description: Recognize the major perspectives of personality psychology.
Demonstrate how to integrate different perspectives to analyze a subject.
Demonstrate the ability to read, summarize, interpret, and integrate information pertinent to personality-related topics.
Identify a research question, devise an action plan to conduct a study, gather and analyze the relevant information, and present the findings in a written report.

courses.title: Skill Seminar I
courses.description: This skill seminar will be offered to develop the students' essential business and communication skills necessary to work in a global business environment such as communication, teamwork, negotiation and presentation skills. Some possible skill seminars include topics on time management, inter-cultural skills, group work abilities, international negotiation techniques, presentation skills, to name a few.

cilos.description: Develop essential business communication skills for various business objectives in a global context.
Deliver well prepared and organized writing and presentation results.

courses.title: Skill Seminar II
courses.description: This skill seminar will be offered to develop the students' essential business and communication skills necessary to work in a global business environment such as communication, teamwork, negotiation and presentation skills. Some possible skill seminars include topics on time management, inter-cultural skills, group work abilities, international negotiation techniques, presentation skills, to name a few. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Develop essential business communication skills for various business objectives in a global context.
Broaden international business prospects for various companies.
Discuss and interact with key managers from different firms.

courses.title: Business Project
courses.description: This is a supervised study of a real-life issued faced by an organization, including identification of strategic questions, design of studies, collection and analysis of data, development and reporting recommendation. Students will develop consultant-client relationship with the participating sponsoring companies and work in teams to conduct a strategically focused study which results in a comprehensive report containing analyses and practical recommendations for management decision making.

cilos.description: Create professional quality project deliverables including agendas, briefs, proposals, models and reports.
Manage a business project effectively.
Integrate disciplinary knowledge and apply appropriate analytical tools in formulating solutions to practical business problems in real world settings.
Deliver clear and engaging business presentations for a senior management audience.

courses.title: International Internship
courses.description: Students are required to work on a minimum of 10-week international internship to get practical work experience to prepare for graduate employment. The location of international internship together with students' home country, home school and exchange school must cover at least three countries. Students' performance in the internship will be assessed and evaluated by the company upon completion of the internship. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Solve management problems in a real global business environment by integrating various trainings from the program.
Deliver good performance with evaluations from corporations.

courses.title: Foundations of Data Analytics
courses.description: This course will provide fundamental techniques for data analytics, including data collection, data extraction, data integration and data cleansing. The students will learn how to manage and optimize the analytics value chain, including collecting and extracting the suitable values, selecting the right data processing processes, integrating the data from various resources, data governance, security and privacy for Big Data applications.

cilos.description: Identify useful data to extract and collect.
Use skills of data integration to integrate heterogeneous data.
Apply data cleaning technique to clean dirty data.
Use various data analytic techniques to help decision making.

courses.title: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
courses.description: Data mining has recently emerged as a major field of research and applications. Aimed at extracting useful and interesting knowledge from large data repositories such as databases and the Web, data mining integrates techniques from the fields of database, statistics and AI.

cilos.description: Apply the clustering techniques to find clusters within the data.
Use the classification techniques to conduct classification and predication.
Use the knowledge of frequent pattern mining to discover patterns from the data.
Conduct mining over social media and text data and detect outliers from the data.

courses.title: Big Data Computing
courses.description: Big data systems, including Cloud Computing and parallel data processing frameworks, emerge as enabling technologies in managing and mining the massive amount of data across hundreds or even thousands of commodity servers in datacenters. This course exposes students to both the theory and hands-on experience of this new technology. The course will cover the following topics. (1) Basic concepts of Cloud Computing and production Cloud services; (2) MapReduce - the de facto datacenter-scale programming abstraction - and its open source implementation of Hadoop. (3) Apache Spark - a new generation parallel processing framework - and its infrastructure, programming model, cluster deployment, tuning and debugging, as well as a number of specialized data processing systems built on top of Spark.

cilos.description: Build a Hadoop Ecosystem.
Manage the data over Spark systems.
Apply the knowledge of Spark and Hadoop Ecosystems for maintaining and monitoring Big Data Computing Systems.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods for Data Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce mathematical formulations and computational methods (convex/non-convex optimization) to exploit structures contained in the data. Moreover, specific computational methods (Randomized computational methods) will be explored for big data analysis.

cilos.description: Represent the Big Data with structured data models.
Apply convex and non-convex approaches for various Big Data optimization tasks.
Apply randomized optimization techniques to get approximate solutions for optimization problems on Big Data.

courses.title: Data Visualization
courses.description: This course will introduce visualization techniques for data from everyday life, social media, business, scientific computing, medical imaging, etc. The topics include human visual system and perception, visual design principles, open- source visualization tools and systems, visualization techniques for CT/MRI data, computational fluid dynamics, graphs and networks, time-series data, text and documents, Twitter data, and spatio-temporal data.

cilos.description: Apply human visual system and perception on designing a visual system.
Use open-source visualization tools and systems to complete various design and visualization tasks.
Visualize different types of data including graphs, networks, texts, documents, social media and spatio-temporal data with the visualization techniques.

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis of Financial Time Series
courses.description: Analysis of asset returns: autocorrelation, predictability and prediction. Volatility models: GARCH- type models, long range dependence. High frequency data analysis: transactions data, duration. Markov switching and threshold models. Multivariate time series: cointegration models and vector GARCH model.

cilos.description: Recognize market indexes, financial time series and their features.
Recognize the foundation of time series and basic time series models.
Formulate time series models to study financial data, including market returns and volatility.
Evaluate the relationships of different markets via the cointegration time series and ECM models.
Analyze the real financial data with the statistical techniques from this course via a course project.

courses.title: Optimization and Matrix Computation
courses.description: The course will introduce basic techniques about optimization, including unconstrained optimization and constrained optimization, and matrix computation, including matrix analysis, linear systems, orthogonalization and least squares and eigenvalue problems.

cilos.description: Apply unconstrained optimization and constrained optimization techniques on data optimization problems.
Carry out various data analysis tasks over Matrixes by using Matrix computation techniques.
Use optimization and Matrix computation techniques together to solve real-life optimization problems, such as community detection or leadership discovery.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Computing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to social information network analysis and engineering. Students will learn both mathematical and programming knowledge for analyzing the structures and dynamics of typical social information networks (e.g. Facebook, Twitter, and MSN). They will also learn how social metrics can be used to improve computer system design as people are the networks. It will cover topics such as small world phenomenon; contagion tipping and influence in networks; models of network formation and evolution; the web graph and PageRank; social graphs and community detection; measuring centrality; greedy routing and navigations in networks; introduction to game theory and strategic behavior; social engineering; and principles of computer system design.

cilos.description: Use the knowledge of social networks to discover influential nodes and communities.
Identify human behavior on social networks and recommend events or users based on user profiles and connections.
Recognize the influence of nodes and edges and design viral marketing based on social influence analysis.

courses.title: Parallel Programming
courses.description: Introduction to parallel computer architectures; principles of parallel algorithm design; shared-memory programming models; message passing programming models used for cluster computing; data-parallel programming models for GPUs; case studies of parallel algorithms, systems, and applications; hands-on experience with writing parallel programs for tasks of interest.

cilos.description: Apply principles of parallel algorithm design to verify the correctness of parallel programs.
Design and deploy parallel programs on shared-memory programming models.
Design and deploy parallel programs on shared-nothing programming models via message passing.
Improve execution efficiency via parallel programming models for GPUs.

courses.title: Image Processing and Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce the basic techniques for image data processing and analysis. Topics include image processing and analysis in spatial and frequency domains, image restoration and compression, image segmentation and registration, morphological image processing, representation and description, feature description, face recognition, iris recognition, fingerprint recognition, image analysis topics, such as medical image analysis.

cilos.description: Enhance image quality or effect by applying image representation, restoration and filtering.
Apply segmentation, registration and compression techniques to reduce the volume of images.
Apply various image analysis techniques on different recognition tasks and pattern discovery on media images.

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: The course introduces fundamentals of machine learning, including concept learning, evaluating hypotheses, supervised learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning, Bayesian learning, ensemble methods.

cilos.description: Apply concept and decision tree learnings to various decision making tasks.
Use Bayesian learning and Artificial Neural Networks for classifications and recommendations.
Use computational learning theory to improve the learning efficiency.
Identify the requirements of learning tasks and apply suitable learning techniques.

courses.title: Statistical Prediction
courses.description: This course will introduce statistical predication models and algorithms, including regression models, classification, additive models, graphical models and network, model assessment and selection, model inference and model averaging.

cilos.description: Conduct prediction based on statistical models.
Investigate different predication tasks and apply different models.
Revise the current statistical models to meet the requirements of real-life predication problems.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course will cover advanced topics in AI including machine learning, agent design, mulitiagent systems, game search, natural language processing and knowledge representation and reasoning systems.

cilos.description: Examine and formulate problems as AI heuristic search problem.
Model and design autonomous agents.
Examine and formulate multiagent problems as games.
Examine and formulate problems as machine learning problem.
Integrate reasoning and machine learning in natural language understanding.

courses.title: Deep Learning Meets Computer Vision: Practice and Applications
courses.description: Computer vision and relevant algorithms have started to make their way in various applications and become more relevant in our daily life: face detection, drones, and self-driving cars to name a few. Recent developments in deep neural network architectures, large datasets and training techniques have greatly advanced the performance of these state-of-the-art visual recognition systems. This course will investigate common deep learning architectures with a focus on learning effective models for various computer vision tasks. Part of the course evaluation involves student-proposed course projects focusing on building a working computer vision system using deep learning algorithms and techniques.

cilos.description: Put together a simple image classification pipeline, based on the k-NN or the SVM/Softmax classifier.
Write backpropagation code, and train Neural Networks and Convolutional Neural Networks.
Implement recurrent networks, and apply them to image captioning on Microsoft COCO.
Explore methods for visualizing the features of a pretrained model on ImageNet.
Train a generative adversarial network to generate images that look like a training dataset.
Design and implement a deep neural network for computer vision applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Blockchain Technology
courses.description: This course introduces basic concepts and technologies of blockchain, such as the hash function and digital signature, as well as the blockchain applications, especially in Fintech. The students will learn the consensus protocols and algorithms, the incentives and politics of the block chain community, the mechanics of Bitcoin and Bitcoin mining. The course also covers the limitations and possible improvements of the blockchain system.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental technologies about blockchain and cryptocurrencies.
Analyze the algorithms, optimization, and tradeoff of the distributed system.
Develop de-centralized applications over blockchain.
Write smart contracts on Ethereum platform.
Identify the token economy and mining eco-system.
Design advanced consensus algorithms taking into consideration of scalability, security, and privacy.
Write blockchain technical white paper supporting solid business plan.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Natural Language Processing. It covers a brief overview of the subject, including the task background, its computational problem setting and general thoughts of methodologies. Several state-of-the-art techniques that well support the industrial level services, including topic modelling, deep learning models, and their applications in search engine, chatbot and QA system will also be included.

cilos.description: Identify the basic principles behind machine learning algorithms for Natural Language Processing (NLP) data
Implement programs for NLP tasks
Formulate machine learning solutions to domain problems
Describe an understanding of the complexity of real world problems

courses.title: Spatial and Multimedia Databases
courses.description: Data types in many new applications domains, such as spatial, multimedia and a wide range of scientific applications, are often represented as multi-dimensional data. Data management and query processing techniques for multi-dimensional data are significantly different from the relational data. This course covers a selection of database topics to provide students with the critical thinking of issues related to techniques for multidimensional data management and analytics. Spatial and multimedia database management concepts, theories and technologies, from data representation, indexing, fundamental operations to advanced query processing, as well as challenges and solutions for high dimensional data will be introduced.

cilos.description: Identify data management and analytics challenges for large-scale complex data, especially for spatial and multimedia data.
Represent complex data types as multi-dimensional vectors to support similarity-based search.
Identify fundamental operations and advanced query processing techniques for spatial, spatiotemporal and multimedia data.
Use the knowledge of multidimensional databases to process queries with spatial, spatiotemporal and multimedia data.
Identify challenges and solutions for high dimensional data in the context of big data and data science.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: The course introduces students to both the theory and practice of big data management using a database system. Topics covered include analysis and representation of data requirements (entity-relationship (E-R) model, relational model, JSON); querying data using database query languages (relational and non-relational); storing, managing, processing and analyzing big data; safeguarding data in a multi-user environment. Hands-on experience in designing, implementing and querying databases using relational and non-relational database technologies will be provided.

cilos.description:
Explain important concepts in database systems including data models; database system architectures; logical and physical database design; query languages and query processing; differences between relational
and non-relational database systems; database services including transaction management and crash recovery.
Apply database theories and techniques to practical big data applications.
Analyze a real-world problem requiring data management, design a database for the problem and implement the database using a database system.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning with Financial Applications
courses.description: With the application of artificial intelligence (AI) growing rapidly in finance industries and related sectors, this course introduces the use of reinforcement learning techniques in financial applications. Topics include finite action space and finite state space problem, classical RL algorithms, Q learning, policy gradient methods, and deep Q learning.

cilos.description: Apply mathematical theories to derive models of reinforcement learning in finance applications.
Apply programming techniques in implementing the reinforcement learning models.
Analyze problems with real industry data (such as trading data).
Draw meaningful implications to capture market behaviors in trading.
Conduct independent research to handle the complexities in real-world trading applications.

courses.title: Fintech: Foundation and Applications
courses.description: This course dives into the evolving landscape of financial technology. Students will gain a thorough understanding of the diverse participants within the financial industry, from traditional banks to disruptive start-ups. The curriculum emphasizes practical application, equipping learners with the skills to harness cutting-edge technology in various financial practice areas. Through a blend of case studies, hands-on projects, and interactive discussions, students will explore the integration of technology in financial services, ensuring they are well-prepared to drive innovation in this dynamic sector.

cilos.description: Explain the structure and functioning of financial markets and instruments, and describe how fintech innovations are reshaping these areas.
Analyze the end-to-end lifecycle of financial transactions and identify the roles of different stakeholders, systems, and controls involved.
Evaluate key business functions in financial services—such as investment management, brokerage, risk management, compliance, and data governance—through the lens of technology application.
Apply business knowledge to fintech case studies, demonstrating the ability to link technical solutions with client needs, regulatory requirements, and organizational goals.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in big data reflecting recent developments in techniques and tools which are not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Recognize the major issues and technical problems in a specific topic in the big data field.
Identify key technical solutions to the problems in the topic.
Solve specific problems in this topic.

courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: An independent project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. This course may be repeated for credit.

cilos.description: Investigate existing problems on Big Data and conduct original Big Data research.
Apply acquired knowledge of Big Data on privacy protection and policy making.
Design solutions to improve the existing computing and analytic techniques on Big Data.

courses.title: Introduction to Computational and Modeling Tools
courses.description: Basics of the Linux operating system and shell scripting; basic ideas of version control using Git and GitHub; basics about CPU, GPU and their applications in high performance computing; introduction of the parallel program design, implementation and applications in physics and other areas; introduction of libraries useful in high performance computing; introduction to quantum computing and basic quantum algorithms. Python will be the main programming language used in this course.

cilos.description: Write simple scripts to automate tasks in Linux environments.
Use Git and GitHub for version control.
Explain the basic structures of CPU and GPU.
Explain the basics about parallel computing.
Identify when parallel computing is useful.
Use common libraries to design and program parallel solutions to some numerical problems.
Explain the basics of quantum computing.

courses.title: Scientific Programming and Visualization
courses.description: The Python programming language and its application to scientiﬁc programming (packages such as Scipy, Numpy, Matplotlib); introduction to Matlab, Mathematica, Excel and R; visualization techniques for data from scientiﬁc computing, everyday life, social media, business, medical imaging, etc. (stock price, housing price, highway traffic data, weather data, fluid dynamics data) (3 hours lecture in computer lab)

cilos.description: Use Python to write computer programs.
Apply Matlab, Mathematica, Excel and R to write programs.
Select suitable figures to represent data clearly.
Create animation to show the evolution of data.
Solve simple scientific problems and show the results clearly.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes and Applications
courses.description: Probability theory; maximum likelihood; Bayesian techniques; principal component analysis, data transformation and filtering; Brownian motion and stochastic processes; cross-correlations; power laws; log-normal distribution and extreme value distributions; Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution; Monte Carlo methods; agent-based models; evolutionary games; Black-Scholes equation.

cilos.description: Use appropriate mathematical tools to reveal the statistical parameters of data sets.
Process data sets to extract their salient features.
Formulate mathematical equations for stochastic processes.
Summarize the behaviors of data sets using typical statistical laws and distributions where applicable.
Relate stochastic process equations to the macroscopic properties of many-component systems in real-life based on their microscopic behaviors.
Apply stochastic process techniques to make predictions in real-life problems.

courses.title: Numerical Methods and Modeling in Science
courses.description: Fundamental numerical techniques: error, speed and stability, integrals, derivatives, interpolation and extrapolation, least squares ﬁtting, solution of linear algebraic equations, mathematical optimization, ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations; Fourier and spectral applications, random processes, Monte Carlo simulations, simulated annealing.

cilos.description: Apply numerical methods for derivatives and integrals and explain their errors.
Apply numerical methods for interpolation, extrapolation, and least squares fitting.
Apply numerical methods to solve linear algebraic equations.
Apply numerical methods to solve ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations.
Apply mathematical optimization.
Explain Fourier and spectral methods.
Apply Monte Carlo simulations.

courses.title: Innovation in Practice
courses.description: Three topics will be selected each term. For each topic, specialists from the industry will be invited to introduce the industrial landscape and related issues. Students will then form groups to explore methodology of collecting useful data and propose innovative solutions related to the topics based on real data. This course enables students to apply mathematical theories to real context and gives students hands-on experience on data science.

cilos.description: Explain the use of data science as a platform to impact the society and business decisions.
Identify and describe the common themes and topics in data science in modern business and society.
Conduct experiential workshops using data from industries under real life or simulated situation.
Apply data analytics model, coding in real life situations.
Apply Web scraping, Web robots, and other Ai automation tools.

courses.title: Algorithm and Object-Oriented Programming for Modeling
courses.description: Data structures (such as list, queue, stack), algorithms (such as recursion, sorting and searching), concepts and design patterns of object-oriented programming are introduced. Students are expected to understand and use these techniques to handle data.

cilos.description: Define and use data structures in solving programming problems.
Describe and implement recursion, searching and sorting algorithms.
Explain and apply object-orientated programming.
Explain and apply design patterns in modeling.

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis of Time Series
courses.description: The course introduces some fundamental concepts of time series, including strict stationarity and weak stationarity, and series correlation. Students will study some classical time series models, including autoregressive model, moving averages model and ARMA model, seasonal ARIMA models, multivariate time series models, and some new financial time series models, including ARCH and GARCH models. Students will also learn the forecasting techniques based on those time series models and build up time series models for real time series data in natural science, engineering and economics.

cilos.description: Check if a data set is from white noise/series correlation.
Identify relevant models of time series.
Perform estimation and model selection.
Make forecasts based on time series.
Model volatilities.

courses.title: Statistical Machine Learning
courses.description: This course introduces modern methodologies in machine learning, including tools in both supervised learning and unsupervised learning. Examples include linear regression and classification, tree-based methods, kernel methods and principal component analysis. Students will practice R or Python, and apply them to real data analysis.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important concepts in machines learning.
Describe the methods in machines learning and apply them in concise form.
Apply machine learning tools in real data analysis.
Explain and use software such as R or Python.

courses.title: Deep Learning for Modeling: Concepts, Tools, and Techniques
courses.description: This course introduces deep learning methodologies, including basic concepts, programming frameworks, and practical techniques. Topics include regression neural network, convolutional neural network, generative adversarial network, variational autoencoder, normalizing flow, reinforcement learning, and sequential models. Students will learn to implement typical models in PyTorch and apply them to various datasets in many real-world applications.

cilos.description: Explain and use appropriately important concepts in deep learning.
Explain important algorithms in deep learning.
Assess programming frameworks, such as NumPy and PyTorch.
Apply appropriate deep learning algorithms in real data analysis cases.
Implement important algorithms in deep learning.

courses.title: Network Modeling
courses.description: Empirical study of networks in social science, economics, ﬁnance, biology and technology, network models: random networks, small world networks, scale free networks, spatial and hierarchical networks, evolving networks, methods to generate them with a computer, dynamical processes on complex networks: network search, epidemic spreading, rumor and information spreading, community detection algorithms, applications of network theory.

cilos.description: Analyze real world networks empirically.
Apply fundamentals of graph theory and techniques to calculate various properties of complex networks.
Predict the outcomes of dynamical processes that evolve on networks.
Apply network theory to trace the factors determining the properties of real world complex (social, financial, biological, technological) systems.
Develop computational algorithms for calculating network properties and analyzing large scale networks.

courses.title: Business Literacy for Data Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed to build essential business acumen to equip students with the attitudes, skills and knowledge needed to thrive in today’s data-driven world. Diving into specialized modules covering management, decision making, business communications and collaborations, the course will help students to develop a foundational understanding of key business concepts and terminology. Students will work in groups and get exposure to industry experts to gain authentic learning experience.

cilos.description: Demonstrate understanding of fundamental business concepts and terminology.
Understand the role of data in solving complex business problems.
Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders using data-driven insights.
Analyze real-world business scenarios through an interdisciplinary lens.
Present and showcase integration of business literacy with data skills.

courses.title: Information Science
courses.description: This course will cover: (1) decision theory and its applications to finance; options and payoff diagrams, binomial trees, Wiener Process, Ito Lemma, Black-Scholes-Merton Model; (2) portfolio management of financial time series using mean variance analysis; (3) evolutionary computation for optimization, with applications in finding good prediction rules in finance; (4) measure of information, various information entropies, and methods of maximum entropy; (5) Nonlinear time series: Hurst exponent, multifractality in time series, detrending and decomposing a nonlinear time series; (6) Causality and information flow.

cilos.description: Apply the concept information measure, mutual information, and various types of information entropy to study real-world complex systems.
Describe and explain the method of Bayesian decision criterion and other common tools in decision theory.
Explain association rule in prediction using decision theory and data pre-procession.
Define options with examples in payoff diagrams and binomial tree.
Explain the method of mean variance analysis in portfolio management.
Assess financial time series databases to form new tools of FinTech.
Apply nonlinear time series methods to analyze real-world time series.

courses.title: Operations Research and Optimization
courses.description: This course will introduce the concepts and techniques of optimization and modeling in systems and applications with many variables and constraints. Topics to be discussed include pivot tables, linear programming, network flow models, project management, support vector algorithms, kernel methods, convex sets, duality, Lagrange multipliers, 1-D optimization algorithms, unconstrained optimization, guided random search methods, and constrained optimization.

cilos.description: Explain the underlying principles of optimization techniques and algorithms.
Assess the differences and pros and cons of different optimization techniques and algorithms.
Select the appropriate optimization methods for solving various optimization problems.
Apply software tools to solve optimization problems.
Formulate real-world problems in terms of models and solve them.
Assess whether optimization techniques used in applications are used effectively.

courses.title: Data-Driven Modeling Seminars and Tutorials
courses.description: All students in the MSc in Data-Driven Modeling program are required to take this course. Appropriate seminars and small group tutorials are scheduled to expose students to a variety of issues in data science and industry, and to enhance students' communication with industry experts and faculty. This course lasts for one year. The students are required to attend the seminars and tutorials in two regular terms. For students of MSc in Data-Driven Modeling only. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Formulate the future plans about their careers and explain them to faculty members and fellow students in both small and large group settings.
Identify the latest key developments in data industry from the expert sharing seminars.
Participate in small group discussions with confidence on various topical issues.
Apply communication skills at work, both as individuals and when in large groups.
Search for and retrieve information on a variety of topics relevant to career development and lifelong learning in data science.
Apply basic skills for preparing successful resumes, cover letters and job interviews.

courses.title: Computational Modeling and Simulation Project
courses.description: Under the supervision of a faculty member, students will carry out an independent research project on computational modeling and simulation. At the end of the course, students need to summarize their results in the form of short theses and give oral presentations. Enrollment in the course requires approval by the course coordinator and supervisor.

cilos.description: Initiate new research areas, identify goals of significant importance, search relevant literature, and collect new data.
Construct data-driven models, test hypothesis, write simulation programs, and interpret simulation results.
Draw meaningful conclusions, write convincing reports, and propose further directions.

courses.title: Semiconductor Devices and Processing
courses.description: This course will introduce the electronic, transport and optical properties of semiconductor materials and their relations with the device performance. Various fabrication techniques (i.e., MBE, MOCVD, PVD and CVD) and processing steps such as photolithography, etching, thermal oxidation, ion-implantation and thin-film deposition for semiconductor device fabrication will be presented.

cilos.description: Explain the physics of p-n junctions, metal-semiconductor contacts, and metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) capacitors.
Explain the basic working principles of transistors and photonic devices.
Understand the basic device processing steps and operation principles of the techniques involved.
Appreciate and better understand the advanced technologies involved in modern electronic devices.

courses.title: Quantum Materials and Technologies for Quantum Devices and Sensors
courses.description: The course is an introduction to the physics of quantum materials and quantum technologies at the graduate level. Topics include: qubits, quantum gates and quantum circuit model, entanglement and quantum communication, quantum algorithms and computing, and realization of quantum technologies in various physical systems.

cilos.description: Understand the basic concepts of quantum information physics.
Learn principles of quantum devices and their operational mechanisms.
Analyze simple quantum algorithms.
Understand how different physical systems realize quantum information, pros and cons of each system.

courses.title: Metamaterials and Applications
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental physics of metamaterials and their potential applications, e.g. for photonic/phononic devices. The course will enrich students with hands-on experience in modeling techniques to achieve new functionalities for these metamaterials.

cilos.description: Acquire a basic understanding of metamaterials.
Explain phenomena observed in metamaterials.
Perform modeling of metamaterials using various software tools.
Design devices to achieve specific functionalities.

courses.title: Topological and 2D Materials: Physics and Applications
courses.description: The physics and potential application of topological and correlated phenomena appearing in two-dimensional material platforms will be covered: Chern and topological insulators, superconductivity, Mott insulator, quantum spin liquid, quantum hall effect, and superconductivity and edge state arising from 2D and topological materials will be introduced. The potential of these phenomena and platforms toward their use in opto-electronic, spintronic and quantum information applications are also discussed.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles underlying topological and correlated phenomena in two-dimensional materials, including Chern and topological insulators, superconductivity, Mott insulators, quantum spin liquids, and the quantum Hall effect.

Apply theoretical knowledge of topological and correlated phenomena to real-world applications in opto-electronics, spintronics, and quantum information technologies, evaluating the potential of these materials for practical applications.

Analyze and interpret experimental data related to topological and correlated phenomena in two-dimensional material platforms, and draw meaningful conclusions and contribute to ongoing research in the field.

Critically evaluate research literature in the field of condensed matter physics, staying abreast of recent advancements and emerging trends related to topological and correlated phenomena, and effectively communicate their findings.

Design and conduct independent research/study projects focused on topological and correlated phenomena in two-dimensional materials, fostering a spirit of inquiry and innovation in their academic pursuits.

courses.title: Data Analysis for Physics
courses.description: This course serves as an introduction to statistical data analysis in its application to physics experiments. The topics covered include basic probability distribution functions, Monte Carlo simulation techniques, estimation of parameters, hypothesis testing and more.

cilos.description: Perform analysis of experimental data.
Estimate experimental statistical uncertainties.
Predict experimental results using Monte Carlo techniques.
Test hypotheses and estimate parameter values.

courses.title: Contemporary Physics
courses.description: Latest advances in surface science, quantum and 2D materials science and technology, soft matters, biophysics, computational physics, particle physics and cosmology will be showcased.

cilos.description: Learn various advances in a wide range of physics topics.
Understand core principles of selected topics in physics, such as surface science, quantum and 2D materials, soft matters, biophysics, lasers, computational physics, particle physics and cosmology.
Recognize Physics as a multidisciplinary field related to many branches of science such as materials science, engineering, computer science and life science.
Communicate disciplinary knowledge and findings in written and/or oral form.
Appreciate the contribution of physics discoveries to many modern technologies.

courses.title: Physical Properties of Materials
courses.description: This course introduces the various physical properties of materials such as mechanical properties (i.e., strength, durability, hardness, flexibility, etc.), optical properties (i.e., refractive index, absorption coefficient, luminosity, etc.), thermal properties (i.e., melting point, expansion, conductivity, etc.), electrical properties (i.e., resistance, conductivity, etc.) and chemical properties (i.e., pH, corrosion resistance, reactivity, surface tension).

cilos.description: Learn the mechanical, electrical and optical properties of various materials.
Understand the rationales for the materials used at different layers in some electrical and optoelectronic devices.
Analyze device performance limitation and durability from its material compositions.
Design device structure incorporating materials with specific functionality and physical properties to improve performance.
Understand and appreciate the important role materials play in many modern devices and technologies.

courses.title: Experimental Techniques for Material Characterization
courses.description: This course introduces various techniques such as SEM, TEM AFM, XPS/UPS, XRD, Photoluminescence, Raman and optical spectroscopy to characterize the physical, optical and electronic properties of film and nanomaterials.

cilos.description: Learn various methods and techniques for characterizing bulk crystals, films and micro/nanostructures.
Understand the basic principles of various materials characterization techniques and their application to the quantification of material properties.
Design and plan experiments to assess the physical, optical and electronic properties of materials using various characterization techniques.
Assess the technical feasibility of potential applications based on the structural, morphological, and spectroscopic properties of materials.

courses.title: Computational and Simulation Tools
courses.description: This course introduces hardware and software computational and modeling tools. Hands-on experience on some common mathematics and physics simulation and modeling software such as MATLAB, Mathematica, COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS Lumerical will be presented. The basics about CPU, GPU and their applications in high performance computing in areas such as operating systems, parallel program design and quantum computation will also be introduced.

cilos.description: Identify hardware requirement for high performance computing.
Explain the basic structure of CPU and GPU.
Use the basic algorithms for some of the numerical problems.
Explain the basics about parallel computing.
Use some standard software to simulate or numerically solve problems in physics and related areas.

courses.title: Computational Methods in Science
courses.description: Basics of numerical analysis; Random processes and Monte Carlo method; Matrix methods and Eigenvalue problems; Ordinary differential equations: Initial and Boundary value problems; Partial differential equations; Systems of nonlinear equations; Optimization problems and optimization algorithms; Spectral analysis: Fourier transform, Wavelet Transform, Hilbert-Huang Transform; Causality and information flow.

cilos.description: Apply numerical methods to study random processes.
Apply numerical methods to solve initial and boundary value problems of ordinary differential equations.
Apply numerical methods to solve partial differential equations.
Apply numerical methods to solve systems of nonlinear equations.
Apply practical optimization algorithms to optimization problems.
Apply spectral methods to analyze real-world systems.

courses.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Science
courses.description: This course provides students with an overview of the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) focusing on machine learning (ML) and its applications. It introduces several popular AI/ML Python software packages with an emphasis on the practical aspect of using existing software to solve problems in science. Throughout the course, students will learn systematically a set of commonly used ML models together with a framework for training, validating, and evaluating models. Students will also gain intuition and heuristics via hands-on experiences of using modern AI/ML techniques in their homework assignments and projects. Students without the prerequisites but possess equivalent background knowledge may seek instructor's approval for enrolling in the course.

cilos.description: Explain basic knowledge about the field of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML).
Apply state-of-the-art Python AI/ML packages to build popular models to solve realistic problems such as regression and classification.
Gain hands-on experiences of using AI techniques in scientific research.
Develop frameworks for using AI techniques to solve specific scientific problems.
Understand and appreciate the impact and challenges of AI on society and science.

courses.title: Advanced Research Projects
courses.description: Experimental or theoretical research project under supervision of a faculty member. Program Director’s approval is required. A final report and presentation by the student is required at the conclusion of the project. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Learn new physics and/or enhance their computational skills through their projects.
Formulate strategies and experiments to reach a certain goal or complete a task/project.
Enhance their communication skills through the interaction with the supervisor, group mates and project presentation.
Develop a good foundation for a career in industrial/academic research or further study.

courses.title: MSc Physics Seminars and Tutorials
courses.description: Exposure in latest development in science and career paths through Physics departmental seminars, and invited speakers from industry to talk about career/job/research. This course lasts for one year. The students are required to attend the seminars and tutorials in two regular terms. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Identify the latest and key developments in materials and computational physics areas from the research seminars and expert sharing talks.
Participate in small group discussions with confidence on various topical issues.
Apply communication skills at work, both as individuals and when in large groups.
Search for and retrieve information on a variety of topics relevant to career development, postgraduate study and lifelong learning.
Apply basic skills for preparing successful resumes, cover letters and job interviews.

courses.title: Technology Leadership and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course will provide a common level of knowledge among students on topics in technology innovation management, leadership and entrepreneurship. Particularly, the course examines how the technology innovation process works; how to lead and manage innovation processes and how to create an environment that rewards innovation and entrepreneurship.

cilos.description: Describe technology innovation management and techniques.
Identify and assess product market potential and conduct competitive analysis.
Describe leadership thoughts and behaviors and steps to motivate teams to get results.
Identify the basics of product development and management.
Develop soft skills to more effectively interact with people.

courses.title: Product Development and Prototyping
courses.description: This is a project-based course that emphasizes the self-learning approach to engineering problem solving. The students will be given a design brief to rapidly produce a prototype. This is followed by a deeper analysis of the specification non-conformance, with students using self-learning guided by the instructor(s) to re-design and produce an engineering prototype.

cilos.description: Produce a testing prototype based on design specifications.
Analyze failure modes for a product prototype.
Apply background engineering/ analytical skills to guide product design.
Produce an engineering prototype and test it for performance.
Use computing tools for detailed engineering analysis.

courses.title: Startup Workshop
courses.description: This is a practical course designed to expose students to the practical issues in launching a startup together with case studies of several startups to gather some insight into root causes for success and failures. The case studies will be covered in open format lectures, while the practical topics will be covered via workshops. Topics covered in the workshop will be focused on the Hong Kong (HK) and Pearl River Delta (PRD) region with coverage of local laws, regulations, agencies and organizations. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyze a startup business to identify potential risks and opportunities.
Identify unique/novel elements of an idea/product based on patent searches.
Register a company in HK/PRD area.
Execute operational details related to setting up a start-up, including banking, personnel, accounting and tax.
Articulate the various government and non-government support structures in HK and PRD area for a given area-focused startup.

courses.title: Special Topics in Technology Leadership and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Selected topics in technology leadership and entrepreneurship reflecting recent developments and trends. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Identify the updated developments in technology leadership and entrepreneurship.
Analyze the major problems in the special topic.
Apply the knowledge to solve the problems in the special topic.

courses.title: Technology Leadership and Entrepreneurship Project
courses.description: This 3-term project course is the hallmark of the MSc Program in Technology Leadership and Entrepreneurship. The students will be expected to brainstorm, prototype, and launch an alpha release of a product or a service over the duration of the course. In the first term, students will engage in early stage brainstorming, ideation, team-forming, product contest, pitches, including participation in case competition. In the second term, each team will go through a sustained and concentrated effort in prototype building and complete an alpha-release, or engineering prototype of their product which is launch-ready in the third term. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Identify a market need.
Create a multi-functional team and clearly define member roles.
Investigate existing IP data and differentiate a product from pre-existing ones.
Create initial prototype and mock-up.
Identify and learn background foundations for a new product.
Analyze and perform detailed design of sub-components of a design.
Perform experiment analysis and failure mode analysis on prototypes and components.
Produce engineering prototype and identify downstream avenues for product launch.

courses.title: Chemistry of Nanomaterials
courses.description: Chemistry of materials with nano-dimensional structures and advanced functionalities. Working principles of liquid-crystalline displays and organic light-emitting diodes. High-tech applications of luminescent materials in optoelectronic systems, chemical sensors and biological probes.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of materials science and technology.
Recognize the power of chemical synthesis and materials preparation and carry out investigative research work with independent judgment.
Apply chemical principles to formulate and analyze analytical and synthetic problems.
Conduct analysis and interpretation of experimental data.
Communicate problem solutions using correct materials chemistry terminology and good English.

courses.title: Computational Energy Materials and Electronic Structure Simulations
courses.description: This course will introduce atomistic computational methods to model, understand, and predict the properties and behavior of real materials including solids, liquids, and nanostructures. Their applications to sustainable energy will be discussed. Specific topics include: density-functional theory (DFT), Kohn-Sham equations, local and semi-local density approximations and hybrid functionals, basis sets, pseudopotentials; Hartree-Fock method; ab initio molecular dynamics with interatomic interactions derived on the fly from DFT, Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics; Monte-Carlo sampling; computational spectroscopy from first principles, IR and Raman. Students will learn how to use free open-source packages to do materials simulations on a Linux computer cluster.

cilos.description: Explain the principles of density-functional theory, including Kohn-Sham equations, band gap discontinuity, exchange-correlation potentials, basis sets, and pseudopotentials.
Explain the Hartree-Fock (HF) method and Koopmans' theory, and describe the basic principles of post-HF methods: Cl, MP2, and CCSD.
Explain the principles of molecular dynamics and identify the relation between classical and quantum molecular dynamics.
Assess the electronic and vibrational properties of molecules or nanostructures using an open-source DFT code.
Assess the band structures and transport properties of crystal materials using an open-source DFT code.

courses.title: Solid State Physics
courses.description: This is an introductory course on postgraduate level solid state physics. The topics covered include: electronic band structures of solids, phonons, electron dynamics in crystals, electron interactions in solids, linear response theory, electronic transitions and optical properties of solids, electron phonon interactions, integer quantum Hall effects, superconductivity and magnetism.

cilos.description: Derive the electronic band structures of materials with simple lattices.
Calculate phonon band structures.
Calculate the energy of electronic systems using Hatree-Fock approximations.
Formulate the electron responses to external electric and magnetic fields.
Derive the expression of the conductance of Quantum Hall Systems.
Calculate physical properties of superconductors and magnets.

courses.title: Physics of Nanostructured Semiconductors
courses.description: Fundamental physics on electronic, vibrational, transport, and optical properties of semiconductors and nano-scaled solid materials based on quantum mechanics.  Emphasis on nanostructured heterostructures, quantum size and low-dimensional effects, and application to modern electronics and opto-electronics.

cilos.description: Apply the fundamental knowledge from Quantum Mechanics and Solid State Physics to explain new physical phenomena and new or improved device operations that low dimensional semiconductor heterostructures can offer.
Explain the basic principles of common experimental methods for structural, electrical and optical characterizations of low dimensional semiconductor heterostructures.
Demonstrate the team work, independent learning, and scientific presentation skills.

courses.title: Nano Beam Technology
courses.description: Basic physical principles underlying many nano-beam techniques for fabricating and characterizing nanomaterials.  Introduction to nano process, e-beam and focus ion-beam lithograph, interaction between crystalline nanomaterials and electron/ion beams.  Electron beam diffraction and imaging, imaging contrast mechanism, nanostructure characterization and analytical electron microscopy.

cilos.description: Apply the fundamental knowledge from crystallography and physics to explain the phenomena of high energy electron beams in diffraction and imaging of solid materials.

Explain the basic principles of experimental methods for determining atomic structures, interactions between electrons and solid crystalline materials and application in nanomaterials and nanotechnology.
Demonstrate the independent learning, scientific presentation skills and ability to solve materials science problems.

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics I
courses.description: Laws and applications of thermodynamics, kinetic theory, phase transitions, classical statistical physics foundations, canonical and grand canonical ensemble, quantum statistical physics foundations, Fermi and Bose distributions, introduction to non-equilibrium statistical physics.

cilos.description: Explain how the core principles of thermodynamics can be derived from the statistical mechanics of Nparticle systems.
Use the basic tools of statistical mechanics (such as the partition function) to predict the macroscopic properties of a system from a given microscopic model.

Apply these tools in conjunction with appropriate approximation techniques to solve problems in a variety of physical systems, including (but not limited to) fluids and interacting assemblies of spins in magnetic
fields.
Use the tools of statistical physics to predict the behaviour of systems in the neighbourhood of a phase transition.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Nano Science and Technology
courses.description: Advanced topic series presented by the professors who are listed in the Nano PG Program and guest speakers, on most updated frontier researches in nano science and nano technology. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand the major issues and acquire a comprehensive set of professional skills and knowledge in nano science and nano technology.

courses.title: Independent Study in Nano Science and Technology
courses.description: An individual in-depth study of a current topic in nano science and technology under the supervision of a faculty member.  For students of NANO program only.  The instructor's approval is required for taking this course. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Conduct literature review.
Write professional researh paper or report.
Obtain in-depth understanding on a specific research topic in Nano Science or Technology.
Explain working principles or apply experimental techniques on a research topic in Nano Science and Technology.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate research contriutions in form of a thesis.
Demonstrate research achievements, on knowledge in advanceing a research field in Nano Science and Technology, in the form of thesis.
Defend the research achievements and contributions through seminar or oral examination.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate research contriutions in form of a thesis.
Demonstrate original research achievements with impact on a research field in Nano Science and Technology, in the form of thesis.
Defend the research achievements and contributions through seminar or oral examination.

courses.title: The Earth as a Blue Planet
courses.description: The ocean is the largest life supporting habitat on Earth, and yet, it is less explored than the surface of the moon. This survey course introduces students to the fundamental, cross-disciplinary knowledge of our ocean from its formation, to the physics in circulation and climate modulation, to the chemistry and biology of the living systems within.

cilos.description: Describe the physical, chemical, geological, and biological characteristics of the ocean.
Demonstrate knowledge of the diversity of marine life and marine ecosystems.
Understand fundamental ocean processes through the integration of cross-disciplinary core scientific concepts.
Explain how ocean processes influence Earth’s climate and biodiversity.
Recognize the role of humans in shaping the ocean’s future and evaluate solutions for sustainable ocean stewardship.

courses.title: Principles and Applications of Environmental Science
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with a science background to learn and address the environmental issues caused by humans. Key topics include emerging global, regional and local environmental issues; renewable and non-renewable energy; life-supporting systems of our planet and its biodiversity; atmosphere, air pollution and global climate change; water resources and water pollution; ocean plastics and solid waste management; environmental health and toxicology. Through the course, students will be able to understand fundamental knowledge of the inter-relationship between life and our environment, the characteristics of the environmental sustainability, pollution and monitoring measures, and technologies used in pollution control and remediation.

cilos.description: Demonstrate fundamental understanding of environmental concepts, such as Earth’s life-supporting systems and biodiversity, natural resources, pollution and mitigation, and their inter-relationships.
Address challenges in environmental science by integrating scientific knowledge, technical applications, and innovative technology.
Identify and describe different scientific methods to critically evaluate complex, emerging environmental problems at global and local scales.
Recognize the importance of harmony among humans, nature, and a sustainable living society.
Develop a broad interest in the environment and connect the knowledge to their major study.
Apply the knowledge in daily life to live more sustainably and contribute to environmental protection.

courses.title: Environmental Science
courses.description: The course introduces students without a science background to the general concepts of environment, natural resources, and sustainable development. Topics include pressing global, regional and local environmental issues; renewable and non-renewable energy; life-supporting systems of our planet and its biodiversity; atmosphere, air pollution and global climate change; water resources and pollution; ocean plastics and solid waste management; environmental health and toxicology. Throughout the course, students will gain a sufficient background and a better understanding of the root causes of key environmental issues. They will also become more aware of their role, as individuals, in environmental protection and sustainable development.

cilos.description: Describe the environment as an integrated system involving air, land, water and human activities
Apply basic concepts of environmental principles to real-life decision making and problem solving
Identify environmental hazards and recommend appropriate technological innovations to tackle environmental problems
Explain the importance of harmony among humans, the natural environment, and a sustainable living society
Use scientific language to address pressing environmental issues globally and locally
Explain how an understanding of scientific principles in environmental science helps us make better decisions for the benefit of society, the economy and the environment

courses.title: Marine Chemistry
courses.description: This course is an introduction to chemical oceanography. It describes the chemistry of the ocean based on distribution and dynamics of elements, isotopes, atoms and molecules. This ranges from fundamental physical, thermodynamic and kinetic chemistry to two-way interactions of ocean chemistry with biological, geological and physical processes. It encompasses both inorganic and organic chemistry, and includes studies of ocean-atmosphere dynamics and marine sediments. Non-OST students may enroll in the course upon instructor’s approval only.

cilos.description: Explain the composition of seawater, including major and minor dissolved constituents.
Describe the roles of salinity, dissolved gases, and nutrients in marine systems.
Understand carbonate chemistry and the cycling of key elements including carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, oxygen, and trace metals.
Explain how physical, biological, geological and chemical processes in the ocean influence the chemical distributions.
Understand how chemical components can be used as tracers to investigate the physical, biological, geological and chemical processes in the ocean.

courses.title: Descriptive Physical Oceanography
courses.description: This course is an introduction to physical oceanography that includes topics such as physical description of the sea, physical properties of seawater, methods and measurements, wind-driven ocean circulation, abyssal ocean circulation, boundary processes, and wave motions. Large-scale distributions and processes that are central to the ocean’s role in Earth’s climate and biosphere will also be addressed and discussed.
courses.prerequisite: (PHYS 1101 OR PHYS 1111 OR PHYS 1112 OR PHYS 1312) AND (MATH 1005 OR MATH 1006 OR MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023)

cilos.description: Describe the large-scale distributions of the ocean’s physical properties (e.g. temperature, salinity and currents).
Explain the basic principles of ocean physics (e.g. equation of state of seawater, consequence of stratification, effects of Earth rotation, transport by mean and fluctuating ocean currents).
Identify ocean processes from the observations (e.g. meridional heat transport by geostrophic and Ekman layer currents).
Use modern observational evidence and arguments for a changing ocean (e.g. IPCC Climate Change).

courses.title: Sustainable Ocean
courses.description: This course explores the principles and practices of sustainability as they apply to the world's oceans. Students will learn about the impacts of human activities on marine ecosystems and how to develop strategies for sustainable use and conservation of ocean resources. The course combines aspects of marine ecology, oceanography, environmental science, and socio-economics.

cilos.description: Exemplify the complex interactions within marine ecosystems and the principles that underpin sustainable management of ocean resources.
Recognize the effects of anthropogenic pressures on the marine environment, including pollution, overfishing, and climate change.
Apply critical thinking skills to identify, analyze, and propose solutions to problems related to sustainable use and conservation of ocean resources.
Develop the ability to conduct research, including data collection, analysis, and interpretation, within the context of ocean sustainability.
Evaluate the effectiveness of existing policies and management strategies aimed at conserving marine ecosystems and promoting sustainable use of ocean resources.
Develop a strong sense of ethical responsibility towards the conservation of marine biodiversity and the sustainable management of ocean resources.
Explain complex sustainability issues and proposed solutions clearly and persuasively to a variety of audiences, including scientists, policymakers, and the public.

courses.title: Coastal Marine Habitats
courses.description: The course introduces students to a range of local marine coastal habitats through lectures and various field trips. Students are expected to deepen their understanding of and interest in marine ecology, biodiversity and natural conservation. After receiving training related to Hong Kong marine ecology and biodiversity, students will conduct group projects on local marine conservation, acquire skills for scientific exploration, and devise related applications. This course emphasizes positive attitudes and values education, which encourage students to care for the environment and respect for life. For OST students only.

cilos.description: Define and explain the concepts of biodiversity and conservation.
Describe the diversity of coastal marine habitats in Hong Kong, and explain how these habitats contribute to both biodiversity and ecological integrity.
Apply critical thinking skills to identify, analyze and propose solutions to problems related to conservation of marine habitats and their biodiversity.
Develop the ability to conduct research, including data collection, analysis and interpretation, within the context of marine biodiversity and conservation.
Evaluate the effectiveness of existing policies and management strategies aimed at conserving coastal marine habitats and its biodiversity.
Demonstrate a strong sense of ethical responsibility towards the conservation of coastal marine habitats and its biodiversity.
Communicate complex environmental issues and proposed solutions clearly to a variety of audiences, including their peers, scientists, policy makers and the general public.

courses.title: Conservation Field Trips
courses.description: This course introduces students to a range of local conservation efforts through various field trips. Through this course, students are expected to enhance their appreciation of our nature, to recognise the importance of harmony between human and the environment, as well as to learn how to contribute to environmental conservation as a responsible citizen. Guided tours may be conducted in Cantonese by the request of hosting organizations. Instructor's approval is required for enrolling in the course.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the environment as an integrated system involving air, land, water, and human activities.
Apply academic knowledge to the real-life situation.
Communicate environmental science knowledge through written presentation.
Recognize the importance of the harmony among human, the nature, and a sustainable living society.
Become a responsible citizen towards their community and contribute to a sustainable environment.

courses.title: Marine Biology
courses.description: Survey of the major marine living organisms; their habitat and community structures; trophic interactions and the marine ecosystem.

cilos.description: Describe in detail a diverse range of marine habitats and the organisms that inhabit them.
Evaluate the extent to which a variety of environmental settings may influence marine life, taking particular account of the interaction between marine organisms and the environment.
Evaluate the extent to which biological adaptation and ecological processes structure marine communities.
Identify potential resources from the seas and assess their use for and by humans.
Critically examine how marine ecological research projects are developed, implemented and interpreted.

courses.title: Internship
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with hands-on experience in environmental and ocean science fields. Students will undertake training and duties under the internship supervisors. Graded P or F. Maybe graded PP. Cantonese may be used in off-campus trainings and internships, in some situations. Instructor’s approval is required for enrolling in the course.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge to the real-life situation.
Communicate environmental science knowledge through oral and written presentations.
Work independently and collaborate in team work.
Reflect on their learning progress, and develop a motivation in lifelong learning.

courses.title: Marine Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Both laboratory and field investigations will provide the opportunity to apply and adapt the experimental methods developed here to specific groups of marine organisms, diversified marine habitats, and practical issues in marine/environmental science. Tutorial sessions and field trips will be used to enhance student's understanding of the practical work and the theories covered in the lectures.

cilos.description: Appraise the diversity, form and function of marine organisms.
