Use economic principles and non-market valuation techniques to address a variety of continuing and contemporary environmental issues.
Explain the method in policy evaluation and develop policy evaluation report(s).
Demonstrate effective writing and communication skills in report preparation and presentation.

courses.title: Emerging Markets in Comparative Perspective
courses.description: Emerging markets are now the main engine of global GDP growth; most have also made rapid progress in poverty reduction and other development outcomes over the last three decades. At the same time, the pandemic has raised doubts about the prospects of emerging markets. Both the pandemic-induced global recession and the possible reversal of globalization threaten the gains emerging markets have made in recent decades. Using growth diagnostics, this course examines the economic prospects of the key emerging markets in Asia – China, India, the ASEAN-5 (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand), draws lessons for development policy, and examines the implications for emerging markets in a pandemic-disrupted world.

cilos.description: Think, reason, and argue as development economists.
Apply key concepts in development economics and political economy.
Explain growth diagnostics and how to use it.
Evaluate key emerging markets in Asia and speak intelligently about their prospect and risks.
Analyze the interconnections between development and technology and sustainability.

courses.title: Technology Disruptions and Public Policy
courses.description: Rapid advances in disruptive technologies over the last two decades have significantly altered our lives. They have upended old business models, disintermediated incumbent firms in many industries, and disrupted supply chains. This module gives students a broad introduction to the key disruptive technologies that are likely to transform our economy and society in the next decade or so. We will examine the practical applications of these technologies and discuss their policy implications and socioeconomic impacts. We will also look at the potential for governments to leverage new digital technologies to deliver new services or improve existing ones and enhance public value. Above all, we will examine the implications for public policy and how government should respond.

cilos.description: Recognize and identify the key emerging disruptive technologies, their potential applications in business and government, and the attendant policy implications.
Exemplify and classify how the operating environment might change as a result of technology disruptions, and reflected on the policy or regulatory responses that would be required of governments.
Define, differentiate and analyze the various roles of the state in dealing with technology disruptions, and the policy options corresponding to each of these roles.
Apply the concepts/frameworks of public policy process to the applications of technological disruptions.
Apply and construct policy analysis and other analytical frameworks in assessing the effectiveness and efficacy of different policy options to disruptive technologies in a given context.

courses.title: The Politics and Policy of Global Health
courses.description: What is the relationship between global health and policy? What are the socioeconomic and political determinants of disease? How have such tiny microorganisms affected the government and politics of states, supranational institutions, and non-state actors throughout history and today? Who are the key actors involved in global health governance and security? And what are key political consequences and concerns of global health policy? This course grapples with these questions as an interdisciplinary take on the complex relationship between government, governance, health, and policy issues through the lens of public policy, political science, and public health. Theoretical concepts from all three fields will be studied and used to analyze real-world problems and evaluate policy options to deal with them from across the globe. The course does not assume any previous knowledge of microbiology, public health, or epidemiology.

cilos.description: Apply and generate the intersections between the health of infectious diseases and international relations in both the historic and contemporary era,  and grasp relevant overlaps in the literature between science and technology studies, international relations, and global health governance.
Critique and judge the political and theoretical debates that underscore several case studies of political challenges associated with disease.
Exemplify national and international governance concerns and classify the complexity of the network of stakeholders involved in infectious disease issues.
Compare and evaluate the competing hypotheses about the political implications of disease by utilizing social science methodology.

Differentiate and define realistic policy proposals that are meant to address problems associated with disease (e.g. outbreaks, biothreats, the lack of certain public service provisions, state weakness and failure).

courses.title: Public Management through the Lens of the Asian Development Bank
courses.description: Taught by a former Asian Development Bank (ADB) Head of the Risk Management Unit of the Private Sector Operations Department, this course enables its students to go deep-dive to examine and discuss current public management strategies in dealing with major social issues at the ADB. Specific questions to be explored include: How are policies and processes formulated? How are projects and programs recommended, approved, implemented, monitored, and independently evaluated in an MDB (Multilateral Development Bank)? How results orientation is emphasized at ADB in achieving better quality projects and programs? And how institutional reforms take place at MDBs such as ADB which ensure improved staff resource reallocation and skills-mix changes in meeting evolving operational needs with efficiency and effectiveness? Specific cases will also be discussed to enhance professional skills valued at MDBs.

cilos.description: Develop and generate social issues in a constantly changing institutional and political context of public affairs.
Attribute to the agenda to deal with social issues among stakeholders including nations and civil society.
Exemplify country partnership and regional cooperation strategies at the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
Analyze and appraise how projects and programs are prepared, approved, implemented, monitored and evaluated.
Develop and execute professional skills at Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs), such as leadership, management, teamwork and communication, based on respect, openness and integrity.

courses.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
courses.description: This course introduces students to the political dimensions of environmental policy. It explores how various political actors and institutions interact with each other in shaping environmental policy. The course is divided into two parts. First, it presents the normative and ideational foundations for environmental politics and discusses the major forms of collective action. Second, it analyzes the government’s policy responses to environmental ideas and collective action in the context of capitalist political economy. Students will benefit from the ability to think politically about the environment, which is essential for successful environmental policymaking in practice.

cilos.description: Explain the key ideas and issues in environmental politics and policy.
Analyze the roles and impacts of actors and institutions in environmental collective action and policy making.
Apply concepts and theories to evaluate the debates in environmental politics and policy.
Exercise independent and critical judgements as well as formulate and communicate arguments effectively.

courses.title: Research, Analysis and Evaluation Methods: Survey and Interview Design
courses.description: This course aims to equip students with the essential knowledge and skills for designing and conducting survey and interview research in various policy contexts and domains at a foundational level. Students will learn the theoretical foundations and practical applications of survey and interview methods, and how to use them to collect primary data from the public, stakeholders, and experts on diverse and contemporary policy issues and problems. Students will also learn how to critically evaluate the quality and validity of survey and interview data, and how to identify and address the sources of error and bias that may affect the results and their interpretation.

cilos.description: Explain the theoretical foundations and practical applications of survey and interview methods in policy research.
Design effective and ethical surveys and interviews that address specific policy issues and problems.
Apply appropriate sampling techniques and data collection strategies to ensure the validity, reliability, and representativeness of survey and interview data.
Analyze and interpret quantitative and qualitative data from surveys and interviews using various statistical and thematic methods.
Evaluate the strengths and limitations of different survey and interview methods and their implications for policy decisions and outcomes.
Communicate clearly and respectfully with different audiences using survey and interview data.
Apply relevant perspectives and links to the professional practice of public policy and public management using survey and interview data.

courses.title: Sustainable Urban Design and Development
courses.description: This course is designed for postgraduate students who want to learn about urban sustainability, an emerging and still developing field that draws on different disciplines, such as industrial ecology, urban political ecology, urban ecology, and planning and how public policy and public management approach it. It will explore how to make cities more sustainable in terms of environmental, social, and economic aspects and equip students with the theoretical and methodological tools to draft and analyze strategies and their viability. The course will also introduce and evaluate various approaches to foster more sustainable and resilient forms of urbanization and urban life, such as localization, industrial symbiosis, and ecological restoration and review processes of reducing the dependence on external resources and increasing the local production and consumption of goods and services. These approaches will be examined in different contexts and scales, from local to global, and from individual to collective.

cilos.description: Compare and contrast different models and theories of urban sustainability and their implications for urban policy and practice.
Explain and analyze the concept of urban sustainability and its social, economic and environmental dimensions.
Assess the strengths and weaknesses of different methods and tools for collecting and analyzing data on urban sustainability issues and solutions.
Develop strategies to counteract or mitigate the impact of urban population trends and climate change on urban sustainability and resilience.
Evaluate the benefits and challenges of various approaches to foster more sustainable and resilient forms of urbanization and urban life.
Develop and communicate interdisciplinary and integrative strategies to address complex urban challenges and opportunities.
Critically reflect on their own role and responsibility as urban citizens and professionals in promoting urban sustainability and resilience.
Demonstrate ethical and professional practices in working with diverse urban communities and stakeholders to promote urban sustainability and resilience.

courses.title: Comparative Social Welfare Policy
courses.description: This course teaches students basic theories and practices of social welfare policies through an international comparative perspective. Key policy areas include poverty alleviation, health care, old-age protection, elderly care, public housing, and labor protection. A variety of pedagogies will be used: seminar, movie-screening, and guest lecture.

cilos.description: Understand the concepts and approaches of social policy studies.
Appreciate the value of social welfare policies to human dignity and development.
Be equipped with useful analytical skills in examining poverty alleviation, health, labor protection, old-age protection, and public housing policies.
Compare and contrast the policy strategies of governments in Asia in promoting social development and make assessment.

courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.description: This course addresses three fundamental questions about energy policy: Why do we need energy policy? How do governments influence energy systems and their socio-economic and environmental impacts? What is the role of innovation in driving energy transitions? The class begins with an overview of the context in which today’s energy policies are designed: climate change, environmental degradation, the global competition for natural resources, as well as major successes and gaps in energy innovation. Policy types are introduced through the lens of energy technologies and their past and ongoing development. Students examine the role of data, models, and uncertainties in policy decisions and acquire basic literacy in energy technology and policy assessment methods.

cilos.description: Understand how energy policies are designed, implemented, and evaluated.
Describe the challenges that energy policies are meant to address and the opportunities they provide.
Distinguish socio-economic, technological, and political dimensions of current energy debates.
Develop and effectively communicate energy policy-related arguments.
Master basic concepts and tools for energy technology and policy evaluation.
Critically examine policy assessment methods and models as applied in the energy field.
Identify synergies and tradeoffs between energy, environmental, and sustainability policy.
Understand the role of energy technologies in achieving energy policy goals.

courses.title: Technology and Global Security
courses.description: This course introduces the technical aspects of key technologies, reviews their impacts on global security, and explores how states and the international community manage these risks. Technologies such as AI, biotechnology, nuclear technology, quantum computing and other technologies with geopolitical importance are reviewed. The goal of this course is to equip students with basic knowledge on technologies that are shaping the international order to better understand their impacts and respond to them when in leadership positions.

cilos.description: Solve basic scientific problems related to technologies such as nuclear, missile and biotechnologies.
Assess the relation between technical aspects of a technology and potential impacts on global security.
Analyze a technology of their choice and evaluate policies to manage its impact on global security.
Develop a policy report presenting the results of their analysis.
Communicate the results of their analysis.
Engage in teamwork to conduct analysis and produce the policy report and the oral presentation.
Prepare and deliver arguments during a debate on a controversial topic around a technology and geopolitics.

courses.title: Political Economy of Poverty, Inequality, and Development
courses.description: This course introduces students to how structural power shapes and influences the global fight against poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment, three of the most fundamental and persistent societal challenges that humans have ever faced. First, it explains how poverty, inequality, and development are defined and measured, why some definitions and measurements are preferred over others, and how the three concepts are intertwined. After that, it examines how different classical and contemporary theories of political economy and development interpret the root causes of poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment, which of the theories became more dominant, and why. Finally, it explores the successes, failures, and potential of the various mainstream and alternative approaches that have been used or proposed to address poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment.

cilos.description: Explain how poverty, inequality, and development are defined and measured, why some definitions and measurements are preferred over others, and how the three concepts are intertwined.
Analyze how different state and non-state actors wield structural power to shape and influence the global fight against poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment.

Distinguish between the main classical and contemporary theories of political economy and development, the different ways in which they interpret the root causes of poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment, and the different ways in which they impacted developmental practice around the world.

Evaluate the effectiveness of the most common mainstream approaches that have been used or proposed to address poverty, inequality, and underdevelopment, and the potential effectiveness as well as the technical and political feasibility of more ambitious alternative approaches.

Develop essential critical thinking, analytical, research, writing, and presentation skills necessary for the creation and implementation of comprehensive policy strategies and effective enforcement mechanisms aimed at eradicating poverty, reducing inequality, and fostering development that is truly sustainable.

courses.title: Rise, Fall, and Resurgence of the East Asian Developmental State Model
courses.description: This course introduces students to the tumultuous evolution of the East Asian developmental state model, which through its unique blend of state-led capitalist planning, industrial policymaking, and severe disciplining of capital and labor offers important insights not only about the most impressive economic growth miracles of the 20th century, but also about many of the major political and economic shifts of the 21st century. First, it explains the theoretical and historical origins of the model, its main characteristics, and its impact on key debates about catch-up development under authoritarian and democratic regimes. After that, it examines the different applications of the model across East Asia, and why it succeeded in some economies and not in others. Finally, it explores why the model seemingly fell out of favor for a time, and the reasons behind its contemporary resurgence.

cilos.description: Explain what the East Asian developmental state model is, what its theoretical and historical origins and main characteristics are, and how it has evolved over time.

Analyze the different ways in which the East Asian developmental state model was applied across East Asia, and the various endogenous and exogenous political, economic, social, cultural, and historical reasons why it was such a resounding success in some economies but not in others.
Distinguish between different types of state-society and state-market relations, different forms of industrial policymaking, and different paths of technological upgrading across East Asia.

Evaluate the impact of the East Asian developmental state model and its evolution on the key theoretical, empirical, and practical debates about catch-up development, authoritarian developmentalism, authoritarian modernism, and the modernization theory of democracy.

Develop essential critical thinking, analytical, research, writing, and presentation skills necessary for the creation and implementation of comprehensive policy strategies and effective enforcement mechanisms aimed at fostering growth and development in East Asia and beyond.

courses.title: Preventing and Combating Corruption in Public and Private Sectors
courses.description: This course introduces students to the never-ending fight against corruption, the all-pervasive phenomenon which at once constitutes one of the earliest concerns of moral and political discourse, a persistent blight on the full spectrum of human affairs, and one of the most serious global threats of our time. First, it explains what corruption is, what its global impacts are, and the distinct forms it takes in different types of political systems. After that, it examines the unique ways in which corruption manifests across public and private sectors, and the most common institutional, technological, and societal approaches to preventing and combating it. Finally, it explores the impacts of corruption on selected key issue areas.

cilos.description: Explain what corruption is, what forms and degrees it comes in, how it is measured, and the unique ways in which it manifests in different political systems and across public and private sectors.
Analyze the impacts of corruption on a wide range of global challenges and the key issue areas of human rights, gender, education, and peace and security.
Distinguish between the objectives and strategies of different state and non-state actors in their attempts to either engage in corruption or struggle to prevent and combat it.

Evaluate the effectiveness of the most common institutional, technological, and societal approaches to preventing and combating corruption, and the potential effectiveness as well as the technical and political feasibility of more ambitious approaches.

Develop essential critical thinking, analytical, research, writing, and presentation skills necessary for the creation and implementation of comprehensive policy strategies and effective enforcement mechanisms that adequately address the challenges posed by corruption.

courses.title: Political Economy of Global Offshore Finance and Its Regulation
courses.description: This course introduces students to the complex workings of global offshore finance, the parallel universe of secretive tax havens and unscrupulous accountants, lawyers, bankers, and other professionals that enable the world’s wealthiest individuals, multinational enterprises, transnational criminal networks, and rogue states to circumvent their societal obligations. First, it explains how global offshore finance operates and why it has grown so influential within the global economy. After that, it examines its impact on a wide range of global political, economic, social, and security challenges. Finally, it explores the evolving regulatory and legislative landscape designed to curb its worst excesses. The course will appeal to students pursuing careers in international institutions, national regulatory agencies, consulting and advisory firms, corporate compliance departments, think tanks, civil society organizations, news media outlets, and other relevant bodies.

cilos.description: Explain the key concepts, mechanisms, and structural characteristics relevant to the functioning of global offshore finance, as well as the historical, geographical, political, and economic factors that led to its original formation, continuing evolution, and contemporary significance.

Analyze the impact of global offshore finance on a wide range of challenges facing the world, including offshore tax evasion and avoidance, income and wealth inequality, unfair market competition, financial instability, persistent underdevelopment, and continuing volatility of the global security environment.

Distinguish between the objectives of different state and non-state actors, the diverse reasons behind their objectives, and the various strategies and tools they deploy in their attempts to preserve or change the regulatory and legislative status quo of global offshore finance.

Evaluate the effectiveness of existing policies, frameworks, reforms, initiatives, campaigns, and other efforts aimed at reining in global offshore finance, and the potential effectiveness as well as the technical and political feasibility of more ambitious approaches.

Develop essential critical thinking, analytical, research, writing, and presentation skills necessary for the creation and implementation of comprehensive policy strategies, informed policy proposals, and effective enforcement mechanisms that adequately address the challenges posed by global offshore finance.

courses.title: Green and Sustainable Finance
courses.description: Achieving global climate and other sustainability goals faces significant challenges, one of the most important being the investment gap. This course introduces students to the foundations of green and sustainable finance, such as its definition, markets and instruments, as well as the three elements of ESG investing. At the end of the semester, students should have a strong background to be able to study for the CFA Institute’s Certificate in ESG Investing and the Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP)’s Sustainability and Climate Risk (SCR) Certificate, which will give them a cutting edge when applying for jobs related to ESG and sustainable finance in general.

cilos.description: Understand why green finance is crucial for sustainable development and climate action.
Define what constitutes green and sustainable finance and what are common sustainable and green finance instruments and products.
Identify and discuss motivations for firms to adopt green strategies.
Define different types of climate risks and describe how climate risks affect individual corporates and the financial system.
Explain how climate risk is measured and managed, covering both physical and transition risks.
Understand the general methodology and application of ESG investing, including common ESG ratings, metrics and indexes.
Understand the steps to prepare an ESG report according to the HKEX ESG reporting guide.
Propose recommendations as to how to develop Hong Kong into a global green finance center.

courses.title: Innovation Policy for Critical Technologies amidst Great Power Competition
courses.description: As nations increasingly view technological leadership as central to economic prosperity, national security, and global influence, innovation ecosystems have become arenas of intense international competition and strategic maneuvering. This course explores the intersection of innovation policy, critical emerging technologies, and contemporary geopolitical dynamics.

cilos.description: Analyze the primary theoretical frameworks linking innovation, economic growth, national security, and international relations.
Identify and evaluate the diverse range of policy tools governments use to promote innovation and manage its geopolitical implications.
Compare and contrast the national innovation strategies and policy approaches of major global actors in key technology sectors.
Assess the impact of geopolitical competition, supply chain dynamics, and techno-nationalism on innovation ecosystems and policy choices.
Analyze the challenges and opportunities for international cooperation on science and technology amidst geopolitical tensions.
Critically evaluate the ethical and societal implications of innovation policies pursued in a competitive environment.
Develop and articulate evidence-based policy recommendations addressing challenges at the intersection of innovation and geopolitics.
Understand the basics of the scientific and technological principles that underpin critical technologies.

courses.title: Urban Studies, Disaster Governance and Resilience
courses.description: This academically rigorous and interdisciplinary course equips students with a critical understanding of the interplay between urban development, disaster governance, and resilience. It emphasizes academic research skills through training in qualitative and quantitative methodologies. Students will conduct literature reviews, analyze data, and develop case studies that bridge theory and practice.

cilos.description: Identify and articulate key urbanization trends and their implications within regional and global policy contexts.
Analyze complex urban and regional planning challenges through critical engagement with theoretical and empirical literature.
Apply planning and policy theories to real-world urban development scenarios and case studies.
Design policy interventions and planning strategies to address specific urban issues such as housing, infrastructure, or environmental sustainability.
Develop and carry out independent research projects in a chosen area of urban policy or planning.
Evaluate the effectiveness and implications of existing urban policies using appropriate analytical and resilience-thinking frameworks.
Conduct policy analysis and present planning strategies through well-structured written reports and oral presentations.
Engage in critical discussions to formulate and defend informed perspectives on contemporary urban policy issues.

courses.title: Governing Global-City Hong Kong
courses.description: This course takes a practitioner-oriented look at governance and public policies in Hong Kong, one of Asia’s leading global cities. It will examine foundational concepts in governance and economic development and situate Hong Kong’s experience in these contexts. The course will feature guest lectures by former senior officials of the Hong Kong SAR government.

cilos.description: Describe how Hong Kong is governed and explain its exceptionalism.
Articulate the key features of the Hong Kong economy and highlight its strengths, weaknesses and differences with other successful Asian economies.
Highlight key achievements and challenges in selected policy domains in Hong Kong, e.g. transport, housing, the environment, technology and innovation, labor and welfare.
Discuss the opportunities and challenges for Hong Kong presented by the Greater Bay Area.
Analyze contemporary policy developments and comment intelligently on their impacts/implications for Hong Kong’s prospects.

courses.title: Professional Development for Taught Postgraduate Students
courses.description: This course aims at equipping taught postgraduate students with transferrable skills conducive to their professional and career developments. Students are required to attend a mandatory training session on topics including plagiarism, group work and approaching the case study methods as well as a series of compulsory and optional sessions of career talks, presentation skills and English enhancement workshops in their course of program study. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Develop a comprehensive set of essential transferrable skills to enhance professional development in the discipline.
Recognize the major issues and updated development in the area of public policy.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study in a designated subject under direct guidance of a faculty member to provide students the advanced knowledge and research skill sets on a public policy topic. Required readings, tutorial discussions, and submission of report(s) will be used for assessment. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are studied. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Appreciate the importance of global and regional public policy development.
Communicate complex ideas in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of public policy impacts.
Identify the different levels of organization and structure within public policy.
Analyze the efficiency and equity implications of government interference in various markets/stakeholders.

courses.title: Special Topics in Public Policy
courses.description: This course covers emerging topics of public policy concerns not covered in the present curriculum. The course aims to provide students with advanced knowledge and research skill sets on a public policy topic. Required readings, tutorial discussions, and submission of report(s) will be used for assessment. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are studied.

cilos.description: Recognize the importance of global and regional public policy development in the topic concerned.
Communicate complex ideas related to the topic in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of public policy impacts in the topic concerned.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation in public sector.

courses.title: Policy Analysis Project
courses.description: An independent group project carrying 6 credits cover two consecutive regular terms for students to work on selected topics in public policy under the supervision of a faculty member. The project is designed to help student learn how to identify some public policy problem and prepare, design and select public policy measure or program to mitigate/solve it. Participation of both internal communities of the university and external organizations in these projects will be highly encouraged. The responsibility of control, administration and assessment of the projects rest with the University. Students will hone their ability to work in team, analyze policy issues and develop concise report of their findings and recommendations. The paper should be written as though for a particular decision-maker in government or a nonprofit organization, with the writer assuming the role of a staff assistant to this decision-maker. This course is for MPP students only. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Analyze the background of a policy problem from multiple perspectives and also the needs of the client.
Develop research questions and plans that articulate the client's needs.
Demonstrate clear and sound reasons for their literature selection and consideration for their methods adoption; which at the same time are adequate to address their client's policy problem.
Collect data that is appropriate to address the client's policy problem.
Systematically sort out collected data and use a comprehensive analytical framework to interpret the data.
Draw practical and theoretical inferences from the data analysis.
Construct cogent argument for policy decision.
Present confidently and persuasively.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: Capstone project offers a unique opportunity for students to focus on specific areas of public policy and management in Hong Kong, China, or Asia and carry out in-depth studies. Students may expect discussions of issues that have been the cornerstones of the regions’ development that they choose. HKUST is well-positioned to share the experience of effective governance across Greater China in particular, and Asia-Pacific in general. Faculty supervisors will work with students to reach out to the practitioners in the public sector. Students will apply what they have learnt in class to analyze and solve the problems in the real and dynamic society. The project brings students to reflect on the overall training in the MPM Program and helps them consolidate their knowledge in the area.

cilos.description: Identify, design, and apply appropriate methods to conduct rigorous research.
Integrate and apply knowledge and skills gained in MPM courses to a public management problem.
Communicate complex research findings effectively.
Provide new information and analysis to inform policymaking.

courses.title: Study Visit to An Asian Global City
courses.description: This course takes students to one of the global cities in Asia - Tokyo or Singapore - to study their economic development and their contemporary economic and policy challenges. The study visit to Japan would examine Japan’s lost decades and its balance sheet recession between the late 1990s and early 2010s. It will help students appreciate how the country survived nearly two decades of economic stagnation and examine lessons for contemporary China, which is grappling with similar problems of debt deleveraging, deflation, decline of asset values, and aging demographics. The study visit to Singapore would offer participants a broad introduction to Singapore’s long-term approach in urban planning and infrastructure development, public housing, economic development, water security, and financial sector development.

cilos.description: Articulate Japan/Singapore’s development history and current economic challenges.
Articulate the key features of the Japanese/Singaporean economy and highlight its strengths, weaknesses and differences with other Asian economies.
Highlight key achievements and challenges in selected policy domains in Japan/Singapore.
Analyze contemporary policy developments and comment intelligently on their lessons for China/Hong Kong.

courses.title: Professional Development in Public Policy
courses.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students with basic training in career development and related professional skills. This course consists of a number of division-specific workshops. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Develop a comprehensive set of essential transferrable skills to enhance professional development in the discipline.
Recognize the major issues and updated development in the area of public policy.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal on science/technology-based public policy research in their chosen fields.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal on science/technology-based public policy research in their chosen fields.

courses.title: Risk Management in Financial Institutions
courses.description: Risk exists in every aspect of our daily life, and risk management is essential for any organization to achieve their business objectives. This course provides an opportunity for students to examine the various kinds of risk existing in society, and learn about the benefits and impacts of risk management. The course focuses on risk measurement and analysis in enterprise business and modern financial institutions. Learning activities consist of a mixture of lectures, case studies and lab exercises. From taking this course, students’ awareness of risk management will be raised. They can also improve their critical thinking and analytical skills, and become responsible and ethical citizens.

cilos.description: Define and classify various kinds of risks in financial institutions
Discuss the reasons and benefits of risk management
Articulate the general risk management framework in a business setting
Examine various risk measurement techniques and practice in the industry
Apply a certain level of quantitative risk analysis in various business scenarios

courses.title: Business Intelligence for Data-Driven Decisions
courses.description: Business intelligence is a discipline that comprises a set of theories, methodologies and processes to analyze business data with the aim of improving an organization's decision making, business planning and projection. Tomorrow’s employees and executives may not need the advanced skills of a data scientist, but they must be data literate. Therefore, there is a need to bring together data skills and business management by introducing a common core course, specializing at applying data analytics techniques to business scenarios for the implementation of business intelligence. The aim of this course is to introduce the general workflow of business intelligence and various applications of data analytics models in business scenarios. The course also focuses on an analysis of the strengths, limitations, causes and benefits of the use of business intelligence. The course also includes hands-on practical exercises by using data mining and statistics models on real business data sets.

cilos.description: Outline and describe different types of business intelligence methods
Examine and describe how business intelligence methods can facilitate business decision making and improve the profitability of a company
Articulate the difficulties and complexities of managing BI projects, as well as the social and economic impact of such applications
Apply data analytics techniques on small datasets for a simple implementation of business intelligence

courses.title: Special Topics in Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This special topics course provides an opportunity for students to understand the fundamental knowledge and current development in the field of risk management and business intelligence. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings, structured readings, discussion sessions etc depending on the nature of topics. The course maybe repeated for credits if different topics are taken. Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
Understand the importance of the fundamental knowledge required for learning the RM / Bl related techniques.
Better plan their studies and future career path.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development in Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This course is designed to provide academic advising to students throughout their studies in the RMBI program, to enhance their understanding of the industries relevant to Risk Management and Business Intelligence and the related techniques expected by the market. Students are required to attend seminars and discussion sessions. For RMBI students only. Graded P/PP/F.

cilos.description: Plan their studies according to the future career they pursue.
Recognize the relevant industries of Risk Management and Business Intelligence and the future development.
Understand the importance of the fundamental knowledge required for learning the techniques relevant to RM and BI.

courses.title: Special Topics in Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This special topics course provides an opportunity for students to gain a more in-depth knowledge required for learning the techniques relevant to RM and BI. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings, structured readings, discussion sessions etc depending on the nature of topics. The course maybe repeated for credits if different topics are taken. Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
Gain a more in-depth knowledge required for learning the techniques relevant to RM and Bl.
Better plan their studies and future career path.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Data Analytics with R
courses.description: This course provides a hands-on introduction to R as a programming language and environment for data analytics and visualization. It will cover the basic syntax including functions and flow control, some commonly used data structures such as vectors, lists, matrices and data frames, as well as data importing and visualization in R. The course will also introduce a few primary data cleaning techniques in dealing with missing values, duplicates and inconsistency, and means to implement simple data transformation and normalization with R. Classic data mining models and the corresponding packages in R will also be presented, with the focus on model fine tuning and parameter calibration for practical applications. For RMBI students only.

cilos.description: Demonstrate competency in the use of data structures and functions in R.
Test, trace and debug small programs written in R.
Apply basic exploratory techniques and classic data mining models in R to real data analysis problems.

courses.title: Practicing Risk Management using Case Studies
courses.description: This course will examine various types of risks that many business enterprises face nowadays; for example, financial markets risks can be further divided into equity risk, foreign exchange risk, credit risk, interest rate risk and commodity risk. In addition, other non-financial risk factors such as operational risk, reputational risk, catastrophe risk (earthquake/typhoon), geopolitical risk, cybersecurity risk, counterparty risk and liquidity risk will also be discussed. The format of the course is based on a series of real-life case studies from well-known companies (Alibaba, GM, Enron, Citibank, Merrill Lynch etc.) and educational institutions (Harvard & Yale etc.) Students must prepare for every class by having read the assigned cases before arriving class. Participation in every case discussion is mandatory.

cilos.description: Acquire domain knowledge on assessing financial risk and non-financial risk.
Learn to apply qualitative and quantitative risk analysis skills in various business cases.
Develop effective communication skills between teams and individuals with opposing views under the risk management context.
Enhance problem solving skills and decision-making skills for business scenarios with uncertainty and limited sources by risk mitigation planning.
Make legal and business arguments based on facts and logical interpretations of precedent successful/failed risk management cases.

courses.title: Introduction to Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This course presents basic concepts and techniques for risk management and business intelligence. Various types of risk such as market risk, credit risk and operational risk are discussed with business applications and regulatory issues. Modern development of business intelligence, data management techniques and related applications like financial analysis, risk assessment, customer relationship management and human capital productivity analysis are also presented.

cilos.description: Apply and evaluate quantitative risk analysis tools to make smart decision in financial markets.
Interpret and apply the business intelligence technique to make smart decision in financial markets. .

courses.title: Special Topics in Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This subject provides an opportunity for students to learn about the current development in the field of risk management and business intelligence. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings or structured readings.

cilos.description: Describe key milestones and emerging issues in the fields of risk management and business intelligence.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Risk Management
courses.description: The course covers statistical analysis, simulation and optimization methods that are commonly used in management of both market and credit risk. Risk factors and loss distribution. Losses over several periods and scaling. Coherent measures of risk. Capital allocation. Extreme value analysis. Importance sampling. Simulation techniques, including random number generations, variance reduction methods and statistical analysis of simulation outputs. Bernoulli mixture models. Financial and actuarial pricing of credit risk. Case studies of major credit losses.

courses.title: Life Contingencies Models and Insurance Risk
courses.description: The topics discussed in this course include survival models, life tables and selection, insurance benefits, annuities, premium calculation, and insurance policy values.
courses.prerequisite: ELEC 2600 OR ISOM 3540 OR MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431

cilos.description: Understand the models used to model decrements used in insurances, annuities, and investments and how to calculate probabilities based on those models.
Understand the models used to model cash flows of life insurances and annuities and how to calculate the present values of the cash flows based on those models.
Understand the methods for calculating benefit reserves for traditional life insurances and annuities and basic universal life insurances.
Understand the models used to model cash flows for basic universal life insurances and how to calculate present values and contract level values.
Understand the relationship between expenses and gross premium and how to calculate contract level values based on the gross premium for life insurances and annuities.
Enhance the ability of using advanced mathematics (calculus, probability, statistics, etc.) to solve real-world problems.
Enhance the ability of building stochastic and statistical models for life contingencies.
Enhance the ability of using computational software such as Matlab and implementing mathematical models using computer programs.

courses.title: Advanced Data Mining for Risk Management and Business Intelligence
courses.description: This course will explore some advanced principles and techniques of data mining, with emphasis on applications in risk management and business intelligence. Topics include data mining process for data transformation and integration, data preprocessing, data mining algorithms and evaluation of data mining models and results. Advanced topics include data stream analysis, using data warehouse for decision support, supervised, semi-supervised and unsupervised learning techniques in data mining. We will cover advanced data mining applications in credit risk analysis, scale up methods for mining massive customer data and various novel applications such as data mining applications in social network analysis. Projects are aimed at familiarize the students with the entire data mining process rather than isolated applications.

cilos.description: Understand issues related to real-world data mining.
Demonstarte an ability to master the tools and skills for large-scale data mining projects.
Describe the key concepts and applications of business intelligence and social media analytics.

courses.title: Risk Management and Business Intelligence Capstone Project I
courses.description: Student conducts an in-depth study on selected topics in Risk Management and Business Intelligence under the supervision of a faculty. Scope may include the identification of a non-reference problem, followed by subsequent analysis and solution of the problem. Creative and critical thinking in the decision processes made under uncertainty are expected to be demonstrated in the project.

cilos.description: Write a proposal for a company project.
Suggest a scope for a company research problem.
Identify suitable risk management and business intelligence techniques to solve the research problem.
Decide the timeline of the project.
Present and deliver all outcomes of the project.

courses.title: Risk Management and Business Intelligence Capstone Project II
courses.description: This is the continuation of RMBI 4980. Student conducts an in-depth study on selected topics in Risk Management and Business Intelligence under the supervision of a faculty. Scope may include the identification of a non-reference problem, followed by subsequent analysis and solution of the problem. Creative and critical thinking in the decision processes made under uncertainty are expected to be demonstrated in the project.

cilos.description: Write a proposal for a company project.
Suggest a scope for a company research problem.
Identify suitable risk management and business intelligence techniques to solve the research problem.
Decide the timeline of the project.
Present and deliver all outcomes of the project.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct crossdisciplinary research in Robotics and Autonomous Systems.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: Business Study Trip
courses.description: This course is offered in the form of a study trip to another country in the winter and summer term.  Each study trip will consist of at least three elements, namely lectures delivered by faculty members at the host institution, company visits and cultural adventure in the host country.  Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course.  Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Demonstrate cultural awareness and adaptability by actively participating in cultural adventures, showcasing the ability to engage with diverse environments and practices.

Apply knowledge gained from study trip activites to critically analyze real-world business operations and strategies in the host country, fostering an understanding of practical applications in a global context.

Reflect on the overall experience of the study trip, integrating insights from trip activities, including but not limited to lectures, company visits, and cultural interactions to articulate a comprehensive understanding of international business dynamics.

courses.title: Business Student Induction
courses.description: This is an induction course designed for all new students in the School of Business and Management. Students will be divided into 10 cohorts and assigned to designated academic advisors. They will also be participating in a series of planned activities, aiming to help them build bonds and simultaneously identify personal academic interest, examine educational goals, and develop plans to meet objectives through academic advising and other personal development workshops and programs. Graded P or F.

courses.title: Community Services Project
courses.description: This course is offered in a form of a community project at a designated non-governmental organization (NGO) under the supervision of the School. Students are required to attend all the training sessions, design and implement the service project or participate in the service learning tasks as instructed by the host NGO and/or the course instructors. By the end of the course, students have to submit a reflective statement in the format of a paper, a group project report or a presentation to demonstrate the attainment of all intended learning outcomes, in addition to other requirements of the relevant NGO as appropriate. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded PP, P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Gain and apply solid working experience at a real workplace, engaging with the front stage and backstage of the service, and understand the society from a social good perspective.
Understand the society from a social good perspective.

Apply skills to real-world challenges, applying expertise in areas such as project management, research, advocacy, fundraising, communications, or any other relevant field to contribute to the organization's mission and goals.

Explore the careers in NGOs and SE, gaining experience in different roles, departments, or even different organizations within the sector. The goal is to broaden knowledge, gain exposure, and identify areas of interest and expertise.
Facilitate personal growth, engaging in activities that foster personal growth, resilience, and self-awareness.

courses.title: Social Enterprise Internship Program
courses.description: The course is intended to give business undergraduate students an opportunity to gain exposure in the area of social entrepreneurship and apply their knowledge to solve real-world challenges facing these organizations. It is conducted in the form of an internship program at a designated social enterprise under the supervision of the School of Business and Management. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Analyze basic organizational and the Project Partner issues from both internal and external perspectives.
Participate interactively in team discussions and decision-making.
Present essential findings in both written and oral form to a variety of stakeholders in the project.
Applies concepts, knowledge, skills and methodologies learned from business courses to specific, real-world business problems and issues.

courses.title: SBM Cooperative Education Program
courses.description: This course is intended to enhance SBM students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For SBM Year 2 students or above only. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

courses.title: Special Topics in Business and Management
courses.description: Special topics in an identified area of Business and Management; topics vary with instructor.  May be graded P or F.

cilos.description: (Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Business Field Study Fundamentals
courses.description: The course is mostly a supervised study of a real-life issue faced by an organization.  Students will be given opportunities to support organization's effort through assisting in collection and analysis of data, identification of strategic questions, design of studies, development and reporting.  At the end of the course, students will be given a taste of real-life business experience.  Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course.  May be Graded DI/PA/F.

courses.title: Corporate Project
courses.description: Students apply skills and knowledge learned from business courses to focus on specific projects in a corporation setting. Students will work on group projects sponsored by participating corporations and supervised by faculty members. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded PP, P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.

cilos.description: Apply the business knowledge and innovative approaches to real-world business problems.
Serve as student consultants and provide solutions to business issues faced by corporate partners.
Participate interactively in team discussions and decision-making.
Present essential findings in both written and oral form to a variety of stakeholders in the project.

courses.title: Business Competitions
courses.description: In each business competition, students will be required to examine the conceptual and practical aspects of business policies and policy decision making by utilizing all the concepts, theories and tools that they learned in previous courses. This 1-credit course is offered in recognition of the students' outstanding performance in their participation of business competitions. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different case competitions are taken.

cilos.description: Acquire effective techniques for interpersonal communication and teamwork in addition to real life opportunities and experience of thinking-on-your-feet.
Simulates the urgency, complexity, and uncertainty prevalent in "real-world" business organizations.

courses.title: SBM Undergraduate Honors Research Project
courses.description: The two‐term SBM Undergraduate Honors Research Project is for SBM students who are interested in pursuing systematic research at the senior undergraduate level. The course will act as a pre‐doctoral training program to help students expand their options in seeking future doctoral study opportunities. Students are expected to research a focused problem under close supervision by a faculty and produce a thesis after completing this course. For SBM students in their final year of study only. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Describe the process of academic research in a selected business discipline.
Describe, compare, and contrast different research methodologies.
Analyze the contextual features leading to particular individual, organizational, or social outcomes in a chosen business setting and problem.
Apply or adapt appropriate research methodology to study the chosen problem.
Develop a research paper with scope and quality commensurate with a top conference paper in the selected business discipline.
Present the research to an expert panel.

courses.title: Accounting for Managers
courses.description: The first part of the course provides students with a basic foundation and practical understanding of financial accounting.  Focus is on the design, use and impact of financial information and accounting measures in organizational planning and control.  The second part of the course is to apply and analyze accounting information in managerial decision making with the fundamental concepts of accrual accounting given in the first part.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Comprehensively explain major principles governing financial and managerial accounting.
Develop analytical and basic technical skills required to prepare financial accounting records and reports, as well as to use and interpret them.
Identify the role of managerial accounting in decision-making process of managers in business organizations.
Form critical judgement by identifying and defining accounting and business problems, applying analytical and quantitative techniques, and making and justifying decision.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Economics and Finance
courses.description: The first part of the course covers managerial economics: understanding of economics and the application of economic analysis in the context of the needs of management and of managerial decision-making in today's changing environment.  The second part of the course covers the basic concepts in finance.  Topics include time value of money, valuation of securities, capital budgeting including computation of cash flows, NPV, IRR, portfolio theory and capital asset pricing model, and rudimentary concepts about options and futures contracts.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Identify basic Microeconomic theories such as consumer theory, firms' optimal decision making under different contexts, and the operation and properties of perfectly competitive markets.
Recognize the Economics methodology and apply economic analysis in managerial decision making.

courses.title: Marketing Management and Strategy
courses.description: The first part of this module covers marketing management using the framework of the 4P's (Product, Price, Promotion and Place).  Topics include consumer needs and wants, marketing research, advertising and sales promotion, pricing theory, etc.  The impact of the Internet on all aspects of marketing will also be examined.  The second part will cover marketing and business policy from a strategic perspective.  Decision making in a competitive environment in the face of environmental constraints will also be examined.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.

cilos.description: Conduct a marketing environmental analysis and identify market opportunities that will be strategically fit with the company or organization.
Identify and evaluate segments, and decide on the appropriate target(s) within a given market.
Construct a persuasive value proposition and positioning statement for a given offering.
Formulate marketing strategies and make strategic marketing decisions, including specific marketing mix strategies.
Monitor and control strategic marketing plans.
Make effective presentations of a company’s or organization’s marketing plan.

courses.title: Applied Statistics in Business Intelligence for Decision Making/ Business Forecasting
courses.description: Applied Statistics is a tool that can be used in a variety of business settings, but despite the widespread discussion of terms like Business Intelligence, the truth is that these areas are actually not very well understood. Advances in computing power can now give businesses ways to analyze data that they never could before. This course examines with these advances, how firms can make decisions about pricing, marketing, new products, and resource allocation more effectively than they have ever been able to in the past. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Define statistical concepts.
Explain the use of statistical tools in a business setting.
Exemplify the broad applications of business intelligence.
Explain in general terms what steps firms need to take to implement business intelligence.
Identify areas where business intelligence can alter the way a company conducts operations.

courses.title: ESG Investing and Green Finance Strategy for Portfolio Management
courses.description: This course examines the different frameworks for incorporating environmental, social and governance (ESG) and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives. The various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, ESG integration, ESG engagement and ESG screening will be covered comprehensively. The full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes will be covered.

cilos.description: Understand different frameworks for incorporating ESG and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives.
Master the various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, integration, engagement and screening.
Familiarize with full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes.
Acknowledge traps and pitfalls in implementing an ESG strategy via case study of practical ESG investing application.
Understand carbon pricing and trading.

courses.title: Creativity and Innovation in Marketing
courses.description: This course will cover several systematic creative problem-solving methodologies which are appropriately implemented when a decision has been made to search for a creative solution. Apart from focusing on new product ideation and creative marketing actions, it offers skills to learn how to solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.

cilos.description: Master systematic creative problem-solving methodologies and its implementation.
Solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.
Understand product ideation and creative marketing actions.
Identify and resolve communications dilemma.

courses.title: Sustainability Applications in the Corporate World
courses.description: Sustainability is a topic of increasing focus for public and private companies around the world. With global environmental and other societal challenges increasing, and with increasing interest anticipated, trillions of dollars in market share are beginning to shift. This battle for future market share may well be won by those who respond best to this new corporate, policy and investment paradigm. This course provides students with the experience, tools and community of practice they will need to become an important part of this global paradigm. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand real-world applications of sustainability.
Develop responses to Environmental, Social and Governance challenges.
Analyze short-term profitability versus long-term sustainability and tradeoffs.

courses.title: C-suite Life
courses.description: The course aims to provide a simulated and role-play environment to enable students to apply their MBA learnings and experience in a complex management world. C-Suite Life is a real-time, live case study that covers a broad range of business challenges spanning the field of management. Full engagement from students is expected.

cilos.description: Analyze the crisis with managerial insight and instinct.
Generate well-structured solutions, actions, and responses timely when a crisis occurs.
Apply theory and practice for effective decision-making.
Develop a crisis management team.

courses.title: Enhancing Professional Skills
courses.description: It aims at helping MBA students work intensively on developing or improving some key presentation skills which will be useful to them throughout their business careers. Simply put, the essence of Enhancing Professional Skills as “Making a Logical, Effective and Persuasive Business Presentation". Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify the key issues from a tangle of issues, to analyze and develop solutions.
Create and deliver logical, effective and persuasive business presentations.
Enhance communication effectiveness.

courses.title: Business Plans Competition
courses.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to start a successful business from the business plan, to funding, to beginning operations.  Students will go overseas to participate in international business plan competitions.  Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Create ideas and formulate feasible strategies for startups or venture at early growth stage.
Develop and deliver persuasive business presentations.
Integrate and apply the knowledge learnt in business operation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

courses.title: Case Analysis Competition
courses.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to analyze a real-life business case.  Students will go overseas to participant in international case competitions.  Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Analyse a relevant  current case.
Evaluate various business solutions.
Develop and prepare a convincing presentation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

courses.title: AI, Innovation, and Product Management
courses.description: This course provides the basic principles and tools that business managers need to ensure outcomes align with business needs. Students will gain an industry insider’s view that goes beyond theory to cover actionable guidelines, practical tips, and best practices. By examining the differing modes of product development in Silicon Valley and China, this course provides a new framework and approach for competition and innovation in the Age of AI. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Explain the basic concepts, use cases, applications, and limitations of artificial intelligence.
Apply the skills to leverage AI to capture market opportunities and address operational needs.
Explain the basic methodology, tools, and concepts of product management, including how to build AI into a company’s products and services.
Develop product strategy at both the corporate and startup level.
Differentiate the different modes of innovation and AI between the East and West.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Accounting
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in financial accounting, managerial accounting and finance to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. The course will also cover the basic business concepts, financial statement analysis, cost classifications and how to do managerial decisions. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in both financial and managerial accounting.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Evaluate cost-volume-profit analysis and apply core managerial accounting information to strategic decision making.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Python
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in technical skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. Python is used for creating high-level abstractions for well-written and well-optimized frameworks, where business applications rely on. The course will cover Python programming language for developing business applications, the practical libraries and packages. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in business programming and Python syntax.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in technical knowledge level among students from different background to assist  smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Design and debug Python programs.
Develop business applications with Python.

courses.title: MBA Accelerator - Data Analysis
courses.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in quantitative and analysis hard skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. It will cover data and variation, probability model and association between random variables at introductory level. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental knowledge in quantitative skills and statistics analysis.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of statistics and hard skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Recognize and describe statistical methods typically used in the analysis of business data.

courses.title: Fundamental Value Investing: Applications to Public and Private Equity
courses.description: This course covers value investing from a practitioner’s perspective and is oriented around the value investing framework and process culminating in an interactive presentation to an Investment Committee. Participants will learn key concepts and tools used in value investing, how to analyze and determine what makes a good business, and how to assess intrinsic value.

cilos.description: Identify and evaluate investment opportunities.
Develop value investment analysis, including analyzing businesses, financial modelling and valuation.
Recognize risks and the due diligence process.
Differentiate the commonalities and differences between value investing in private and public companies.

courses.title: Financial and Money Markets from Macroeconomic Perspectives
courses.description: The course will discuss the main financial markets, their characteristics and how they are linked to the economy. It starts by explaining how global financial markets are structured and how this structure services both borrowers and investors. Asset classes for investor funds are reviewed before the focus turns to the macroeconomic environment. Fixed income, equities, commodities and real estate are also covered in detail and students will explore how hedge funds and private equity firms create value for their stakeholders.

cilos.description: Analyze the impacts from the release of economic data.
Compare the key derivative products which are relevant to most major securities markets.
Evaluate time value of money, yield curves, the price/yield relationship and market quoting conventions.
Recognize the process of investing in real estate assets.

courses.title: From MBA to Stock Market: Applied Value Investing
courses.description: This course will deliver the frameworks and processes of value investing that some of the most successful investors in the world employ to manage and preserve capital. Students will learn to use quantitative valuation techniques, such as asset-based, earning power, and the value of growth, to develop a strategic methodology for estimating a company's franchise value. A number of case studies will be used throughout the program to improve students’ ability to manage a value portfolio. Graded P or F.

courses.title: Personal Wealth Management for Working Professionals
courses.description: The course aims to focus on several major financial products which are widely traded, but not widely understood, such as stock, foreign exchange, bonds, insurance and other derivatives. Students will learn about managing own personal wealth by using technical analytics skills to breakdown different common investment products and examine the impacts of behavioral psychology in the trading market. The course will also systematically introduce how the macro-economic cycles and megatrends affect businesses and markets. Students will acquire how to identify and analyze the investment opportunities, manage risks and articulate their views in portfolio construction. An overview of common insurance products available in the retail market will be discussed, with an emphasis on finding the right insurance coverage for individual needs, as part of one’s wealth management strategy.

cilos.description: Execute the portfolio construction.
Recognize the foreign exchange (FX) market, the commonly traded FX derivatives and the reasons for trading them.
Evaluate appropriate insurance package for different individual needs.
Apply technical skills to analyze different investment products.

courses.title: Economic Development in Asia: A Practitioner’s Perspective
courses.description: This course examines how economic development has occurred in East Asia, emphasizing the importance of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity. Throughout the course, students will discover growth opportunities for businesses in Asia not only from a corporate strategy and operations perspective but also from an investor’s perspective.

cilos.description: Recognize the key principles and practices of economic development, focusing on the role of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity.
Analyze and evaluate contemporary growth and development challenges faced by major Asian economies.
Identify and interpret the implications of growth and development challenges on business opportunities and investment strategies.

courses.title: Special Topics
