In addition, the course provides an introduction to SAS, one of the most widely used statistical programming languages for manipulating and analyzing data.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.
Present their discipline knowledge, teach independent courses, and/or lead discussion sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

courses.title: Navigating Business Decisions with Data and Causality
courses.description: This course aims to teach students basic conceptions and methods for conducting causal estimations in business problems. The course will cover classical causal inference framework, and different methodologies that could be used in various settings, including randomized, quasi-, and natural experiments, and observation data.

cilos.description: Understand some common applications of causal inference in business problems.
Evaluate the validity and value of an experiment for causal analysis.
Collect appropriate observational data sets for causal analysis.
Design rigorous experiments to properly measure the causal impact of a given policy.
Identify appropriate methodology for conducting causal estimates using a given dataset and context.
Avoid expensive mistakes in their research work by using appropriate experimental design or methodologies.
Derive valuable insights from their causal research to improve business decision making.

courses.title: Marketing Communication
courses.description: Marketing communication is a part of the marketing mix that establishes and builds relationships with the market through directly or indirectly --- informing, persuading, and reminding customers about their offering. This course is designed to help students develop an integrated marketing communication plan and evaluate its effectiveness.

cilos.description: Explain the importance of marketing communication in marketing strategy.
Discuss the communication process to the core customers by establishing points of parity and points of differentiation for the brand.
Present the important issues in planning and evaluating integrated marketing communication.
Apply the appropriate marketing framework, theories and tools to plan, develop, and evaluate marketing communications.
Propose a complete marketing communication campaign.

courses.title: Business to Business Marketing
courses.description: A comprehensive approach to Business to Business (B2B) marketing that includes specific practical applications as well as theoretical constructs necessary for successful outcomes in the B2B space. The course includes case studies, outside reading, and a group project requiring students to submit a B2B marketing plan for approval, giving students a real-world experience. Throughout the course, the emphasis is on current global best practices.

cilos.description: Enumerate and explain fully the key differences between Business to Consumer (B2C) and Business to Business (B2B) marketing.
Describe in detail the functions and roles of each actor in the Decision-Making Unit (DMU).
Quantify the importance and placement of ESG/DEI in B2B marketing.
Evaluate and quantify the role and significance of personal selling in B2B markets.
Create targeted communications strategy and tactics.
Execute pricing strategies and practices in B2B marketing.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Marketing
courses.description: In the last decade, we have seen a significant increase in the number of startups being founded globally with their biggest challenges being growth and expansion. In this course, students will learn how to think entrepreneurially when it comes to marketing. The course will discuss topics such as business planning, building brand awareness and growth using strategic and innovative marketing approach. Whether students are looking to start their own business, join a startup, or join a corporation that values an intrapreneurial spirit, this course will teach them the essentials/basics they need to succeed.

cilos.description: Understand what is entrepreneurship: launching and working at a startup – the opportunities and challenges.
Assess market opportunities and challenges in the global marketplace.
Build a strategic, scalable and sustainable marketing journey.
Use technology to build a sustainable and eco-friendly footprint.
Understand how marketing software (AI and data analytics) can enable quicker growth.

courses.title: Marketing Strategy Simulation
courses.description: This course draws upon knowledge participants acquired from various marketing courses. The course adopts an experiential learning approach using a marketing business simulation, a learning-by-doing mindset. Students will come as close to a real-world business environment as they can get in a classroom setting. Students will play the role of a marketing team of a firm and compete against other teams making a variety of marketing strategic and tactical decisions. Teams will have to develop a comprehensive, workable and successful marketing strategy, making use of a wide variety of marketing analytical tools to guide their environmental analysis and decision making. The simulation will stretch over several rounds. The course will be complemented with case analyses related to the topics covered in the simulation.

cilos.description: Understand and know how to use marketing analytical tools.
Develop marketing strategies.
Realize the importance and possible impact of the external environment.
Develop a long-term thinking mindset.
Look at the “big picture” instead of being short-sighted.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
courses.description: This course will give students a high-level overview of Artificial Intelligence technologies, concepts, and business use cases related to Marketing. After the course, students will be able to identify and leverage AI to enhance and/or disrupt business models both within marketing functions and on a larger organizational level. We will also devote part of the course to explore how careers of marketing professionals may change in the future because of AI and get students to think about their professional development in a world where AI and human beings will inevitably work together.

cilos.description: Build an understanding of the fundamental branches of AI and their applications in marketing.
Gain the ability to select what type of AI may be applicable to specific business use cases.
Develop an appreciation for the potential risks and ethical issues involved with the proliferation of AI in marketing and business in general.
Identify business skillsets and personal development goals which will allow them to adapt to jobs of the future in marketing.

courses.title: Analytical Modeling in Marketing
courses.description: This course provides Marketing MPhil/PhD students with foundational knowledge in quantitative marketing, with a focus on analytical modeling. It will cover a range of theoretical topics including pricing, advertising, two-sided markets, consumer search and learning, and information design.

cilos.description: Understand basic marketing theories.
Develop intuitions for important models.
Evaluate research papers with analytical models.

courses.title: Current Topics in Consumer Research
courses.description: Advanced seminar covering current research and theory in consumer behavior and marketing. Topics will vary with the term, but may include areas related to consumer judgment and decision processes, attitude formation and change, reactions to advertising, consumer information procession, affective, motivational and cognitive determinants of consumer behavior, and cultural and individual differences in consumer behavior. May be repeated for credit. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Study of selected areas in marketing knowledge and thought; topics may vary by term; individual projects and reports.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

courses.title: Marketing Action Learning Project
courses.description: A team project that focuses on analyzing and solving a real-world marketing challenge within an organization (e.g., company, NGO). Students will develop marketing consulting experience, collaborate to produce a marketing report, and present their in-depth insights and recommended solutions to the sponsor.

cilos.description: Identify marketing opportunities and challenges
Gather in-depth consumer and market insights
Come up with effective marketing recommendations
Sharpen their team-work and communication skills
Develop marketing strategies and tactical solutions based on market intelligence

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Study of selected marketing issues under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.
Present their discipline knowledge and lead discussion sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: This seminar focuses on special topics in marketing; possible topics are measurement and structural equation modeling, agency theory, channel structures, diffusion modeling, group decision making, information processing, attribution theory, philosophy of science and categorization theory.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.
Present their discipline knowledge and lead discussion sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

courses.title: Research Methods in Social Science
courses.description: This is an introduction to research methodology in the social science. It is intended to provide foundational training in the major approaches in the social sciences to the collection and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data, and the specification and testing of theories. The course overs the logic of scientific inquiry and various research techniques such as experimentation, scientific sampling, survey research, field methods, archival data, and quantitative analysis that are commonly used by researchers in economics, education, political science, psychology, and sociology.

cilos.description: Describe the relationship between theory, hypothesis, data collection, and analysis in social science research.
Plan a research study, including specification of hypothesis and selection of data and methods.
Assess whether evidence is indicative of a cause and effect relationship.
Suggest approaches for assessing causal relationships when it is not possible to conduct a traditional experiment.
Describe the most important sources of data used in social science research.
Develop a sampling strategy according to the needs of a research study.

courses.title: Social Statistics I
courses.description: This course teaches basic concepts and skills required to conduct quantitative research in social science. Students will learn to design and conduct statistical analyses to test hypotheses. They will acquire experience in the use of statistical software to carry out analysis of social data.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental concepts and practices in statistics for social science.

Recognize graphic and numerical summary of data with respect to distribution of variables and association between them; data-generating processes and study design; probability theory; probability distributions of continuous variables with a special emphasis on the normal distribution; sampling distributions; principles of statistical inference, including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing; inference for population means and proportions; statistical tests of relationship between two categorical variables; and simple linear regression (OLS).
Operate a popular statistical package for data management and statistical analysis.
Conduct more advanced statistical analysis which is useful in the academic career, financial industries, marketing and consulting.

courses.title: Social Stratification and Mobility
courses.description: This course introduces the concepts and theories in analyzing the pattern of social and economic inequalities in the distribution of resources/rewards/opportunities which are scarce but widely desired, and the process of status attainment or social mobility.

cilos.description: Illustrate major concepts and analytical perspectives sociologists employ to study social inequality and stratification.
Recognize the major empirical findings on social inequality and mobility in mainland China and Hong Kong.
Apply the knowledge to analyze new issues related to social inequality in both mainland China and Hong Kong.

courses.title: Economic Transformations in Post-Mao China
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive account of the transformations in the economic institution of China since the late 1970s.

cilos.description: Critique major works on China’s political economy.
Develop theoretically informed and empirically grounded research papers on important issues in China’s economic transformation.

courses.title: Political Changes and Political Participation
courses.description: This course introduces to students basic theories about political changes, such as democratization and reform, or their absence.  It also discusses the dynamics of such political changes by examining the interactions among different social forces and political actors, including citizens.

cilos.description: Explain the theories on social changes, including reform.
Analyze the dynamics of social and political changes in different political systems.
Identify the problems faced by authoritarian regimes, like China, in managing social changes.

courses.title: Social Statistics II
courses.description: This course provides students with hands-on training on how to use statistical software to analyze non-experimental quantitative data from the real world, to draw sensible conclusions, to convey results, and write a research report.

cilos.description: Explain theoretical foundations of modern regression analysis.
Conduct applied regression analysis using statistical software.
Write academic research paper with a quantitative orientation.
Develop a broader scope for regression analysis in light of further study.

courses.title: Economic Change in Rural China
courses.description: This course is designed to study the development processes of rural China from around the mid-eighteenth century onwards until the present time from primarily (but not exclusively) an economics perspective. In addition to serving the purpose of a survey course, special efforts are made to provide intelligible answers to a number of important issues and puzzles - some of epic proportions - using analytical frameworks in economics.

cilos.description: Explain China’s rural development process, including the difficulties it faced, from the late Qing to the present.

Develop the analytical skills with which to make intelligible sense of this development process, and in understanding the relationship between “variables” in the specific context of rural China, which consists of a number of episodes of salient historical importance.

courses.title: Migration and Globalization
courses.description: This course aims to explore the interrelationship between population changes/ migration and economic development in the era of globalization. Special attention is given to labor migration in China and international migration in China/HKSAR.

cilos.description: Conduct simple demographic analyses, such as population forecast, as well as tempo and international comparison of levels of fertility or mortality.
Apply models and theories of migration to labor migration in and from developing countries, as well as transnational human capital transfer.
Conduct PowerPoint presentation of research of social science topics.

courses.title: Comparative Governance
courses.description: This is a comparative politics course targeting toward advanced postgraduate students. With its long history, comparative politics has covered many different topics. The course will focus on important substantive questions to understand political phenomena around the world. The course consists of five broad and complex topics related to politics: i) basic logic and methodologies in comparative politics; ii) state formation and regime types; iii) election and government system; iv) policy-related issues including economic development and redistribution; and v) challenges in comparative political economy including poverty, foreign aid, natural resources, civil war and political connection/corruption.

cilos.description: Apply key theories and concepts in comparative politics.
Write critical evaluation reports of research papers in comparative politics.
Apply adequate scientific methodologies to individual’s research.
Design and develop an analytic research paper.

courses.title: Economic Development
courses.description: This course examines the economic situations of low and middle-income economies, considering many important topics in the field of development economics. It addresses questions such as what factors help explain why some countries are rich and others poor and whether economic policies can affect these factors. We will study key aspects of life for poor households in the developing world, such as inequality, gender and the intra-household division of resources, education, health, savings and credit, institutions and globalization. Students will also study recent research in the field and examine empirical evidence on these topics.

cilos.description: Identify critical issues in the developing world.
Apply core concepts of economics to critically analyze significant social phenomena and interpret important events related to the developing world.
Analyze the core issues in economic development strategies.
Use simple statistical methods to study some issues related to development.

courses.title: Chinese Politics
courses.description: This course examines Chinese political system and its impact in people's everyday activities. As one of the most influential countries in the world, the Chinese political system carries distinctive characteristics that differ significantly from Western liberal democracies. This course will compare the similarities and differences between China and liberal democracy. Students will learn the classical theories and concepts developed in Western political science and explore how they can and cannot be applied to China.

cilos.description: Understand the functioning of Chinese political system and how it shapes social & economic life.
Learn how to support findings with empirical evidence.
Develop analytical thinking skills by understanding diverse views and theories.
Improve English writing through weekly reports and the final research paper.

courses.title: Topics in Gender and Society
courses.description: A sociologically informed discussion about the role that gender plays in the organization of social life, including education, work and employment, the global economy, technology and innovation, media, family life and international relations.

cilos.description: Develop a sociological mindfulness toward gender.
Understand differential performance of boys and girls in schools.
Understand the gender wage gap, diversity and inclusion in the workplace.
Understand the gendered division of labour in the home.
Understand gendered violence.
Understand how the global economy is gendered.
Understand how international politics and international conflict is gendered.

courses.title: Democracy and Governance
courses.description: This course examines various approaches to study the rise and fall of democracy in disciplines of political economy, political science, political sociology, and historical sociology. It pays special attention to specific historical or political context in which democratization or collapse of democracy occurred. This course also encourages the students to integrate normative understanding of democracy with positivist studies of democracy.

cilos.description: Have an overview of the scholarship of democratization from past to present.
Understand the key concepts and methods in studying the rise and fall of democracy.
Learn how to place social science theoretical research in concrete political and historical contexts.
Understand why the normative knowledge of democracy is important to empirical study of democracy.
Critically review existing literature and learn to come up with new research questions.

courses.title: Geographical Information Systems and Census Analysis
courses.description: This course provides students with comprehensive knowledge of Geographical Information Systems, including basic concepts, software and functions, data structures, and applications to social science and other fields. Students will learn fundamental geospatial concepts, census data and structures, and the joint analysis of large spatial datasets with census socio-demographics through lectures, lab exercises, and a final project.

cilos.description: Apply the most popular forms of Geographical Information System (GIS) software applications for sociodemographic analysis and other purposes.
Analyze social contexts to select and apply the appropriate software packages and techniques.
Explain and incorporate GIS results and their implications in social science and other fields in reports.

courses.title: Understanding Personality
courses.description: This course provides an overview of theories of personality and examines how personality develops through different perspectives.

cilos.description: Recognize the key classical and contemporary studies pertinent to personality theories and assessment.
Identify, relate, and apply the key concepts in everyday life.
Identify a research question, devise an action plan to conduct a study, gather and analyze the pertinent information, and present the findings in a written report.
Conceptualize, structure, and articulate original ideas about personality-related topics.

courses.title: Environment and Human Behavior
courses.description: This course examines the interactions between humans and physical environments from a psychological perspective. It discusses how human behavior is affected by, and affects, their natural and built surroundings. It also explores the human dimension of environmental issues.

cilos.description: Recognize the interactions between humans and physical environments and explain them with reference to theories in psychology and other social sciences.
Analyze the human dimension of environmental issues from psychological and behavioral perspectives.
Analyze their own experience and everyday encounters regarding the physical environments.
Understand, explain, and evaluate research studies that examine human-environment relationships.

courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: This course introduces a psychological perspective in understanding human behavior. It evaluates how psychological research is conducted, and covers major psychological concepts and theories.

cilos.description: Identify key theories and concepts in understanding human behavior from a psychological perspective.
Apply the theories and concepts to their own experiences and daily lives.
Explain how psychological research is conducted and how psychologists investigate human behavior scientifically.
Recognize the scientific basis of psychology.

courses.title: Psychology of Well-being
courses.description: This course examines the psychology of well-being in the Chinese context. Students will be engaged in a series of challenges designed to enhance their understanding of well-being, to increase their happiness, and to bring about positive changes in their lives.

cilos.description: Recognize the various dimensions of well-being and explain them with reference to theories in psychology and other social sciences.
Gain insight into how research on well-being is conducted through a global and comparative perspective.
Explain, evaluate, and conduct research on well-being.
Analyze their own experience and everyday encounters regarding well-being.

courses.title: Developing a Career in Social Science
courses.description: This is a portfolio-based course. Upon completion of this course, students are required to submit a written reflection about their own career plans, in relation to the content of the PGD/MA(SOSC) program. The reflection is carried out by means of collating a portfolio and will include specific reference to the content of seminars and events that have taken place during their program. For PGD/MA(SOSC) students only. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Relate the curriculum and in particular the extra-curricular content and program learning outcomes of the PGD/MA(SOSC) program to their career trajectory.
Formulate a plan of action for their future career based on the reflective activity undertaken in the course.

courses.title: Calculus and Linear Algebra
courses.description: This course teaches basic application techniques in single-variable calculus and linear algebra. Key topics include: systems of linear equations and matrices, functions and graphing, derivatives and optimization, integration and applications.
courses.prerequisite: Level 2 or above in HKDSE Mathematics (Compulsory Part)
courses.exclusion: Level 5 or above in HKDSE Mathematics Extended Module M1 or M2; MATH 1005, MATH 1006, MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26), MATH 1013, MATH 1014, MATH 1020, MATH 1023, MATH 1024

cilos.description: Apply basic techniques in linear algebra and calculus that are commonly used for business school students
Apply rigorous, analytic, highly numerate approach to analyzing and solving problems
Communicate solutions effectively by using mathematical terminology and English

courses.title: Calculus and Statistics
courses.description: The course covers basic applications and techniques of single-variable calculus, statistics and probability. Key topics of calculus include: differentiation and integration of trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions, graphing, optimization, and probability. Key topics of statistics and probability include: basic theory and applications of various discrete and continuous probability distributions, random sampling techniques including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.
courses.prerequisite: Level 2 or above in HKDSE Mathematics (Compulsory Part)
courses.exclusion: Level 5 or above in HKDSE Mathematics Extended Module M1 or M2; MATH 1003, MATH 1006, MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26), MATH 1013, MATH 1014, MATH1020, MATH 1023, MATH 1024

cilos.description: Apply computational techniques of single-variable calculus on solving scientific problems.
Apply basic statistics and probability knowledge on solving scientific problems.
Develop computational skills of single-variable calculus for preparation of intermediate-level mathematics courses.

courses.title: Calculus, Vectors, and Matrices
courses.description: The course covers basic applications and techniques of single-variable calculus, vectors and matrices. Key topics of calculus include: differentiation and integration of trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions, graphing, optimizations, area under a curve, and volume of rotationally symmetric bodies. Key topics of vectors and matrices include: basic arithmetics of matrices and determinants, and geometric and physical concepts of vectors such as dot and cross products.
courses.prerequisite: Level 2 or above in HKDSE Mathematics (Compulsory Part)
courses.exclusion: Level 3 or above in HKDSE Mathematics Extended Module M1 or M2; MATH 1003, MATH 1005, MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26), MATH 1013, MATH 1014, MATH1020, MATH 1023, MATH 1024

cilos.description: Apply computational techniques of single-variable calculus on solving engineering problems.
Apply basic statistics and probability knowledge on solving engineering problems.
Develop computational skills of single-variable calculus for preparation of intermediate-level mathematics courses.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: This is an introductory course in one-variable calculus, the first in the Calculus I and II sequence. Topics include functions and their limits, continuity, derivatives and rules of differentiation, applications of derivatives, and basic integral calculus.
courses.exclusion: MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26), MATH 1014, MATH 1020, MATH 1023, MATH 1024

cilos.description: Apply the basic concepts and methods in one-variable differential calculus
Apply the knowledge in functions and calculus to formulate and solve application problems

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: This is an introductory course in one-variable calculus, the second in the MATH 1013 - MATH 1014 sequence. Topics include applications of definite integral, improper integrals, vectors, curves and parametric equations, modeling with differential equations, solving simple differential equations, infinite sequences and series, power series and Taylor series.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1023 OR (grade A- or above in MATH 1003)

cilos.description: Apply basic integration skills.
Apply the method of integration on formulating and solving problems.
Handle basic problems for the convergence of infinite sequences and series.
Apply various vector operations in dimension 2 and 3.

courses.title: Accelerated Calculus
courses.description: A concise introduction to one-variable calculus, primarily designed for talented secondary school students through the Center for the Development of the Gifted and Talented. Topics include functions, limits, derivatives, definite and indefinite integrals and their applications, infinite sequences and series, Taylor series, first order differential equations.

cilos.description: To understand the basic concepts of one variable calculus and series students need as they pursue careers in business, engineering or science
To apply the techniques of one-variable calculus and series in precise and logical way to solve various daily and professional problems

courses.title: Honors Calculus I
courses.description: This is the first in the sequence MATH 1023 – MATH 1024 of honors courses in one-variable calculus, with particular emphasis on rigorous mathematical reasoning. Topics include inequalities, functions and their graphs, vectors, limit and continuity, extreme value theorem, intermediate value theorem derivatives and differentiation rules, mean value theorem, l'Hôpital's rule, Taylor expansion, and applications of derivatives.
courses.prerequisite: Level 5 or above in HKDSE Mathematics Extended Module M2

cilos.description: Apply the basic concepts and methods in one-variable differential calculus with rigorous mathematical reasoning
Apply the knowledge in functions and calculus to formulate and solve problems

courses.title: Honors Calculus II
courses.description: This is the second in the sequence MATH 1023 - MATH 1024 of honors courses in one-variable calculus, with particular emphasis on rigorous mathematical reasoning. Topics include integral calculus, techniques of integration, improper integrals, applications of integrals, infinite series. Some rigorous theoretical results on integration and infinite series will be discussed.

cilos.description: Understand and calculate definite and indefinite integrations. Understand properties of series, and determine the convergence of series.
Understand the important theorems in analysis, and prove the calculation related theorems.
Argue the calculations and manipulations of concrete integrations and series in rigorous way.
Apply integrations to model, solve, and analyse geometrical and physical problems.

courses.title: Introductory Topics in Mathematical Sciences
courses.description: This is a general science course that introduces students to selected disciplines or topics of high popular interest. The crucial roles that mathematics play are emphasized. Materials are chosen to enrich and enhance students' appreciation of science and mathematics.

cilos.description: Solve some basic statistical problems with SAS.
Use SAS to make inferences about the population by some statistical approaches, say estimation and hypothesis testing.

Use SAS with ANOVA models and regression models to analyze data. For instance, students can find a “good” regression line to describe the relationship between a response variable and an explanatory variable, with a given data set, by SAS.

courses.title: Foundation of Mathematics
courses.description: This course covers a number of foundational concepts and rigorous reasoning in mathematics which are essential for intermediate- and upper levels mathematics courses especially in the field of pure mathematics. The main purpose of the course is to enhance students’ conceptual and logical understanding of mathematics, and strengthen students’ ability on writing mathematical proofs. Topics include mathematical induction, set notations and logic, complex numbers, inequalities, construction of real numbers, elementary number theory, etc.
courses.prerequisite: Level 5 or above in HKDSE Mathematics Extended Module M2 OR MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023

cilos.description: Explain and communicate basic concepts of mathematics such as set, functions, logic argument, number system (integers, rational numbers, real and complex numbers) counting principles, and equivalence relations.
Apply various methods of proofs including proof by contradictions, method of exhaustions, mathematical induction, etc.
Demonstrate and acquire the skills of reading and writing mathematical proofs.

courses.title: Introduction to Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Differentiation in several variables, with applications in approximation, maximum and minimum and geometry. Integration in several variables, vector analysis.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014; OR MATH 1020; OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand the basic concepts and know the basic techniques of differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables.
Apply the theory to calculate the gradients, directional derivatives, arc length of curves, area of surfaces, and volume of solids.
Solve problems involving maxima and minima, line integral, and vector calculus.
Develop mathematical maturity to undertake higher level studies in mathematics and related fields.

courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Sequences, series, gradients, chain rule. Extrema, Lagrange multipliers, line integrals, multiple integrals. Green's theorem, Stoke's theorem, divergence theorem, change of variables.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand the core concepts of multivariable calculus.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and to carry out mathematical work with independent judgment.
Apply rigorous, analytic, and numeric approach to analyze and solve problems.
Explain clearly concepts and calculations from multivariable calculus.
Develop mathematical maturity to undertake higher level studies in mathematics and related fields.

courses.title: Mathematical Analysis
courses.description: Sets and functions, real numbers, limits of sequences and series, limits of functions, continuous functions, differentiation, Riemann integration, additional topics.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand logical deduction of important facts in mathematical analysis and apply differentiation and integration to solve mathematical problems.
Communicate math concepts and approaches effectively to a range of audiences using appropriate equipment and software.
Apply rigorous analytical techniques taught in class to solve problems in convergence frequently appeared in the mathematical profession.

courses.title: Honors Mathematical Analysis
courses.description: The MATH 2043 and 3043 is a rigorous sequence in analysis on the line and higher dimensional Euclidean spaces. Limit, continuity, least upper bound axiom, open and closed sets, compactness, connectedness, differentiation, uniform convergence, and generalization to higher dimensions.
courses.prerequisite: Grade A- or above in MATH 1024

cilos.description: Build a strong background on mathematical analysis, on real line and on metric spaces, for future studies in advanced courses in mathematics, statistics, and related subjects.
Be familiar with the rigorous treatment of single-variable, multivariable functions, and functions on metric spaces.
Develop logical reasoning and critical thinking skills.

courses.title: Matrix Algebra and Applications
courses.description: Systems of linear equations; vector spaces; linear transformations; matrix representation of linear transformations; linear operators, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; similarity invariants and canonical forms.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of matrix algebra, linear transformations, eigenvectors and inner product spaces.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, carry out mathematical work with independent judgement.
Apply rigorous, analytical and numeric approach to analyze and solve problems using concepts of linear algebra.
Communicate problem solutions using correct mathematical terminology and good English.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector space, matrices and system of linear equations, linear mappings and matrix forms, inner product, orthogonality, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, symmetric matrix.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand the key definitions.
Carry out computations.
Know some typical applications.
Solve typical problems in linear algebra.

courses.title: Honors in Linear and Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: The MATH 2131 and 3131  is a sequence of rigorous introduction to linear algebra and abstract algebra. Vector spaces over the fields of real numbers and complex numbers, linear transformations, geometry, groups, bases, abstract fields, rings, change of bases, spectral theorems.
courses.prerequisite: Grade A in AL Pure Mathematics; or grade A- or above in MATH 1014/MATH 1020/MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand and calculate the basic concepts of linear algebra, in the equivalent settings of systems of linear equations, linear combinations of vectors, and linear transformations.
Understand and calculate the most important topics in linear algebra, including orthogonality, determinant, and diagonalisation.
Do mathematics in rigorous, conceptual, and abstract way.
Apply linear algebra concepts to model, solve, and analyse real-world situations.

courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Logic: propositions, axiomatization of propositional calculus, deduction theorem, completeness and soundness. Combinatorics: permutations and combinations, generating functions. Set theory: basic operations on sets, relations, countable and uncountable sets.  Third year and fourth year students require instructor's approval to take the course.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; or MATH 1014; or MATH 1020; or MATH 1024

cilos.description: Develop concrete knowledge to understand the core concept and ideas of discrete structures such as set theory, formal logic, binary relation, number theory, and graph theory, etc.
Formulate problems in the language of discrete structures.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization and carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.

Master the basic concepts and techniques of discrete mathematics; apply the fundamental principles, formulas, algorithms, and other techniques to formulate problems in related areas and solve them in skills.

courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
courses.description: This course provides a concise introduction to linear algebra and differential equations, with exposure to the use of numerical computing software like MATLAB. Topics include systems of linear equations, matrix algebra and determinants, language of vector spaces and inner product spaces, eigenvalue and eigenvector, first order ODEs, linear second order ODEs and oscillations, and homogeneous system of first order ODEs with constant coefficients.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024
courses.exclusion: MATH 2111, MATH 2121, MATH 2131, MATH 2351, MATH 2352, PHYS 2124

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of linear algebra and ordinary differential equations.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, carry out mathematical work with independent judgement.
Apply rigorous, analytical and numeric approach to analyze and solve problems using concepts of linear algebra and differential equations.
Demonstrate skills in reading, interpreting and communicating mathematical content which are integrated into other disciplines or appear in everyday life.
Develop the mathematical maturity to undertake higher level studies in mathematically related fields.

courses.title: Introduction to Differential Equations
courses.description: First order equations and applications, second order equations, Laplace transform method, series solutions, system of linear equations, nonlinear equations and linear stability analysis, introduction to partial differentiation and partial differential equations, separation of variables, and Fourier series.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Model and solve simple problems using first order odes.
Solve linear, constant coefficient second-order odes.
Use the Laplace transform method.
Construct series solutions.
Solve a system of linear, constant coefficient, first-order odes.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: First and second order differential equations, initial value problems, series solutions, Laplace transform, numerical methods, boundary value problems, eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, Sturm-Liouville theory.

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of Ordinary Differential Equations.
Apply rigorous and analytic approach to analyze and solve Differential Equations, including solution methods and proofs of theorems.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and to carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.
Communicate problem solutions using correct mathematical terminology and good English.

courses.title: Applied Statistics
courses.description: A systematic introduction to statistical inference, including the necessary probabilistic background, point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR  MATH 1024

cilos.description: Solve basic problems in probability.
Make inferences about the population by applying suitable statistical approaches, such as estimation, hypothesis testing, and linear regression.
Formulate statistical questions for real-world problems and interpret the results.
Analyze data using R.

courses.title: Probability
courses.description: Sample spaces, conditional probability, random variables, independence, discrete and continuous distributions, expectation, correlation, moment generating function, distributions of function of random variables, law of large numbers and limit theorems.
courses.exclusion: IEDA 2520, MATH 2431, ELEC 2600, ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23), ISOM 3540

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Use axioms of probability to calculate various probabilities.
Understand discrete and continuous random variables and associate them with various random experiments.
Solve real and hypothetical problems using the laws of large numbers and central limit theorem.

courses.title: Honors Probability
courses.description: This is an honors undergraduate course in probability theory. Topics include probability spaces and random variables, distributions (absolutely continuous and singular distributions) and probability densities, moment inequalities, moment generating functions, conditional expectations, independence, conditional distributions, convergence concepts (weak, strong and in distribution), law of large numbers (weak and strong) and central limit theorem. Some rigorous theoretical results in probability will be discussed.
courses.prerequisite: (Grade A- or above in MATH 1014) OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Solve some basic and advanced problems in probability.
Understand more distributions of random variables.
Solve some complicated problems of finding a distribution of a random variable by a new technique --- moment generating function.
Understand how to prove some limit theorems in probability, like the central limit theorem.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental concepts of actuarial financial mathematics and how these concepts are applied in calculating present and accumulated values for various streams of cash flows. The topics covered include interest rates, present value, annuities valuation, loan repayment, bond and portfolio yield, bond valuation, rate of return, yield curve, term structure of interest rates, duration and convexity of general cash flows and portfolios, immunization, stock valuation, capital budgeting, dynamic cash flow processes, and asset and liability management.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 1003 OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Understand the basic concepts related to time value of money, such as interest rates, discount rate, present value, future value, etc. and how to carry out related calculation.
Understand the concepts related to annuities with payments that are not contingent and how to carry out calculation related to the future or present value of an annuity.
Understand the concepts related to loans and sinking fund and how to carry out calculation related to a loan, such as outstanding balance and interest and principal repayment.
Understand the concepts related to bonds and how to carry out calculation related to a bond, such as bond value, bond yield, amortization of premium, etc.

Understand the concepts related to general cash flows and portfolios and how to carry out calculation related to such portfolios, such as present value, yield rate, rate of return, duration, and convexity, etc.
Understand the concepts related to immunization and how to construct an investment portfolio to immunize a set of liability cash flows.
Enhance the ability of using advanced mathematics, e.g., calculus, to solve real-world problems.
Enhance the ability of using computational software such as Excel.

courses.title: Mathematical Problem Solving
courses.description: Discussions on problem solving techniques. Basics materials in combinatorics, number theory, geometry and mathematical games.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics/AL Applied Mathematics; OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization and apply logical reasoning to investigate mathematical work with independent judgement.
Collaborate and communicate effectively for creative solutions.
Apply rigorous deductive reasoning in conjunction with quantitative methods to analyse and solve problems related to the math profession.

courses.title: Real Analysis
courses.description: Functions of several variables, implicit and inverse function theorem, uniform convergence measure and integral on the real line.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 / MATH 2023) AND (MATH 2033 / MATH 2043) AND (MATH 2111 / MATH 2121 / MATH 2131 / MATH 2350)

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important terms and definitions in analysis.
Understand logical deduction of important facts in mathematical analysis of high dimension spaces and apply integration theory to solve mathematical and statistical problems.
Apply rigorous analytical techniques taught in class to solve problems frequently appeared in the mathematical profession.

courses.title: Honors Real Analysis
courses.description: The MATH 2043 and 3043 is a rigorous sequence in analysis on the line and higher dimensional Euclidean spaces. Differentiation and integration in higher dimensions, implicit function and inverse function theorem, Stokes theorem, and Lebesgue measure.
courses.prerequisite: Grade A- or above in MATH 2043

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of Lebesgue measure theory.
Understand the workable knowledge in real analysis for further studies and research in partial differential equations, geometric analysis, probability theory and related fields.
Develop logical reasoning and critical thinking skills.

courses.title: Abstract Algebra
courses.description: Polynomials; Jordan canonical form, minimal polynomials, rational canonical form; equivalence relation; group, coset, group action; introduction to rings and fields.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important concepts and definitions in algebra.
Know the applications of algebra such as symmetry.
Understand how the mathematical knowledge students learnt before can be better organized and generalized.
Know how to solve problems in algebra.
Know how to construct rigorous proofs.

courses.title: Honors in Linear and Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: The MATH 2131 and 3131 is a sequence of highly rigorous introduction to linear algebra and abstract algebra. Groups, rings, homomorphisms, quotients, group actions, polynomial rings, Chinese remainder theorem, field extensions.
courses.prerequisite: Grade B- or above in MATH 2131

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Use algebraic techniques to formulate and apply the fundamental theorems in concise form.
Understand and apply the basic concepts and theorems in abstract algebra.
Understand and apply the techniques of abstract algebra.
Understand and write rigorous proof.

courses.title: Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Basic numerical analysis, including stability of computation, linear systems, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, nonlinear equations, interpolation and approximation, numerical integration and solution of ordinary differential equations, optimization.
courses.prerequisite: (COMP 1021 / COMP 1022P / COMP 1023) AND (MATH 2111 / MATH 2121 / MATH 2131 / MATH 2350) AND (MATH 2031 / MATH 2033 / MATH 2043)

cilos.description: Model and solve simple problems using first order odes.
Solve linear, constant coefficient second-order odes.
Use the Laplace transform method.
Construct series solutions.
Solve a system of linear, constant coefficient, first-order odes.
Solve partial differential equations using separation of variables.

courses.title: Matrix Computation
courses.description: This course will introduce some basic matrix analysis theory and some popular matrix computation algorithms, and illustrate how they are actually used in data science. Specific topics include advanced linear algebra such as orthogonal projections and vector and matrix norms; the theories and computations of matrix factorizations such as QR decomposition, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and Schur decomposition; and applications to data analysis problems such as principle component analysis via SVD and collaborative filtering via matrix completion.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350

cilos.description: Understand QR decomposition and its numerical algorithm.
Understand singular value decomposition and its algorithm.
Understand Schur decomposition and its algorithm.
Implement various matrix computation algorithms on a computing platform and apply them to solve data analysis problems.

courses.title: Data Analytic Tools
courses.description: This course will introduce to the students some mathematical analysis tools that are useful for data analysis. The topics include Fourier analysis, wavelet analysis, function expansions, and basic functional analysis (Banach space, Hilbert spaces, linear operators, contract mapping, etc), and basic convex analysis (subgradient, convex conjugate).
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350)

cilos.description: Understand continuous Fourier and wavelet transform and to do discrete Fourier and wavelet transform for a given data with a computing platform.
Understand various function expansions and use them to approximate given functions.
Understand basic functional analysis.
Understand basic convex analysis.

courses.title: Combinatorial Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to combinatorics: What is combinatorics? Permutations and combinations, binomial theorem, generating permutations and combinations, pigeonhole principle, Ramsey theory, inclusion-exclusion principle, rook polynomials, linear recurrence relations, nonhomogeneous linear recurrence relations of the first and second order, generating functions, Catalan numbers, Stirling numbers, partition numbers, matchings and stable matchings, systems of distinctive representatives, block designs, Steiner triple systems, Latin squares, Burnside's lemma, Polya counting formula.

cilos.description: Develop concrete knowledge to understand the core combinatorial ideas and to taste the style of discrete part of mathematics.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and to carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.
Apply the fundamental principles, counting formulas, algorithms, and other techniques to formulate mathematical problems and to solve them with skills.
Improve the use of correct mathematical terminology and writing of correct mathematical proofs.

courses.title: Statistical Inference
courses.description: Sampling theory, order statistics, limiting distributions, point estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, non-parametric methods.

cilos.description: Understand the main concept of doing statistical inference.
Find the maximum likelihood estimator in some statistical problems.
Understand the new inferential ideas like Fisher information and CR lower bound clearly.
Find different estimates with some special estimation techniques they learn in class.
Do some advanced testing of hypotheses such as likelihood-ratio test.

courses.title: Regression Analysis
courses.description: Estimation and hypothesis testing in linear regression, residual analysis, multicollinearity, indicator variables, variable selection, nonlinear regression.

cilos.description: Get familiar with simple and multiple linear regression, the involved statistical inference, prediction, the measure of goodness-of-fit, and applications on real data examples.
Understand the diagnostics of regression, residuals, checking linearity, leverage, influence, dealing with outliers and applications on real data examples.
Understand how to treat categorical variables as predictors, the transformation of variables, treating heteroscedastic errors and applications on real data examples.
Understand variable selection, the procedures and applications.
Understand logistic regression for classification problem, the quality of fit, determination of important variables and applications on real data examples.

courses.title: Stochastic Modeling
courses.description: Discrete time Markov chains and the Poisson processes. Additional topics include birth and death process, elementary renewal process and continuous-time Markov chains.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Identify and construct Markov processes and apply the limit laws.
Learn to apply the renewal processes and renewal functions to solve real problems.
Know the basic behavior of continuous time Markov processes including Poisson processes and law of rare events.

courses.title: Sampling
courses.description: Basic and standard sampling design and estimation methods. Particular attention given to variance estimation in sampling procedures. Topics include: simple random sampling, unequal probability sampling, stratified sampling, ratio and subpopulation and multistage designs.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions in sampling.
Understand the estimators in different sampling schemes and apply them in concise form.
Apply sampling techniques in familiar situations.
Analyze survey data using different statistical models with R/ Excel.

courses.title: Bayesian Statistics
courses.description: This course provides a basic training of Bayesian statistics. Some ideas and principles of Bayesian including prior and posterior distributions, conjugate priors, Bayesian estimates, empirical Bayes, Bayesian hypothesis testing, Bayesian model selection and Bayesian networking are covered. Other Bayesian tools such as Bayesian decision theory, Bayesian data analysis, and Bayesian computational skills will also be discussed. An open-source, freely available software R will be used to implement these computational and data analytics skills. Hands-on experience and case studies such as pattern recognition and spam filtering will also be provided to students. Completion of this course will give students access to a wide range of Bayesian analytical tools, customizable to real data.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431 OR ELEC 2600 OR ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23) OR ISOM 3540

cilos.description: Elaborate the concept and philosophy of Bayesian statistics and its main difference form the frequentist statistical approach.

Explain the importance of prior distribution (e.g. flat and conjugate priors) in Bayesian inference and how we can conduct posterior inference by using Bayesian estimates and Bayesian hypothesis testing.
Formulate a Bayesian solution to some real-data problems and interpret the results.
Implement some Bayesian computational techniques like MCMC.
Apply the conceptual and practical skills in Bayesian statistics to problems in statistics, data science, and other areas.

courses.title: Statistical Computing
courses.description: This course covers the models, methods and algorithms in computational statistics. Topics include: basics of R programming; basic statistical data analysis and visualisation tools; R implementation of non-standard estimators; simulate random variables and random experiments; estimate variance and prediction performance by data partitioning and randomization (Jackknife, Bootstrap and Cross-Validation); expectation-maximization algorithm and applications; Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling and applications. The students will learn computation-oriented statistical methods with hands-on experience on real data examples.

cilos.description: Use R for standard data analysis and visualization.
Implement R-code for non-standard estimators (more advanced R programming).
Explore Re-sampling technique for variance estimate and cross validation.
Understand EM algorithm and its applications.
Understand MCMC and its applications.

courses.title: Communicating Mathematics to the Public
courses.description: This project-based course allows students to develop expertise in mathematics outreach and knowledge transfer, as well as understand industrially and academically relevant skills. The course exposes students to promoting mathematics to the public. Activities may include lectures, seminars, workshops, and sharing sessions. Outputs will be diverse and may consist of exhibits, workshops, or presentations to be delivered in schools, online activities, and digital apps to be posted on websites or social media platforms. For MATH students only.

cilos.description: Create educational material, communicate mathematical knowledge to unfamiliar audiences.
Show judgment in the selection and presentation of material to communicate.
Demonstrate essential communication skills such as verbal, visual, video, or online/social media communication.
Examine the value of and assume ownership of their mathematics education.

courses.title: Complex Analysis
courses.description: Complex differentiability; Cauchy-Riemann equations; contour integrals, Cauchy theory and consequences; power series representation; isolated singularities and Laurent series; residue theorem; conformal mappings.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023 OR MATH 3043) AND (MATH 2033 OR MATH 2043)

cilos.description: Apply the concept of limits to analyze and solve problems related to continuity and approximation in the mathematical profession.
Compute contour integrals of complex functions and Laurent series of meromorphic functions, and explain these computations clearly using concepts from complex analysis.
Recognize the power of Cauchy’s theory that made some difficult problems solvable, and apply logical reasoning to investigative mathematical work.
Develop mathematical maturity to undertake higher level studies in mathematics and related fields.

courses.title: Calculus on Manifolds
courses.description: Introduction to manifolds, metric spaces, multi-linear Algebra, differential forms, Stokes theorem on manifolds, cohomology.
courses.prerequisite: Grade A- or above in MATH 2023 AND B- or above in MATH 2131

cilos.description: Understand the key definitions.
Know how to carry out local computations.
Understand the connection and relevance to mechanics and electrodynamics.
Solve typical problems in geometry and symmetry.

courses.title: Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.description: Existence and uniqueness theorems of ordinary differential equations, theory of linear systems, stability theory, study of singularities, boundary value problems.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2350 OR MATH 2351 OR MATH 2352) AND (MATH 3033 OR MATH 3043)

cilos.description: Understand the basic theorems of ODEs on existence, uniqueness and stability.
Have solid foundation for future study in pure mathematics, applied mathematics, and other physical sciences.

courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Derivations of the Laplace equations, the wave equations and diffusion equation; Methods to solve equations: separation of variables, Fourier series and integrals and characteristics; maximum principles, Green's functions.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Learn the background of basic partial differential equations, and their types.
Learn techniques to solve elementary partial differential equations.
Find particular solutions to well-posed problems to some PDEs.

courses.title: Functional Analysis
courses.description: Banach space. Hahn-Banach theorem, open mapping theorem, closed graph theorem, uniform boundedness theorem, separation theorem, Krein-Milman theorem. Weak topologies and weak topologies, reflexive spaces, separable spaces, Arzela-Ascoli theorem, uniform convexity. Hilbert space, Riesz representation theorem and Lax-Milgram theorem. Adjoints and duality. Compact, Fredholm, self-adjoint operators and their spectrum. Sobolev spaces, Sobolev inequalities, elliptic boundary value problems, and other applications.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 3043 OR MATH 4061 (prior to 2021-22)) AND (MATH 2131 OR grade A- or above in MATH 2121)

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately rigorous mathematical definitions.
Write rigorous mathematical proofs.
Generalize practical problems to abstract mathematical settings.
Solve real and hypothetical problems by identifying the underlying mathematics and analyzing the problem.

courses.title: Number Theory and Applications
courses.description: Prime numbers, unique factorization, modular arithmetic, quadratic number fields, finite fields, p-adic numbers, coding theory, computational complexity.

cilos.description: Become familiar with the history of mathematical development through elementary number theory.
Work with advanced methods in modern number theory.
Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of analytic number theory for future studies in advanced number theory courses.

courses.title: Introduction to Lie Groups
courses.description: General linear groups, orthogonal groups, unitary groups, symplectic groups, exponential maps, maximal tori, Clifford algebra, spin groups.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023 OR MATH 3043) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350)

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Use calculus and linear algebra to formulate and apply the fundamental theorems in concise form.
Understand and apply the theory of root systems for classification and representations of simple Lie algebras.

courses.title: Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries
courses.description: Axioms and models, Euclidean geometry, Hilbert axioms, neutral (absolute) geometry, hyperbolic geometry, Poincare model, independence of parallel postulate.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 2033 OR MATH 2043 OR MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350

cilos.description: Understand the importance of axiomatic method.
Recognize and use appropriately important concepts and definitions in geometry and know how to study geometric problems using groups and symmetr.
Understand how the mathematical knowledge students learnt before can be better organized and generalized.

courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: Curve theory; curvature and torsion, Frenet-Serret frame; surface theory: Weingarten map, first and second fundamental forms, curvatures, Gaussian map, ruled surface, minimal surface; instrinsic geometry: Theorema Egregium, Coddazi-Mainardi equations, parallel transport, geodesics, exponential map, Gauss-Bonnet theorem.

cilos.description: Acquire workable knowledge on the fundamental concepts of regular curves and surfaces in Euclidean spaces.
Acquire necessary background for further studies in differential geometry, general relativity, and related fields.
Appreciate the beauty of differential geometry, especially the Gauss-Bonnet’s Theorem.

courses.title: Topology
courses.description: Metric, topology, continuous map, Hausdorff, connected, compact, graph, Euler number, CW-complex, classification of surfaces.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important terms and definitions in topology.
Use topology notation to reformulate other seemingly unrelated problems.
Apply topology in familiar situations.
Solve real and hypothetical problems by identifying the underlying topological problem.

courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: Zero-sum games; minimax theorem; games in extensive form; strategic equilibrium; bi-matrix games; repeated Prisonner's Dilemma; evolutionary stable strategies; games in coalition form; core; Shapley Value; Power Index; two-side matching games.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023 OR MATH 3043) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350)

cilos.description: Appreciate how to use quantitative tools to analyse issues related to game theory.
Recognize the importance of applying rigorous and numerate approach to analyse and solve problem in game theory.
Apply mathematical modelling and analytic proofs to describe and explain phenomena in game theory.
Communicate the solutions of mathematical models of game theory using mathematical terminology and English language.

courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Lagrangian and Eulerian methods for the flow description; derivation of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations; sound wave and Mach number; 2D irrotational flow; elements of aerofoil theory; water wave dispersion relation; shallow water waves; ship wave pattern; dynamics of real fluid, stokes flow and boundary layer theory.

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of Fluid Dynamics.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and to carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.
Apply rigorous, analytic, highly numerate approach to analyze and solve problems of fluid dynamics using combined physical and mathematical means.
Communicate problem solutions using correct fluid dynamic terminology.

courses.title: Introduction to Optimization
courses.description: This course introduces fundamental theory and techniques of optimization. Topics include linear programming, unconstrained optimization, and constrained optimization. Numerical implementations of optimization methods are also discussed.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131)

cilos.description: Be equipped with of fundamental knowledge of optimization.
Develop an understanding of basic algorithms of optimization and their implementations.
Set up optimization models for applications problems.
Solve optimization problems independently.
Implement some algorithms by software such as MATLAB.
Communicate using correct mathematical terminology.

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematics of Image Processing
courses.description: This course introduces digital image processing principles and concepts, tools, and techniques with emphasis on their mathematical foundations. Key topics include image representation, image geometry, image transforms, image enhancement, restoration and segmentation, descriptors, and morphology. The course also discusses the implementation of these algorithms using image processing software.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023) AND [MATH 2350 OR (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 AND MATH 2351 OR MATH 2352)]

cilos.description: Be equipped with theoretical knowledge, principles and techniques to image processing problems.
Acquire a good appreciation of roles of mathematics in image processing.
Implement image processing algorithms on computers.
Apply computer algorithms to real-life problems.
Present numerical output from a computer code in a systematical way.

courses.title: Introduction to Graph Theory
courses.description: This course is to equip students with basic knowledge of graph theory that will be needed in mathematics, computer science, and engineering (in particular network analysis). Topics include but not restricted to: Euler tours and Chinese postman problem, Hamilton cycles and traveling salesman problem; minimum spanning trees and searching algorithms; block decomposition, ear decomposition, connectivity and edge connectivity; network flows, Ford‐Fulkerson (Max‐Flow Min‐Cut) theorem, augmenting‐path algorithm; planar graphs, Euler formula, duality, classification of Platonic solids, Kuratowski (planarity) theorem; maximum matchings and perfect matchings, matchings in bipartite graphs, matchings in general graphs, Tutte‐Berge theorem, Petersen theorem; probabilistic method, page rank problem, random walks; cycle spaces and bond spaces, graph Laplace operator, matrix‐tree theorem; Four‐Color problem, colorings and flows, chromatic number and flow number, chromatic polynomials, flow polynomials, Tutte polynomials; matroids.

cilos.description: Formulate related problems in graph language and graph models.
Master standard useful matrix methods such as incidence matrix, Laplace matrix, matrix‐tree formula, and graph Fourier transforms, etc.
Master basic concepts, ideas, techniques and core theorems of graph theory that may be applicable to network analysis and other practical problems.
Demonstrate abilities in applying algorithms, graph analytic skills, and theoretical thinking for software development.
Demonstrate ability in working with unsolved problems and explore new problems for future advanced studies.

courses.title: Numerical Solutions of Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Introduction to finite difference and finite element methods for the solution of elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations; including the use of computer software for the solution of differential equations.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2350 OR MATH 2351 OR MATH 2352) AND MATH 3312 AND MATH 4052

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately numerical technique in computation.
Develop numerical approximation to discretize partial derivatives.
Apply numerical analysis to understand numerical schemes, and construct reliable and accurate numerical methods for different type of partial differential equations.
Solve real and hypothetical problems by applying the numerical schemes.

courses.title: Mathematical Modeling
courses.description: This is an introductory course to mathematical modeling in science and engineering. The first part covers foundations of mathematical modelling. The second part discusses the applications, including mechanical vibrations, population dynamics, and traffic flow. Students will learn diverse modeling approaches to formulate, analyze and evaluate models mathematically. The course comprises both lectures and tutorials.

cilos.description: Understand the foundations of mathematical modeling, including principles, methods, dimensional analysis, scale, approximation, and model validation.
Understand a range of mathematical models built in a range of disciplines, with a focus on mechanical vibrations, population dynamics, and traffic flow.
Analyze problems by building mathematical models, carrying out theoretical analysis, and performing numerical computation.
Apply analysis and computation skills for mathematical models.
Understand the technique used by mathematical modeling to develop mathematical maturity for undertaking higher level studies in applied mathematics and related fields.

courses.title: Nonparametric Statistics
courses.description: The sign test; Wilcoxon signed rank test; Wilcoxon rank-sum test; Kruskal-Wallis test; rank correlation; order statistics; robust estimates; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test; nonparametric curve estimation.

cilos.description: Understand the nonparametric estimation method.
Understand the rank-based hypothesis test.

courses.title: Multivariate Analysis
courses.description: Inferences of means and covariance matrices, canonical correlation, discriminant analysis, multivariate ANOVA, principal components analysis, factor analysis.

cilos.description: Get familiar with multivariate normal distribution, random sample, the distributions of sample mean and covariance, Linear combination of normal random variables.
Understand the testing of mean vector, Hotelling’s test, Likelihood ratio test, Confidence regions and Large sample inference, Comparing mean vectors from two populations, and one-way MANOVA.
Understand the population principal components, Sample variation summarisation.
Understand Canonical variates, correlation, interpretation of canonical variables, Sample canonical correlation.
Understand classification, Linear and quadratic classification rules, Evaluating classification performance.

courses.title: Introductory Time Series
courses.description: Stationarity, (partial) auto-correlation function, ARIMA modeling, order selection, diagnostic, forecasting, spectral analysis.

cilos.description: Understand the features of time series model.
Understand How to fit a model by using the techniques in this course.

courses.title: Survival Analysis
courses.description: The topics discussed in this course include basic quantities like hazard rate function, survival function, censoring and/or truncation; parametric estimation of the survival distribution by maximum likelihood estimation method; nonparametric estimation of the survival functions from possibly censored samples; parametric regression models; Cox's semi-parametric proportional hazards regression model; and multivariate survival analysis.

cilos.description: Estimate failure time and loss distributions for empirical models.
Estimate of the variance of estimators and confidence intervals for failure time and loss distributions for empirical models.
Estimate of the parameters of failure time and loss distributions for parameter models.
Estimate the parameters of failure time and loss distributions with censored and/or truncated data for parameter models.
Estimate the variance of estimators and the confidence intervals for the parameters and functions of parameters of failure time and loss distributions for parameter models.
Estimate failure time and loss distributions.
Determine the acceptability of a fitted model and/or compare models.

courses.title: Loss Models and their Applications
courses.description: This course covers the construction of casualty loss models and their applications to insurance.
