Topics include severity models, frequency models, aggregate loss models, coverage modifications, effect of inflation on losses, risk measures, parameter and variance estimation in loss models, and construction of empirical models.
courses.prerequisite: (ELEC 2600 OR ISOM 3540 OR MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431) AND (MATH 2011 OR MATH 2023) AND MATH 2511

cilos.description: Understand commonly used survival models, how to create new families of loss distributions, how to choose the appropriate loss distributions and apply them in concrete applications.
Understand commonly used frequency models, how to choose the appropriate frequency models, and how to apply them in concrete applications.
Understand how to compute relevant parameters and statistics for collective risk models, how to evaluate compound models for aggregate claims, and how to compute aggregate claim distributions.
Calculate risk measures of VaR and TVaR and understand their use and limitations.
Understand how to apply limited fluctuation credibility including criteria for both full and partial credibility and how to apply Buhlmann and Buhlmann-Straub models.
Understand how to apply conjugate priors in Bayesian analysis and how to apply empirical Baysian methods in the nonparametric and semiparametric cases.
Enhance the ability of using advanced mathematics (calculus, probability, statistics, etc.) to solve real-world problems.
Enhance the ability of building stochastic and statistical models for insurance.
Enhance the ability of using computational software such as Matlab and implementing mathematical models using computer programs.

courses.title: Credibility Theory and its Applications
courses.description: Credibility theory is statistical inference used to make prediction based on both individual risk data and collective risk data. It is widely used in the insurance industry to predict the future claim payment, determine the insurance premium and determine the size of required reserve. This course will provide a mathematical treatment on credibility theory and explore the application of the theory in prediction of future claim payment, premium calculation. Topics include limited fluctuation credibility theory, greatest accuracy credibility theory, credibility premium, Buhlmann models, Buhlmann-Straub models and applications of credibility theory in solving insurance problems such as future loss prediction, premium calculation etc.

cilos.description: Understand the basic idea of credibility theory. Be able to apply the limited fluctuation credibility theory and understand the criteria for both full and partial credibility.
Study the solution of credibility problem using the Buhlmann model and Buhlmann-Straub model.
Apply empirical Bayesian estimation in non-parametric model and semiparametric model; Understand the strengths and weaknesses of nonparametric model and semiparametric model.
Apply credibility theory in insurance problem.

courses.title: Statistical Machine Learning
courses.description: This course provides students with an extensive exposure to the elements of statistical machine learning in supervised and unsupervised learning with real world datasets. Topics include regression, classification, resampling methods, model assessment, model selection, regularization, nonparametric models, boosting, ensemble methods, random forests, kernel methods, support vector machines, neural networks, and some standard techniques in unsupervised learning such as clustering and dimensionally reduction. Lab sessions on using R or Python in data analysis with machine learning methods will be conducted in class. Scientific reports and/or poster presentations are required for project evaluations.
courses.prerequisite: (COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P OR COMP 1023) AND [(IEDA 2520 AND IEDA 2540) OR ISOM 2500 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411 OR MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431]

cilos.description: Understand the fundamental principles and techniques of statistical learning.
Apply these techniques to the study of real-world datasets in class.
Learn advanced materials with the aid of internet and reference.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate mathematical concepts effectively both orally and in writing.

courses.title: Spatial Data Analysis
courses.description: This course provides an overview of and a basic training of spatial statistics with data analysis and examples including meteorological measurements from weather stations, demographics from census, and the incidence of disease over a particular geographic area. Some ideas and principles of spatial statistics including exploratory spatial analysis (e.g. Moran’s I), spatial data visualization, spatial interpolation (e.g. kriging), spatial correlation, spatial clustering, spatial map comparison, and spatial regression models are covered. An open-source, freely available software R and other software will be used to implement the computational and data analytics skills. Hands-on experience and case studies such as disease surveillance will also be provided to students. Completion of this course will give students access to a wide range of spatial analytical tools, customizable to real data.

cilos.description: Elaborate and master the concepts of spatial statistics.
Explain the importance of spatial analysis (e.g. disease outbreak/surveillance) in real world such as epidemiology and the recent pandemic of COVID-19.
Formulate real-data problems in the context of spatial analysis and interpret the results by using appropriate spatial methods and implement some spatial analysis and models in R and other software.
Explore spatial patterning in variables (e.g. does the concentration of some pollutant vary spatially) and perform statistical inference (parameter estimation, prediction) for spatial models.
Apply the conceptual and practical skills in spatial statistics to problems in statistics, epidemiology, public health, data science, and other areas.

courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.description: This course covers some basic concepts and underlying principles of deep learning with modern applications in artificial intelligence (AI). It delves into the fundamentals of machine learning methodologies with insights from case studies of relevant technologies. Allowing for the experimentation of applications of deep learning, this course is designed to encourage students to devise creative ways to put readily-available AI technologies to use to tackle problems in real life. Topics include: Perceptron/Adaline and linear models, gradient descent and boosting, stochastic approximation, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, long short term memory, resnet, transformers, generative adversarial networks, deep reinforcement learning, and self-supervised learning. The students will practice experiments with python programming.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2111) AND MATH 4432

cilos.description: Explore the basic concepts and principles behind deep learning methodology.
Explore the principles of various designs of neural network architectures.
Explore the applications of deep learning in modern AI including image, time series, natural language processing.
Develop programming experience for modern machine learning and AI.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Fixed Income Derivatives
courses.description: Bond, bond markets and interest-rate derivatives markets. Yields, forward rate and swap rates. Yield-based risk management and regression-based hedging. Mortgage mathematics. Binomial models for equity and fixed-income derivatives. Arbitrage pricing and risk-neutral valuation principle. Eurodollar futures. Lognormal models and Black formula for caps and swaptions.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 / MATH 2023) AND (MATH 2111 / MATH 2121 / MATH 2131 / MATH 2350) AND (IEDA 2520 AND IEDA 2540 / ISOM 2500 / LIFS 3150 / MATH 2411) AND (FINA 2203 / FINA 2303 / MATH 2511)

cilos.description: Understand the fixed-income markets and popular securities.
Know bond mathematics and related risk management methodologies.
Understand arbitrage pricing principle for derivatives pricing.
Apply the Black formula to interest-rate derivatives.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Mathematical Finance
courses.description: Duration and horizon rate of return, bond portfolio management and immunization; mean-variance formulation of portfolio choices of risky assets; Two-fund theorem and One-fund theorem; asset pricing under the capital asset pricing models and factor models; investment performance analysis; utility optimization in investment decisions; stochastic dominance.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2011 / MATH 2023) AND (MATH 2111 / MATH 2121 / MATH 2131 / MATH 2350) AND (IEDA 2540 / ISOM 2500 / LIFS 3150 / MATH 2411) AND (MATH 2511 / FINA 2203 / FINA 2303)

cilos.description: Understand the duration and horizon rate of return, bond portfolio management and immunization, application of bond immunization in asset-liability management.
Understand mean-variance formula of portfolio choices of risky assets. Two-fund theorem and one-fund theorem.
Understand asset pricing under the capital asset pricing model (CAPM) and factor models. Investment performance analysis.
Understand utility optimization in investment decisions and stochastic dominance.
Appreciate the use of various quantitative methods to analyse issues related to portfolio choice problems and investment performance analysis.

courses.title: Life Contingencies Models and Insurance Risk
courses.description: The topics discussed in this course include survival models, life tables and selection, insurance benefits, annuities, premium calculation, and insurance policy values.
courses.prerequisite: ELEC 2600 OR ISOM 3540 OR MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431

cilos.description: Understand the models used to model decrements used in insurances, annuities, and investments and how to calculate probabilities based on those models.
Understand the models used to model cash flows of life insurances and annuities and how to calculate the present values of the cash flows based on those models.
Understand the methods for calculating benefit reserves for traditional life insurances and annuities and basic universal life insurances.
Understand the models used to model cash flows for basic universal life insurances and how to calculate present values and contract level values.
Understand the relationship between expenses and gross premium and how to calculate contract level values based on the gross premium for life insurances and annuities.
Enhance the ability of using advanced mathematics (calculus, probability, statistics, etc.) to solve real-world problems.
Enhance the ability of building stochastic and statistical models for life contingencies.
Enhance the ability of using computational software such as Excel.

courses.title: Financial Economics in Actuarial Science
courses.description: The course aims to study some actuarial models and their applications in derivative pricing and financial risk management. Topics include introduction to various derivatives such as forward, futures, European/ American options, exotic options and interest rate derivatives, uses of various options strategies in portfolio management, pricing options using binomial tree model, Black Scholes formula for options pricing and its extension, Options Greeks and their applications in hedging, use of Monte Carlo simulation in options pricing, pricing of interest rate derivatives using the Black-Derman-Toy tree. The course also prepares students to take the Exam MFE (Models for Financial Economics) of the Society of Actuaries.

cilos.description: Recognize various financial derivatives (forward, futures, options, exotic options and interest rate derivatives) and their applications in the financial market.

Recognize the general properties of options such as put-call parity, put-call duality for European currency options, relationship between option price and strike price and relationship between option price and time to maturity.

Understand various option strategies (option spreads, collar, straddle, strangle, butterfly spread etc.) and explain how these strategies be applied to control the risk induced by price movement of the asset price.
Construct suitable binomial tree models in pricing European options, American options and interest rate derivatives.

Understand various concepts and model assumptions in Black-Scholes option pricing model and apply suitable techniques (risk-neutral valuation and Monte-Carlo simulation) to deduce pricing formulas for some European options.
Understand various Option Greeks and their applications in risk management and identify arbitrage opportunities given a set of market data.

courses.title: Statistical and Computational Methods in Financial Mathematics
courses.description: This course covers statistical and computational methods that are essential in financial data analysis, financial modeling, portfolio management and derivatives pricing. These tools are commonly used in quantitative financial models. Topics include: parametric models and parameter estimation, model fitting, multivariate analysis, linear regression, principal component analysis, bootstrapping method, Monto Carlo simulation methods and lattice tree algorithms. The students learn how to execute the tasks using computer software such as RStudio and Matlab.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2111) AND (MATH 2421 OR MATH 2431)

cilos.description: Explore the principles and theories behind various statistical methods.
Explore the principles of some computational methods (Monte Carlo simulation and lattice tree method) in derivative pricing.
Explore the application of statistical methods in financial data analysis, model selection and model fitting etc.
Explore the application of computation methods in pricing financial derivatives and examine the strength and weakness of each method.
Develop programming experience for financial data analysis and derivative pricing.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Focuses on a coherent collection of topics selected from a particular branch of mathematics. A student may repeat the course for credit if the topics studied are different each time.

cilos.description: Formulate related problems in the language of graphs.
Master the basic techniques of graph theory.
Consider unsolved problems and to find new problems for future studies.

courses.title: Special Topics in Pure Mathematics
courses.description: Supplementary study of specialized topics for students of pure mathematics.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately important technical terms and definitions.
Use calculus and linear algebra to formulate and apply the fundamental theorems in concise form.
Understand and apply representation theory of finite groups.

courses.title: Special Topics in Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Supplementary study of specialized topics for students of applied mathematics.

cilos.description: Recognize and use fundamental concepts and facts.
Use basics mathematics and physics to develop understanding of phenomena.
Use simple computation to enhance quantitative understanding.
Develop skills for literature search and journal reading.
Develop presentation skill.
Experience the conduct of peer-reviewing.

courses.title: Special Topics in Statistics and Financial Mathematics
courses.description: Supplementary study of specialized topics for students of statistics.

cilos.description: Gain a deep understanding of statistical principles and frameworks of causal inference.
Master different statistical methodologies in causal inference to estimate treatment effects in both randomized experiments and observational studies.
Know the basic underlying theories of statistical methodologies in causal inference.
Solve real-world problems using appropriate statistical methodologies in causal inference.

courses.title: Special Topics in Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: The course discusses one or two of the following three advanced subjects in actuarial mathematics: (1) advanced life contingencies models, (2) advanced casualty loss models, and (3) advanced financial economics. Based on the specific subjects chosen by the instructor, the topics covered in the course may include: (1) multiple state models, pension mathematics, interest rate risk, and emerging costs for traditional life insurance; (2) estimation of failure time and loss distribution using nonparametric methods, estimation of parameters of failure time and loss distribution with censored and/or truncated data, the acceptability of a fitted model, model comparison, and bootstrap methods; (3) Vasicek and Cox-Ingersoll-Ross bond pricing models, Black-Derman-Toy binomial model, Ito's formula, Black-Scholes option pricing model, exotic options, variance reduction methods in simulation, and delta-hedging.

cilos.description: Understand the multiple state model and how to calculate premiums under the model.
Understand how to value the benefits and contribution of a pension plan under multiple state model.
Understand how to carry out cash flow analysis for traditional life insurance contracts.
Understand how to estimate failure time and loss distributions using non-parametric methods.
Understand how to estimate failure time and loss distributions using parametric methods.
Understand how to determine the acceptability of a fitted model and how to compare models.
Understand how to apply the Vasicek, Cox-lngersoll-Ross, and Black-Derman-Toy model.
Understand how to use Black-sholes model for valuating and delta-hedging derivative securities.
Enhance the ability of using advanced mathematics (calculus, probability, statistics, etc.) to solve real-world problems.
Enhance the ability of building stochastic and statistical models for insurance.
Enhance the ability of using computational software such as Excel and Matlab and implementing mathematical models using computer programs.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development
courses.description: This course is for academic and professional development of students. The course arranges seminars and small group activities to expose students to mathematics in real life, explore their possible career choice, and enhance the interactions between students and faculties. Activities may include seminars, workshops, advising and sharing sessions, interaction with faculty and teaching staff, and discussion with student peers or alumni. Graded P or F. For MATH students only.

cilos.description: Develop relationships with faculty members and staffs.
Become self-directed in planning and accomplishing academic goals.
Identify career and personal plans and work towards these by developing realistic plans.
Examine the value of and assume ownership of his/her education.

courses.title: Student Seminars
courses.description: Working in small teams, students are required to select a topic in pure mathematics, applied mathematics or statistics area. They will discuss and write up their learning and present it at the seminars. The level of the topics can range from simple calculus to advanced topology, geometry or statistics. Students may repeat the course for credit at most two times.
courses.prerequisite: A passing grade in AL Pure Mathematics / AL Applied Mathematics OR MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024

cilos.description: Present their learning in pure mathematics, applied mathematics or statistics area.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Advanced undergraduate topics independently studied under the supervision of a faculty member. May be repeated for credit if different topics are studied. May be graded P/F or letter grade.

cilos.description: Apply advanced mathematical concepts and techniques to solve complex problems independently.

courses.title: Undergraduate Project
courses.description: Work in any area of mathematics under the guidance of a faculty member. The project either surveys a research topics or describes a small project completed by the student.

cilos.description: Develop critical thinking skills by analyzing mathematical theories and their applications in real-world scenarios.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Pure Mathematics
courses.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply mathematical tools to analyze problems in pure mathematics. Specific topics will be chosen by the instructor. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.

cilos.description: Explain advanced mathematical theories, concepts and principles using precise mathematical language.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work.
Apply a rigorous logical and analytic approach to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate mathematical concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.
Analyze the influence of mathematical sciences and their impact of human activity.
Draw on a global perspective and sound scientific evidence to evaluate the role of mathematical sciences in the international science community.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Applied Mathematics
courses.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply mathematical tools to analyze problems in applied mathematics. Specific topics will be chosen by the instructor. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.

cilos.description: Explain advanced mathematical theories, concepts and principles using precise mathematical language.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work.
Apply a rigorous logical and analytic approach to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate mathematical concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.
Analyze the influence of mathematical sciences and their impact of human activity.
Draw on a global perspective and sound scientific evidence to evaluate the role of mathematical sciences in the international science community.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Statistics
courses.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply their statistical knowledge to analyzing data. Students may make use of the statistical package SAS to conduct their project. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.

cilos.description: Examine the key theories, principles and techniques of data analysis.
Apply independent judgment to objective analysis and prediction of quantitative information.
Apply a rigorous analytic and highly numerate approach to analyze and solve both day-to-day and professional problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate statistical outcomes effectively to both lay and expert audiences by utilizing appropriate information and communication technology, through the report writing and project presentation.
Apply an appropriate method to analyze and solve both dayͲtoͲday and professional problems using statistical software.
Appraise the application of statistical modeling to a range of problems and persuade and influence others of its precision and value.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Mathematics and Economics
courses.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply mathematical tools to analyze problems in economics and social science. Specific topics will be chosen by the instructor. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.

cilos.description: Appreciate how to use quantitative tools to analyze issues related to various mathematical models in economics and social science, including fair allocation, voting methods, proportional representation and traffic flows.
Recognize the importance of applying rigorous and numerate approach to analyze and solve problem in economics and social science.
Apply mathematical modeling and analytic proofs to describe and explain phenomena in economics and social science.
Communicate the solutions of mathematical models of economics and social science using mathematical terminology through oral presentation and written reports.

courses.title: Capstone Project for Data Science
courses.description: This is a project-based course that trains students on applying computational and analytical tools (matrix computation, Fourier and wavelet transform, convex optimization, etc.) to real-world data analysis problems (recommendation system, signal processing, computer vision, etc.). Familiarity with a programming language is preferred, such as R, Matlab, or Python. For BSc in Data Science and Technology students only.

cilos.description: Formulate the problem to a mathematical problem.
Find proper analytical and computational tool to solve the problem.
Implement and test the algorithm in a programming language.
Present and interpret the results.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Financial and Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: This is a capstone project for all students majoring in Mathematics under the Financial and Actuarial Mathematics track. Students work on an individual/group project on a selected topic in Financial Mathematics or Actuarial Mathematics under the supervision of an instructor. In particular, the students will explore how to apply various mathematical tools and financial/actuarial knowledge learnt in previous courses to solve some real-life problems in finance or actuarial area.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 4427 OR MATH 4511 OR MATH 4512 OR MATH 4514

cilos.description: Identify problems and formulate the problems using suitable mathematical models.
Explore some advanced and modern mathematical skills for research.
Apply various mathematical tools and statistical method to solve the problems.
Communicate and present research ideas effectively.

courses.title: Independent Capstone Project
courses.description: A capstone project conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. A written report is required. Students need to individually seek a faculty mentor's consent prior to enrollment in this course.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge, principles and use of precise mathematical language in mathematical theories at college level.
Carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.
Apply rigorous, logical, and analytic methods to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate effectively, both in oral and written forms, about mathematical knowledge to audience.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, and develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.
Recognize the importance of complying with ethics of science and academic integrity.
Show appreciation of mathematical sciences and its interface with human activities.
View issues in mathematical sciences with reference to the practices of the international science community.

courses.title: Advanced Real Analysis I
courses.description: Basic topology, continuous function spaces, abstract measure and integration theory, Lp spaces, convexity and inequalities, Hilbert spaces, Banach spaces, Complex measure.

cilos.description: Recognize fundamental concepts in the measure theory.
Identify and describe major theorems in the measure theory.
Develop analytic logic and rigorous reasonings.

courses.title: Complex Function Theory
courses.description: Review of basic properties of analytic functions. Phragmen-Lindelof principle, normal family, Riemann mapping theorem. Weierstrass factorization theorem, Schwarz reflection principle, analytic continuation, harmonic function, entire function, Hadamard factorization theorem, Picard theorem.

cilos.description: Understand the geometric nature of residue calculus and analytic functions; lectures; homework.
Learn about the Möbius transformations and their geometric properties.
Understand the use of normal families in the proof Riemann mapping theorem; lectures; homework.
Acquire knowledge of Schwarz-Christoffel mappings and their applications to elliptic integrals; lectures; homework/project presentations.
Acquire knowledge of entire functions and their infinite product representations such as the Gamma functions; lectures; homework/project presentations.
Acquire knowledge of elliptic functions, modular functions and Picard’s theorems; lectures; homework/project presentations.

courses.title: Advanced Algebra I
courses.description: Advanced theory of groups, linear algebra, rings, modules, and fields, including Galois theory.

cilos.description: Recognize the types of algebraic structures such as groups, rings, modules and fields. Build a solid foundation of algebra.
Identify various algebraic structures among mathematics in the framework of category theory.
Apply the algebraic methods and ideas learned in this course to other fields such as algebraic geometry and homological algebra.

courses.title: Advanced Algebra II
courses.description: Advanced topics in algebra: group representations, associative algebras, commutative algebra, homological algebra, algebraic number theory.

cilos.description: Review the basics of abstract algebra and the main concepts in representation theory.
Introduce the main general results about representations of associative algebras.
Survey the main results about representations of finite groups.
Study some more advanced and special topics in the representation theory of finite groups.
Introduce the representation theory of quivers, and classify quivers of finite type.

Provide an introduction to: category theory and abelian categories in particular; homological algebra and its applications to categories of representations; & representation theory of finite dimensional algebras.

courses.title: Introduction to Lie Algebras
courses.description: Lie algebras. Nilpotent, solvable and semisimple Lie algebras. Universal enveloping algebras and PBW-theorem. Cartan subalgebras. Roots system, Weyl group, and Dynkin diagram. Classification of semisimple Lie algebras. Representations of semisimple algebras. Weyl character formula. Harish-Chandra isomorphism theorem.

cilos.description: Understand the concepts and basic techniques of Lie algebras and their representations.
Descrition of the root systems of semisimple Lie algebras.
Learn the properties of Weyl groups.
Classify simply Lie algebra by irreducible root systems.
Study Verma modules and irreducible highest weight modules.

courses.title: Introduction to Lie Groups
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the structure and representation theory of compact and noncompact reductive Lie groups.  Topics include general properties of Lie groups and Lie algebras, Peter-Weyl Theorems, representations of compact Lie groups, theorems of the highest weight, Harish-Chandra isomorphism, Weyl character formula, the structure theory of noncompact semisimple and reductive Lie groups, classification of simple real Lie algebras, induced representation and Frobenius reciprocity, classical branching theorems.

cilos.description: Understand the concepts and basic techniques of Lie groups, Lie algebras and their representations.
Understand the structure of Lie subgroups and Lie subalgebras, and real forms of complex Lie algebras.
Learn the fundamental theorems of Lie theory.
Study orthogonality of characters and Peter-Weyl theorems.
Applications to harmonic analysis.

courses.title: Differential Topology
courses.description: Manifolds, embedding and immersion, Sard's theorem, transversality, degree, vector fields, Euler number, Euler-Poincare theorem, Morse functions.

cilos.description: Manifold and tangent bundle.
Transversality theorem.
Intersection number mod 2.
Intersection number.
Euler number and Poincare-Hopf theorem.
Differential form and Stokes' theorem.

courses.title: Algebraic Topology
courses.description: Fundamental group, covering space, Van Kampen theorem, (relative) homology, exact sequences of homology, Mayer-Vietoris sequence, excision theorem, Betti numbers and Euler characteristic.

cilos.description: Fundamental groupoid and higher homotopy groups.
Singular homology theory.
CW-complex.
Singular cohomology theory.
Poincare duality.

courses.title: Algebraic Geometry I
courses.description: Projective spaces, algebraic curves, divisors, line bundles, algebraic varieties, coherent sheaves, schemes. Some commumative algebra and homological algebra such as notherian ring, regular ring, valuation ring, kahler differentials.

cilos.description: Learn the relations between commuatative algebra and affine varieties and affine schemes.
Master the techchniques using algebra to study geometry.
Learn the concepts of schemes and basic properties of schemes.
Learn the sheaves of modules on schemes.

courses.title: Algebraic Geometry II
courses.description: Derived functors, cohomology of coherent sheaves on schemes, extension groups of sheaves, higher direct image of sheaves, Serre duality, flat morphisms, smooth morphisms, and semi-continuity, basics of curves and surfaces.

cilos.description: Deeper understanding of using algebra to study geometry.
Learn the key geometry concepts of schemes using algebraic methods.
Master the viewpoint of Grothendieck's cohomology formulation.
Study various cohomology of coherent sheaves.

courses.title: Mathematical Structures in Modern Statistical Physics and Quantum Field Theory
courses.description: Over the past decades, contemporary theoretical physics has substantially influenced the development of numerous novel mathematical theories which became central subjects of current research in mathematics. This course focuses on some of these mathematical theories coming from subjects including Statistical Physics (SP), Quantum Field theory (QFT), and Gravity (Gr). This course aims at introducing advanced mathematical concepts which are pivotal in the rigorous study of various models in SP, QFT and Gr, using basic tools from probability and geometry.

cilos.description: Understand the various mathematical approaches to models in statistical physics and quantum (field) theory, including the constructions of path integrals
Apply probabilistic, analytic, combinatorics and representation methods to study problems in mathematical physics
Understand approaches to problems in physics from geometry and statistical physics
Understand aspects of the discrete and continuum Gaussian Free Field (GFF) and its geometry

courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: This is an introductory postgraduate course on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). We will start with the classical prototype linear PDEs, and introduce a variety of tools and methods. Then we will extend our beginning theories to general situation using the notion of Sobolev spaces, Holder space and weak solutions. We will prove the existence, uniqueness, regularity and other properties of weak solutions.

cilos.description: Recognize the types of second-order PDEs as typified by classical equations of mathematical physics, such as the wave equation, heat equation and Laplace equation.
Identify and describe the major theories of general PDEs.
Apply the tools of calculus, linear algebra and real analysis in a coherent way to PDE problems.
Apply the knowledge of PDEs to physical sciences and engineering, and physically interpret the solutions.
Use different methods, such as Fourier transform, separation variables, characteristics, similarity, power series to solve PDEs.

courses.title: Applied Analysis
courses.description: Contraction mapping theorem, Fourier series, Fourier transforms, Basics of Hilbert Space theory, Operator theory in Hilbert Spaces, Basics of Banach space theory, Convex analysis.

cilos.description: Explain the key ideas and concepts behind various analytical techniques.
Identify situations where analytical techniques are applicable.
Recognize limitations of the analytical techniques.
Develop extension of generalization for the techniques.
Implement the techniques to problems in various situations.

courses.title: Advanced Numerical Methods I
courses.description: Numerical solution of differential equations, finite difference method, finite element methods, spectral methods and boundary integral methods.  Basic theory of convergence, stability and error estimates.

cilos.description: Recognize and use appropriately numerical techniques in computation.
Develop numerical scheme to discretize partial differential equations.
Apply numerical analysis to examine the consistency, stability and convergence of the numerical methods.
Apply appropriate numerical schemes to solve real and hypothetical problems.

courses.title: Advanced Numerical Methods II
courses.description: Direct and iterative methods. Programming techniques and softwares libraries. Sparse solvers, Fast algorithms, multi-grid and domain decomposition techniques.

cilos.description: Understand direct and iterative algorithms for solving linear systems, and their convergence theory.
Identify suitable algorithms to solve linear equations arising from practical science and engineering problems, and implement them on a computing platform.
Understand algorithms and theories of other numerical linear algebra problems including the least squares problem and the eigenvalue problem.

courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics for Inviscid Flows
courses.description: Derivation of the Navier-Strokes equations; the Euler equations; Lagriangian vs. Eulerian methods of description; nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws; characteristics and Riemann invariants; classification of discontinuity; weak solutions and entropy condition; Riemann problem; CFL condition; Godunov method; artificial dissipation; TVD methods; and random choice method.

cilos.description: Understand the characteristics in linear and nonlinear scalar equations, the concept of entropy, and the condition for the formation of discontinuous shock. Solve the Riemann problem for the nonlinear scalar equation with concave and convex flux functions. Develop numerical scheme to solve the Burgers’ equation and traffic flow equation.
Identify the characteristic variables for the linear hyperbolic system. Construct the analytical solution of the Riemann problem. Develop numerical scheme to solve the linear system.

Obtain the characteristic variables for the nonlinear 2x2 system, such as the shallow water equations. Construct the analytical similarity solution for the Riemann problem and apply it to the wave interactions.

Derive the gas dynamic Euler equations. Present the Euler equations in terms of conservative, characteristic and primitive variables. Construct the Riemann solution for the Euler equations. Identify the interaction among different kinds of waves.
Develop numerical scheme for the Euler equations. Understand approximate Riemann solvers. Construct reliable numerical schemes beyond the inviscid Euler equations.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods in Science and Engineering I
courses.description: Modeling and analytical solution methods of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Topics include: derivation of conservation laws and constitutive equations, well-posedness, traveling wave solutions, method of characteristics, shocks and rarefaction solutions, weak solutions to hyperbolic equations, hyperbolic Systems, linear stability analysis, weakly nonlinear approximation, similarity methods, calculus of variations.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to describe problems in science and engineering by partial differential equation models.
Apply analytical solution methods to solve nonlinear partial differential equations.
Apply approximation methods to solve nonlinear partial differential equations.
Demonstrate abilities to interpret the solutions of partial differential equation models for problems in science and engineering.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods in Science and Engineering II
courses.description: Asymptotic methods and perturbation theory for obtaining approximate analytical solutions to differential equations. Topics include: local analysis of solutions to differential equations, asymptotic expansion of integrals, global analysis and perturbation methods, WKB theory, multiple-scale analysis, homogenization method.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to obtain approximate analytical solutions  to differential equations by asymptotic methods.
Identify perturbation problems in science and engineering.
Demonstrate abilities to understand the errors of the obtained approximate analytical solutions.

courses.title: Multiscale Modeling and Computation for Non-equilibrium Flows
courses.description: Introduction of the Navier-Strokes equations and the flow modeling in the hydrodynamic scale. The derivation of the Boltzmann equation in the kinetic scale. The basic mathematical analysis of the Chapman-Enskog expansion and the numerical methods for the Boltzmann equation. The multiscale modeling from the kinetic to the hydrodynamic scales and the discretized governing equations. The study of non-equilibrium transport phenomena in gas dynamics, radiative and heat transfer, and plasma physics.

cilos.description: Derive the Navier-Stokes equations in the hydrodynamic scale.
Model the particle transport and collision and derive the Boltzmann equation in kinetic scale.
Extend the kinetic scale modelling to other scales and construct the corresponding governing equations.
Develop numerical scheme for multiscale transport equations.
Use multiscale method to study transport problems in rarefied gas dynamics, radiative and heat transfer, and plasma simulation.

courses.title: Combinatorics
courses.description: Enumerative Combinatorics: bijective counting, permutation statistics, generating functions, partially ordered sets, Mobius inversions, Polya theory.  Graph Theory: cycle space, bond space, spanning-tree formulas, matching theory, chromatic polynomials, network flows.  Matroid Theory: matroid axioms, representations, duality, lattice of flats, transversals.

cilos.description: Develop a kind philosophy of discrete thinking and bijective counting.
Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of advanced combinatorics.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and apply logical reasoning to investigate mathematical work with independent judgement.
Apply rigorous, analytic, highly quantitative approach to analyze and solve problems using combinatorial technics.
Understand the uni¯cation of discrete and continuous thought by demonstrating part of taught theories.

courses.title: Advanced Probability Theory I
courses.description: Probability spaces and random variables, distribution functions, expectations and moments, independence, convergence concepts, law of large numbers and random series.

cilos.description: Develop a rigorous mathematical framework to analyze randomness based on measure theory.
Derive probability inequality as a useful tool for mathematical analysis.
Demonstrate various forms of laws of large numbers and large deviation and their applications.
Establish the central limit theorem and present their applications.
Apply random walk theory to actuarial analysis.

courses.title: Advanced Probability Theory II
courses.description: Stable laws; infinitely divisible distributions; weak convergence on general metric spaces; Donsker’s invariance principle; basic martingale theory; optional stopping theorem; martingale convergence theorems; martingale CLT; Concentration inequalities; logarithmic Sobolev inequality; large deviation.

cilos.description: Recognize the basic knowledges about martingale, Brownian motion, and functional limit theorems.
Identify and describe the major theories of martingale CLT and functional CLT.
Apply the martingale approach to establish nonlinear functionals of random variables.
Apply functional limiting theorem  to get the limiting behavior of various statistics for stochastic process.

courses.title: Advanced Mathematical Statistics I
courses.description: Theory of statistical inference in estimation. Topics include: sufficiency, ancillary statistics, completeness, UMVU estimators, information inequality, efficiency, asymptotic maximum likelihood theory. Other topics may include Bayes estimation and conditional inference.

cilos.description: Develop a rigorous mathematical framework and lay a firm foundation for statistical inference.
Recognize the most important concepts, including sufficiency, MLE, efficiency, risk, admissibility.
Employ appropriate statistical models for modeling and inference.
Recognize the different criterion for evaluation of statistical models.
Apply the theory in mathematical statistics to real-life problems.

courses.title: Advanced Mathematical Statistics II
courses.description: Theory of statistical inference in hypothesis testing. Topics include: uniformly most powerful tests, unbiasedness, invariance, minimax principle, large-sample parametric significance tests. Concept of decision theory also covered.

cilos.description: Recognise the problem of interest and formulate the corresponding testing hypotheses.
Identify the types of random mechanisms for the problem at hand, and then choose the appropriate models to describe the data.
Choose the most powerful tests if available and/or the most feasible tests.
Evaluate and compare different types of tests.
Decide whether it is appropriate to use parametric tests or nonparametric tests.
Develop problem-solving skills to handle real-life problems with uncertainty.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes
courses.description: Theory of Markov processes, second order stationary theory, Poisson and point processes, Brownian motion, Martingales and queueing theory.

cilos.description: Introduce the general concept of stochastic process  and Markov chain.
Study the properties of  Markov chain   and  its limiting distributions.
Study the periodic Markov chain and its properties.
Study  martingale convergence theory and option sampling theory.
Study  Brownian motion and its properties.

courses.title: Time Series Analysis
courses.description: Basic idea of time series analysis in both the time and frequency domains. Topics include: autocorrelation, partial ACF, Box and Jerkins ARIMA modeling, spectrum and periodogram, order selection, diagnostic and forecasting. Real life examples will be used throughout the course.

cilos.description: Introduce some basic  concepts in time series   such as auto-covariance, stationarity  and ergodicity.
Introduce  time series models, such as AR models, ARMA models, threshold models, GARCH models,  and study their properties.
Study the theory of  estimation and testing statistics of  time series models.
Study the diagnostic tools for  identifying various models in practice.
Introduce for possible applications such as option theory and risk management.

courses.title: Statistical Machine Learning
courses.description: This course covers methodology, major software tools and applications in statistical learning. By introducing principal ideas in statistical learning, the course will help students understand conceptual underpinnings of methods in data mining. The topics include regression, logistic regression, feature selection, model selection, basis expansions and regularization, model assessment and selection; additive models; graphical models, decision trees, boosting; support vector machines; clustering.

cilos.description: Describe the basic procedures in data analysis.
Explain the principles behind statistical learning tools.
Analyze data with real data.
Draw meaningful implications in decision making.
Write a good project report and help decision making in practice.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Learning with Graphs
courses.description: This course will introduce a number of advanced learning methods and modeling principles for analyzing large-scale complex data structures and graph data. Topics covered include semi-supervised learning, spectral graph theory, deep graph modeling, knowledge graph modeling, etc., as well as open research problems in this area.

cilos.description: Demonstrate machine learning algorithm design skills for graph data analytics tasks.
Analyze the quality of results to domain problems.
Develop a program that can handle existing real problems.

courses.title: Computer Age Statistical Inference with Applications
courses.description: This course is designed for RPg students in applied mathematics, statistics, and engineering who are interested in learning from data. It covers advanced topics in statistical learning and inference, with emphasis on the integration of statistical models and algorithms for statistical inference. This course aims to first make connections among classical topics, and then move forward to modern topics, including statistical view of deep learning. Various applications will be discussed, such as computer vision, human genetics, and text mining.

cilos.description: Describe the basic procedures in data analysis.
Explain the principles behind statistical inference.
Analyze real data.
Draw meaningful implications in decision making.
Write a good report.
Implement algorithms for statistical inference.

courses.title: Topological and Geometric Data Reduction and Visualization
courses.description: This course is a mathematical introduction to data analysis and visualization with a perspective of topology and geometry. Topics covered include: classical linear dimensionality reduction, the principal component analysis (PCA) and its dual multidimensional scaling (MDS), as well as extensions to manifold learning, topological data analysis, and sparse models in applied math/high dimensional statistics. Extensive application examples in biology, finance, and information technology are presented along with course projects.

cilos.description: Explain the basics concept of dimensional reduction.
Use Compressed Sensing and High Dimensional Statistics techniques for data analysis.
Use Manifold learning approach for applications.
Apply the data analysis method in applications.

courses.title: Interest Rate Models
courses.description: Theory of interest rates, yield curves, short rates, forward rates.  Short rate models: Vasicek model and Cox-Ingersoll-Ross models.  Term structure models: Hull-White fitting procedure.  Heath-Jarrow-Morton pricing framework.  LIBOR and swap market models, Brace-Gatarek-Musiela approach.  Affine models.

cilos.description: Explain fixed-income markets and the roles of the fixed-income derivatives.
Apply advanced mathematical tools for fixed-income modeling.
Identify risk factors of fixed-income derivatives and formulate major classes of fixed-income models accordingly.
Evaluate the effectiveness of various models for different sectors of fixed-income derivatives.
Analyze exotic derivatives, identify proper pricing models and strategies for hedging.

courses.title: Topics in Analysis
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in analysis.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of analysis.
Apply methods of analysis to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of analysis.

courses.title: Topics in Complex Function Theory
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in complex function theory.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of complex function theory.
Apply methods of complex function theory to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of complex function theory.

courses.title: Topics in Algebra
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in algebra.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of algebra.
Apply methods of algebra to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of algebra.

courses.title: Topics in Number Theory
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in number theory.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of number theory.
Apply methods of number theory to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of number theory.

courses.title: Topics in Geometry
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in geometry.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of geometry.
Apply methods of geometry to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of geometry.

courses.title: Topics in Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in applied mathematics.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of applied mathematics.
Apply methods of applied mathematics to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of applied mathematics.

courses.title: Topics in Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in fluid mechanics.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of fluid mechanics.
Apply methods of fluid mechanics to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of fluid mechanics.

courses.title: Topics in Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in numerical analysis.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of numerical analysis.
Apply methods of numerical analysis to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of numerical analysis.

courses.title: Topics in Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in probability and statistics.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of probability and statistics.
Apply methods of probability and statistics to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of probability and statistics.

courses.title: Topics in Financial Mathematics
courses.description: Advanced topics of current interest in financial mathematics.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of financial mathematics.
Apply methods of financial mathematics to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of financial mathematics.

courses.title: Professional Development Training in Mathematics
courses.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students basic training in teaching skills, research management, career development in and outside academia, and related professional skills in Mathematics. This course lasts for one semester, and is composed of a number of mini-workshops or tasks. Graded PP, P or F.

cilos.description: Exhibit effective skills in the teaching of Mathematics.
Apply essential communication skills for classroom teaching.
Recognize the features of the departmental online teaching system.
Prepare mathematics research papers, teaching notes and presentation slides using software (Tex).
Develop basic understandings of data science and reserch data management.
Demonstrate an understanding of the applications of knowledge and abilities of mathematics in industry.

courses.title: Mathematics Seminar
courses.description: This course will expose our PG students to the current mathematical research and development and provide them with opportunities to make mathematical and social contacts with the speakers and with local and international mathematical communities in general. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Recognize the frontier of modern mathematical research.
Build potential collaborations with seminar speakers.
Develop skills of giving mathematical seminars.

courses.title: Reading Course
courses.description: For individual students or a group of students. Specific topics under the supervision of a faculty member.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to understand the advanced concepts and techniques of the assigned specific topics.
Apply methods of the assigned specific topics to solve problems.
Recognize limitations of methods of the assigned specific topics.

courses.title: Scientific Computation Seminar
courses.description: This course will expose PG students to the current research and new development in scientific computation and provide them with opportunities to make social contacts with the speakers from both the local and international academic communities. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Attend 6 seminars related to the scientific computation from the home or other departments in the whole semester.

courses.title: Student Seminars on Computation Related Research
courses.description: Seminar presentation on computation related research by students in the Scientific Computation Concentration (SCC) within the first four regular terms of study. Students should notify their major department 2-3 weeks in advance for the presentation. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding on computation related research.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to conduct  research in mathematics.
Demonstrate knowledge in the chosen discipline of mathematics.
Synthesize and create new knowledge and to making contributions to the discipline of mathematics.
Demonstrate communication skills in presenting reporting findings in mathematics.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Demonstrate abilities to conduct independent and original research in mathematics.
Demonstrate mastery of knowledge in the chosen discipline of mathematics.
Synthesize and create new knowledge and to make original and substantial contributions to the discipline of mathematics.
Demonstrate a broad knowledge in mathematics and mathematical sciences.
Demonstrate effective communication skills in presenting and publishing findings in mathematics.

courses.title: Solar Energy Science and Technology
courses.description: This course elaborates on the fundamentals and applications of solar energy, which is the most prominent renewable energy option for our carbon-neutral future. It covers the key physics, materials, and device engineering aspects that are important in developing strategies to harness and utilize solar energy more efficiently and cheaply.

cilos.description: Explain the properties of the sun and the sunlight.
Explain the difference between photovoltaic and photothermal energies.
Explain the basic principles of photovoltaic and photothermal devices.
Explain the key science concepts related to the materials and device engineering of solar cells.
Use established methodologies to quantitatively solve the key engineering parameters for solar energy utilization.
Produce a report and presentation related to a key topic of solar technologies.

courses.title: Theory and Practice in Heterogeneous Catalysis
courses.description: Catalysis selection, preparation, characterization and testing. Computer-aided design of catalyst, micro-fabricated catalyst and bio-catalyst. Basic design principles for reactors. Innovative reactor design.

cilos.description: Identify and predict properties of heterogeneous catalysts for chemical reactions.
Design catalysts and catalytic reactions for chemical conversion and transformation.
Apply fundamental principles of chemistry and chemical engineering in selection, design and preparation of catalytic materials.
Create expert knowledge in methodologies and instrumentations for characterizing catalysts.
Design process for the manufacture of heterogeneous catalysts.
Design catalytic reactor and integrate the use of catalyst in such reactor system.

courses.title: Power Generation Technologies
courses.description: Basic knowledge of different power generation technologies, including traditional power plants, renewable generation as contemporary favor and emerging concepts such as virtual power plant, and their relevance to climate change and available energy resources in the earth.

cilos.description: Identify the key drivers shaping the power generation industry.
Identify the deployment trend of different power generation technologies.
Describe the working principles of various power generation technologies.
Compare different power generation technologies based on a systematic and consistent approach.
Develop interest and basic knowledge on chemical processes related to the power generation and emerging/enabling technologies covered in the course through the group project.
Search updated/evolving energy and power generation technology information, data and news from credible sources.

courses.title: Decarbonization Technologies
courses.description: This course aims to deliver the concept and importance of carbon neutrality. The course offers the latest technologies on decarbonization processes, including net-zero electricity generation, energy saving and green buildings, green transport, and waste reduction. Fundamentals and development of each technology will be addressed in terms of the process design, unit operation, and system integration.

cilos.description: Identify the concept and philosophy of carbon neutrality.
Identify the demand and the importance of environmental sustainability.
Describe the significance of decarbonization technologies to the humanities and environment.
Solve the engineering problems on the four main decarbonization technologies, including green transport, waste reduction, net-zero electricity generation, and green buildings.
Design and integrate the processing units into system for decarbonization processes.

courses.title: Advanced Separation Processes
courses.description: This course covers the advanced fundamental principles of separation process that are essential in chemical and energy engineering education. The objective is to challenge the chemical and energy engineering students with advanced separation processes, and to further develop their ability to apply those advanced principles to the solution of important problems.

cilos.description: Describe concepts, principles, relations and experimental basis of the separation processes.
Describe key concepts of separation processes and unit design including equilibrium stages, reflux,countercurrent contacting, limiting cases, efficiency and mass transport effects.
Model and solve problems related to flash distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, batch distillation, cascades,simple and complex binary distillation systems and absorption in packed towers.
Identify the basic principles of evaporation, absorption, liquid-liquid extraction, membrane, drying processes.
Evaluate separation process options in a wider context of sustainability, commercial considerations andcontribution to the society.

courses.title: Deep Learning for Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the application of deep learning methods in chemical and biological engineering. The course will cover the fundamental concepts and techniques in deep learning, such as deep neural networks, backpropagation, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and transformer models. The course will focus on applying these methods to solve problems in chemical and biological engineering, including molecule and reaction property prediction, drug discovery, process monitoring and control, etc.

cilos.description: Understand the problem formulations using deep learning.
Understand the mathematical principle of deep learning methods.
Develop advanced model architectures.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Apply deep learning methods in chemical and biological engineering problems.

courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.description: This course aims to equip the students with the knowledge and skills to understand, analyze and create innovative energy policies for application in public or business sectors. It will give an energy overview and challenges, a detailed review of energy management tools available, and a critical understanding of the role of policy that will integrate all these essential elements to achieve a sustainable development.

cilos.description: Identify the energy supply infrastructures and challenges.
Recognize the scopes and types of energy policies and plans and their impacts.
Acquire the basics of energy engineering technologies and appreciate the limitations.
Identify the basics of energy commercial instruments and their alignment with energy policy.
Offer a framework to help a community or organizations to improve energy performance.

courses.title: Advanced Polymers for Engineers
courses.description: This course offers understandings of polymer science and engineering, and covers polymer history, concepts, synthesis, characterizations, structures/morphology, and properties. This course also introduces covalent organic frameworks along the line of extended networks. After this course, students will understand the concepts and principles of polymerizations, widely used synthetic methods for polymerizations, and ways to analyze properties to understand morphology and structures.

cilos.description: Identify the concepts and principles of polymerizations.
Explain widely used synthetic methods for polymerizations.
Describe ways to analyze properties to understand morphology and structures.
Recognize polymer as advanced materials.
Identify porous crystalline polymeric materials for applications in energy and the environment.

courses.title: Advanced Biochemical Engineering
courses.description: The course will cover the advanced concepts of bioprocessing, including fermentation, bioreactor design, and product recovery. It will explore the production of bioenergy from renewable sources, such as biomass, biogas, and biofuels. Students will gain an understanding of the technical, economic, and environmental aspects of bioproducts and bioenergy production.

cilos.description: Describe the principles of bioprocess engineering and bioenergy production.
Explain how microorganisms and biochemical processes can be applied for various bioproducts and bioenergy.
Select, compare or design a reactor, fermentation processes or bioseparations used for various products, based on cost, safety, operability, etc.
Evaluate the production and potential of bioenergy from economic and environmental aspects.
Communicate biochemical engineering concepts through the use of engineering media, verbally and in writing.

courses.title: Process Safety Management and Risk Analysis
courses.description: Understanding hazard effect, probability and risk. The impacts of some major process accidents - loss of life, economic losses and capital losses. Hazard identification and analysis methods - HAZOP, What If and Index Methods. Fault Tree, Event Tree and Reliability Analysis. Exposures, Fires, and Explosions, Relief System Design. Impact Minimization, Process Safety Management and Designing Processes/Products for Safety.

cilos.description: Effectively describe the process safety management and risk assessment processes.
Categorize the key elements constituting to the building blocks of Process Safety Management framework.
Write up brief functional description, operation procedure and/or start-up/shut down procedures.
Identify and evaluate the risk and hazard by applying the quantitative tools learnt.
Critique on the adoption, implementation, integration and improvement of the Process Safety Management framework.

courses.title: Energy Integration and Optimization for Process Industry
courses.description: For most energy intensive industries, such as process industry, the effectiveness of using energy plays a key role in improving their competitiveness and at the same time reducing environmental impacts. By knowing how energy equipment is designed and can be integrated, engineers could maximize the efficiency of a production system and sometimes simultaneously reduce capital investment and environmental burdens. Students will conduct several design projects in which they will apply computer software, such as Excel, Aspen+, GAMS and SPRINT, to design, integrate and optimize energy systems such as heat exchanger network, power plant, fuel conversion plant, etc.

cilos.description: Model and optimize individual energy equipment such as heat exchanger, boiler, turbine, etc. that are commonly available in chemical plants.
Integrate and optimize energy system such as steam boiler plant, combined cycle, refrigeration system, etc., by combining the indiviual energy equipment studied.
Target, design and optimize heat exchanger network.
Design and integrate energy system with production process.
Create and conduct design or research projects with integration and optimization elements.

courses.title: Energy, Environment and Sustainable Development
courses.description: This course attempts to highlight the basic issues on the relation between material/energy resources, the environment and sustainable development. Potential directions for technological changes on greater efficiency of energy utilization, exploitation of renewable energy, adoption of cleaner environmental practices and waste reduction that can lead to sustainable development will be explored. Management of energy and environment towards sustainability will be introduced.

cilos.description: Identify the relationship between energy, environment and sustainable development.
Conduct energy analysis on energy systems.
Relate the global demand for energy with the impact on the environment.
Relate global warming with greenhouse gases emission.
Explain how various forms of non-renewable and renewable energies are produced and evaluate their impacts on the environment and sustainable development.
Propose possible practices and enhancement of energy efficiency in industry and commerce, which can contribute to sustainable development.

courses.title: Electrochemical Energy Technologies
courses.description: Electrochemistry fundamentals; thermodynamics; electrokinetics; energy conversion and storage; fuel cells; batteries; supercapacitors; solar cells; electrolyzers; fuel production; CO2 reduction.

cilos.description: Describe fundamentals of electrochemical energy technologies and use electrochemistry to explain reaction mechanism.
Explain the design principles of fuel cells, batteries, supercapacitors, etc.
Study in depth a particular energy topic and write a review/give a presentation.
Select active materials and test them for various electrochemical energy devices.

courses.title: Chemical Product Engineering
courses.description: Chemical process engineering had been instrumental for the success in the manufacture of traditional chemical products in large quantities. The manufacture of these commodities products focused on the design of the production process, This course aims to redress the balance between commodities and high-value-added chemical products by expanding the scope of chemical engineering design to encompass both product design and process design.

cilos.description: Conduct the process of identifying customers' needs and developing ideas that may satisfy these needs.
Identify product needs and fundamental design features for products in the energy sector.
Identify the critical importance of product purity in the fabrication of microelectronics products and develop process operations that could satisfy these needs.
Identify the opportunities for the development of food and personal care products.
Demonstrate the design of products and processes for the benefit of the environment.
Conduct "process synthesis" for the manufacture of chemical products.
Discover the basis of using nanotechnology for the manufacture of new products.

courses.title: Process Reactor Selection and Design
courses.description: This course will look into various types of process reactors; how they are categorized, what they are best suited for and the constraints. It will also go through the general design principles for most reactor types of which one of the most commonly will be adopted (e.g. stirred tanks) for in-depth studies. The class will briefly touch on other key industrial design considerations such as operability, scalability, safety evaluation, ease of maintenance, control strategies, capital and operation cost implications.

cilos.description: Describe and compare reactor types.
Effectively describe the mechanisms involved within the reactor for any particular processes and hence the relevant parameters required to quantity the situation for selection and design.
Be familiar with the essential chemical and physical models critical to reactor design.
Identify the rate limited steps and leverage this to simplify the design.
Appreciate the impact of other key industrial parameters on reactor design.
Design a relatively safer reactor by adopting an inherently safer design and multiple layers protection strategies.
Adopt techniques for reactor integration, scale-up and optimization.
Gain insight on the future development of reactor design.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics in chemical and biomolecular engineering.

cilos.description: Identify the most recent progress in chemical and biomolecular engineering.

courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: An independent project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.

cilos.description: Develop the skills of modern analytical, experimental and computational techniques in chemical and biomolecular engineering.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: This course is tailored for Year 1 and Year 2 MAE students, focusing on career guidance and exploration of various career options. It will feature guest speakers who will share insights on local and global job markets, along with organized site visits to companies. It is a two-year course (PP for first 3 terms and Pass/Fail for Spring Term of Year 2.)

cilos.description: Explore Career Opportunities in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering.
Understand Industry Trends and Workplace Environments.
Gain Awareness of Professional Practices.
Connect academic learning to real-world applications.
Prepare for Academic and Professional Growth.

courses.title: Energy Systems in a Sustainable World
courses.description: Various fuels used by mankind, fossil and renewable sources; power generation technologies and the controversies; energy efficient technologies and the applications in buildings and consumable products; energy efficient manufacturing technologies; low energy infrastructure and impact to modern life style; myths behind sustainable energy systems and the debates; energy entrepreneurship, case studies and social impact.

cilos.description: Acquire basic knowledge of the different energy systems used in modern sustainable society
Establish ability in carrying out scientific debates on energy related topics in society
Develop ability in building own thinking on energy issues with technical justification
Develop ability in conducting relevant in-depth analysis that can lead further to reaching some levels of conclusion in energy related issues
Polish skills in engaging in intellectual discussion in energy system related topics

courses.title: Buildings for Contemporary Living
courses.description: This course introduces the applications of modern mechanical engineering technologies to buildings systems and how they relate to our livings. A wise design of building systems offers high convenience to the occupants. Building systems, such as structural design, water supply, safety and air conditioning are of high importance to maintain a satisfying temperature, humidity, lighting and indoor air quality for comfortable living and efficient working. The course introduces the latest trend of building design, such as intelligent, and green buildings, micro sensors, Internet of Things (IoTs), VR/AR and metaverse and AI and how to maintain the sustainability and efficiency of the whole building in terms of building duration, energy and operation. The aim of the course is to provide students fundamental understanding and latest case studies on the current technologies for attaining contemporary living, and the difficulties we are facing that we may be ready for future challenges.

cilos.description: Evaluate building system engineering by applying the basic principles of science
Explain how energy is used and the corresponding impact on global climate change due to carbon emission
Analyze societal and behavioral issues arising from the developments of contemporary living
Identify and explain the importance of physical, psychological, social, and occupational wellness
Evaluate the social and philosophical implications of scientific discoveries related to building technologies

courses.title: Mechanical Engineering for Modern Life
courses.description: Mechanical Engineering covers the broadest range of engineering amongst all related disciplines. In addition to the production of modern products useful in daily life, it is also associated with power generation and distribution, as well as new materials development. These will be used to explain mechanical engineering principles and their usage in product design and manufacture. Contents include Engineering Materials, Solid Mechanics and Structural Design, Renewable Energy, Indoor Environmental Quality, Smart Green Building, Energy Design, Sensors and Instrumentation, Robots and Controls, together with MEMS and LED Fabrication. First year students are preferred.

cilos.description: Comprehend and apply the basic principles of mechanical engineering technologies for modern life
Evaluate the social and philosophical implications and impacts of the advancements of mechanical engineering technologies

courses.title: Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the field of Aerospace engineering, discussion of basic aerospace systems and disciplines, working vocabulary of the field. Basic concepts. Demonstration through examples.

cilos.description: Understand the vocabulary related to aerospace engineering: components and principles of an aircraft or spacecraft, their purpose and features.
Be familiar with general concepts in aerodynamics, aircraft performance, propulsion, space engineering, and preliminaries of aircraft design and systems engineering.
Use the basic vocabulary of the field. Connect between the various disciplines of aerospace engineering.
Perform basic computations and quantitative evaluations on the main disciplines in aerospace engineering.

courses.title: Exploration of Mechanical Design and Engineering
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the field of mechanical engineering and its growing intersection with the generative design principle. Mechanical engineering, a discipline that applies scientific principles to design and construct machines and structures, has far-reaching impacts on our daily lives. Throughout this course, the broad spectrum of mechanical engineering, covering various subdisciplines and their unique applications of mathematics and science will be explored.
