Students will examine how mechanical engineering solutions are integral to our lives and work from the simplest tools to complex systems. By engaging with the course activities, students will be able to develop critical problem-solving skills applicable to real-world engineering challenges. This course aims to equip students with a foundational understanding of mechanical engineering principles and the ability to assess the integration of generative design process.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental principles of mechanical engineering and their applications in everyday life
Identify and describe various subfields within mechanical engineering
Understand the relationship between mechanical engineering and technological innovation
Apply basic problem-solving techniques used in mechanical engineering to simple real-world scenarios

courses.title: Foundations of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
courses.description: This course serves as an introduction to Mechanical and Aerospace engineering, covering theoretical concepts and basic core principles across four key sub-areas: (1) aerospace engineering; (2) mechanics and materials; (3) thermo-fluids; (4) design and manufacturing. It provides a solid foundation for students to develop essential analytical and problem-solving skills, enabling them to approach future major courses with confidence. The curriculum includes topical studies organized into these four main modules. Fundamental concepts and principles are demonstrated and visualized through real-life examples.

cilos.description: Understand the theoretical concepts in mechanical and aerospace engineering.
Be familiar with the basic core principles in mechanical and aerospace engineering and able to explain how they are applied to meet societal needs.
Apply the analytical thinking and problem – solving skills.
Function with engineering mindset and teamwork spirits in addressing real – world challenges.
Recognize the impact of aerospace and mechanical engineering as a profession.

courses.title: Industrial Training
courses.description: A practical training course in an industrial simulated environment. For students of the Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering Department only. Graded P, PP or F.

cilos.description: Apply mathematicals, scienctific, and engineering principles to solve practical mechanical engineering problems.
Operate the standard manufacturing tools for mechanical engineering tasks.
Use the techniques, skills, and modern engineering tools necessary for engineering practice.
Identify the key professional practices of an engineer.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: This course is designed for Year 3 and Year 4 MAE students as a continuation of MECH1001. It prepares students for the job market by focusing on essential skills such as resume writing, interview techniques, and networking. The department will organize practical workshops and guest lectures from various engineering industry disciplines, aimed at inspiring students and helping them set clear career goals. It is a two-year course (PP for first 3 terms and Pass/Fail for Spring Term of Year 4.)

cilos.description: Develop effective job application materials.
Demonstrate interview competence.
Understand and apply networking skills.
Establish career goals and strategies.
Build industry awareness and professionalism.

courses.title: Aerospace Engineering: Principles and Systems
courses.description: Basic principles in key disciplines of aerospace systems and interconnections among the various disciplines. This course covers major disciplines in aerospace engineering, such as aerodynamics, propulsion, aircraft performance, space engineering (astronautics), and aerospace systems engineering. In addition, this course aims to introduce aerospace engineering from a modern perspective and cover the latest development trends in aerospace engineering, such as systems design, data-driven modeling, sustainable aviation, advanced air mobility, space logistics, etc.

cilos.description: Understand the vocabulary related to aerospace engineering: fundamental concepts, components of aircraft and spacecraft, and their purposes.

Know the fundamentals of important disciplines of aerospace engineering, including aerodynamics, aircraft performance, propulsion, aircraft design, space engineering, and aerospace systems engineering.
Know the latest development trends and important research areas in modern aerospace engineering.
Use the basic vocabulary of the field. Explain the relationship between the various disciplines of aerospace engineering.

courses.title: Statics and Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamental course on the analysis of the equilibrium and dynamic behavior of mechanical systems. Statics: equilibrium of particles and of rigid bodies; distributed forces; analysis of structures, including, trusses, frames, cables and beams. Dynamics: kinematics of particles; kinetics of particles, Newton's second law, energy, momenta, impact dynamics; systems of particles; kinematics of rigid bodies; kinetics of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions. For students with major in MECH, AE and MEGBM only.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023) AND (PHYS 1111 OR PHYS 1112 OR PHYS 1312)

cilos.description: Apply equilibrium for systems of particles and rigid bodies.
Calculate kinematics of particles and rigid bodies.
Apply equations of motion for particles.
Calculate dynamics of rigid bodies in 2 and 3 dimensions.
Analyse static structures, such as trusses, frames, and cables.
Analyse and model simple mechanical systems.

courses.title: Solid Mechanics I
courses.description: Forces, moments, equilibrium; principles of virtual work; analysis of structural members under axial load, torsion and bending; shear force and bending moment diagrams; statically indeterminate trusses; buckling and structural stability.

cilos.description: Describe the basics of and relationship between stress and, strain, and distinguish normal and shear stress, extension and shear strain, and the corresponding material properties.
Identify the qualitative features of the stresses, strains, material properties and area properties associated with axial loading, torsion and bending.
Solve for stresses in a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Solve for the deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bend loads, acting individually or in combination.
Solve for the principal stresses in structural components subjected to a combined state of loading.
Identify, formulate and solve statically indeterminate structural components.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts; hydrostatics; integral and differential equations of fluid flows; conservation of mass, momentum and energy; dimensional analysis; pipe flow; channel flow and boundary layers.

cilos.description: Explain key fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics.
Understand the role of mathematics in studying fluid mechanics problems.
Employ mathematics to scientifically analyze practical fluid mechanics problems.
Apply fluid mechanics principles to explain natural phenomena.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts; pure substance; work and heat; control volume; Ideal and real gases. First and second laws of thermodynamics. Entropy. Elementary power and refrigeration cycles.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023

cilos.description: Explain fundamental thermodynamic concepts and describe the first and second laws of thermodynamics.
Perform basic thermodynamic analysis on a given system or device using the first or second law of thermodynamics.
Evaluate the performance of common energy systems.
Evaluate the influence of energy technologies on the environment and human society.

courses.title: Engineering Materials I
courses.description: Atomic bonding of materials; crystal structure and defects; mechanical properties of materials; phase diagrams and phase transformations; heat treatment of metals; processing and applications of metallic materials.

cilos.description: Analyze key physical and mechanical behaviors of classical engineering materials.
Explain underlying mechanisms for material properties based on atomic structure, bonding, and crystallography.
Explain relationships between processing parameters and associated mechanical properties and phenomena (e.g., modulus, ductility, strengthening).
Identify appropriate materials with specific physical and mechanical properties for suitable engineering applications.

courses.title: Design and Manufacturing I
courses.description: Introduction to the engineering design process and engineering graphics; design specification, concept generation, and concept evaluation; geometric construction, sketching, orthographic projection, auxillary views, sectioning, dimensioning, tolerancing, and working drawing. For students under the four-year degree only.

cilos.description: Develop an engineering design specification for a product based on initial concepts.
Develop mechanical designs and conduct design evaluations based on a design specification.
Communicate effectively via engineering drawings and design presentations.
Conduct detailed component design to meet the engineering specification of parts or assemblies.
Select appropriate manufacturing processes for engineering parts based on design requirements.

courses.title: Mechanisms of Machinery
courses.description: Application of kinematics and dynamics in the analysis, design and synthesis of mechanisms. Type and dimensional design of linkages, cams and gears based on motion requirements and force transmission, in contrast to the strength requirements. Graphical, analytical and computer methods in analysis and design of mechanisms. Design considerations in mechanism synthesis.

cilos.description: Comprehend the basic key elements of mechanisms: four-bar linkage, different types of gears, cams.
Comprehend and apply the graphic, analytical and computer methods to analysis and design of mechanisms.
Identify and categorize the type of the connection of the links (joints).
Develop analytical equations describing the relative position, velocity and acceleration of all moving links.
Build upon the foundations in kinematics and dynamics with application to machine design activities. Knowledge in basic engineering science is applied to analysis and design of machine systems.
Design projects and homework sets provide the students with experience in the design of mechanisms and machine systems.
Identify engineering problems and formulate methods for their solution through projects and homework.
Complete their projects using computational tools and software, including programming in their language of choice and use of Working Model software and other appropriate software.
Be familiar with standards in gear and cam machine components.

courses.title: Materials for Energy Technologies
courses.description: The societal energy transition from fossil fuels to renewable sources requires novel energy technologies, with material design and engineering at the center of the innovation process. In this course, we will explain the enabling materials science and engineering behind advanced energy technologies by answering questions such as why lithium powers our batteries and why it takes silicon to make a solar panel. Major material challenges of emerging energy technologies will also be discussed. During the course, the students will be exposed to 1) the knowledge of material structure-property correlations used in energy technologies, 2) materials synthesis and fabrication techniques for their incorporation into energy devices, and 3) material evaluation principles in energy applications. After taking the course, students will be able to identify desirable material properties and potentially propose new materials and manufacturing methods for specific energy technologies.

cilos.description: Acquire the knowledge of materials structure-property correlations utilized in energy applications.
Understand operating principles of advanced energy devices.
Understand critical material challenges facing the adoption of renewable energy sources.
Study literature in multidisciplinary fields.
Connect scientific principles to daily lives.

courses.title: Energy Conversion
courses.description: Thermodynamics of combustion, chemical equilibrium, refrigeration and mixtures of gases.  Analysis of power generation, propulsion systems.  Performance of modern steam plants, gas turbines, internal combustion engines and refrigeration plants.

cilos.description: Select and define appropriate control volumes for analyzing energy systems in classical power and refrigeration cycles, and calculate energy interactions across the control volume boundary, including heat, work, and mass flow, using thermodynamic property tables and diagrams (T-s, P-v).
Analyze and evaluate the performance of power cycles (e.g., Otto, Brayton, Rankine) and refrigeration cycles, determine their efficiency, and identify sources of irreversibility.
Compute the exergy (maximum useful work) for thermodynamic systems, identify sources of irreversibility, and assess how these affect the performance of energy conversion systems.

Apply appropriate assumptions, simplifications (idealization), and modeling techniques to solve practical engineering problems involving energy systems, and interpret the results to evaluate cycle performance under varying operating conditions.

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Transient and steady heat conduction.  Natural and forced convection.  Radiative exchange.  Introduction to computational methods.

cilos.description: Explain the basic concepts of conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer.
Formulate and solve simple conduction heat transfer problems, using techniques including both closed form and numerical methods.
Apply empirical correlations for both forced and natural convection to determine values for the convection heat transfer coefficient.
Examine blackbody and gray surface radiation, and evaluate radiation exchange between surfaces.
Apply the principles of conduction, convection and radiation heat transfer to analyze thermal energy related problems.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Composite Materials
courses.description: The course will introduce fundamentals of engineering composite materials, which include the following elements: 1) mechanics in engineering materials, strain, stress, tenor and elastic behavior. 2) concepts of composite materials, classification, characteristics, manufacturing. 3) micromechanics and macromechanics of composite materials. 4) failure mode and damage mechanisms. 5) Inspection and material testing methods for engineering components.

cilos.description: Understand mechanics of engineering materials and structures and how to calculate the mechanical properties.
Identify the properties of matrix materials and reinforcement materials (especially fibers) as well as the corresponding manufacturing techniques.
Predict the mechanical properties of fiber reinforced composites, and understand how these properties affect the laminated structures of composites.
Calculate the macromechanical properties and identify the failure mechanisms according to various loading conditions.
Understand the various testing and property characterization techniques.
Understand non-destructive evaluation methods for composite materials.

courses.title: Engineering Materials II
courses.description: MECH 3420, as an extension of MECH 2410, is an advanced course on materials science and engineering offered in this department. This course is composed of three modules, i.e. (1) electrical, thermal, magnetic, and optical properties of general engineering materials; (2) green and smart building materials including ceramics, polymers, advanced insulation and glazing materials; (3) aerospace engineering materials including application of Aluminum alloys, Magnesium alloys, Titanium alloys, as well as superalloys in aerospace structures and engines.

cilos.description: Conduct calculation and analysis of parameters of electrical, thermal, magnetic, optical properties of engineering materials.
Analyze basic structure and properties relationship of ceramics and polymers, respectively.
Analyze the materials selections factors in design of green buildings.
Perform analysis of advanced metal alloys applications in aerospace structures and engines.

courses.title: Computer-Aided Design and Manufacturing
courses.description: This course covers topics: curves and surfaces, geometric modeling basics, data structures in CAD/CAM, finite element analysis, optimization, tool path generation. It also introduces the fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence and machine learning, specifically focusing on their applications in design and manufacturing. In addition to lectures, intensive labs of ANSYS for finite element analysis and Python programming will be offered.

cilos.description: Become an expert user of Python -- be able to efficiently use the language to program and implement efficient algorithms of CAD/CAM from the very early conceptual design till the final machining G-code generation or additive manufacturing operation, in a team-work environment.
Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental mathematical theories and computer algorithms underlying CAD/CAM/CAE software tools.
Be able to design and implement a computer program of moderate complexity for CAD/CAM/CAE tasks.

courses.title: Control Principles
courses.description: Introduction to system equations, block diagrams, signal flow graphs, state-space systems, transient response using convolution integral, root locus and frequency response methods. Design by root locus, frequency response and state space method. Nyquist stability test.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental concepts and terminology of control engineering, including the purpose of feedback, system stability, and types of control systems.
Construct dynamic models of physical systems in the continuous-time domain using differential equations and Laplace transforms.
Analyze and interpret the transient and steady-state responses of zero-, first-, and second-order systems in the time domain.
Evaluate the stability of closed-loop systems by examining the locations of poles in the s-plane and relating them to system performance characteristics.

Design controllers for negative feedback systems to meet performance specifications (e.g., rise time, overshoot, settling time), using analytical and graphical methods in both time and Laplace domains.
Implement PID control strategies to regulate the behavior of dynamic systems in simulation or design contexts.

courses.title: Aircraft Design
courses.description: Students will work in teams to develop a conceptual design for a complete flight vehicle, using knowledge and skills acquired in the Aerospace Engineering Major curriculum. Specific considerations will include market conditions, mission requirements, aircraft size and layout, airfoil/wing geometry, aerodynamics, engine selection, airframe-engine integration, fuselage design, electrical and hydraulic systems, landing gear arrangement, flight stability and control, structures and materials, avionics and navigation systems, human factors, safety, manufacturing processes, and cost analysis. The teams will present their proposed designs via oral presentations and written reports.

cilos.description: Develop an understanding of aircraft design methodology through lectures, and then apply that understanding to a real-life case study involving a complete aircraft through team-based projects.
Acquire management, communication, team work and research skills; solve problems as part of a team and assume leadership duties.
Understand and implement the design and development process for aerospace vehicles.
Perform open-ended iterative tasks related to aircraft/engine design and airframe-engine integration.
Integrate a variety of systems and sub-systems within aircraft to demonstrate design feasibility.
Demonstrate design viability through computational testing and verification.
Prioritize design requirements/trade-offs and organize project schedules/deadlines; use formal structured design methods to develop aircraft that meet or exceed customer expectations.
Give oral presentations and write technical reports required of aerospace design engineers.

courses.title: Electrical Technology
courses.description: Electromagnetic circuits, transformers, electromechanical energy conversion, DC machines, asynchronous and synchronous machines, special machines, transients and dynamics, three-phase circuits and power electronics, applications in electrical building services.

cilos.description: Use basic knowledge in physics and mathematical tool to develop new analysis tools, concepts, and models.
Use electromechanical devices, such as transformers, DC machines, induction machines, and power devices for mechanical system design and development.
Conduct design analysis for products that involve electromechanical energy conversion.
Be aware of safety issues in use of electromechanical devices and power devices.

courses.title: Aerodynamics
courses.description: Irrotational flow, circulation, lift and drag, aerofoil, conformal mapping, lifting line theory, Elliptical wing, swept wing, delta wing, supersonic flow. For science and engineering students in their second year of study or above.
courses.prerequisite: CENG 2220 OR CIVL 2510 OR MECH 1907 OR MECH 1910 OR MECH 2210

cilos.description: Explain the physical causes of lift and drag, and the differences between subsonic and supersonic flows.
Explain the flow behavior around 2D airfoils and 3D wings.
Predict lift, drag, and pitching moment for 2D airfoils and 3D wings using analytical methods.
Extrapolate 2D airfoil data to 3D wing performance, accounting for finite-span effects.
Perform wind-tunnel experiments or numerical simulations to verify theoretical predictions.
Apply software to model complex flows around airfoils and wings.

courses.title: Aircraft Structural Analysis
courses.description: Elasticity, structural analysis, energy and matrix methods, fatigue, vibration, airworthiness and aeroelasticity. For science and engineering students in their second year of study or above.
courses.prerequisite: CIVL 2120 OR MECH 1907 OR MECH 1910 OR MECH 2040

cilos.description: Visualize the complexity of structural components and materials of the aircraft and understand their functions.
Analyze how external aerodynamic loads are transferred to internal stresses and deformations.
Apply the theories to analyze various aircraft structural components subject to different loading conditions.
Apply energy methods for deformation analysis.
Have the capability to assess whether aircraft structural components are able to withstand the applied loads and meet specified performance.

courses.title: Gas Turbines and Jet Propulsion
courses.description: Rotating machinery, turbojet, compressor blades, turbine blades, combustion, high temperature material, high by‐pass fan jet, rocket. For science and engineering students in their second year of study or above.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2350 OR MATH 2351) AND MECH 3640

cilos.description: Gain skills in problem solving for aircraft propulsion systems including gas-turbine engine-based systems.
Develop abilities to conduct performance analysis of a gas turbine engines, including turbojet, turbofan, etc.
Understand the working of various parts of aircraft propulsion systems.
Determine the applicability of propulsion systems for various flight missions.
Appreciate the environmental impact of aircraft and their propulsion systems, e.g., Nox, CO2 and noise.

courses.title: Aircraft Performance and Stability
courses.description: Introduction to the dynamics and control of atmospheric flight vehicles. Airplan performance, static longitudinal stability, maneuvering flight, directional stability and control, control surfaces, aerodynamic coefficients, flying modes, Laplace transform, open and feedback control, stall recovery. For science and engineering students in their second year of study or above.
courses.prerequisite: CENG 2220 OR CIVL 2510 OR MECH 1907 OR MECH 1910 OR MECH 2020 OR MECH 2210

cilos.description: Understand  the fundamental laws of flight dynamics and the key concepts of aircraft static and dynamic stability.
Be familiar with analysis tools pertaining to aircraft performance and stability.
Solve typical problems related to aircraft performance and stability.
Assess the performance and stability characteristics of aircraft.
Conduct a team effort pertaining to aircraft performance and stability.

courses.title: Avionics Systems
courses.description: This course covers avionic systems and communications, including analog and digital systems, aviation bands and frequencies, satellite and aircraft communications, selective calling, emergency locator transmitter, omni-directional range, instrument and microwave landing systems, and automatic direction finder. Other relevant topics may also be discussed in the course.
courses.prerequisite: ELEC 2420 AND (COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P OR COMP 2011)

cilos.description: Recognize the importance and necessity of avionics systems in aircraft.
Understand the history and evolution of traditional/analog instrumentation to modern computerized digital display systems.
Comprehend the four major avionics subsystems and their functionalities including: navigation equipment, electronics, communications, and electrical power.
Explain the different operating principles of external and internal navigational systems, their pros and cons.
Acquire knowledge in more advanced features including autopilot, fly‐by‐wire, and instrument landing.
Use the above knowledge to supplement their appreciation of “aeronautical engineering”.
Comprehend the four major avionics subsystems and their functionalities.

courses.title: Aerospace Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamentals of instrumentation and measurement and their application in engineering testing and experimentation. Focuses primarily on application of the fundamental principles learned in MECH 3640, MECH 3650, MECH 3660, MECH 3670 and MECH 3680 to more advanced test and measurement applications. Includes principles of analog and digital data acquisition, analysis of discrete measurement data, statistical assessment of hypotheses, design of experiments, and similarity scaling of data. For AE students only.
courses.corequisite: LANG 4034 AND (MECH 3640 OR MECH 3650 OR MECH 3660 OR MECH 3670 OR MECH 3680)

cilos.description: Identify the basic components of a measurement system.
Be familiar with the concepts, protocols and techniques that are commonly used in experimental testing.
Design, conduct and post-process an experimental test pertaining to basic fluid or structure phenomena.
Be proficient in data analysis and results interpretation.
Be proficient in technical communication via the writing of reports.

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes and Systems
courses.description: Introduction to the principles of manufacturing processes; process characteristics, capabilities and limitations; related machinery and equipment; automation and common aspects of manufacturing, including metrology and quality assurance.

cilos.description: Describe the relationship between product characteristics and the selection of appropriate manufacturing processes.
Apply manufacturing formulas and process parameters to solve practical engineering problems in real-world scenarios.
Analyze manufacturing workflows to identify inefficiencies and propose improvements based on process data and constraints.
Evaluate the effectiveness of assistive strategies and interactive assessment tools in supporting critical analysis of engineering applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Aerospace Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)
courses.description: This course introduces students to computational fluid dynamics (CFD) relevant to aerospace engineering. Students should be familiar with multivariate calculus and linear algebra, preferably with some experience with MATLAB or PYTHON. Topics include the governing equations of fluid flows, the use of applied mathematics to solve partial differential equations, and their implementation into a computational framework. Students will learn how to perform CFD simulations and post-process data to extract meaningful physics and insight for flows relevant to aerospace engineering. The course offers hands-on CFD laboratories focusing on laminar and turbulent, as well as steady and unsteady, flows over airfoils/wings. For minor (AE); or MECH and AE students in their third year of study or above.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental principles of computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
Create and validate CFD models with suitable numerical and meshing schemes.
Run steady and unsteady simulations using CFD software.
Analyze and interpret results to reveal key flow physics.

courses.title: Vibration, Control and Programming
courses.description: Single-degree-of-freedom vibration, multiple-degree-of-freedom vibration, beam theory, energy method, passive control, active control, programming, MATLAB, finite element analysis, energy harvesting, sensors, smart materials, and structures.

cilos.description: Derive 1DoF system equations.
Modify, in a design scenario, the system parameters such as stiffness, mass and damping ratio to alter vibration response.
Determine natural frequencies and vibration shape(s).
Apply modern computational techniques (i.e., Matlab and ANSYS for basic vibration analysis).
Select and use sensors and actuators.

courses.title: Laboratory
courses.description: Introductory laboratory course to provide training in experimental techniques and laboratory procedures, data acquisition, analysis and presentation.

cilos.description: Develop understanding of fundamental concepts in physical measurements, including the working principles of various measurement tools, signal processing techniques, and data analysis methods.
Gain hands-on experience in designing and performing mechanical engineering measurements in group settings, while evaluating and interpreting the results.
Apply a range of diagnostic techniques and analytical approaches to identify and implement effective solutions to diverse engineering measurement problems.
Perform scientific data analysis and present findings clearly and effectively, using appropriate technical terminology and standard reporting practices.
Practice engineering measurement techniques across a wide variety of scenarios.

courses.title: Mechatronic Design and Prototyping
courses.description: This is an extended version of industrial training designed for MAE students. The course's aim is to broaden the professional and engineering interests of students by enhancing their practicum/team-based experience through initiatives different from those of traditional lectures and tutorials. The training is project-based to develop the students' knowledge/experience in designing and building a practical mechatronics system (formerly called Industrial Training). Students will work in teams to identify the needs for their designed prototype. Also, students will be given the opportunity to design and build various mechatronics components including electronic circuits, motors, sensors, etc. from CAD drawings, and practise their engineering knowledge through all laboratory sessions. The main goal is to develop and nurture skills in problem-solving, communication, interpersonal interaction, project and time management, etc. via the entire project.

cilos.description: Comprehend and apply the basic principles of engineering design.
Design and build a practical engineering system.
Explain the applications of the key mechanical and electrical components.
Identify, analyse and rectify engineering problems.
Exercise project management skills by working through product development cycle.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Covers selected topics of current interest to the Department not covered by existing courses. Offerings announced each semester.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Materials Failure in Mechanical Applications
courses.description: Failure analysis, brittle and ductile fracture, creep rupture, fatigue cracking, environmental degradation of materials, damage tolerance design, life predication of engineering components, case studies.

cilos.description: Have the fundamental knowledge of material damage and failures.
Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental failure mechanisms of engineering materials.
Conduct simple failure analysis for industrial practice, and moreover the students will be able to estimate the service life of an engineering component.
Enhance the self-learning ability.

courses.title: Experiential Projects in Aerospace Engineering
courses.description: This course takes an experiential approach to aerospace engineering through (i) a series of seminars and workshops delivered by faculty and industry professionals, (ii) student-initiated tutorials on aerospace-related topics, and (iii) participation in an international aerospace competition. As well as giving students the opportunity to apply theoretical classroom knowledge to real-world engineering problems, this course will nurture skills in technical communication, teamwork, conflict resolution, and project management. This course will initially be led by faculty and then self-directed by students with faculty retreating as coaches. Students should seek approval from the course instructor prior to enrolling.
courses.prerequisite: MECH 1907 OR MECH 1910 OR (MECH 2020 AND MECH 2310)

cilos.description: Understand the fundamental engineering and mathematical principles underpinning aerospace engineering, from aerodynamics to structures to flight dynamics to propulsion as well as flight testing and optimization.
Be familiar with the current technologies used in aircraft design, construction and testing.
Use state-of-the-art hardware and software to design, build and fly an aircraft.
Work and communicate effectively in a multidisciplinary team.

courses.title: Air Conditioning Systems
courses.description: Introduction of heating, ventilating and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, moist air properties, heat transmission in building structures, solar radiation, air conditioning cooling load and heating load calculation, air distribution system design, indoor air quality, economic analysis, alternative cooling systems.

cilos.description: Understand the principles of various types of HVAC systems.
Analyze various types of HVAC systems.
Design and size major components of air conditioning systems.
Rationalize and interpret the design and analysis results.
Keep abreast with the cutting - edge cooling and refrigeration technology.

courses.title: Indoor Air Quality in Buildings
courses.description: Indoor air pollutants in buildings and their transport dynamics with respect to building ventilation systems.  Design methodology in handling indoor air quality in buildings and enclosed spaces.  Building environmental assessment method.

cilos.description: Gain a comprehensive understanding of both fundamental and emerging topics related to indoor air quality in buildings. This includes knowledge of various types of indoor air pollutants, the basics of particle mechanics and aerodynamics, and the design of ventilation systems. This understanding will be developed through lectures and group projects.

Be equipped with the ability to identify indoor air quality issues and sources of indoor pollution. They will understand the fundamental design principles of ventilation and air cleaning systems, as well as other strategies for mitigating practical problems.

Apply building environmental characterization technologies for assessing air quality. They will also understand how to utilize modern filtration and cleaning technologies to achieve and maintain high indoor air quality.

courses.title: Introduction to Intelligent Building Systems
courses.description: Introduction to intelligent building and building automation, communication, safety and security systems; modeling and control of noise, illumination, mechanical transportation, electrical, electronic, fire safety subsystems; system integration and optimization with the building envelope; code of practice in design, operational characteristics and performance specifications.

cilos.description: Understand intelligent building design concepts, intelligent building index, key effects on thermal comfort and human sensation, building energy saving and green factors.
Design vertical transportation, HVAC, lighting and fire safety systems in commercial and residential buildings using standards and codes.
Model and perform simulation for evaluating and optimizing building performance.
Select proper sensors, actuators and controllers for the design of thermal comfort control and building automation.

courses.title: Materials Characterization
courses.description: Study of microstructure, morphology, and chemical compositions of engineering materials using optical, X-ray and electron methods; specimen preparation, instrumentation and case studies.

cilos.description: Identify suitable techniques for specific materials characterization.
Use light microscopy for characterization.
Analyse the basic microscopy images of materials.
Analyse the basic spectra of materials characterizations.

courses.title: Introduction to Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Basic concepts of finite element methods, element equations for basic structural elements, implementation and application of FEMs in 1-D and 2-D structural analysis and heat conduction.

cilos.description: Have a basic understanding of the principles and concepts related to finite element methods.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically solve for stresses, strains and deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Numerically solve for temperature profile and heat flux in 1-D and 2-D heat conduction problems.
Numerically solve for stresses, strains and deformation of a structure under either plane-stress or plane-strain conditions.
Have a basic knowledge about finite element methods for solving time-dependent and/or non-linear problems.
Use commercial software package to perform structural analysis and heat transfer modeling, and are able to conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
courses.description: Rigid body motion, forward and inverse kinematics, manipulator Jacobians, force relation, dynamics and position control robot manipulators, force control and trajectory generation, collision avoidance and motion planning, robot programming languages.

cilos.description: Describe common applications of robotic systems across different engineering domains.
Explain the fundamental principles of kinematics and dynamics as applied to robotic arms.
Formulate and analyze the kinematic and dynamic equations for various types of robotic arms.
Apply basic methods to assess, select, and integrate robotic arms into engineering systems based on their kinematic and dynamic characteristics.

courses.title: Introduction to Precision Engineering
courses.description: Principles of precision design, precision machining, and precision measurement; mathematical definitions and theoretical studies of tolerances for one-, two-, and three-dimensional precision assemblies; applications and industrial practices.

cilos.description: Use basic knowledge in mechanisms and mathematical tool to model to design products with quality.
Conduct tolerance allocation and analysis for precision machine design and assessment.
Conduct sensibility analysis for precision design optimization.
Be aware of the needs and benefits of precision engineering.
Be aware of the technical and social issues in the manufacturing industries in the Pearl river delta and the need for industrial transformation.

courses.title: Numerical Methods in Engineering
courses.description: This course is intended for teaching numerical methods for engineering students at the senior level as well as at the beginning graduate level.  The course will have three important objectives: (1) to teach the basic theories and fundamentals of numerical methods; (2) to help the students to acquire skills to implement these methods for computer solution; and finally (3) to provide an environment where the students can familiarize themselves with many today's popular commercial software systems, such as MATLAB, and their use in the solution of engineering problems.
courses.prerequisite: (MATH 1014 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1024) AND (COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P)

cilos.description: Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental mathematical theories and algorithms underlying modern numerical methods.

Become an expert user of an advanced engineering computing system MATLab -- the students will be able to efficiently use the system to implement representative numerical algorithms to solve practical engineering problems, individually or as a team.

courses.title: Unmanned Aviation Vehicle
courses.description: This course will introduce students unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) that are capable to operate remotely or autonomously in various environments. The knowledge of the mechanics of flight and the design of quadrotors and other types of UAVs will be explored. The topics will be covered include: introducing UAV and its subsystems, developing aviation models, analyzing flight controllers, designing dynamic navigation systems, and planning the operation in complex environments.

cilos.description: Understand the principle forces acting on a UAV, including aerodynamics of propellers.
Be familiar with the geometry and mechanics of UAVs.
Understand typical sensors, control strategies, and their pitfalls.
Analyze flight control and system operation.
Comprehend navigation systems, analyze data and plan flight operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Nanosatellite Engineering
courses.description: This course will introduce the fundamental concepts of CubeSat. In this experiential course, a number of labs have been prepared with a different focus on orbits dynamics, analysis of control and thermal subsystems. Every student should finish fundamental labs individually, and organize in groups to work on an advanced design topic. The course shall offer students with both hands-on experience software simulation and hardware implementation. The topics in this course are introduced with mathematical derivations and case studies. After taking this course, students are expected to acquire an understanding of  the fundamentals of satellite engineering and more importantly a common sense in technical and managerial aspects of engineering design projects with focus on aerospace applications.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 2011 AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2350 OR MATH 2351) AND (PHYS 1111 OR PHYS 1112 OR PHYS 1312)

cilos.description: Obtain fundamental understanding of components of spacecraft (especially nanosatellites) and how the design / operation is related to mathematical models developed from first principles.
Use software tools to simulate the behavior of spacecraft engineering (especially for Nanosatellite) such as orbits dynamics, and sizing for subsystems.
Understand and identify the practical constraints in Nanosatellite engineering design and research projects.
Deliver design / proposal for engineering solutions related to the Nanosatellite topics.

courses.title: Final Year Design Project
courses.description: A one-year project course offers practice of engineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Each student will be assigned a component of a large project which may be sponsored by industry. Credit load will be spread over the year.

cilos.description: Identify and formulate mechanical system design and optimization challenges under real‐world constraints.
Develop and execute comprehensive project plans.
Analyze project outcomes using experimental or computational methods.
Collaborate effectively within teams.
Integrate AI methodologies into project development (for AI extended major students).

courses.title: Green Technologies for Buildings, Energy and Water
courses.description: This course introduces principles and technologies for sustainable and traditional cooling technologies for buildings, sustainable energy conversion, water desalination and purification. The first part discusses cooling techniques for building including the traditional air conditioner and sustainable solar driven cooling technologies for buildings. The second part discusses solar to thermal and chemical energy conversion technologies including solar collecting and concentrating technologies including solar collecting and concentrating technology, photovoltaic cells and solar thermophotovoltaics. The last part will focus on the water harvesting technologies which include water desalination and purification.

cilos.description: Explain the basic concepts of environmental characteristics, e.g., declination latitude and azimuth angle et al..
Examine blackbody and gray surface radiation, and evaluate radiation exchange between surfaces using Stefan-Boltzmann law.
Formulate and solve the simple heat transfer process in the solar heat conversion process, e.g., solar swimming pool heating and solar cooling process of the buildings.
Understand the basic principles of the solar water desalination, solar chemistry and solar electricity process.
Understand the photovoltaic effects, the fundamental of photovoltaic as well as the applications of photovoltaic devices in buildings.
Analyze the economy of the solar energy conversion technologies and solar energy savings.

courses.title: Co-op Program
courses.description: This course is intended to provide final year UG students with practical hands-on training in the form of a co-op program in an engineering company located in Hong Kong or China. Students must obtain approval from the UG Coordinator before enrolling in the course.

cilos.description: Critically assess various engineering techniques, identify and justify the most suitable methodology for a specific practical engineering problem proposed in the Co-op project.
Evaluate different design and manufacturing processes, select the most appropriate one and effectively implement it to accomplish the tasks in the Co-op project.

Examine and summarize the Co-op project works and clearly communicate the analysis and results in a series of well – structured written (monthly, progress and final) reports, utilizing precise technical language.

courses.title: Final Year Aerospace Design Project
courses.description: A one-year Design project offers practice of aircraft design for the modern aerospace industry. Students will gain an overview of how to manage a design team and will also gain skills in carrying out detailed design problems. The course will cover design requirements; conceptual design methodology developed and applied incorporating center of gravity, inertias, structural layout, materials, propulsion integration, stability and control, vehicle sizing, performance, and acquisition costs; sources of information for aircraft design; configuration design: performance, weight and balance, propulsion; aerodynamic design: lift, drag and control; structural design: loads, materials; philosophies of design and analysis; system design: requirements and specification; system design procedures; systems integration. For AE students in their fourth year of study only. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Identify and formulate mechanical system design and optimization challenges under real‐world constraints.
Develop and execute comprehensive project plans.
Analyze project outcomes using experimental or computational methods.
Collaborate effectively within teams.
Integrate AI methodologies into project development (for AI extended major students).

courses.title: Aerospace Research Project
courses.description: An individual one-year research project under the close supervision of a faculty member of the department. The individual student will conduct research on a specified topic related to aerospace engineering. Normally, a project proposal and a final report are required. For MAE students only. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Formulate an aerospace research problem from a critical literature review.
Select and apply suitable experimental, computational, or analytical methods.
Collect, analyse, and interpret data, acknowledging uncertainty.
Evaluate alternative solutions on technical, economic, environmental, and safety grounds.
Communicate research processes and results.
Work independently and safely while managing time and records.

courses.title: Research Project
courses.description: An individual one-year research project under the close supervision of a faculty member of the department. The individual student will conduct research on a specified topic related to mechanical engineering. Normally, a project proposal and a final report are required. For students of the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering only. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Formulate a research problem from a critical literature review.
Select and apply suitable experimental, computational, or analytical methods.
Collect, analyse, and interpret data, acknowledging uncertainty.
Evaluate alternative solutions on technical, economic, environmental, and safety grounds.
Communicate research processes and results.
Work independently and safely while managing time and records.

courses.title: Foundation of Solid Mechanics
courses.description: Continuum concept for deformation of solids; analysis of stress and strain; constitutive equations; solution of problems relevant to materials processing, fracture mechanics and structural analysis; energy methods and numerical solutions.

cilos.description: Execute the capability of establish governing equations using physical principles and laws.
Acquire the analytical capability through solving practical problems in solid mechanics.
Identify the key loading and deformation parameters in deformation and stress fields in solid structures.
Develop capability of analysis and quantification through exercising theoretical derivation and analytical solutions.
Capability of solving real engineering problems.
Establish skills to inrepret numerical solutions.

courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Tensor notation, derivation of Navier-Stokes equations, vorticity transport, viscous flow, flow separation, boundary layer, flow instability, turbulent boundary layer, stratified flow, rotating flow.

cilos.description: Be familiar with fundamental and advanced concepts in fluid mechanics.
Theoretically analysze some practical fluid mechanics problems.
Explain certain complex flow phenomena.

courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer
courses.description: Numerical simulation of viscous incompressible flows and heat transfer; finite-difference and finite element methods; accuracy and stability; grid generation; stream function and primitive-variable formulations; application to internal, external flows, diffusion, convection, and dispersion problems.
courses.prerequisite: MECH 2210 or equivalent AND MECH 3310 or equivalent

cilos.description: Identify and formulate problems in multidisciplinary environment with an understanding of basic mechanism and constraints.
Apply numerical tools and programming skills to solve fluid dynamic and heat transfer related problems.
Develop numerical methods adapt to practical applications.
Apply knowledge of mathematics, science, and engineering for problem solving.

courses.title: Transport Phenomena and Its Application in Energy Systems
courses.description: Elementary statistical concepts; ensembles and postulates; partition functions and their properties; calculation of thermodynamic properties; kinetic theory of transport process; fluctuation-dissipation theorem; Langevin equation; mass and heat transfer in fuel cells.

cilos.description: Equipped with essential knowledge of phonons.
Demonstrate the capability to derivate the basic variables in nano heat transfer.
Develop the cooling strategies in microelectronics by appling nano heat transfer.
Execute the energy conversion by applying nano heat transfer.

courses.title: Convective Heat and Mass Transfer
courses.description: Laminar and turbulent boundary layer heat transfer by similarity, integral and superposition methods; effects of roughness, curvature, transpiration and high turbulence; forced and free convections, free-shear flows and buoyant flows; numerical methods.

cilos.description: Identifiy fundamental quantities in convective heat and mass transfer.
Identifiy fundamental quantities in convective heat and mass transfer.
Implement the differentiial and integral methods in solving problems in convective and heat mass transfer.
Analyse problems using dimension analysis and scale analysis.
Evaluate different approaches in enhancing heat and mass transfer.

courses.title: Advanced Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: Relationships between microstructure and mechanical behavior in crystalline materials; temperature-dependent deformation in elasticity, viscosity and creep; embrittlement, fatigue and fracture of engineering materials; strengthening mechanisms in crystalline materials.

cilos.description: Capacity to model the behaviors of solids subjected to stresses.
Ability to calculate the elastic and plastic deformations of solids under stresses.
Capacity to relate the macroscopic mechanical properties and the microscopic mechanisms of solids.
Ability to analyze the strengthening, fracture and fatigue phenomena of solids.

courses.title: Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Materials
courses.description: An advanced treatment of the thermodynamics, kinetics and transport properties in solids, solutions, surfaces, and heterogeneous reactions.

cilos.description: Examine the materials and materials processes from the perspective of both thermodynamics and kinetics.
Identify the laws of thermodynamics and solution theory of materials.
Explain the diffusion and phase transformation in terms of its kinetics.
Explain the effect of thermodynamics and kinetics on the microstructure of materials.

courses.title: Precision Engineering
courses.description: Principles of precision engineering, 3D tolerancing for precision design, flexure and nano-positioning, interferometry for precision measurement, dynamic control for precision machining of engineering materials, ductile machining for brittle materials, applications and industrial practices.

cilos.description: Estimate machine tool and instrument’s precision and accuracy.
Perform precision design and analysis for 1D tolerance chain.
Perform precision design and analysis for 2D single and also multi vector chains.
Conduct sensitivity analysis for precision design optimization.
Perform nano positioning system analysis in terms of performance, cost, and safety factor.
Use of Nyquist criteria to evaluate a metrology system’s capability for a given surface gradient. Use PSI and phase unwrapping to reconstruct a precision surface.

courses.title: Precision Machining
courses.description: Basic concepts of precision machining; the well developed methods and systems of fixed and free abrasive technology for micro- and nano- precision machining and fabrication applications; methods and techniques for process control modeling and characterization; advanced applications of abrasive technology such as free form machining and micro fabrication.

cilos.description: Use of kinematic uncut chip model to conduct precision analysis for abrasive machining.
Evaluate increases in contact length, force, and friction, temperature, and also thermal damage for ceramic grains.
Evaluate 3 stages of deformation by a cutting grain. Evaluate cutting grain’s wear flat area reduction by dressing to avoid deterioration in precision.
Use temperature model to identify effects of machining parameters and also effects of cutting tool material properties.
Evaluate effects of active tribochemistry agents for machining force and tool wear reduction.
Evaluate properties of abrasives for tool conditioning for precision machining.

courses.title: Robot Manipulation
courses.description: Extensive introduction to robot manipulation theory from a geometric viewpoint. Rigid-body kinematics; spatial and body representation of rigid-body velocities; coordinate transformations; forward kinematics of open-chain manipulators; solution of inverse kinematics; robot workspaces; nonlinear decoupling control and force control.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamentals of robot mechanics.
Explain the basics of robotic planning and control.
Implement robotic solutions on real robot platforms.
Advance technical writing and presentation skills.

courses.title: Finite Element Methods
courses.description: Finite element formulation; variational principles for structural and continuum mechanics; numerical interpolation and integration; plane stress and plane strain analysis; plate bending and three dimensional solids; solution of large systems of algebraic equations.

cilos.description: Students have a basic understanding of the principles and concepts related to finite element methods.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically solve for stresses, strains and deformation of 1D and 2D structures due to a combination of mechanical loading.
Have a basic knowledge about finite element methods for solving time-dependent, eigenvalue and non-linear problems.
Use commercial software package to perform 2D and 3D structural analysis and heat transfer modeling, and are able to conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

courses.title: Introduction to Mechanics of Defects in Materials
courses.description: This course presents a brief integrated view on the roles of defects in mechanical behavior of materials. The basic concepts, equations and methods used in the analysis of defects by continuum mechanics and thermodynamics approaches are introduced in the course. The important roles of defects such as cracks, dislocations, second phase inclusions, grain- and phase-boundaries in behavior of materials are described intensively with illustrative examples.

cilos.description: Explain basic physics ideas, assumptions, approaches and skills in quantifying the roles of defects in mechanical behavior of materials.
Describe basic principles used in the analysis of defects and physical pictures of the roles of defects.
Discuss the roles of defects in mechanical properties of materials.

courses.title: Continuum Mechanics for Crystalline Solids
courses.description: This is an interdisciplinary course covering the fundamental laws of the mechanics and physics of crystalline solids, the general description of a periodic structure and their specific characterization methods. The course will start with tensor analysis, and basic calculations of tensor fields. After that, basic kinematics such as deformation gradient, Cauchy-Green tensor will be introduced and defined, followed by the mathematical description of symmetry of crystals. Finally, the course will discuss reciprocal lattices and the X-ray diffraction for structural solving.

cilos.description: Define the scales at which theories of continuum mechanics are applicable.
Perform indicial calculations.
Identify and explain the basics of kinematics: deformation map, deformation gradient, stretch tensors, incompressible conditions, SO(3), pure shear and so on.
Describe and use point group and space group of crystals.
Express the translational symmetry of crystals.
Describe the differences among all diffraction methods.

courses.title: Introduction to Microsystems: Technology and Devices
courses.description: Physics of Scaling; energy transduction, sensing and actuation principles; micro-fabrication technology and technology fundamentals; film formation, photolithography and etching; integrated Microsystems and Microsystems packaging.

cilos.description: Have a a basic understanding of microsystem engineering and principle of microsensors and actuators.
Develop the knowledge of key microfabrication processes for the design of microsensors and microactuators.
Understand the basic transduction principles and electromechanical analysis for the design of microsensors.
Develop the knowledge and skills for the design of practical microsensor systems.
Identify the pros and cons of typical packaging methods for microsensors and microactuators.

courses.title: Flow Instability
courses.description: Capillary instabilities, centrifugal instabilities, shear instabilities, thermal-convective instabilities, normal mode decomposition, spatial vs. temporal analysis, linearization, nonlinear dynamics, routes to chaos, phase space reconstruction, transition to turbulence, and fluid-structure interactions.

cilos.description: Describe why even a fluid flow with nominally steady boundary conditions may be unsteady due to flow instability.
Analyze the stability of simple flows by determining whether small disturbances grow or decay with time.
Describe how a laminar liquid jet breaks up under the destabilizing action of surface tension.
Apply concepts in nonlinear dynamics and chaos, such as phase space diagrams and bifurcations, to describe fluid flows.
Explain external flow around flexible structures and recognize the consequences of vortex-induced vibration.

courses.title: Acoustics and Aeroacoustics
courses.description: The aims of this module are to acquaint students with the knowledge of acoustics and aerodynamically generated sound, its generation either through turbulent flow or unsteady aerodynamic force‐surface interaction, and numerical methods for accurate numerical prediction of aerodynamically generated noise as well as its propagation and far‐field characteristics. The wide applications of the subject are noise, environmental impact of noise and transport related noise.

cilos.description: Analyze and solve aerodynamically generated sound phenomena through numerical means.
Select suitable approaches to solve sound problems.
Conduct basic acoustic measurements using key equipment.
Perform numerical simulations of sound using high‐order accurate schemes (and perform error and stability analysis).
Use commonly employed solution options in the industry environment.

courses.title: Processes in Manufacturing Systems
courses.description: Valued added processing in manufacturing systems is covered in the course. Emphasis is placed on how each process works to convert materials into shapes with the desired properties, and its relative advantages and disadvantages. Fundamental processes for metals, ceramics, polymers, composites and new processes including 3D printing methods are covered. In addition, inspection methods inclusion non-destructive examination methods, manufacturing automation; robotics; process control and quality control are covered.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental science underlying processing and manufacturing methods.
Identify the engineering factors controlling properties.
Explain the role of quality control in manufacturing processes.
Implement engineering changes on the processing to obtain desired structure.
Implement engineering changes on the processing to obtain desired properties.
Apply statistical tools to control manufacturing quality.

courses.title: Seminar in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Technical seminars in various disciplines of mechanical engineering; presentations are given by students, faculty, or guest speakers. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify research focus in different directions.
Summarise recent research progress in specific areas.

courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Selected topics in mechanical engineering of current interest to the Department and not covered by existing courses.

cilos.description: Apply the knowledge learned from the selected topic to solve advanced scientific and engineering problems.
Explain some special topics related to phenomena in engineering and daily life.
Perform quantitative analysis for practical problems in the selected areas.

courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: An independent research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. (Only one independent studies course may be used to satisfy the course requirements for any postgraduate program in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.)

cilos.description: Apply the knowledge acquired independently to solve advanced scientific and engineering problems.
Expand on existing related to phenomena in engineering and daily life.
Solve quantitatively selected problems using independently acquired knowledge.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Critically apply theories, methodologies, and knowledge to address questions in Mechanical engineering.
Pursue recognized research in Mechanical engineering through an independent research project.
Write publishable peer-reviewed research and communicate orally the research outcomes.
Master advanced Mechanical engineering skillset at an international level.
Work collaboratively and productively with team members and leaders with integrity and professionalism.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Critically apply theories, methodologies, and knowledge to address fundamental and impactful questions in Mechanical engineering.
Pursue internationally recognized research in Mechanical engineering by planning and conducting an independent research project under the mentorship of a research advisor.
Write publishable peer-reviewed research and communicate orally the research outcomes demonstrating knowledge of the field and mastery of the most advanced methodologies.
Demonstrate a mastery of technical skills required in Mechanical engineering at the highest international standard.
Work collaboratively and productively with team members and leaders with integrity and professionalism.

courses.title: Foundation of Solid Mechanics
courses.description: Continuum concept for deformation of solids; analysis of stress and strain; constitutive equations; solution of problems relevant to materials processing, fracture mechanics and structural analysis; energy methods and numerical solutions.

cilos.description: Apply solid mechanics knowledge to advanced stress analysis and practical problems.
Explain some solid mechanics related phenomena in engineering and daily life.
Perform quantitative analysis for practical solid mechanics problems.

courses.title: Fracture Behavior of Polymers
courses.description: Introduction to both fundamental and practical knowledge on the microstructure, physical and mechanical behaviors, particularly the fracture behavior and toughening mechanisms, of polymers and composites. Discussions and critiques on related research activities in the literature. Case studies to help students prepare for the industry.

cilos.description: Explain the microstructure-property relationships of polymers and select proper polymeric materials for specific engineering applications.
Characterize polymer fracture and evaluate fracture toughness of polymers using rigorous fracture mechanics methods under various conditions.
Explain the fundamental fractography of polymers and carry out basic failure analysis using microscopes and thermal analysis equipment.

courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Basic concepts of fluid flows, derivation of governing equations, viscous flow, potential flow, boundary layer, flow instability, transition to turbulence, turbulent boundary layer.

cilos.description: Apply fluid mechanics knowledge to certain practical problems.
Explain some fluid mechanics related phenomena in daily life.
Analyze practical fluid mechanics problems.

courses.title: Composites and Nanocomposites
courses.description: This course is designed to provide fundamental understanding of fiber-reinforced composites (FRPs) and emerging nanocomposites technologies. The topics include constituent materials, microstructure-property relationships, fabrication and processing techniques, fundamental mechanics of stress transfer, lamination theory and failure mechanisms and fracture of FRPs in the first part. The topics in the second part include synthesis of nanoscale reinforcements, fabrication and processing techniques of nanocomposites; dispersion and functionalization of nanoreinforcements; interfacial adhesion; mechanical and functional properties of nanocomposites, and their design and applications.

cilos.description: Distinguish different fabrication and processing methods for FRPs and nanocomposites.

Explain the mechanical and functional properties of these composites based on the microstructures/properties of the fillers and the matrix material, as well as the way how these constituents are combined to produce composites.
Identify potential applications of FRPs and nanocomposites utilizing these properties.
Identify the mechanics of stress transfer through the filler/matrix interface and interphase, lamination theory and failure mechanisms behind the fracture of FRPs and nanocomposites.

courses.title: Advanced Numerical Methods in Engineering
courses.description: This is an advanced level course in numerical methods, targeted at graduate students of engineering majors. It will teach fundamental math and algorithms of numerical methods such as analysis of errors, roots of equations, linear and algebraic equation systems, optimizations, curve-fitting and approximation, numerical differentiation and integration, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. In addition, the students will have tutorials in scientific programming tools such as MATLAB and Excel VBA and learn how to use them to implement their own numerical methods.

cilos.description: Recognize the commanding knowledge in fundamental mathematics and algorithms underneath today's popular numerical methods.
Apply basic MATLAB computer programming to implement some representative numerical methods.
Describe the history and evolution of the technologies and innovations in mechanical engineering.
Describe and formulate a mechanical engineering problem in a format suitable for solution by numerical methods.

courses.title: Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Materials
courses.description: An advanced treatment of the thermodynamics, kinetics and transport properties in solids, solutions, surfaces, and heterogeneous reactions.

cilos.description: Examine the materials and materials processes from the perspective of both thermodynamics and kinetics.
Identify the laws of thermodynamics and solution theory of materials.
Explain the diffusion and phase transformation in terms of its kinetics.
Explain the effect of thermodynamics and kinetics on the microstructure of materials.

courses.title: Intermediate Heat and Mass Transfer
courses.description: The scope of this course is intended to establish the conservation laws of heat and mass transfer, with the aims to provide the required knowledge for industrial applications. The topics in a sequential sense covers: Concepts of continuum in multiscale thermal and mass flow systems; Definitions of thermodynamics properties; Conservation equations of fluid flow and heat and mass transfer; Dimensional analyses; Heat conduction and mass diffusion; Convective heat and mass transfer; Computational heat and mass transfer; Special topics and industrial applications.

cilos.description: Describe in-depth the concepts of continuum through statistical physics.
Apply the conservation laws to fluid flows and transports of heat and mass.
Demonstrate the dimensionless parameters that play the key roles in heat and mass transfer.
Illustrate the basic physics of transport phenomena through the analytical solutions of simple heat and mass transfer problems.
Apply the numerical technique for solving the practical engineering problems where the analytical solutions are not available.

courses.title: Fundamental Theories and Algorithms of CAD/CAM/CAE
courses.description: Representations of curves and surfaces, geometric modeling, mesh generation algorithms, optimization algorithms, NC machining part programming, NC machining tool path generation algorithms, digital manufacturing.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental mathematical theories and algorithms underlying modern CAD/CAM/CAE systems/technologies.
Use a computer language (e.g. MATLAB) to implement some classical algorithms in curves, surfaces, optimization, and numerical controlled machining tool path generation.

courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Introduce the basic concepts related to industrial robots.  Course will cover the following contents: rigid body motion, forward and inverse kinematics, manipulator jacobians, force relation, dynamics and position control robot manipulators, force control and trajectory generation, collision avoidance and motion planning, robot programming languages.

cilos.description: Describe the basics of robotic systems.
Define the needs, acquire necessary information and select appropriate robots for various industrial applications.
Apply the knowledge learned for the design and development of simple robots.
Explain the principles of robot kinematics, dynamics, motion planning, trajectory generation and control.

courses.title: Precision Manufacturing Technologies
courses.description: Principles of precision engineering; mathematical definitions and theoretical studies of 2D precision assemblies; micro- and nano- positioning for precision machining; nanometrology, data processing for precision measurement; dynamic control for precision machining of engineering materials, applications and industrial practices.

cilos.description: Use basic knowledge in mechanisms and mathematical tool to model to design products with quality.
Conduct tolerance allocation and analysis for precision machine design and assessment.
Conduct sensibility analysis for precision design optimization.
Evaluate the needs and benefits of precision manufacturing technologies.
Recognize the technical and social problems in the manufacturing industries in the Pearl River Delta and the need for industrial transformation.

courses.title: Precision Machining
courses.description: Basic concepts of precision machining; tribosystems of abrasive machining processes; kinematic models; contact mechanics; force, friction, and energy; thermal design; molecular dynamics; tribochemistry of abrasive machining; abrasive tools and conditioning; methods and systems of fixed and free abrasive technology for micro- and nano- precision machining and fabrication applications; advanced applications of abrasive technology such as free form machining and micro fabrication.

cilos.description: Apply the process models of precision machining, such as kinematics, mechanics, force, friction, energy, thermal design, and tribochemistry, for precision machining process design.
Evaluate the key factors affecting surface quality in precision machining.
Analyze the types of machining tools and their characteristics for machining process design.
Evaluate the relationships between precision, energy efficiency, thermal damage, and cost, with the machining parameters, for machine tool design and development.

courses.title: Topology Optimization and Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: This course focuses on analysis and optimal design techniques and fabrication methods of structures and devices. The underlying principles of calculus of variations, constrained minimization, and design parameterization and solution methods of topology optimization will be fully studied. Key applications include mechanical metamaterials, compliant structures/mechanisms and multi-material soft robots. The course will bring out methodologies for designing optimal materials/structures/machines and fabrication techniques of 3D printing.

cilos.description: Recognize the commanding knowledge in fundamental mathematics and algorithms underneath today’s topology optimization methods.
Apply basic MATLAB computer programming to implement some representative numerical methods.
Describe the history and evolution of the technologies and innovations in mechanical engineering.
Describe and formulate a mechanical engineering problem in a format suitable for solution by design optimization methods.

courses.title: Finite Element Methods
courses.description: Finite element formulation; variational principles for structural and continuum mechanics; numerical interpolation and integration; plane stress and plane strain analysis; plate bending and three dimensional solids; solution of large systems of algebraic equations.

cilos.description: Derive finite element formulations for structural mechanical problems and heat conduction.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Numerically calculate temperature profile and heat flux in 1-D and 2-D heat conduction problems.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structure under either plane-stress or plane-strain conditions.
Derive finite element formulations for time-dependent and/or non-linear problems.
Perform structural analysis and heat transfer modeling using commercial software package, and conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

courses.title: Advanced Materials Analytics
courses.description: This course focuses on advanced materials analytics, including roles of engineering materials, material processing and their properties in products and manufacturing. Process selection analytics with focuses on product type, product volume, designs, precision and usage will be emphasized.

cilos.description: Introduce the relationships among the engineering material properties and process variables in a given manufacturing process.
Understand the principles of traditional and recently developed manufacturing processes.
