Compute the tax liabilities for individuals and companies.
Explain the tax implications of transactions on business activities.
Apply their tax knowledge to tax cases and in real-life contexts.

courses.title: Tax and Business Strategy
courses.description: This course provides students with the framework of strategic tax planning. Students learn how to integrate the role of tax in various corporate decision-making.

cilos.description: Apply the framework of strategic tax planning.
Analyze how taxes impact choices of organizational forms.
Evaluate the role of tax in corporate investment and financing decisions.
Analyze cross-border tax planning opportunities for multinationals.
Explain the ethics of tax planning.

courses.title: Auditing
courses.description: It covers the relevant principles, objectives and ethical requirements of audit and assurance services; identifies the audit process from client acceptance, design of audit procedures and express an appropriate audit conclusion based on the audit evidence obtained. Topics include: audit planning, audit evidence and documentation, internal control, completion of audit, audit opinion and reporting, professional ethics, rights and obligation of auditors.

cilos.description: Describe the auditing profession, and the regulatory, legal and reporting framework of auditing.
Recognize the basic principles, objectives and ethical requirements of audit and assurance services.
Identify the audit process from client acceptance, design of audit procedures and recommend an appropriate audit conclusion based on the audit evidence obtained.
Assess risks and threats to an audit of financial statements through analytical and critical thinking.
Communicate effectively in writing and verbally.

courses.title: Business Law
courses.description: This course is designed for the study of Business Law with practical examples of the application of law in the real business world. The course materials cover  topics highly relevant to the business managers in the decision making process. The end goal is to elevate the student's level of understanding of the surrounding legal environment.

cilos.description: Apply the legal knowledge studied to situations they are likely to encounter in their daily life and future careers.
Recognize the importance of different functional areas of the law, and solve legal and business problems critically and creatively by referring to the well-established cases and ordinances.
Recognize the importance of the law of professional negligence and duty of care on the part of the accountants and auditors, and become a responsible and capable member of the accounting profession.
Develop selected skills like analytical and critical thinking, effective communication and team work through the group project and presentation.
Recognize the importance of ethical responsibility, identify the ethical dilemmas, apply the ethical standards and recognize the consequences of breaching the ethical standards.
Recognize the importance of ethical responsibility and corporate social responsibility in the context of Chinese business ethics.

courses.title: Company Law
courses.description: Law relating to companies registered in Hong Kong; company formation and records; share and loan capital; management and administration; reconstructions; mergers and take-overs; liquidation and receivership.

cilos.description: Explain the documents that lay down the features of a company and its internal procedures, and evaluate whether they can be altered.
Explain the role of key personnel in the management and administration of a company, and judge their rights and obligations.
Apply the rules in relation to company meetings.
Explain legal considerations and apply the legal rules in raising share or loan capital.
Explain the schemes of arrangement and apply the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy-backs.
Explain the law in relation to commencement, conduct and consequences of winding up and apply the avoidance powers.
Explain the role, structure, duties, powers and procedures of some important external bodies in relation to the work of an accountant.

courses.title: Corporate Governance and Compliance
courses.description: The course covers corporate governance at two levels. At the practice level, it builds on students' prior knowledge of company law, and introduces them to the various requirements of compliance by company boards as stipulated in the Hong Kong regulatory framework. At the company policies level, this course introduces students to broader aspects of corporate governance, focusing on the multitude and interaction of stakeholders and how their interests may be protected.

cilos.description: Describe the background of development of corporate governance, and its importance to the sustainability of businesses by way of protecting stakeholders’ interests.

Explain the objectives and roles of directors, accountants and other responsible persons in the corporate governance system, and how stakeholders’ interests can be protected under different corporate governance theories and models.
Comply with the legal and regulatory framework for governance of companies in Hong Kong, while acknowledging recent developments in China and other countries.
Promulgate corporate governance principles and best practice.
Apply probity and ethical standards in governance.
Assert the value and importance of internal control functions and risk management to sound corporate governance.
Explain corporate social responsibility and its emerging importance to modern businesses, and recent developments in related corporate governance practice.

courses.title: Data Analytics in Accounting
courses.description: Data analytics is the process of collecting, organizing and analyzing big data in order to discover useful information for different uses. This course aims to provide students with knowledge of the nature and role of data analytics and how important it is to accountants, and enable students to apply and understand big data issues and utilize data mining, data modeling, data analysis and data visualization techniques to solve accounting and business related issues.

cilos.description: Explain and define the nature and role of data analytics and its application in accounting and business.
Explain and define issues related to big data and how to utilize big data.
Apply data mining modeling, analysis, and visualization techniques to solve accounting and business issues.
Utilize data analytics application(s) to perform and develop skills in business analysis.
Diagnose problems and issues by using big data to make responsible and ethical decisions.

courses.title: Advanced Data Analytics in Accounting
courses.description: With the foundation of ACCT 5710 Data Analytics in Accounting, this course aims to provide students with advanced and practical knowledge of applications in data analytics designed by accounting professionals and enable students to apply and understand data analytics technologies to perform audit, enhance financial reporting, and minimize risks as accounting professionals.

cilos.description: Describe and apply knowledge and accounting applications on common ERP capabilities - collection, cleaning and analysis of data.
Identify common data analytics challenges and risks in accounting issues.
Utilize and apply accounting data analytics and its applications on modeling patterns of data, and identifying outliers and anomalies.
Apply and evaluate accounting analytics techniques on analysis for fraudulent activities in corporations.
Identify and incorporate accounting analytics technology and options for visualizations.
Identify and explain accounting issues in decision making in the data age - the future of data analytics in accounting.

courses.title: Equity Investment with Machine Learning
courses.description: This course introduces the application of quantitative and machine learning technology in equity investing. It covers classical equity valuation theories, cutting-edge capital market research and recent development in quantitative and machine learning technology. Students will be required to apply the knowledge to develop and test equity investment strategies.

cilos.description: Describe the current landscape and challenges of the asset management industry.
Explain the philosophy, theory, and process of quantitative equity investing.
Evaluate the performance of equity funds and investment strategies.
Be familiar with multifactor stock-selection models.
Identify the potential applications of machine learning technology in equity investment.
Design and develop quantitative investment strategies.
Conduct backtests on quantitative strategies and evaluate their performance.

courses.title: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain and Their Business Applications
courses.description: This course discusses cryptocurrencies (including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and others), blockchain, also known as distributed ledger technology (DLT), and their multidimensional business applications. The course provides a basic set of skills to understand cryptocurrencies and blockchain/DLT. We will also discuss the latest development in the field.

cilos.description: Describe the history of blockchain technology and its recent development.
Explain the technical details of blockchain/distributed ledger technology including consensus mechanisms.
Identify real-world applications of blockchain technology.
Understand smart contracts.
Recognize regulations on cryptocurrency.

courses.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) in China
courses.description: This course aims at equipping the next-generation business leaders with knowledge and competence to navigate the nascent, rapidly evolving environmental, social, and governance (ESG) landscape in China, effectively assess and manage the rising ESG risks and opportunities, and seek long-term value creation by taking into account the needs of all their stakeholders and society at large.

cilos.description: Understand and apply fundamental concepts and analytical tools related to ESG and corporate sustainability.
Analyze and evaluate the strategies and practices of leading companies in sustainable supply chain management, ESG ratings and investing, ESG disclosure, and sustainability reporting.
Understand the science and public policy underlining climate change and apply the corporate strategies for mitigating and adapting to climate change.
Identify and assess the driving forces behind ESG adoption and expansion at the levels of individual firms, specific industries, and an industrializing country as a whole.
Evaluate and rate the ESG practices and reporting of a China-based listed company, while offering innovative and practical solutions for improvement.

courses.title: Introduction to Financial Crime
courses.description: This introductory course explores into the dynamics of financial crime, its detection, and prevention. Spanning historical perspectives, legal frameworks, and investigation techniques, students will explore the multifaceted nature of financial crime including money laundering, tax evasion, bribery, and corruption. The course integrates criminology and psychological theories to understand offender behavior, alongside the use of professional investigative skills. The course also places emphasis on responsibilities of financial institutions in monitoring and reporting suspicious activities, employing customer due diligence including conducting investigations into beneficial owners and politically exposed persons.

cilos.description: Understand the historical development and criminalization of financial crime, including what is shadow economy, and the responsibilities of financial institutions in detecting and reporting suspicious activities.
Critically apply criminology theories to understand the motivations and behaviors of offenders in financial crime.
Understand and apply critical thinking, professional skepticism and various financial crime investigation methodologies effectively.
Utilize and analyze financial flow diagrams, associated matrices, and real-world cases to understand money laundering, and spot and investigate complex money laundering schemes.
Apply Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), sources of funds (SOF), Net Wealth assessments in mitigating and identifying suspicious financial flows.

courses.title: Financial Crime Regulation, Compliance and Sanctions
courses.description: In today's interconnected world, combating financial crime requires a deep understanding of international regulations, enforcement processes, and emerging trends. This comprehensive course delves into the intricate landscape of financial crime prevention, investigation, and prosecution on a global scale. Students will explore the roles and responsibilities of key agencies, analyze Anti-Money Laundering (AML)/ Counter Terrorism Finance (CTF) frameworks across different jurisdictions, and dissect the anatomy of money laundering prosecutions. From compliance standards to the confiscation of proceeds of crime, this course offers a thorough examination of the tools and strategies employed to tackle financial crime effectively.

cilos.description: Explain the fundamental principles underlying transnational crime, such as organized crime, terrorism, and war and conflict.
Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of international financial crime regulations.
Acquire a comprehensive toolkit of techniques and strategies for preventing, detecting, and investigating financial crime.
Critically analyze the responses demonstrated by law enforcement agencies and other relevant entities in addressing the challenges posed by financial crime.

courses.title: Financial Crime Transaction Monitoring and Investigation
courses.description: Money laundering is a common financial crime methodology to integrate the illicit funds from a variety of predicate offences. in this comprehensive course, theoretical knowledge is integrated with practical application and relevant case studies to teach a variety of common types of money laundering schemes. Students will also learn strategies for detecting, investigating and reporting financial crimes.

cilos.description: Differentiate and explain the features and red flags associated with simple and complex money laundering operations.

Describe and differentiate the roles of various personnel, including board of directors, management, internal auditors, front line staff, and cybersecurity professionals, in the fight against financial crime.
Relate and explain what transaction monitoring is, its purpose and importance as part of financial crime risk management.

Compose an effective Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) Report which complies with legislative requirements and assess what constitutes "reasonable grounds for suspicion" that money or property being processed relates to the proceeds of crime.
Differentiate between a SAR Report and other reporting requirements and describe the risks of not reporting or submitting incomplete reports.

courses.title: Financial Crime Risk Management and Governance
courses.description: Rapid advances in technology in recent years have helped increase corporate productivity and enabled a global reach for companies, but such advances have also exposed them to criminal and fraudulent behavior. This course takes an advanced approach to managing and identifying risks associated with financial crime activities via the use of entity wide risk management and governance framework. The role of internal controls, governance, monitoring and communication responsibilities are also covered in the course.

cilos.description: Discuss the origins and key concepts of risk, risk management and risk management standards.
Explain the significance of issues of culture, appetite, and tolerance in managing risks, including their impact on a firm's financial reporting.

Evaluate the key features of corporate governance models, and the relationships between governance, risk oversight, board, management, internal control and assurance, and how they fit in the management and  reporting of financial crime risks.
Recognize and describe common mechanisms for illicitly moving money and schemes leading to occupational and financial statement fraud.

courses.title: Data Analytics for Financial Crime Investigation
courses.description: This course undertakes a systematic approach to the study of the theory and practice of financial crime investigation. The overall outcome of the course is to equip students with the tools and skills to detect and report financial crime. It aims to provide an understanding of common types of financial crime perpetrated, and to introduce students to strategies and techniques for detecting, investigating, and reporting financial crime as well as for preventing and deterring it.

cilos.description: Define key concepts and typologies of modern slavery and human trafficking and recognize relevant red flags.
Describe the impact of environmental crimes and explain the nexus between environmental crimes and financial crimes.
Identify and discuss some applications of data visualization, social network analysis, AI and machine learning in an AML/CTF approach.
Utilize analytical software to assist in forensic financial crime investigation.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in an identified area of accounting. This course may be repeated for credit if based on a different selection of topics.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a sound grasp of the literature in their specialization.
Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve business problems within their area of specialization.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

courses.description: Study of selected accounting issues under the supervision of a faculty member.  (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)

courses.description: Discussion of research in managerial accounting, auditing and corporate governance. Use of analytical and empirical tools in economics, finance and statistics to examine important accounting issues in the above areas.

courses.title: Fracture Behavior of Polymers
courses.description: Introduction to both fundamental and practical knowledge on the microstructure, physical and mechanical behaviors, particularly the fracture behavior and toughening mechanisms, of polymers and composites. Discussions and critiques on related research activities in the literature. Case studies to help students prepare for the industry.

cilos.description: Explain the microstructure-property relationships of polymers and select proper polymeric materials for specific engineering applications.
Characterize polymer fracture and evaluate fracture toughness of polymers using rigorous fracture mechanics methods under various conditions.
Explain the fundamental fractography of polymers and carry out basic failure analysis using microscopes and thermal analysis equipment.

courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Basic concepts of fluid flows, derivation of governing equations, viscous flow, potential flow, boundary layer, flow instability, transition to turbulence, turbulent boundary layer.

cilos.description: Apply fluid mechanics knowledge to certain practical problems.
Explain some fluid mechanics related phenomena in daily life.
Analyze practical fluid mechanics problems.

courses.title: Advanced Aerodynamics
courses.description: Circulation, Kutta-Joukowski theorem, thin airfoil theory, lifting line theory, wingtip vortices, induced drag, elliptical wings, boundary layers, normal and oblique shocks, bow shocks, Prandtl-Meyer expansion fans, linearized potential flow theory, Prandtl-Glauert transformation, wave drag, transonic flow, swept wings, critical Mach number, supercritical airfoils.

cilos.description: Apply the basic tools of incompressible inviscid aerodynamic analysis to estimate lift and drag for an airfoil.
Explain and quantify the effects of viscosity on airfoil performance.
Explain the differences in aerodynamic performance between an infinite-span (2D) airfoil and a finite-span (3D) wing.
Account for the effects of compressibility in aerodynamics situations.

courses.title: Advanced Aircraft Structures
courses.description: Aircraft structural design, wing structural details, elasticity, maneuver and gust loading, fatigue analysis, vibration theory, static and dynamic aeroelasticity, energy and matrix methods.

cilos.description: Apply the fundamental equations of elasticity to aircraft loading situations.
Use various deformation theories and fatigue analyses to obtain analytical solutions for situations in aircraft structural deformation.
Specify the materials used in aircraft structures and identify their failure modes.
Apply the basic principles of stressed-skin aircraft construction.

courses.title: Advanced Aircraft Design
courses.description: Flight mission requirements, aircraft size and layout, airfoil/wing geometry, aerodynamics, engine selection, airframe−engine integration, fuselage design, electrical and hydraulic systems, landing gear arrangement, flight stability and control, structures and materials, avionics and navigation systems, human factors, safety, manufacturing processes, and cost analysis.

cilos.description: Apply the formal design and development process for aeronautical vehicles.
Optimize aircraft/engine design and airframe-engine integration.
Create feasible designs integrating a variety of aircraft systems and sub-systems.
Test and verify the feasibility of aircraft designs.

courses.title: Aircraft Propulsion
courses.description: Propulsion cycle analysis, with emphasis on gas turbines, basic component performance and function, engine installation effects, aero-thermodynamics of steady isentropic compressible flow, shock waves, diffusers and nozzles, centrifugal compressors, axial flow compressors, combustion chambers, thermoacoustics, fuels and control, turbines, thrust augmentation.

cilos.description: Make design choices between aircraft propulsion systems based on perfonnance considerations.
Calculate energy release, e.g. adiabatic flame temperatures, and equilibrium composition of gases at known temperatures and pressures.
Analyze the thermodynamic performance of engine cycles and compute relevant performance parameters.
Size jet engines using preliminary design calculations.

courses.title: Composites and Nanocomposites
courses.description: This course is designed to provide fundamental understanding of fiber-reinforced composites (FRPs) and emerging nanocomposites technologies. The topics include constituent materials, microstructure-property relationships, fabrication and processing techniques, fundamental mechanics of stress transfer, lamination theory and failure mechanisms and fracture of FRPs in the first part. The topics in the second part include synthesis of nanoscale reinforcements, fabrication and processing techniques of nanocomposites; dispersion and functionalization of nanoreinforcements; interfacial adhesion; mechanical and functional properties of nanocomposites, and their design and applications.

cilos.description: Distinguish different fabrication and processing methods for FRPs and nanocomposites.

Explain the mechanical and functional properties of these composites based on the microstructures/properties of the fillers and the matrix material, as well as the way how these constituents are combined to produce composites.
Identify potential applications of FRPs and nanocomposites utilizing these properties.
Identify the mechanics of stress transfer through the filler/matrix interface and interphase, lamination theory and failure mechanisms behind the fracture of FRPs and nanocomposites.

courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamental knowledge of computational fluid dynamics, specific applications of CFD to industrial and environmental flows, learn how to write a complex two-dimensional solver and some engineering applications.

cilos.description: Apply the basic theory of Computational Fluid Dynamics, including discretisation, accuracy and stability.
Assess the impact of fluid mechanics problems commonly encountered in industrial and environmental settings.
Construct and apply computational models, determine critical control parameters and relate them to desired outcomes.
Use a state of the art commercial computational fluid dynamics package for numerical simulations of fluid mechanics problems.

courses.title: Avionics Technology
courses.description: Avionics are today at the very heart of the aircraft, controlling and monitoring a safe and efficient mission. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to present an accurate overview of what is an avionics platform, its systems, functions and operations. The course covers system fundamentals, current instruments and future development.

cilos.description: Identify how to derive the performance of various avionics systems.
Assess the requirements for individual avionics subsystems and provide guidance for future development.
Define the architecture of modern avionics and demonstrate conceptual understanding of its integration design.

courses.title: Hong Kong Airworthiness
courses.description: The civil aviation industry is one of the safest modes of transportation, yet complex and highly regulated. Almost every part of the industry is regulated. From the design, manufacturing and operation of an aircraft, people operating and maintaining the aircraft to organizations handling, operating and maintaining the aircraft, all are regulated by various rules and regulations. This course introduces the concept of airworthiness and examines the framework of both international and Hong Kong aviation regulations governing the aviation industry, allowing the students to understand the whole journey of the life of an aircraft.

cilos.description: Identify and explain the difference between Initial and Continuing Airworthiness.
Identify the applicable airworthiness regulations that an aircraft needs to comply with during its operating life and the conditions for safe operation.
Identify how operations and organizations in the aviation industry are regulated.

courses.title: Aerospace Materials and Applications
courses.description: Advances in aerospace systems such as aircraft, spacecraft, and launch vehicles are strongly dependent on advances in materials and processing technologies. This course aims to introduce aerospace materials and their applications in different aerospace systems. It equips students regarding the selection of the materials and their applications in various systems. It attempts to cover the entire field of aerospace materials in a condensed fashion with emphasis on aerospace structures and propulsion systems applications. At the end of this course, students are expected to achieve a comprehensive idea about how to select the best available material in every case in the field of aerospace engineering.

cilos.description: Recognize the visualization of the complexity of structural components and materials of the aerospace vehicles and understand their functions.
Apply the commonly used aerospace materials: metals and alloys, polymers, composites, and ceramics for different applications.

Identify a variety of functional requirements with constraints (manufacturability, geometric limits, environmental aspects, etc.) to arrive at the “optimum” choice of structural concept and materials selection for a given weight and/or cost.
Identify the capability to solve the real-world problems with engineering mindset.

courses.title: Airline Marketing
courses.description: In the airline business, marketing and airline/aircraft engineering work closely together, fulfilling the company vision, mission and strategy. This course covers the fundamental concepts of marketing, focusing on the airline business and the interrelationship with engineering in making the business a success.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental concepts of marketing, focusing on the airline business.
Identify the interrelationship between airline marketing and airline/aircraft engineering.
Apply acquired knowledge to analyze airline marketing  projects/campaigns, figuring out the role of engineering.

courses.title: Building Airport Operational Resilience
courses.description: One of the most affected industries in our inter-connected and inter-dependent world is civil aviation, which at one point collapsed to just 5% of its former self because of the effects from a pandemic. One lesson learned in the aviation industry is the need for all industry stakeholders to build up operational resilience. Strengthened operational resilience enables all stakeholders to meet risks and threats that are inter-connected and that can come from anywhere around the globe. This course will explore what is operational resilience, why it is important, and how to achieve it.

cilos.description: Identify aviation risks and threats in the 21st century aviation risk landscape.
Identify and explain the crossroads concept of 21st century airport management.
Identify the importance of operational resilience.
Examine building operational resilience and need for integration amongst all stakeholders within the airport community.

courses.title: Strategic Procurement Management in Aviation Industry
courses.description: In a rapidly evolving global market, aviation companies must enhance their capabilities or risk losing market share. This course explores how strategic procurement management can be a critical tool for survival and success in the aviation industry. With a focus on the impacts of outsourcing and offshoring, students will learn to manage procurement processes and mitigate risks effectively, understanding how these strategies influence the profitability and success of airlines and maintenance organizations in today’s competitive business environment.

cilos.description: Acquire a comprehensive understanding of the strategic procurement management process and identify its potential value creation.
Distinguish between strategic and tactical activities, recognizing their unique impacts and applications.
Utilize a diverse set of tools and techniques to thoroughly analyze internal and external environments.
Develop an appropriate strategy selection framework that analyze internal and external environments and create value for their organization.
Acquire a thorough grounding of negotiation planning for sourcing plan development.
Design effective value-for-money evaluation mechanisms to select the best offers in an objective and transparent manner.
Establish and manage efficient processes to ensure the performance of strategic sourcing contracts.
Design and implement a supplier management process focused on compliance with the statement of work and ensuring performance standards are met.

courses.title: Finite Element Methods
courses.description: Finite element formulation; variational principles for structural and continuum mechanics; numerical interpolation and integration; plane stress and plane strain analysis; plate bending and three dimensional solids; solution of large systems of algebraic equations.

cilos.description: Derive finite element formulations for structural mechanical problems and heat conduction.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Numerically calculate temperature profile and heat flux in 1-D and 2-D heat conduction problems.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structure under either plane-stress or plane-strain conditions.
Derive finite element formulations for time-dependent and/or non-linear problems.
Perform structural analysis and heat transfer modeling using commercial software package, and conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in aeronautical engineering of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Identify the updated development in the emerging area and apply the knowledge accordingly.

courses.title: Aeronautical Independent Project
courses.description: An independent research project on Aeronautical Engineering carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.

cilos.description: Address the existing problems in Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering through literature search and technical communication.
Apply acquired knowledge to analyze and investigate existing problems on Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering.
Design solutions to improve the existing techniques and conduct experiments/numerical simulations in the Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering area.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Artificial Intelligence.
Critically apply theories, methodologies and knowledge to address fundamental questions in AI.
Demonstrate practical skills in building AI systems.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.description: This special topics course will help students to gain a better understanding on the topics related to their interdisciplinary studies. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings or structured readings. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: AIS Cooperative Education Program
courses.description: This course is intended to enhance AIS students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs offered by the Career Center or those as recognized by the School, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For AIS Year 2 students or above only. Graded P of F.

cilos.description: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor. For DDP, RMBI, EVMT, and IIM students or those with approval from instructor for enrolling in the course. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Enhance understanding on selected interdisciplinary topics and real world issues, such as Technology, Entrepreneurship, Business and Sustainability.
Acquire updated market knowledge and skills through the interactions with instructors/ guest speakers from industry professions.
Develop multi-dimensional perspectives and interdisciplinary problem-solving skills that allow them to tackle cross-cultural and multi-faceted issues with a holistic approach.
Develop the potential to be caring leaders of society.

courses.title: Special Topics for Interdisciplinary Studies
courses.description: This course covers selected topics of current interest in emerging interdisciplinary areas which are not covered in the present curriculum. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter, P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Communicate complex ideas related to interdisciplinary topic in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of impacts in the topic concerned.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation.

courses.title: Professional Development for Interdisciplinary Programs
courses.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students basic training in ethics, teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills. This course consists of a number of mini-workshops. Graded PP, P or F.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Project
courses.description: An independent project on selected interdisciplinary topics carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. The course may be repeated once for credit. Enrollment requires approval of course instructor. Maybe graded by letter, P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Develop and apply self-learning and task management skills to effectively manage an independent project on a specific interdisciplinary topic.
Critically analyze a selected topic to identify, formulate and solve problems and apply solutions to practical implementations.
Apply the interdisciplinary approach in reviewing the latest developments, technologies or management strategies of the chosen topic.
Communicate effectively in writing, using accurate technical and scientific terminology, and demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Advanced Materials.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
Synthesize and create new knowledge, and make a contribution to the field.

courses.title: Independent Study in Arts and Machine Creativity
courses.description: Independent studies or projects under the directed guidance of a faculty member. Course requirements include readings on the relevant topic and a research or survey project specifically defined for the research topic. Credits assigned depend on the workload and may be repeated if different topics are taken. Enrollment requires approval of the course instructor. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the interplay between art and technology, including historical and contemporary contexts.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.
Strengthen and advance students’ knowledge and research skills sets for them to construct their specific research projects.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, develop motivation and creative skills for lifelong learning.
Work effectively in interdisciplinary teams, demonstrating strong communication and collaborative skills in the context of art and technology.

courses.title: Creative Convergence: Foundations of Arts and Machine Creativity
courses.description: This foundational course will be delivered by various faculty members to encompass a broad spectrum of topics related to arts and machine creativity, including Introduction to Art and Technology, Machine Creativity Tools and Techniques, as well as discussions related to Art, Technology, and Society.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the interplay between art and technology, including historical and contemporary contexts.
Acquire practical skills in using various machine creativity tools and techniques, enabling the creation of innovative artistic works.
Analyze and evaluate the societal implications of technological advancements in the arts, fostering informed discussions on ethical considerations.
Apply creative problem-solving strategies to integrate technology into artistic practices, resulting in original projects.
Work effectively in interdisciplinary teams, demonstrating strong communication and collaborative skills in the context of art and technology.
Identify and critically assess current trends and emerging technologies in arts and machine creativity, preparing for future developments in the field.

courses.title: Research Methodology in Arts and Machine Creativity
courses.description: This course provides postgraduate students with an in-depth understanding of the research methodologies and techniques utilized in the fields of arts and machine creativity. Students will explore various approaches to generating creative outputs through machines, including artificial intelligence, computational creativity, and algorithmic art, while developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the creative domain.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental concepts of the research methods in doing research related to the Arts and Machine Creativity.
Apply creative techniques in various research projects.
Develop problem-solving skills in developing the research methodologies from ideas.
Explore advanced topics and research through understanding the future trend in the area.

courses.title: Programming for Arts and Creativity
courses.description: This introductory programming course is designed specifically for students with an art background, focusing on fundamental programming concepts through creative problem-solving. Students will learn to decompose arts related challenges into manageable sub-problems and solve them using programming with the assistance of AI tools like ChatGPT. By blending technical skills with artistic expression, students will develop computational thinking while creating interactive and visually engaging works of art.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of fundamental programming concepts, including variables, data types, and control structures.
Apply problem decomposition techniques to break down complex art-related challenges into manageable sub-problems.
Create interactive visual projects using a programming environment like Processing or p5.js.
Implement functions and loops to enhance reusability and dynamic behavior in the projects.
Utilize AI tools like ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas, generate code snippets, and refine project concepts.
Collaborate effectively with peers to share feedback and improve project outcomes.
Present a final project that integrates programming skills with artistic expression, demonstrating creativity and technical proficiency.

courses.title: Generative Art: Algorithms and Creativity
courses.description: In this course, students will delve into the world of generative art by exploring algorithmic techniques for creating visual and interactive artworks. Through a series of hands-on projects, students will learn to implement algorithms that mimic natural processes and generate complex visual patterns. AI tools like ChatGPT will be integrated throughout the course to facilitate brainstorming, code generation, and project refinement, empowering students to harness technology as a medium for creative expression.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of key concepts in generative art as well as the historical context of generative art.
Analyze and modify existing algorithms for generative art.
Create generative art pieces using various algorithmic techniques and programming tools.
Employ AI tools effectively to enhance learning, brainstorming, and project development.
Collaborate effectively in a group project to present a final generative art piece that reflects the integration of programming skills and artistic expression.

courses.title: AI for Visual Arts and Creativity
courses.description: This course explores AI (especially machine learning) techniques for creating visual content in images and videos. The objectives of synthesis research range from modelling statistical distributions of visual data to creating realistic, picture-perfect graphics. Additionally, we delve into interactive tools for artistic expression. Throughout the course, we will cover key machine learning algorithms, including classical methods like nearest neighbour, PCA, and Markov Random Fields, as well as deep learning models such as ConvNets, GANs, VAEs, and Diffusion models. Students will gain practical skills to build applications and create new visual effects using their own photos and videos.

cilos.description: Understand classical and modern machine learning algorithms, including nearest neighbor, PCA, ConvNets, GANs, VAEs, and Diffusion models, and their applications in visual content creation.
Apply machine learning techniques to create innovative visual effects using photos and videos, demonstrating practical skills in AI-driven content creation.
Design interactive tools for artistic expression that utilize artificial intelligence algorithms to foster innovation and creativity in visual computing.
Demonstrate the ability to experiment with and innovate new AI techniques for visual content creation, presenting a portfolio of original work.

courses.title: Visual Computing for Visual Arts and Creativity
courses.description: This course introduces the basic knowledge of visual computing for visual arts and creativity including analysis, editing, creation covering basic concepts of image processing, computer vision, human-computer interaction and computer graphics. It covers mathematical and engineering foundations, including advanced geometry, multivariate calculus, linear algebra, image and signal processing, and human vision. Students will explore sophisticated algorithms for image warping, morphing, stitching, enhancement, inpainting, color processing, rendering, programmable media, graphical interface. By the end of the course, students will understand how visual computing can enhance artistic expression and creativity.

cilos.description: Explain the key theories and practices of image processing, computer vision, human-computer interaction, computer graphics.

Get a foundation in image/video editing and synthesis including texture synthesis and style transfer, image colorization and inpainting, video generation and editing, image-to-image translation, image and video editing.
Utilize visual computing techniques to enhance artistic expression and creativity in various media.
Gain hands-on experience with graphical interfaces and tools, enabling the creation and manipulation of visual content.

courses.title: AI-Driven Animation and Video Generation
courses.description: This course delves into the intersection of artificial intelligence and visual arts, with a focus on AI-driven animation and video generation. Students will explore cutting-edge models such as Transformers, Diffusion, Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DiT), and autoregressive systems. Emphasizing hands-on learning, the course guides students in implementing key AI components like LSTMs, attention mechanisms, and diffusion models. By the end of the course, students will gain both theoretical knowledge and practical skills for creating AI-driven media.

cilos.description: Understand the key principles behind modern AI-driven animation and video models.
Implement AI components such as LSTM, attention mechanisms, and diffusion models.
Analyze the performance and limitations of different AI-driven video and animation models.
Design AI-driven models for media generation, using state-of-the-art techniques.
Apply AI techniques to create animations and videos in real-world projects.
Evaluate AI-generated media in terms of quality, consistency, and artistic value.
Synthesize AI models to innovate and push the boundaries of creative media production.
Present project outcomes, explaining technical and creative aspects of their work.

courses.title: Interactive Visual Art with Generative Models
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of generative AI and visual arts, focusing on how interactive artworks can be created using models like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), transformers, and diffusion models. Students will gain practical experience building and fine-tuning generative models while integrating them into interactive artistic installations. Through hands-on projects and critical discussions, the course fosters an understanding of how generative AI shapes contemporary art and interactive experiences. Basic concepts in discrete mathematics and Python Programming language are required.

cilos.description: Understand the theoretical foundations of GANs, diffusion models, and transformers in the context of visual art.
Implement generative models to create interactive and dynamic visual artworks.
Analyze the creative potential and limitations of AI-driven models in visual art installations.
Design interactive visual systems that leverage generative models for real-time interaction.
Evaluate the artistic quality and user engagement of AI-generated interactive art pieces.
Collaborate with peers from diverse backgrounds to create interdisciplinary generative art projects.
Present interactive visual art projects that integrate generative models, showcasing both technical and artistic elements.
Innovate by pushing the boundaries of AI-driven art to explore new creative possibilities in visual art and media.

courses.title: Practice and Techniques for Visual Creatives
courses.description: This course equips students with practical skills and advanced techniques essential for visual creativity in the digital age. Through hands-on projects and theoretical insights, students will explore various aspects of visual arts, including digital imaging, graphic design, and multimedia production.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental concepts of the practice and techniques for visual creatives.
Apply visual creating techniques in artworks.
Develop problem solving skills in developing the artworks from ideas.
Foster interdisciplinary understanding through communicating ideas through various mediums.
Explore advanced topics and research in the creative industry.

courses.title: Technology in Music and Sound Art
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of technology with music and sound art, covering both fundamental concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain hands-on experience with digital audio workstations, sound synthesis, recording techniques, and audio effects.

cilos.description: Understand fundamental concepts of digital audio and music technology.
Apply industry-standard tools and techniques in music production and sound design.
Analyze and manipulate audio signals using various processing methods.
Create original works integrating advanced music technology concepts.

courses.title: Filmmaking with AI Innovations
courses.description: This course explores the transformative impact of AI on filmmaking, guiding students through AI-driven tools for screenwriting, previsualization, production, and post-production. The course covers ethical considerations and practical applications, enabling students to create compelling visual and narrative content with AI. Through hands-on workshops and projects, students will gain the skills to innovate and adapt in the rapidly evolving field of AI-enhanced storytelling.

cilos.description: Gain a solid understanding of AI applications in filmmaking, including screenwriting, previsualization, production planning, cinematography, post-production, visual effects, and animation.
Develop practical skills in using AI-driven tools and software for different filmmaking tasks, such as scriptwriting, storyboarding, scheduling, editing, and creating visual effects.
Apply AI tools to plan, execute, and manage film projects effectively, optimizing workflows and resource management.
Explore emerging technologies and future trends in AI filmmaking, preparing to adapt to and innovate within a rapidly evolving industry.
Engage in collaborative projects and peer reviews, fostering a community of learning and continuous improvement.

courses.title: Art Education and Technology
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of art education and emerging technologies. It aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to integrate digital tools into their art practice and pedagogy. Students will learn how technology can be applied to create, curate, and teach art, focusing on both theoretical and practical applications. Topics include digital media, virtual and augmented reality in art, online learning environments, and the impact of technology on artistic expression. Through hands-on projects and collaborative discussions, students will gain insights into how technology can transform both the creation and teaching of art.

cilos.description: Demonstrate proficiency in digital literacy by effectively using emerging technologies, including digital media, virtual and augmented reality, and multimedia tools, in both artistic creation and teaching methods.
Develop innovative art education techniques by leveraging technology to engage learners in dynamic, creative, and interactive ways.
Critically analyze the role of technology in shaping artistic expression, education, and societal values, identifying both opportunities and challenges in integrating technology into art education.
Create adaptable teaching strategies for hybrid and online educational environments, preparing to implement digital tools in modern educational settings.
Incorporate digital technologies into personal artistic practice and educational methods, effectively combining traditional art education with modern technological advancements.
Apply leadership skills in managing technology-enhanced art projects.
Address legal and ethical considerations in the use of AI and emerging technologies in art.
Engage in collaborative artistic practices that integrate machine creativity and human expression.

courses.title: Art ID, Blockchain and NFTs for Digital Creations
courses.description: This course investigates the convergence of art, web3, blockchain technology, and digital identity management. It provides students with a comprehensive understanding of how these technologies are reshaping the landscape of digital creations, including games, edutainment, AR/VR experiences, films, 3D digital artifacts, music, and more. Students will explore the concepts of metadata and Art ID for effective categorization and ownership tracking of diverse digital works. Through lectures, discussions, case studies, and hands-on workshops, participants will learn to create and manage their digital creations while considering the legal, ethical, and market implications associated with blockchain and Web3 technologies. The course emphasizes the transformative potential of blockchain and Web3 / NFTs in establishing ownership, authenticity, and support for new monetization avenues across various forms of digital art and creative expressions.

cilos.description: Evaluate and analyze the impact of Web3, blockchain technology and NFTs on the digital arts and entertainment industries using critical thinking skills.
Apply strategic thinking to identify and develop innovative solutions that combine traditional art practices and new digital art creations with emerging technologies.
Refine and justify approaches to digital ownership, provenance, and monetization strategies in the context of NFTs, Web3 and decentralized identity.
Formulate a comprehensive plan for creating, marketing, and monetizing digital artworks across various platforms and media.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders, including artists, collectors, and industry professionals, regarding the implications of blockchain technology in art.
Articulate a business proposal that includes a roadmap for launching Web3 and NFT projects within the digital arts ecosystem.
Integrate technical knowledge of blockchain and NFTs with business acumen to solve complex problems in digital creation projects.
Develop a professional portfolio that demonstrates mastery of digital art creation, NFT projects, and an understanding of market dynamics in the evolving landscape of digital arts.

courses.title: Management Strategies for Art and Technology Projects
courses.description: This course immerses students from interdisciplinary backgrounds in the dynamic and evolving fields of art and technology project management. It explores specialized management strategies tailored to these domains, emphasizing the contrasts and synergies involved in managing creative and technical projects. The course addresses common perceptions and misconceptions about project management, equipping students with practical tools to navigate these complexities. Through interactive lectures, hands-on practice, and collaborative projects, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of how effective management practices can significantly enhance project outcomes.

cilos.description: Identify and analyze the challenges and strategies inherent in managing art and technology projects.
Develop and apply practical skills in project planning, execution, and evaluation, utilizing tools and methodologies.
Cultivate leadership skills to lead and collaborate in interdisciplinary teams.
Engage in immersive project-based experiential learning that applies project management theories and tools in real-world contexts.
Create a comprehensive project proposal that integrates learned strategies and is ready for real-world applications.

courses.title: Art Administration and Art Business in the New Era
courses.description: The course teaches students key concepts and practices related to traditional and new practices in art administration and art business. They will be informed of the latest development in these two fields with a focus on the impacts from technological advancements including blockchain, immersive technology, and artificial intelligence. Professionals in the fields will be invited to give guest talks on the state-of-the-art practices. Students will acquire practical knowledge in both fields through case studies.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the essential concepts and practice of art administration and art business.
Analyze strategies of the management of different types of arts organizations with regard to human resources, venue operation, budgeting and revenue generation.
Apply the knowledge of operation, financing and marketing of arts organizations to a case study and report on their findings.
Understand the legal aspects of the art business, including contracts, copyright issues, provenance verification, and ethical considerations in art transactions.

Analyze the dynamics of the contemporary art market, identifying opportunities for applying new digital technology immersion, business models and economic factors that influence art valuation and investment.
Critically assess emerging trends in art administration and art business to address future challenges and opportunities within the evolving landscape of the arts sector with machine creativity.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders, including artists, collectors, and industry professionals, regarding the implications of new machine creative practices in art.

courses.title: Digital Art Provenance and Informatics
courses.description: The course provides a comprehensive understanding of the historical context and unique challenges of digital art provenance, focusing on authenticity, ownership, preservation and value in the art world. It covers digital provenance mechanisms such as metadata and blockchain technology, while addressing ethical considerations related to ownership, restitution, and transparency in transactions. Students will learn best practices for archiving and data management, engage with digital preservation standards, and gain hands-on experience with software tools for tracking provenance. Students will explore the evolving landscape of art provenance, the concepts of metadata and Art ID for effective categorization and related digital informatics. Through lectures, discussions, case studies, and hands-on workshops, students will learn to create and manage their digital creations while considering the legal, ethical, and market implications.

cilos.description: Evaluate the historical context and evolution of digital art, identifying its unique provenance challenges compared to traditional art forms.
Analyze various digital provenance mechanisms, including metadata, linked-data models, and blockchain technology, and their roles in establishing and verifying provenance.
Critically assess collaborative projects within the Digital Humanities that relate to art provenance research, evaluating their impact on the field.
Examine ethical considerations surrounding ownership, attribution, and distribution of digital artworks, considering the implications of emerging technologies.
Implement best practices for creating and maintaining digital archives and interoperable databases for provenance information.
Articulate a project proposal that applies knowledge of digital provenance to digital art projects in AI, VR/AR, and data art and address archival challenges within these projects.
Conduct a thorough analysis of community driven culture heritage informatics projects to understand their implications for provenance and ethical practices with new digital art immersion.

Develop a professional portfolio that demonstrates mastery of digital art provenance to demonstrate the ability to navigate the evolving landscape and contribute meaningfully to the field of arts and machine creativity.

courses.title: Business Development for Art and Technology Projects
courses.description: This is an innovative course tailored for students keen on mastering the business aspects at the crossroads of art and technology industries. The course delves into strategic planning, market analysis, entrepreneurship, and funding mechanisms specific to the art and technology sectors, utilizing real-world case studies and project-based learning. The course is designed to foster entrepreneurial skills and strategic thinking, preparing participants to launch and manage successful ventures within these dynamic fields.

cilos.description: Use quantitative and qualitative analysis to assess trends and consumer behavior in the emerging art-tech market industry.
Apply strategic management theories and methodologies to formulate comprehensive business strategies for art-tech ventures addressing real-world challenges.
Develop and model innovative business models for digital and interactive art enterprises to meet market demands.
Develop financial plans and financing strategies to address the complex regulatory frameworks and financial challenges of the art and technology industry.
Communicate concepts and models persuasively to a variety of stakeholders.
Assess the ethical implications of technology in art and its global impact on culture and society to ensure sustainability and respect for multicultural values.
Apply project management principles and agile methodologies to manage art-tech projects, ensuring flexibility and responsiveness to change.
Demonstrate entrepreneurial skills by planning, launching and managing a new art and technology start-up based on review feedback.

courses.title: Legal Issues in Art and Technology
courses.description: This is a pioneering course designed to address the complex legal frameworks influencing the intersection of art and technology. It explores crucial topics such as intellectual property, copyright laws, privacy, and ethical implications of AI in art, using a hybrid delivery model to cater to a diverse student body. Ideal for graduates and professionals in Art Management, Digital Media, and Intellectual Property Law, this course equips students to navigate and influence the evolving legal landscapes in creative and technological industries.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a thorough understanding of legal principles governing art and technology, and apply knowledge of intellectual property rights, privacy laws, and regulatory standards to real-world situations

Analyze various types of intellectual property protections for artistic and technological creations, and develop effective strategies to safeguard digital and interactive media, such as software and digital art.

Identify and interpret national and international regulations impacting the art and technology sectors, and evaluate their implications for global operations and cross-border transactions of creative tech products.

Solve complex legal issues arising from technology integration in new media and artistic expressions, and advise on legal considerations for emerging technologies like AI in art, blockchain for copyright management, and VR exhibitions.

Clearly convey complex legal concepts and strategies to non-legal stakeholders in art and technology projects, and prepare and present legal analyses and recommendations to peers, faculty, and industry professionals.
Assess the ethical and social implications of legal decisions in the art and technology sectors, and promote ethical practices that consider cultural sensitivity and potential global impact.

courses.title: Models of New Cultural Space
courses.description: The course informs students of the various types and models of cultural space developed from the post-war period to the present. Students will learn the definition, the architectural types and the new strategies in the formation of cultural spaces, as well as the theories and representative examples of such spaces. Professionals of cultural management will be invited to give guest talks on relevant topics. Students will be required to do field trips to study cultural space first-hand and report on their visits. They will also have the chance to develop a hypothetical cultural space project.

cilos.description: Understand the concept of cultural space and its significance in the contemporary world.
Know the architectural types for culture and their evolution.
Critically review the new strategies of development of new cultural spaces.
Explore the city as a collective cultural space, its value and meanings to the inhabitants.
Analyze new policies in the active making of cultural spaces and their consequences.
Examine the impact of globalization and digitalization in the creation of new cultural spaces.
Apply the knowledge acquired to the proposal of a new cultural space.

courses.title: Art Theory: Past and Future
courses.description: This course is a survey of different approaches to the interpretation of art and their influence on artistic creation through time. By reviewing the traditions of art theory from its very beginning in the 15th century to the 20th century, the course guides students to think critically about the theoretical bases of different approaches, and to contemplate art in the age of AI in the 21st century. Students will learn to use the key terms and definitions of the approaches and their applications, as well as the criticisms of the approaches.

cilos.description: Understand the major Western art theories from the 15th to the 20th century.
Utilize the terminology of art theories for the interpretation and communication of art.
Analyze art from philosophical, historical, cultural and social perspectives.
Develop new ideas for a possible art theory for machine-generated art of the 21st century.

courses.title: History of Motion Picture Science
courses.description: This course explores the evolution of motion picture technology from its inception to the present day, highlighting key innovations and scientific principles that have shaped the industry. The course delves into the historical milestones in cinematography, visual effects, sound, and editing, while also examining the latest advancements in AI, machine learning, and virtual production. Students will gain an understanding of both the technical and creative aspects of motion picture science, preparing them for future innovations in the field.

cilos.description: Analyze the key historical milestones in motion picture technology and their impact on the industry.
Evaluate the technological innovations that have shaped the development of cinematography, sound, and visual effects.
Demonstrate knowledge of the evolution of film practices, including the transition from silent films to digital cinema.
Critically assess the role of AI and machine learning in contemporary filmmaking and their implications for creative expression.
Explore the applications of virtual and augmented reality in storytelling and audience engagement.
Discuss the cultural and societal influences of motion pictures throughout history.
Create a project that integrates historical knowledge with contemporary technological practices in motion picture science.
Present findings on selected topics related to motion picture history and technology, demonstrating effective communication skills.

courses.title: Postgraduate Seminar
courses.description: Seminar topics presented by students, faculty and guest speakers. MPhil students must register and pass this course for one term before they graduate. PhD students must register and pass this course for two terms before they graduate. Graded PP, P or F. For students in the Division of Arts and Machine Creativity only.

cilos.description: Understand current research trends and applications.
Demonstrate effective presentation skills in seminar presentations.
Gain insight into research on topics that are directly related to their own research.
Gain insight into research and research methodologies used by other scholars working on areas not directly related to their own focus area.

courses.title: Professional Practice and Research (Projects)
courses.description: This course provides students with professional practice and research opportunities through a (research) project related to arts and machine creativity. The project idea is originated from the students, faculty members, or outside parties.

cilos.description: Plan, execute, and manage a creative project from inception to completion.
Analyze and evaluate project challenges, applying creative problem-solving techniques to develop innovative solutions.
Effectively incorporate research methodologies into the project development process, supporting creative decisions with data.
Work effectively as part of a team, demonstrating strong communication and collaboration skills.
Present project outcomes clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences, utilizing appropriate visual and verbal communication techniques.
Understand and apply ethical practices in project management and creative producing.
Engage in self-reflection to assess personal growth and learning throughout the project experience.

courses.title: Professional Practice and Research (Internships)
courses.description: This course provides students with professional practice and research opportunities through an internship related to arts and machine creativity at a research institution, a company, a public agency, or other organizations.

cilos.description: Gain hands-on experience in a professional setting, applying theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges in arts and machine creativity.
Develop professional relationships and networking skills that enhance career opportunities in the industry.
Identify and address real-world challenges faced by the host organization, demonstrating adaptability and resourcefulness.
Seek and incorporate feedback from mentors and supervisors to improve performance and professional development.
Reflect on the internship experience to evaluate personal strengths, weaknesses, and areas for future growth.
Understand and navigate workplace culture and dynamics effectively.
Demonstrate readiness for a career in the arts and machine creativity fields, showcasing skills and experiences gained during the internship.

courses.title: Special Topics in Arts and Machine Creativity
courses.description: This course covers selected topics of current interest in arts and machine creativity which are not covered in the present curriculum. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter, P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Communicate complex ideas related to the topic in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of impacts in the topic concerned.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation.

Credits assigned depend on the workload and may be repeated if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or PP for different offerings.

cilos.description: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge and understanding on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.
Articulate and present their arguments in a systematic way in a professional quality written report or oral presentation.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.

courses.title: Special Projects in Arts and Machine Creativity
courses.description: An independent project on selected topics related to arts and machine creativity under the supervision of a faculty member. The course may be repeated once for credits.  Enrollment requires approval of instructor. May be graded by letter, P/F or PP for different offerings.

cilos.description: Develop and apply self-learning and task management skills to effectively manage an independent project on a specific topic.
Critically analyze a selected topic to identify, formulate and solve problems and apply solutions to practical implementations.
Apply the interdisciplinary approach in reviewing the latest developments, technologies or management strategies of the chosen topic.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal in their research area in arts and machine creativity.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal in their research area in arts and machine creativity.

courses.title: Advanced Python Programming for Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course covers advanced Python programming skills for artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Students will learn to use popular AI libraries such as NumPy, Matplotlib, and Pandas, as well as deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch. Topics covered include data manipulation, visualization, and building neural networks. Prior experience in object-oriented programming is required.

cilos.description: Develop advanced Python programming skills, including the ability to manipulate and analyze large datasets, visualize data, and build and train neural network models.
Gain proficiency in using popular AI libraries and frameworks.
Learn how to deploy AI models for real-world applications.

courses.title: AI Fundamentals: Concepts and Methods
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive coverage of the theoretical and practical foundations of artificial intelligence. Students will learn the basic concepts and techniques of the core AI subareas, including search, logic, knowledge representation, machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, sequential decision making, and probabilistic reasoning. This course is designed to prepare students for more specialized AI courses.

cilos.description: Identify real-world problems where artificial intelligence techniques can be applied and propose appropriate solutions.
Apply a wide range of artificial intelligence techniques to solve problems.
Design intelligent systems that can learn from experience and make decisions based on data.

courses.title: Foundations of Machine Learning
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive coverage of both conventional and modern machine learning models and algorithms. Students will learn the theoretical foundations of machine learning and gain hands-on experience through software project experience. Topics covered include supervised and unsupervised learning for solving a wide range of machine learning tasks. Students will also learn how to evaluate and select machine learning models and apply these techniques to real-world problems.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of the theoretical foundations of representative machine learning models and algorithms for different learning paradigms.
Apply machine learning models and algorithms to solve real-world problems.
Evaluate the performance of machine learning models and algorithms using appropriate metrics and techniques.
Design and implement machine learning models and algorithms for various application sectors.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics
courses.description: This course explores ethical considerations in the design, development, and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Students will examine the social impacts of AI and the ethical challenges that arise in areas such as privacy, bias, transparency, and accountability. Through case studies and discussions, students will develop a framework for ethical decision-making in the development and deployment of AI systems.

cilos.description: Identify ethical issues that arise in the design, development, and use of artificial intelligence systems.
Evaluate the fairness and bias of artificial intelligence systems and propose ways to mitigate these issues.
Analyze the impact of artificial intelligence on society and the workforce and propose ethical guidelines for its development and deployment.
Develop ethical frameworks for the governance and regulation of artificial intelligence.

courses.title: Machine Learning for Computer Vision
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of machine learning techniques for computer vision and their applications in the field of artificial intelligence. Students will learn how to build and train different machine learning models for a wide range of computer vision tasks, including segmentation, recognition, and generation of visual data. Prior knowledge of Python programming and machine learning is required.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of computer vision and its applications in the field of artificial intelligence.
Gain proficiency in building and training popular machine learning models for a wide range of computer vision tasks.
Integrate conventional and machine learning techniques to solve computer vision problems in real-world applications.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement computer vision systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Machine Learning for Natural Language Processing
