courses.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of machine learning techniques for natural language processing and their applications in the field of artificial intelligence. Students will learn how to build and train different machine learning models for different natural language processing tasks, such as sentiment analysis, text classification, and language translation. Prior knowledge of Python programming and machine learning is required.

cilos.description: Develop a deep understanding of natural language processing and its applications in the field of artificial intelligence.
Gain proficiency in building and training popular machine learning models for a wide range of natural language processing tasks.
Integrate conventional and machine learning techniques to solve natural language processing problems in real-world applications.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement natural language processing systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Foundation Models and Generative Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course aims to help students explore the rapidly growing technologies underlying foundation models and generative artificial intelligence. Not only will students learn the fundamental concepts and techniques used for training foundation models, but they will also learn how to make effective use of them through prompting and integration into other artificial intelligence systems. Prior knowledge of Python programming and machine learning is required.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental concepts of foundation models and generative artificial intelligence.
Interact effectively with large language and multimodal models through prompting for a wide range of tasks in real-world applications.
Integrate foundation models into AI application development.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to design and implement generative artificial intelligence systems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of advanced AI techniques, including Markov decision processes, Q-learning, policy gradient methods, and deep reinforcement learning. Students will learn how to apply these techniques to real-world applications, such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems. Through hands-on projects and assignments, students will develop specialized skills useful for developing intelligent systems. Prior knowledge of Python programming and machine learning is required.

cilos.description: Identify the fundamental concepts and techniques of reinforcement learning.
Apply different reinforcement learning algorithms to solve real-world problems.
Evaluate the performance of different reinforcement learning models for a variety of tasks.
Develop and implement end-to-end reinforcement learning systems for real-world applications.
Critically analyze and compare different approaches to reinforcement learning.

courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Human-computer interaction (HCI) is an interesting and important area of study, providing the human perspective to computing. This course emphasizes on techniques, models, theories, and applications for designing, prototyping, and evaluating current and future interactive intelligent systems for human use. Besides technology and innovation, it also touches on issues like ethics and social responsibilities related to technologies, especially the emerging innovations of artificial intelligence, in the real world. Selected topics may include multimodal interaction design, ubiquitous/mobile computing, virtual/augmented reality, agents and robots, and HCI applications in various domains such as education, health, urban sustainability, and scientific discoveries.

cilos.description: Identify the basic concepts and methods in HCI research.
Identify the foundations and trends of HCI applications.
Design an interactive system using various methods through different design activities.
Prototype an interactive system with assorted digital and physical tools.
Evaluate an interactive system through user studies.
Communicate effectively with target users and different stakeholders in academia and industry.

courses.title: Medical Image Analysis
courses.description: This course will equip students with practical knowledge of medical imaging and analysis with deep learning techniques. It will cover fundamental knowledge of medical imaging and various medical image analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, segmentation, diagnosis and prognosis. Deep learning methods for solving these tasks will be introduced and state-of-the-art methods will be discussed. The remaining significant challenges and limitations will also be presented, including limited amount of labeled data, deep learning with interpretation and generalization issues, etc.

cilos.description: Explain the different medical imaging techniques and various medical image analysis tasks.
Acquire the fundamentals of deep learning methods with application to medical imaging and analysis.
Explain and apply the skills of deep learning technologies in medical image analysis tasks.
Identify and explain the state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for medical imaging applications.
Understand the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of medical imaging and analysis.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity
courses.description: This course aims to teach students using artificial intelligence (AI) to solve cybersecurity problems. Students will learn general principles in different cybersecurity domains, e.g., cybersecurity mindsets, cryptographic methods, software security, network security, and hardware security. Moreover, they will also learn how to effectively apply AI techniques to solve problems in cybersecurity domains and contexts.

cilos.description: Describe mainstream security issues in different computer systems and applications.
Use AI techniques to solve common security challenges and protect computer systems and applications.
Identify common security and privacy pitfalls in AI and technical solutions to harden AI systems.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to use AI techniques to solve cybersecurity problems that meet specific requirements and constraints.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
courses.description: With large-scale medical datasets being available, artificial intelligence, especially deep learning, has dramatically advanced the field of medicine and healthcare. Computer-aided analytical tools have been developed to assist doctors in disease diagnosis and prognosis. This course will introduce the fundamentals of deep learning methods, including discriminative and generative models, and apply these methods for analyzing a variety of medical data modalities, such as structural and functional medical imaging, genomics, electrical health records, etc. In addition, various applications covering cancer diagnosis and prognosis will be introduced. This course will equip students with practical knowledge of artificial intelligence for healthcare and medicine.

cilos.description: Identify the different AI techniques for various medical analysis tasks.
Acquire the fundamentals of deep learning methods for healthcare applications.
Explain and apply the state-of-the-art of deep learning technologies in medical analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, diagnosis and prognosis, etc.
Review the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of artificial intelligence for healthcare.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Software Engineering
courses.description: The course aims to introduce the concepts, methods, and applications of automated and AI techniques in software engineering problems. The course will cover topics such as software fault detection, code coverage, unit test generation, mutation analysis, search-based software engineering, fault localization, code repair, code generation, vulnerability analysis, large language models for code, performance and benchmarking of coding models, and empirical studies. The course will also explore the challenges, opportunities, tool support, and industry adoption of using AI in software engineering.

cilos.description: Apply fundamental concepts of the automated/AI technologies for software engineering.
Deploy automated/AI tools for fault detection and diagnosis on open-source software.
Evaluate potential issues in adopting automated/AI solutions on real software projects.
Design an appropriate automated/AI solution for a given software engineering task.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This course covers selected topics in artificial intelligence and its applications that reflect recent developments not covered by existing MSc(AI) courses. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Recognize the major issues and technical problems in a specific topic in artificial intelligence.
Identify key technical solutions to the problems in the topic.
Solve specific problems in the topic.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: This course aims to provide practicum training to MSc(AI) students through a capstone project on a specific topic of artificial intelligence (AI) relevant to MSc(AI). Students will learn and practise the project planning and reporting skills necessary for completing an individual or group project. Students will also learn to demonstrate professionalism and integrity in AI system development. Subject to approval, part of the project may be conducted in the form of internship. Nevertheless, project management and assessment will still be the responsibility of the University.

cilos.description: Apply project planning and management skills effectively by taking into consideration the characteristics of AI projects.
Develop effective written and oral communication skills to facilitate interdisciplinary collaboration and project reporting.
Develop an understanding of ethical and legal issues in AI.
Demonstrate professionalism and integrity in AI system development.
Conduct feasibility study to facilitate project planning.
Apply advanced AI technologies to solve real-world problems.
Apply project management tools for effective teamwork support.
Design experiments to generate results for project reporting.

courses.title: Data Science in Bioengineering
courses.description: This course will introduce the basic concept in data science, as well as the application of several data science technologies in the study of biomedical problems. It will include principles in network biology, machine learning and statistical analysis, and basic methods for sequencing data processing. Students will be evaluated based on group projects and student presentation.

cilos.description: Obtain a basic understanding of data science.
Identify high-throughput biomedical data.
Become familiar with the most popular computational methods.
Apply computational software to solve practical problems.
Enhance the ability to mathematically model scientific questions.
Enhance the ability in writing and presentation.

courses.title: Biomaterials Engineering
courses.description: The course covers fundamentals of material science and its interface with medicine. The design principles of biomaterials will be described for different applications, ranging from implants to drug carriers and tissue regeneration. Latest technologies to advance biomaterials design and fabrication will be taught. Considerations in regulatory approval process, manufacturing, and commercialization will be discussed.

cilos.description: Describe the roles of biomaterials in advancing modern medicine.
Identify the methods for preparation and assessment of biomaterials.
Outline design principles for major applications of biomaterials.
Appreciate the regulatory hurdles for commercialization of biomaterials.
Identify the GMP principles for manufacturing biomaterials.
Communicate knowledge learnt from class via oral presentation and written report.

courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Bioengineering
courses.description: This course will introduce the fundamentals in the molecular and cellular bases of life from an engineering perspective. Topics include analysis and engineering of biomolecular structure and dynamics, enzyme function, molecular interactions, metabolic pathways, signal transduction, synthetic biology, and cellular mechanics, etc. The lectures will be complemented by tutorials in protein engineering, AAV preparation, bioinformatics and machine learning, and structure visualization.

cilos.description: Describe and be familiar with biomolecular terminologies, molecules, cellular mechanisms, and networks.
Perform quantitative analysis in biological systems using a programming language (MATLAB, R, Python, etc.).
Apply modern-day machine learning tools for biomolecules (protein, virus) prediction and design.
Analyze and critique literature in related research areas and write professional report in the style of a journal article.
Apply problem solving and experimental thought processes in a wide range of settings.
Communicate scientific knowledge via oral presentation and written reports.

courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Sensing Technology in Healthcare
courses.description: The course will introduce the basic concepts in detection of biosignals. Students will learn about the biosensing components, transduction mechanisms, novel materials in sensing, and analytical techniques to capture diverse health information. The course will also touch upon the physical and chemical sensors used for healthcare applications. We will also discuss about the emerging flexible, wearable technology toward personalized healthcare. Students will have opportunities to design and propose biosensors and bioelectronics at the end of the course.

cilos.description: Explain how a biosensor work.
Identify the necessary components and their functions in a biosensor.
Describe different methods of biosignal determination.
Evaluate biosensors performance.
Identify the roles of nanomaterials in biosensors.
Visualize the biosensing market in diverse applications.
Propose biosensors for real world applications.

courses.title: Bioimaging and Bio-signal Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces various bioimaging methods and their data analysis approaches, including optical coherence tomography, fluorescence microscopy, nonlinear microscopy, super-resolution microscopy, ptychographic microscopy, and photoacoustic tomography. Students will be able to understand, design, and evaluate those imaging techniques. This course requires basic knowledge of linear algebra, calculus, and geometry. Familiarity with a programming language such as MATLAB is needed.

cilos.description: Describe the working principles of widely used bioimaging technologies.
Design and evaluate the imaging techniques that can acquire biological information.
Identify how the bioimaging technologies can address clinical needs in practice.
Identify the ways to process imaging data.
Analyze the processed imaging data and understand their associated important clinical outcomes.
Present professionally both in writing and orally.

courses.title: Synthetic Biology
courses.description: Synthetic biology, which echoes the assertion “What I cannot create, I do not understand” made by Richard Feynman, has been hailed as a revolution for modern science and technology. Unfledged as it is, the field, arising from the synergistic combination of chemistry, biology, engineering, data science, and information/control theory, has already shown great promise in addressing energy and health-related global challenges. This course aims to expose students with diverse backgrounds to this highly interdisciplinary field and furnish them with necessary guidance and ideas for taking on synthetic biology projects.

cilos.description: Explain the basic technical concepts, scientific and engineering principles in synthetic biology.
Describe the ramifications of synthetic biology for real-world problems.
Analyze the impacts of synthetic biology on other research areas such as materials science, developmental biology, and regenerative medicine.
Identify the key elements contributing to synthetic biology.
Recognize, evaluate, and criticize research topics in synthetic biology.
Communicate technical ideas more effectively.

courses.title: Genomics, Proteomics and Metabolomics
courses.description: This course will introduce the theory and practice of omics technologies for the high-throughput characterization of complex mixtures of biomolecules, including DNAs, RNAs, proteins and metabolites. Applications of omics approaches in life science research and clinical practice will also be covered.

cilos.description: Describe the basic principles of information flow in biology, and the molecular basis of biological information.
Describe the working principles behind high-throughput technologies for nucleic acid sequencing.
Describe the working principles of biological mass spectrometry for the high-throughput identification and quantification of proteins and metabolites.
Discuss the benefits and challenges of various omics analysis, and evaluate the applicability of each technology to a particular biological problem.
Analyze and interpret data generated from omics experiments with sound statistical principles.
Formulate experimental strategies for leveraging omics technologies to address biological questions, and to design omics experiments with appropriate controls and quality control measures.
Develop an appreciation of omics technologies’ impact on life science research and clinical practice, as well as the possibilities of the future.

courses.title: Pharmaceutical Engineering
courses.description: This course aims to equip students with broad knowledge in pharmaceutical engineering. The topics span from early drug discovery to late commercial manufacturing. Theory and practice of the chemical synthesis and the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), solid-state characterization of APIs, and formulation of various pharmaceutical dosage forms are covered. The course also introduces students to some of the main challenges in current pharmaceutical research and development related to selected topics such as continuous manufacturing and advanced process analytical technologies.

cilos.description: Explain key mechanisms for drug action, measurement, and administration routes.
Explain the SELECT criteria for commercial API synthesis and workup.
Classify and identify different solid forms of APIs and explain their importance for the manufacture and product quality of drugs.
Design and analyze pharmaceutical crystallization processes and workup steps.
Describe several key trends of innovation in the pharmaceutical industry.
Synthesize and explain the formulation of various liquid-dosage forms.
Synthesize and explain formulations of oral solid-dosage forms and design a process sequence for tablet manufacturing.
Synthesize and explain the main formulation strategies and the manufacture of controlled-release formulations.

courses.title: Protein Engineering
courses.description: This course introduces fundamentals of protein science and common approaches for protein engineering. It will provide students with the basic knowledge of protein structure and function. The protein engineering part will cover two important approaches—computational design and directed evolution—toward protein engineering. The course will involve several case studies to illustrate the use of modern computational tools for designing protein molecules including catalysts, biosensors, biomaterials, etc. The course will also cover the topics concerning directed evolution, including theoretical basis of of biomolecular evolution, concept of fitness landscapes, important applications.

cilos.description: Explain the basic technical concepts, scientific and engineering principles in protein engineering.
Describe the impacts of protein engineering on health and energy related real-world problems.
Analyze the influence of protein engineering on other emerging fields such as synthetic biology and genome engineering.
Identify the key components contributing to protein engineering.
Recognize research topics in protein engineering.
Communicate technical ideas more effectively.

courses.title: Advanced Biochemical Engineering
courses.description: The course will cover the advanced concepts of bioprocessing, including fermentation, bioreactor design, and product recovery. It will explore the production of bioenergy from renewable sources, such as biomass, biogas, and biofuels. Students will gain an understanding of the technical, economic, and environmental aspects of bioproducts and bioenergy production.

cilos.description: Describe the principles of bioprocess engineering and bioenergy production.
Explain how microorganisms and biochemical processes can be applied for various bioproducts and bioenergy.
Select, compare or design a reactor, fermentation processes or bioseparations used for various products, based on cost, safety, operability, etc.
Evaluate the production and potential of bioenergy from economic and environmental aspects.
Communicate biochemical engineering concepts through the use of engineering media, verbally and in writing.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Medical Imaging
courses.description: Nowadays medical imaging is rapidly growing and plays an indispensable role in healthcare. Recent advances of deep learning techniques have made significant breakthroughs in medical imaging applications. This course will cover fundamental knowledge of medical imaging and various medical image analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, segmentation, diagnosis and prognosis. State-of-the-art deep learning methods for solving these tasks will be introduced and discussed. This course will equip students with practical knowledge of medical imaging and analysis with deep learning techniques.

cilos.description: Explain the different medical imaging techniques and various medical image analysis tasks.
Obtain the fundamentals in deep learning methods with application to medical imaging and analysis.
Explain and apply the skills of deep learning technologies in medical image analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, diagnosis and prognosis, etc.
Identify and explain the state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for medical imaging applications.
Gain the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of medical imaging and analysis.

courses.title: Regulation, Ethics, Innovation, and Career Development in Biotechnology Industry
courses.description: This course offers weekly seminars from various industrial and academic speakers to broaden students’ understanding of industrially relevant topics in the biotechnology industry and its drivers for innovation. Students will engage with regulatory cases and will be briefed on ethical subjects in biotechnology industry. Furthermore, industrial and academic speakers will discuss important innovative trends in biochemical engineering and health informatics. Overall, this course aims to better prepare students for a career in biotechnology industry.

cilos.description: Recognize and engage in professional discussions on pressing ethical issues in biotechnology industry.
Define and discuss several regulatory approval processes in pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry.
Recognize and explain drivers for innovation in biotechnology industry.
Identify career paths in pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry.
Develop the skills to concisely communicate the outcome of a group project in a report and presentation.

courses.title: Equilibrium Behaviors, Rate Processes, and Transport Phenomena in Biological Systems
courses.description: Many physical, chemical and biological processes in nature and biological systems could be better described and appreciated by engineering and quantitative principles commonly used in chemical and biological engineering discipline. This course is intended to equip students with fundamental and integrated knowledge of core principles in thermodynamics, reaction engineering and transport processes that can be used to interpret some exemplary biological processes and provide mechanistic understanding of commonly known biological and physiological systems.

cilos.description: Describe a biological process or system using engineering intuition.
Apply engineering principles and conservation equations for better understanding of biological processes.
Acquire basic knowledge for quantitative analysis of a physical or biological process.
Describe a biological process or system in a quantitative way.
Acquire quantitative skills to make mechanistic interpretation of a biological process.
Delineate a biological process using engineering expressions.
Enhance soft skills, including communication in oral and writing.

courses.title: Deep Learning for Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the application of deep learning methods in chemical and biological engineering. The course will cover the fundamental concepts and techniques in deep learning, such as deep neural networks, backpropagation, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and transformer models. The course will focus on applying these methods to solve problems in chemical and biological engineering, including molecule and reaction property prediction, drug discovery, process monitoring and control, etc.

cilos.description: Understand the problem formulations using deep learning.
Understand the mathematical principle of deep learning methods.
Develop advanced model architectures.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Apply deep learning methods in chemical and biological engineering problems.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics in biomolecular engineering and health informatics. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.

cilos.description: Identify the most recent progress in biomolecular engineering and health informatics.

courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: An independent research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Acquire and process data from experiments or computations in the realm of biomolecular engineering and health informatics.
Develop practical skills of modern analytical, experimental, and computational techniques in biomolecular engineering and health informatics.
Develop the skills to concisely communicate the outcome of a research project in a report and presentation.
Effectively utilize academic literature and gathered knowledge to support a research project.
Critically reflect on observations and data to solve open-ended problems.
Engage in professional discussions with peers on topics in biomolecular engineering and health informatics.

courses.title: Integrated Design Project
courses.description: A design project on a topic in the realm of biomolecular engineering and/or health informatics carried out as a team effort under the supervision of a faculty member. It focuses on design thinking and getting hands-on experience with the engineering design process in a broad sense, and aims to accommodate students with more industry-oriented interests. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Develop design skills by performing a conceptual design of a chemical process and/or product in biomolecular engineering and/or health informatics.
Acquire and process data from experiments or computations for the purpose of design.
Develop the skills to concisely communicate the outcome of a design project in a report and presentation.
Acquire practical skills and knowledge required for biomolecular process/product design or health informatics through self-learning.
Critically reflect on observations and data to solve open-ended design problems.
Communicate and cooperate effectively in a team.

courses.title: Biotechnology and Business Seminar
courses.description: Study on selected current topics in biotechnology and business through attending seminars in related areas. This course provides a platform for students to interact and learn from different academic and practitioner leaders in both biotechnology and business fields. Graded P or F. For BIBU students only.

cilos.description: Understand the scientific principles underpinning those biotechnological innovations which achieve and maintain the competitiveness of biotechnology enterprises.
Critically evaluate contemporary biotechnological innovations and product ideas.
Understand the standards and conventions relating to social responsibilities and ethics practiced within a biotech firm.

courses.title: Biotechnology Entrepreneurship and Business Operations
courses.description: This course allows students to acquire a combination of essential scientific principles and practical business know-how in the biotechnology market, with an emphasis on the uniqueness and complexities of biotechnology entrepreneurship. Special focus will be placed on analyzing the critical factors that are pertinent to a successful venture in biotechnology. These factors will include scientific and technological advancements, intellectual property rights, as well as regulatory and commercial considerations. Students will eventually learn how to translate the knowledge into a business plan for start-up processes within the biotechnology industry. Guest speakers will include those who have experience in starting or managing biotechnology companies. For BIBU and BIOT students in their fourth year of study only. Other students may seek instructor’s approval for enrolment.

cilos.description: Critically understand and identify scientific principles, product sectors, business management, manufacturing requirement, regulatory guidance and marketing opportunities of biotechnology products in order to complete the due diligence, and delineate the milestones for their commercialization.

Carefully analyze and evaluate a selective product idea by identifying and discussing the strength, weakness, opportunity and threat of its development; in order to determine its suitability for commercialization.
Work and coordinate effectively in a team environment to research, prepare and deliver a business proposal of a selective biotech project for potential investors.
Apply scientific, regulatory, and management knowledge toward the registration, organization, daily operation, and growth of an entrepreneur enterprise.
Identify potential sources of funding through government or private investment locally and globally.
Ethically consider the social impact, benefit and requirement of a new biotech product, in order to minimize development time and improve revenue outcome.

courses.title: Biotechnology Management
courses.description: This course provides students with a general outlook of the roles and responsibilities in managing the biotech business. Business constraints like sales and marketing, partnerships, critical success factors in operations, market entry barriers, risk management and relationships with stakeholders will be covered in this course, with special focus on strategic development in the biotech business. Guest speakers will contribute their personal experience to offer a professional view of the key issues, pitfalls and opportunities in their daily business activity. A large use of case studies and other process management techniques will simulate potential scenarios in which students may be called to operate soon after they completed their university career. For BIBU students in their fourth year of study only.

cilos.description: Distinguish among all relevant priorities which flood and afflict the daily life of an entire biotech business such as R&D, manufacturing, testing (QC, QA), regulatory affairs, marketing and sales, distribution, logistics, finance, legal, communication.
Explain the role of stakeholders that gravitate around the biotech industry.
Identify Partnerships, Joint Ventures and Strategic Alliances as potential tools for increasing the company value and foster business opportunities in complex or hostile environments.
Practice "soft-tools" that are paramount to personal and business relationships with colleagues, customers and any other stakeholders.
Evaluate the commercial "risk" involved in daily commercial operations, as well as the overall corporate risk faced by the company as a large, autonomous and stand-alone organism.
Recognize the ethical implications of commercializing a biotech product in different geographical regions of the world.

courses.title: Biotechnology and Business Capstone Project
courses.description: Under the supervision of faculty members, students in small groups will undertake a project to investigate selected topics relevant to the biotechnology industry and its business operations. The project will be delivered through the format of literature review. Course assessment will be based on students’ written report and oral presentation that documents the project work and learning experiences. For BIBU students with approval of the course instructor for enrollment in the course.

cilos.description: Demonstrate knowledge of scientific research principles and methodology relating to the field of biotech business.
Apply knowledge and techniques acquired from the Program in addressing the issue relating to biotech business.
Demonstrate well-developed problem-solving skills for a wide range of problems in the biotech industry by taking into account of real-life constraints.
Develop critical thinking when making decisions in the real-life biotech business.
Recognize the operation of real-life biotech business, leading to understanding of professional, ethical, social issues and responsibilities.
Develop effective interpersonal and teamwork skills through written and oral presentation.

courses.title: Biotechnology and Business Project Research
courses.description: This is a one-year course. With a one-on-one supervision by faculty member, students will undertake a research project of their choice in biotechnological innovation/ideas: design of experiments, analysis of data, submission of a business plan/proposal in order to commercialize the selected biotechnological innovation/ideas. Credit load will be spread over the year. For BIBU students with approval of the course instructor for enrolling in the course. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Demonstrate Lab skills and methods relating to the field of biotechnology.
Utilize knowledge and techniques acquired from the Program for commercializing the biotechnological innovation/ideas.
Demonstrate well-developed problem-solving skills for a wide range of problems in the biotech industry by taking into account of real-life constraints.
Develop critical thinking when making decisions in the real-life biotech business.
Recognize the operation of real-life biotech business, leading to understanding of professional, ethical, social issues and responsibilities.
Develop effective interpersonal and teamwork skills through written and oral presentation.

courses.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
courses.description: This course is designed as an introductory course in biomedical engineering. The aim of this course is to present some of the basic science and human physiology knowledge used by biomedical engineers and illustrates the first steps in applying this knowledge to solve problems in human medicine. The second goal of this course is to link knowledge of basic science and engineering to fields of specialization and current research. This course also introduces the sub-specialties in biomedical engineering and through real-life examples to emphasize the types of problems biomedical engineers solve.

cilos.description: Summarize the key points of the areas in bio/medical engineering and demonstrate the applications of these areas in our daily life
Explain how to apply the engineering principles in solving bioengineering problems in daily life by showing examples
Explain why it is important for bioengineers to understand the human body
Critique the medical technologies in the markets based on your knowledge in bioengineering
Evaluate the social, ethical and economic impacts of innovations/technologies in bio/medical engineering
Demonstrate you are a good team player and presenter

courses.title: Introduction to Bioengineering
courses.description: This course provides an overview and lays the foundation for the bioengineering discipline. Students will delve into diverse topics such as biomaterials, biosensors, tissue engineering, and bioimaging. Through lectures with case studies, students will analyze the design and development of technological advances in healthcare and life science, including biomolecular tools, medical devices, and regenerative medicine applications.

cilos.description: Understand the foundational principles of bioengineering, including the integration of engineering concepts with biological systems.
Analyze and evaluate various bioengineering topics such as biomaterials, biosensors, tissue engineering, and bioimaging.
Apply knowledge gained to design and develop innovative solutions in healthcare, including medical devices, biomolecular tools, and regenerative medicine applications.
Evaluate and discuss the ethical implications and societal impact of bioengineering advancements in healthcare practices.
Develop the ability to address complex healthcare challenges in a team using bioengineering principles and interdisciplinary collaboration.

courses.title: Engineering Life: Synthetic Biology and Innovations for Human Health
courses.description: This course offers an introductory overview of synthetic biology and its innovations for human health, encompassing both technical and business aspects, tailored for undergraduate students. It is suitable for those intrigued by the cutting-edge technologies driving the emerging biopharmaceutical industry and interested in the transformation of synthetic biology. This course begins by exploring the timeline of biotechnology's emergence and development, delving into the discovery of groundbreaking pharmaceuticals in human history and the evolution of synthetic biology. It provides students with a framework for critical thinking while exploring the current landscape of synthetic biology. The course covers key milestones, explains foundational scientific concepts, and highlights the transformative impact of synthetic biology on human health. Through case studies, students gain insights into the opportunities and limitations in current and future technological advancements. Additionally, the course features guest lectures by experts from the industry and investment sector, offering valuable perspectives on course-related topics.

cilos.description: Explain the basic technical concepts, scientific and engineering principles in medical synthetic biology
Describe the opportunities and challenges facing the synthetic biology industry
Analyze the potential and impact of synthetic biology on human health and bioeconomy
Identify the key components that contribute to commercially relevant synthetic biology
Work in a team with complementary strengths
Communicate technical ideas clearly and effectively to diverse audiences
Evaluate personal interests in synthetic biology and the broader biotech industry through reflection on the course project

courses.title: Modeling for Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: Modeling of physical, chemical and biological processes. Balance Equations. Dimensional and scaling analysis. Analytical and numerical solutions to initial and boundary value problems. Use of computer tools for engineering calculations. This course uses examples in the Bioengineering discipline. For BIEN students only.

cilos.description: Model simple physical, chemical and biological processes as mathematical equations.
Develop and interpret differential equations in initial and boundary value problems.
Solve differential equations analytical and/or numerically.
Describe elementary concepts in statistics and perform simple hypothesis testing and regression analysis.
Use computing tools for engineering calculations.

courses.title: Cellular and Systems Physiology for Engineers
courses.description: Essential cellular and systems physiology for engineers. Hierarchical organization of a complex organism: from organelles to organ systems. Cellular physiology, neurophysiology, vision, muscle and movement, and the cardiovascular system.
courses.prerequisite: LIFS 1901 OR Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology

cilos.description: Describe the essential concepts in cell biology and systems physiology.
Describe the principles of the neural and cardiovascular systems.
Appreciate the connection between cellular and systems physiology and the design and engineering of pharmaceutical products and biomedical devices.

courses.title: Chemical Biology for Engineers
courses.description: A concise introduction of biochemistry, cell biology, and pharmacology to engineers. Molecular and supramolecular building blocks of biological systems. Analysis and engineering of biological systems by chemical principles. Introduction to transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics.
courses.prerequisite: (CHEM 1010 OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

cilos.description: Describe at a basic level the biochemical machinery of living cells.
Describe and apply analytical techniques for biomolecules, including omics.
Describe techniques and application of biomolecular engineering.
Describe concepts in basic pharmacology and drug discovery.
Apply concepts in chemistry to evaluate innovative ideas in bioengineering.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development I
courses.description: For students in the Bioengineering major. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students, to enhance their understanding of the bioengineering field, to encourage them to pursue co-curricular learning opportunities available to them, and to improve their communication skills. Students are required to attend discussion sessions with advisors and fellow students and selected workshops and seminars. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Be motivated and equipped to pursue the co-curricular learning opportunities available to bioengineering students.
Be aware of possible career paths of bioengineers and how to prepare for them.
Form a strong community with faculty and fellow students in the program.
Communicate effectively in group settings.

courses.title: Rate and Transport Processes in Biological Systems
courses.description: Analysis of transport phenomena and rate processes, including fluid flow, energy and mass transport, and reactions in biological systems. Applications in human physiology, bioreactors, medical devices, drug delivery, and biosensors. Mathematical and computational tools for solving problems and designing applications involving such processes.

cilos.description: Describe the fundamental principles of transport phenomena and reaction kinetics.
Describe and model rate and transport processes in biological systems.
Formulate and solve problems involving rate and transport processes.
Appreciate the connection between rate and transport processes and animal physiology and how it influences the effective design of various biomedical devices.
Use computing tools for problem solving involving rate and transport processes.

courses.title: Data Science for Molecular Engineering
courses.description: This course is an introductory course on the application of machine learning methods in molecular engineering problems. It covers fundamental data processing and machine learning methods to analyze data in chemistry and biology such as molecular similarity calculation and property prediction.

cilos.description: Identify problems that can be formulated as a supervised learning task.
Process different types of data to be ready for model training.
Understand the principles of supervised learning methods.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Know the application of data science methods in molecular science related problems.

courses.title: Data Science for Neural Engineering
courses.description: This is an introductory course on data science and its applications in neural engineering. The course introduces the fundamentals of data science, principles of  neuroscience, and the technologies and implementations of neural engineering. The  topics include probability, random variables, statistical detection and estimation, random process, structure and function of the nervous system, encoding and  decoding, population coding, neural network, plasticity and learning, neural interfaces and rehabilitation.
courses.prerequisite: (BIEN 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23) OR MATH 2111) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411)

cilos.description: Understand the basic concepts of probability, random processes, expectation and averages.
Obtain a holistic view of neural engineering.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Comprehend fundamentals of basic coding theory and computation methods.
Analyze neural data and implement on neural-controlled device/robot.
Enhance the knowledge in neural engineering, signal processing and practical programming.

courses.title: Data Science for Biology and Medicine
courses.description: This is an introductory course for the application of data science in biology and medicine. The course will introduce the fundamental principles on data science, the technologies and implementations of data mining, as well as the modeling of several practical questions in biomedicine. The topics include introduction to biomedical data, data visualization, regression methods and classification methods.
courses.prerequisite: {COMP 1021 OR [(COMP 1022P OR COMP 2011) AND COMP 1029P]} AND (LIFS 1901 OR level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology)

cilos.description: Obtain a basic understanding of data science as a discipline.
Understand high-throughput biomedical data of various types.
Visualize, analyze and interpret biomedical data with sound statistical principles.
Apply computational methods and software tools in data science in the context of biomedicine.
Develop mathematical models for scientific questions.

courses.title: Bioimaging and Image Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces various bioimaging methods and their data analysis approaches, including optical coherence tomography, fluorescence microscopy, nonlinear microscopy, super-resolution microscopy, ptychographic microscopy, and photoacoustic tomography. Students will be able to understand, design, and evaluate those imaging techniques. This course requires basic knowledge of linear algebra, calculus, and geometry.

cilos.description: Describe the working principles of widely used bioimaging technologies.
Design and evaluate bioimaging devices that can acquire biological information from the human body.
Describe how bioimaging technologies address biological and clinical needs in practice.
Research and evaluate information about bioimaging technologies and their applications.

courses.title: Biosensors and Bioinstrumentation for Healthcare
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamental principles in bioinstrumentation and biosensing devices, and practical examples of such in biomedical applications. Concepts in bioelectric and biochemical signals, their measurement and transduction will be introduced.

cilos.description: Describe the working principles of widely used bioinstrumentation and biosensors.
Design and evaluate bioinstrumentation and biosensors that can acquire bioelectrical or biochemical signals from the human body.
Describe how bioinstrumentation and biosensors address clinical needs in practice.
Appreciate how technological advances in this field can potentially revolutionize healthcare in the future.

courses.title: Bioengineering Laboratory
courses.description: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only.

cilos.description: Describe the principles behind the experimental modules and how they are applied in the experiments (tentatively molecular biotechnology, biomaterials, biosensors, sequencing and bioimaging).
Design and conduct experiments relevant to the bioengineering discipline.
Process, analyze and interpret experimental data in a statistically sound manner.
Develop soft skills including teamwork, open-ended problem solving, report writing and presentation.

courses.title: Special Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest not covered by existing courses. May be graded by letter, P/F, or DI/PA/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

courses.title: Regulatory Affairs in the Healthcare Industry
courses.description: This course aims to introduce basic concepts of regulatory science, while familiarizing students with product development, manufacturing, medical and engineering operations, and quality control / quality assurance processes in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry. Students will also be introduced to the associated regulatory requirements, with an emphasis on Hong Kong, Great Bay Area, China and beyond, in topics such as Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), pharmaceutical product registration, pharmacovigilance, and clinical trials.

cilos.description: Form a conceptual framework of regulatory science and engineering that underpins regulatory affairs of medical products worldwide.
Outline the current practices of medical and engineering operations in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry.
Describe the importance and processes of quality assurance / quality control in the manufacture of both pharmaceutical products.
Outline how Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and Pharmaceutical Inspection Convention and Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) are implemented.
Outline the roles of medical affairs, medical science liaison, and pharmacovigilance in the pharmaceutical industry.
Describe the principles and practice of clinical trials and the importance of clinical trials in drug development.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent studies or projects under the directed guidance of a faculty member on a bioengineering topic. Enrollment in the course requires prior approval of the course instructor, and credits assigned depend on the workload. Students may repeat the course if different topics are taken. The course may be grade by letter or P/F subject to different offerings. May be graded PP.

cilos.description: Learn the professional and technical knowledge in the bioengineering research area.
Equip students with written and presentation skills in engineering disciplines.

courses.title: Bioengineering Capstone Design
courses.description: A final-year project course offers practice of bioengineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Bioengineering Thesis Research
courses.description: A final-year project course offers an opportunity to conduct individual bioengineering research under the direct supervision of a faculty member, which leads to a Bachelor's thesis. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Manage a research project effectively by personal management and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.
Obtain and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own research.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering research on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Articulate research questions and outcomes effectively both in writing and orally.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Conduct scholarly research in the realm of bioengineering.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments.
Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.

courses.title: Bioengineering Industrial Project
courses.description: This course is intended to provide final-year bioengineering students with practical hands-on training in the form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in a bioengineering company. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.

cilos.description: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Development II
courses.description: For final-year Bioengineering students. This course is designed to prepare students for the workplace, to instill in them a sense of professional responsibility, and to enhance their career management skills. Students are required to attend selected workshops and seminars by practicing bioengineers. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Understand the career opportunities available to bioengineering graduates.
Approach the job search process with preparedness and confidence.
Function effectively in the workplace as a professional.
Appreciate the standard of ethics and professional responsibility expected of bioengineers.

courses.title: Molecular Biology for Bioengineering
courses.description: The course introduces the basics of cell biology, molecular biology techniques, and discusses the principles of macromolecular interactions in those contexts. We will also discuss various applications of these techniques and how combined with engineering concepts, they have contributed to innovations and breakthrough tools in the world of basic research and medicine. Topics to cover include: overview of basic molecular biology and macromolecular interactions; basic biophysical structures, imaging and characterization techniques; molecular engineering; biodevices; and genomics. Active student discussion is required and students will also do a final project team presentation on a current bioengineering topic.

cilos.description: Describe the central dogma of molecular biology, and be able to recall the various molecular components (molecules, proteins/enzymes) involved in the components of the central dogma. Describe their main physical features and select appropriate tools/techniques for characterizing them.

Explain the mechanisms and functions of basic molecular biology assays, including PCR, qPCR, gel electrophoresis, molecular cloning, protein separation and purification; be able to analyze and interpret results of above assays.
Compare different types of imaging tools, and describe their usage and importance in modern biotechnology/medicine.

Explain what a stem cell is, and compare differences between embryonic stem cells, fetal stem cells, adult stem cells, and induced pluripotent cells; recall modern applications of stem cell therapies, and explain the mechanism of action for these therapies; describe current major challenges in using stem cell therapies in the clinic.

Explain and critique recent breakthroughs in molecular biology and bioengineering fields, including those outside your research area; be able to suggest potential applications of these new technologies to a relevant clinical challenge.

Present and discuss the taught ideas and concepts with peers with clarity and evidence-based reasoning; collaborate with team mates with positive attitude and strong work ethic in a group project setting.

courses.title: Introduction to Neural Engineering
courses.description: This course will provide a survey of Neuroscience and Neuroengineering research areas to provide our research postgraduate students a broad appreciation of interdisciplinary research in context. The course aims to help student recognize and understand how knowledge from science and engineering interface in this interdisciplinary application. Concepts such as neural interfacing and neural prosthesis will be introduced so that students can understand the impact of the latest technologies. The course will enhance the vision of the students and encourage them to work in future inter-disciplinary research fields.

cilos.description: Obtain a holistic view of systems neuroscience fundamentals and methods.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Write a literature review on a topic within systems neuroscience.
Explain basic neural coding theory and computation method.
Enhance the knowledge in related area, such as neural engineering.

courses.title: Global Health Ethics
courses.description: Through real-time videoconferencing with participants from different countries such as the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Mexico, and Philippines, this ONLINE course aims at helping students learn the definitions of global health ethics and bioethics, the different protocol and systems in place to ensure adherence to ethical principles, and how different stakeholders and cultures may interpret ethics differently. Through case studies on ethical challenges from real-world situations, students will analyze and discuss the complexities of global health practice and research ethics in a global context. This course is co-offered with the University of Southern California. Besides the joint LIVE sessions, face-to-face sessions and group projects are also arranged for the introduction of background knowledge, case studies, group project discussion, and technical support.

cilos.description: Articulate the important ethical considerations of biomedical research, basic and clinical, involving human subjects.
Outline the unique ethical and social implications of conducting such research in developing countries of different economic status.
Identify key trends and emerging issues in global health ethics.
Analyze situations of ethical challenges in global health practice and research from diverse perspectives.
Appreciate the role culture and religion play in the development of a sense of right and wrong and views on ethics and how protocol fitting to the local context can be justified
Describe best practices in ethical health research and practice to protect human subjects and their legal right

courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Sensing Technologies in Healthcare
courses.description: The course will introduce the basic concepts in detection of biosignals. Students will learn about the biosensing components, transduction mechanisms, novel materials in sensing, and analytical techniques to capture diverse health information. The course will also touch upon the physical and chemical sensors used for healthcare applications. We will also discuss about the emerging flexible, wearable technology toward personalized healthcare. Students will have opportunities to design and propose biosensors and bioelectronics at the end of the course.

cilos.description: Explain how biosensors work.
Describe different techniques for bio-signal determination.
Evaluate biosensors performance.
Propose biosensors for real world applications.

courses.title: Synthetic Biology
courses.description: Synthetic biology, which echoes the assertion “What I cannot create, I do not understand” made by Richard Feynman, has been hailed as a revolution for modern science and technology. Unfledged as it is, the field, arising from the synergistic combination of chemistry, biology, engineering, data science, and information/control theory, has already shown great promise in addressing energy and health-related global challenges. This course aims to expose students with diverse backgrounds to this highly interdisciplinary field and furnish them with necessary guidance and ideas for taking on synthetic biology projects.

cilos.description: Describe the basic concepts and engineering principles in synthetic biology.
Describe the central dogma of molecular biology and control strategies of gene replication, transcription, post-transcriptional modification, and translation.
Describe the genetic parts, devices, circuits, and systems in synthetic biology.
Explain the design of genetic circuits, including genetic input, biological computing, and output Modules, and describe what Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is in synthetic biology.
Explain the mechanisms of synthetic biology tools, including Gibson assembly, Golden Gate assembly, DNA recombination, DNA synthesis, directed evolution, and genome editing.
Recognize, evaluate, and criticize the design of genetic circuits in scientific literature of synthetic biology.
Explain real-world applications of synthetic biology.
Enhance communication skills.

courses.title: Microfluidics and Biosensors
courses.description: Introduction to Microfluidics and Biosensors; Overview of microfabrication materials & techniques; microfluidic principles; miniaturized biosensors; micro total analysis system (µTAS) & lab-on-a-chip (LOC) for clinical and research applications.

cilos.description: Describe core concepts in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Describe trends and motivations in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Analyze/critique research articles in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Formulate a potential solution for a clinical problem using Microfluidics & Biosensors.

courses.title: Bioengineering Seminar
courses.description: Seminar topics presented by students and faculty. Students are expected to attend regularly and demonstrate proficiency in their seminar presentation in accordance with the program requirements. Graded P or F.

cilos.description: Identify current research of interest in various topics of bioengineering.
Obtain insights to how peer researchers design and conduct experiments.
Gain opportunities to make academic and social contacts with the peer researchers.
Demonstrate proficiency in presentation of research outcome coherently and thoroughly (as presenters).

courses.title: Bioengineering Colloquia
courses.description: Bioengineering Colloquia is a seminar course that brings prominent researchers in the field of bioengineering to share their research with BIEN colleagues and students. The course aims to provide a platform for discussions and exchange of ideas on the late advancements in the field of bioengineering. Students will have the opportunity to engage with the speakers and ask questions, fostering a deeper understanding of the research presented. The course will cover a broad range of topics, including chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, synthetic biology and more. Students are expected to attend regularly. Grade P or F.

cilos.description: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the latest advancements and research trends in various areas of bioengineering.
Develop the ability to critically analyze and evaluate research presentations, recognizing the significance and implications of the findings.
Improve their ability to articulate questions and engage in discussions, enhancing their communication skills in a professional setting.
Appreciate the interdisciplinary nature of bioengineering by exploring topics across chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, and synthetic biology.
Learn how to network effectively with professionals and researchers, building connections that may benefit their academic and career pursuits.
Develop informed perspectives on current challenges and future directions in the field of bioengineering.

courses.title: Special Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Selected topics in bioengineering of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to integrate knowledge and to analyse, evaluate and manage the different aspects of a special topic in bioengineering.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work.
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

courses.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
courses.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

courses.title: MPhil Thesis Research
courses.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.

cilos.description: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

courses.title: Principles and Application in Biotechnology
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide an interdisciplinary, state-of-the-art introduction to biotechnology.  Topics include the molecular foundations of biotechnology, molecular microbiology, biotech process development and scale-up, product approval and regulatory affairs, genomics, microarray analysis, proteomics, computational biology, molecular modeling, analytical biotechnology, and bioterrorism and biotechnology.

cilos.description: Process factual knowledge comprehensively across the principal area of biotechnology.
Explain information related to the principles of cutting-edge biotechnology.
Evaluate information related to and data derived from experimental models in biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to research methodology of biotechnology.
Identify complexity of issues facing biotechnology and types of contributions that can be offered to society.

courses.title: Business Operations of Biotechnology
courses.description: Management perspective of R&D process, methods for planning and organizing biotechnology ventures, basic concepts of intellectual property rights and methods and principles of marketing new technology-based products and services.

cilos.description: Demonstrate a broad based knowledge in core business and management perspective of pharmaceutical industry.
State basic concepts of intellectural property rights.
Recognize the aspect of regulatory affairs of pharmaceutical products.
Apply appropriate marketing methods for new technology-based products.
Develop business plan for biotechnology-based products via team work.
Engage with professionals in the field of biotechnology business.

courses.title: Bioanalytical Technology
courses.description: The use and development of biomolecules for analytics: enzymes and immunotests, DNA probes, biosensors and biodipsticks.  Application of other analytical techniques for bio- and medical sciences will also be introduced.

cilos.description: Apply functional methods in biotechnology to solve problems in analytical work.
Identify knowledge in the experimental design for development of bioanalytical tools.
Evaluate different analytical methods used for measuring biological substances.
Describe the value of biomedical analysis on human health.

courses.title: Biomarkers and Medical Devices
courses.description: Introduction to biomarkers and its examination by medical devices, with a focus on utilization of biomarkers in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, and a comprehensive overview on the regulatory affairs and marketing strategy of medical devices.

cilos.description: Explain knowledge about biomarkers and its instrumentation.
Evaluate the wide scope of application of biomarkers in diagnosis and therapy for various diseases.
Apply functional knowledge of biomarkers for cases of clinical diagnosis and disease treatment.
Describe the methodology related to biomarker analysis.
Interpret the business competence and market potential of biomarkers.

courses.title: Biopharmaceutical Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to various laboratory techniques commonly applied in the biopharmaceutical industry for drug discovery and development applications, with a focus on gaining hands-on experience through laboratory practices. Advanced techniques such as automated screening and multiplex detection will be covered.

cilos.description: Demonstrate hands-on laboratory techniques applied to cell culture, transfection, protein detection and quantification, cytotoxicity, etc.
Evaluate the wide scope of applications for laboratory protocols involved in the process of various bioassay.
Integrate various biological and pharmacological concepts to establish possible schemes for drug screening.
Design and perform experiments for automated screening of potential drug candidates with defined targets.
Devise team-based laboratory tasks and construct formally-written report for experimental data.

courses.title: Drug Discovery and Development
courses.description: Overview of methodology employed in identification of lead compounds, drug synthesis and development.  Receptor screening technology for target identification, high-throughput screening for lead identification, and the process for turning lead compounds into marketable drug products.

cilos.description: Explain basic and in-depth information about drug discovery and development.
Apply functional knowledge in the design and selection of drug discovery assays.
Evaluate information and data derived from drug screening activities.
Describe the fundamental concepts of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.
Employ different approaches to identify lead compounds and optimize candidates for drug development.
Identify regulatory affairs and key factors in relation to the drug development process.

courses.title: Nutraceuticals and Transgenic Products
courses.description: Highlights in current applications of biotechnology on the research and development of nutraceuticals and transgenic products.  Scientific approaches to natural product drug discovery, TCM-based health products, and nutritional products will be discussed.

cilos.description: Explain the general concept underlying the use of nutraceuticals and transgenic products.
Describe how nutraceutical and transgenic products are developed.
Describe in a broad sense about experimental and clinical studies on nutraceuticals.
Evaluate the scientific and commerical potentials of a candidate nutraceutical and transgenic product, and to produce a feasibility report on it.

courses.title: Recombinant DNA Technology and Bioproducts
courses.description: The course focuses on upstream and downstream processings in biotechnology.  Molecular biology of recombinant DNA techniques, the properties of fermentation broths, the selection of source material or organisms and the separation technology for the recovery of products.

cilos.description: Review the wide scope of applications of biotechnology in medicine, agriculture, biomass utilization for energy generation, and environmental conservation.
Apply functional knowledge in microbial selection and manipulation for bioproduct synthesis.
Evaluate the key concepts and scientific principles of fermentation technology in relation to industrial biotechnology.
Describe the day-to-day business management and operation undertaken in a biotechnology corporation.
Identify the legal, social and ethical concerns in biotechnology.

courses.title: Concepts in Bioprocessing
courses.description: Weaves concepts and fundamentals common to various aspects of bioprocessing.  They include the analysis of transport phenomenon in biological systems (for example, immobilized cell or enzyme systems, artificial organs, and drug delivery systems); genetic engineering techniques applied to microorganisms, animals, and plants; and the cellular machinery and process by which biological products are synthesized by the cell.

cilos.description: Recognize the basic information of bioproduct and bioprocessing.
Define the flow of bioreactor industries from upstream to downstream processes.
Explain major examples for application and research in the bio-productive processes.
Indicate the advanced knowledge of fermentation technology in relation to industrial biotechnology.
Apply functional knowledge in molecular farming.

courses.title: Immuno Biotechnology
courses.description: A systematic review of the overall organization and function of the immune system with a special emphasis on antibody-based technology and its broad applications in various aspects of scientific research and medicine.

cilos.description: Describe basic knowledge of immunology.
Define the principles and operations of immune cell development, immune diversity and response.
Explain immunological applications and their uses in research and medicine.
Describe the latest trend in antibody-based technology.
Identify the potential of immunology for biotechnology.
Critically review the literature in immunology.
Analyze and solve problems related to immune responsiveness.

courses.title: Case Investigation in Biotechnology
courses.description: Students will review a topic of their choice in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member.  An in-depth reading and analysis by the student of the selected topic leading to the submission of a written report, and its presentation in a seminar.

cilos.description: Retrieve and explain information correlated with the business values of a biotechnological company.
Evaluate information based on comprehensive search of scientific databases, websites and international journals.
Produce high quality reseasrch independently.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking through reading, analysis and synthesis of information, and production of research reports.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Directed Biotechnological Research
courses.description: Students will undertake a research project of their choice in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member.  The results of the research will be presented in a seminar and be formally written in the form of a final report.  For MSc student who can participate in day-time laboratory work only.

cilos.description: Develop laboratory skills and methods related to research work of biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to qualitatively and quantitatively appraise experimental data and outcomes.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking for experimental design and production of research reports.
Conduct laboratory research via team work.
Engage with fellow graduates and/or professionals in the field of biotechnological research.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Advanced Biotechnological Research
courses.description: Students will undertake a research project in an area of biotechnology under the supervision of a faculty member. The results of the research will be presented in a seminar and be formally written in the form of a final report. For full time MSc students only.

cilos.description: Develop laboratory skills and methods related to research work of biotechnological applications.
Apply functional knowledge to qualitatively and quantitatively appraise experimental data and outcomes.
Demonstrate self-reflective thinking for experimental design and production of research reports.
Conduct laboratory research via team work.
Engage with fellow graduates and/or professionals in the field of biotechnological research.
Present research results clearly and convincingly in seminars and research reports.

courses.title: Foundations of Chemical and Biological Engineering
courses.description: This foundational course is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the core principles of the disciplines within the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering (CBE).
